### 1.1  FRA Hedge Deal Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The maturity profile of a bank’s interest bearing liabilities and assets does not generally match, resulting in a gap that entails interest rate risk. To manage or hedge the identified interest rate risk there are several interest rate derivatives and one of them is FRA instrument (which is widely t...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acrd Mkt Ex Profit in Lcy*, *Acrd Mkt Exch Profit*, *Choose FRA Deals*, *Daily Accrual Amount*, *FRA Long Rate*, *FRA Type*, *MKT Exch PL Amt*, *MKT Exch Profit in Lcy* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The maturity profile of a bank’s interest bearing liabilities and assets does not generally match, resulting in a gap that entails interest rate risk. To manage or hedge the identified interest rate risk there are several interest rate derivatives and one of them is FRA instrument (which is widely traded in Over the Counter market).

When a FRA deal is undertaken by the bank, it is required to identify the purpose as either Trade or Hedge so that it becomes easy to apply the appropriate accounting method and correct treatment of profit and loss arising out of FRA deal.

- When the deal is undertaken to hedge the identified interest rate risk in the balance sheet is termed as FRA hedge deal.
- When the deal is undertaken without any interest rate risk to be hedged is termed as FRA trade deal.

A bank enters into an FRA deal for hedging purpose on the following conditions:

- The bank needs to have net assets or liabilities, which are subject to interest rate risk. This condition must exist after commitments and anticipated transactions to reduce the risk.
- The FRA transaction needs to be designated as a hedge to reduce the interest rate risk on exposed assets and liabilities.

FRA is an OTC traded instrument, it offers the flexibility to customise the trade terms to the requirements of both the parties to the deal.


#### 🔧 Working With

FRA transactions are inputted using the FRA.DEAL application. FRA Hedge Deal is handled by selecting the appropriate versions available within the Model Bank system.The basic details pertaining to input a FRA.DEAL are:

- Counterparty
- Principal (notional)
- Currency
- Rate
- Commission
- Brokerage
- Settlement details

The FRA Type field is one of the key fields for FRA input, as it specifies whether the deal is a Trade or Hedge. FRA.DEAL does not accept input of a transaction unless the FRA Type is specified, as this determines accounting rules for the transaction. If booked incorrectly, the classification of a FRA cannot be changed, and needs to be reversed and rebooked.

A deal identified as Hedge is treated differently with regard to revaluation, accounting and amortization of P and L on rate fixing event.

Treasury Customer and Treasury Rate fields are used to identify a customer as a treasury customer. These fields allow the users to input the treasury rate (if required). The Treasury Customer field holds either the value Null or No, which denotes the following:

- By default, this field defaults the value as Null, which indicates that the counterparty is a treasury customer.
- If set as No, it is construed that the counterparty is not a treasury customer.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the value is set as No, it is mandatory for the user to input a value in the Treasury Rate field.

Input to these fields is not allowed after authorisation of the deal.

##### Marketing Exchange P&L Calculation on Settlement Date

When the market exchange profit or loss figure is posted on the trade date, it is not discounted as the settlement rate is not known upfront. If recalculation of market exchange profit or loss is required on the settlement date, that is, when the settlement rate is known, the Recalc Mkt PL field on FRA.PARAMETER is set to Yes. After authorisation, this field becomes a no change field. Mkt Ex PL Categ and Mkt Ex Pr Categ fields within FRA.PARAMETER file holds either a Null value or relevant category codes.

The following fields are also used to display and record certain elements of the contract throughout the term of the trade:

- MKT Exch PL Amt
- Market Exchg Profit
- Daily Accrual Amount
- Total Accrual Amount
- Acrd Mkt Exch Profit
- Acrd Mkt Ex Profit in Lcy
- MKT Exch Profit in Lcy


##### FRA Interface with Position Management

FRA application is fully integrated with Position Management (PM) module.

There are two main events in FRA that lead to an update to PM. One at the time of recording the deal in the system and the other at the time of rate fixing of the contract.

The following rules apply for the interface to the various components of the PM module:

For hedge contracts, from the input of the FRA contract to the rate fix date, a projected cash flow is shown in PM Cash-flow and the same represents the mark to market (MTM) value of the contract. Revaluation process during each COB supplies these number to PM Cash-flow, until the rate fixing event, when the estimated number is replaced by the true value.

The rate fixing date is defined on the FRA.PARAMETER table as follows:

- Foreign currency - normally two days before settlement date
- Local currency - same as the settlement date

The settlement amount is calculated and the resulting profit (in) or loss (out) is included in the cash flow under the settlement value date.

By default, only hedging contracts are included in PM module. The Ref Price on the FRA.DEAL contract is used for the long period rate. The short period rate is calculated/derived according to the standard formula.

The FRA Long Rate field in PM.PARAMETER offers an option to treat an FRA deal as a synthetic loan and deposit. To opt for this, a user exit routine is required to be attached to the field.

The standard FX position request is performed within the accounting process, whenever entries have an impact on the foreign exchange position. This can be seen in the following:

- Foreign currency charges and commission
- Settlement amount in foreign currency
- Accruals on hedge contracts in foreign currency


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (FRA)
- FRA Trade Deal Processing
- Treasury Processes

FRA – Hedge Buy

A Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) Hedge Buy is a contract, where the buyer makes an agreement to borrow the notional amount with an aim of hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest, which is fixed at the start of the contract.

FRA – Hedge Sell

A FRA Hedge Sell is a contract, where the seller makes an agreement to lend the notional amount with an aim of hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest, which is fixed at the start of the contract.


##### Workflow

This sections allows the user to perform the below activities:

To create a FRA Hedge Buy deal, perform the below steps:

1. Capture FRA Deals
2. Select the FRA Hedge Buy option from the Choose FRA Deals field drop-down.
3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Amount Currency Interest Rate Agreement Type FRA Period
4. In the Settlements tab, enter settlements details.
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

1. Capture FRA Deals
2. Select the FRA Hedge Sell option from the Choose FRA Deals field drop-down.
3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Amount Currency Interest Rate Agreement Type FRA Period
4. In the Settlements tab, enter settlements details.
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

Amend FRA is a processes of making changes to the settlement instructions and to fix the rate on the rate fixing date of FRA deal.

To amend a Forward Rate Agreement deal, follow the below steps:

1. Maintain FRA Deals .
2. Click the Amend icon corresponding to a FRA Deal record.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate Icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

This enquiry helps the user to authorise or delete a FRA Group Fix.

1. Group Fix Authorisation .
2. Click the Authorise icon corresponding to a FRA group Fix record.

To delete a FRA Group Fix, follow the below steps:

1. Group Fix Authorisation .
2. Click the Delete icon corresponding to a FRA group Fix record.
3. Click the Delete icon to delete the record.

Broker Confirmation is a deal that is executed without Broker confirmation and yet to receive the confirmation. Users can view and record broker confirmation using this enquiry.

To record broker confirmation for a FRA Deal, follow the below steps:

1. Broker Confirmation on FRA .
2. Click the Verify icon corresponding to a FRA Deal.
3. Amend the deal with the required broker confirmation details.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

This enquiry displays the list of FRA deals for which the counterparty confirmation is yet to be received from the counterparty involved in the deal. The user can view the deal details and record the confirmation received.

To record a counterparty confirmation, follow the below steps:

1. Counterparty Confirmation of FRA .
2. Click the Verify icon corresponding to a FRA Deal record.
3. Amend the deal with the required confirmation details.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

This enquiry helps the user to authorise or delete a Forward Rate Agreement.

To authorise a FRA deal, follow the below steps:

1. Trade Authorisation .
2. Click the Authorise icon corresponding to a FRA deal record.
3. Click the Authorise icon to authorise the record.

To delete a FRA deal, follow the below steps:

1. Trade Authorisation .
2. Click the Delete icon corresponding to a FRA deal record.
3. Click the Delete icon to delete the record.

This enquiry displays the list of authorised FRA deals and allows the user to reverse or cancel the records.

To reverse an FRA deal, follow the below steps:

1. Reverse FRA .
2. Click the Reverse icon corresponding to a FRA Deal record.
3. Click the Reverse icon to submit the deal for reversal or cancellation.

This enquiry allows the user to modify the Unauthorised Forward Rate Agreements.

To modify the Unauthorised FRA Deals, follow the below steps:

1. Unauthorised FRA .
2. Click the Amend icon corresponding to a FRA Deal record.
3. Amend values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.


#### 📊 Outputs

In FRA enquiries, the user can view, amend, delete and perform Rate Fixing on FRA deals. FRA reports display the various outputs related to FRA, such as, Revaluation, Profit and Loss, Outstanding FRAs and so on.


##### Enquiries and Reports

The user can view the following enquiries and reports:

FRA Hedge Deal Report

This close of business report displays the list of Outstanding FRA Hedge Deals. The user can view the complete report for a FRA Hedge Deal by clicking the View Report icon corresponding to a record.

FRA Overdues Report

This report displays the list of FRA deals for which the interest fixing is overdue. The user can view the complete report by clicking the View Report icon corresponding to a record.

Outstanding FRAs Report

This close of business report displays the list of outstanding FRA deals. The user can view the deal details in report by clicking the View Report icon corresponding to a record.

FRA Hedge Position

The enquiry displays the position information on all the Hedge contracts. The information about the deal that makes up the position in addition to the profit data is displayed. The user can view the individual transaction by clicking the View FRA Record icon corresponding to a record.

Today’s Deal

This enquiry lists the FRA deals done today. It is possible to drilldown to the FRA.DEAL from this enquiry.


##### SWIFT Messages

The below list of SWIFT Messages are generated by the core banking system pertaining to FRA Trade Deal.

MT340 is a FRA agreement confirmation sent to the counterparty by SWIFT or Print.

MT341 is a message exchanged by or on-behalf of institutions or corporates and between parties, who have agreed to a Forward Rate agreement (FRA). This message is used to confirm the settlement details of FRA, when the settlement rate is fixed on the fixing date.


##### Advices

The below list of advices are generated by the core banking system pertaining to FRA Hedge Deal.

This is a confirmation notice to the counterparty in Forward Rate Agreement deal. It consists of trade details, such as, Contract Currency, Amount, Contract Period, Settlement Date, Maturity Date, Contract Rate and so on.

This is a confirmation notice of settlement sent to the counterparty in Forward Rate Agreement deal. When the settlement takes place through rate fixing, a confirmation notice is generated with the trade details, such as, Contract Currency, Amount, Contract Period, Settlement Rate and so on.

### 1.2  FRA Positions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The FRA module updates a separate position file, FRA.POSITION .*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Calculate or Book*, *Hedge Reval Method*, *Loss*, *Profit*, *Profit Loss Equi*, *Profit or Loss*, *Reval Method*, *Reval Status* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The FRA module updates a separate position file, FRA.POSITION .

Trade FRAs are part of FRA.POSITION file, either on a consolidated or an individual deal basis. Option to choose deal-wise position exists in FRA.PARAMETER .

By default, hedge FRAs are not part of the FRA.POSITION table. However, depending on the configuration on FRA.PARAMETER , position is updated, revalued and details made available in FRA.HEDGE.POSITION .


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section helps the user to understand the configuration of FRA Position.

- Trading FRAs are revalued either on a consolidated or individual deal basis, according to the configuration in the Tr Deal Wise Reval field in FRA.PARAMETER . Depending on the rules setup within FRA.PARAMETER table, the booking of the revaluation profit and loss happens.
- FRA.POSITION contains position information about all the trade contracts.
- Hedge FRA usually offsets an identified interest rate risk within the bank’s balance sheet, and are not included in the FRA.POSITION file. However, the Hedge Reval Method field on FRA.PARAMETER can include them in Position under a separate table ( FRA.HEDGE.POSITION ), for revaluation purpose according to the IFRS accounting rules.
- Unlike trading FRAs, where positions are valued either on a consolidated or individual basis, hedging FRAs are always revalued on an individual basis.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Trading FRAs

Consolidated FRA position in FRA.POSITION table is created based on currency, dealer desk and period. FRA position records information of the deals that make up the position and the information on the combined profit data.

Position is created for every deal when the option to revalue on an individual contract basis is chosen.

FRA position is maintained and revalued on a consolidated basis, created based on currency, dealer desk and period or deal-wise, optionally.

The example below illustrates the consolidated position related to a trade type contract:

For each FRA position, the user can view the following:

- Current position, position at start of business today, cost of position
- Profit realised today from FRA closures. Closure profit from previous days, and from back valuations
- Revaluation of total open position
- Discount period
- Discount rate

Each position also records information about the constituent deals, if it is a consolidated revaluation. Trades done today are kept separate from previous business but the following information is stored for both:

- Deal ID
- Trade date
- Principal
- FRA rate
- Profit (if closed)

The following example illustrates the position on individual deal basis:


##### Hedging FRAs

The position for FRA hedge deals with a value Book or Calculate in the Reval Method field is maintained in the FRA.HEDGE.POSITION file. Unlike trade deals, where the position is maintained group-wise, the FRA.HEDGE.POSITION is always maintained on individual deal basis.

The FRA.HEDGE.POSTION table records information along with other things, whether the deal is a Buy or Sell, the rate at which the deal is marked to market (MARKET RATE), the deal rate, the notional amount of the deal and the FRA period. Reval Method field displays whether the unrealised profit or loss needs to be booked (Field Value - Book) or not (Field Value - Calculate) and just display the calculated value.

The Reval Status field displays the following statuses of the deals: unfixed, fixed, overdue for fixing and reversed. Accordingly, the profit or loss available against the Profit or Loss field mentions whether it is realised or unrealised. The Reval Status field when contains unfixed status, the profit or loss mentioned on Profit or Loss field is unrealised.

For deals, whose rates are fixed during the day, Reval Status field is updated with the text FIXED.REAL (during the Close of Business processing), and the Profit or Loss field then records the realised profit or loss.

If the deal is in foreign currency, the Profit or Loss displays the profit or loss in foreign currency and the Profit Loss Equi displays the local currency equivalent of the same.

The various values of the Reval Status field are as follows:

- UNFIXED – The deal is yet to be fixed.
- FIXED – The deal is fixed.
- FIXED.REAL – The deal is fixed. Realised profit or loss is calculated.
- UNFIXED.DUE – The deal is yet to be fixed. Fixing date is crossed.

When a deal is reversed, the Reval Status field is updated with a suffix ‘.REV’. FRA.HEDGE.POSITION record does not exist for deals without a value in the Calculate or Book field.

### 1.3  FRA Revaluation and Settlement


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Revaluation measures the estimated profit and loss on account of the FRA position held. What follows revaluation is the accounting treatment for the unrealised revaluation P&L for which several options exist on FRA.PARAMETER for trade and hedge types separately.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Reference Rate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Revaluation measures the estimated profit and loss on account of the FRA position held. What follows revaluation is the accounting treatment for the unrealised revaluation P&L for which several options exist on FRA.PARAMETER for trade and hedge types separately.

Settlement in an FRA deal includes determination of profit and loss upon rate fixing event, discounting the P&L to present value (if opted for) and accounting for the same.

In hedge transactions, an option is available to amortise or not to amortise the P&L arising out of the rate fixing event.

Revaluation process involves the following three distinct steps:

- Finding the estimated unrealised P&L
- Future rate calculation
- Discounting the P&L to present value

Settlement calculation involves the following three distinct steps:

- Rate Fixing event
- Calculation of realised P&L
- Discounting the P&L to present value


#### ⚙️ Configuration

- The rates for various dates are fetched from PERIODIC INTEREST table and the key to the table is mentioned in Reference Rate field within FRA application. The rates are either directly consumed or interpolated from the rate curve defined.
- The formulae for discounting the future value of P and L is available on FRA.PARAMETER table. Options include no discounting, discounting using the rate contract is fixed and discounting using the long rate prevailing at the time of rate fixing or revaluation.
- The P&L category and reserve or suspense account category codes for both realised and unrealised profit or loss are maintained in FRA.PARAMETER .

##### Discounting the P&L to Present Value

FRA contract is settled and the formula for the present value of the profit or loss is based on different settlement formulae (currently there are three formula while there is a provision to define nine different formulae). The user can choose one of the following that is applicable for all currencies, or for each currency, a different formula can be applied. This option is available in FRA.PARAMETER .

- Settlement Formula 1 – The discount rate is same as the market rate, and the discount period is same as the FRA period.
- Settlement Formula 2 – No discounting is required.
- Settlement Formula 3 – The discount rate is the long rate used to find the market rate, and the discount period is the one corresponding to the long rate.

#### 📖 Introduction

Apart from dealing with FRA for hedging purpose, bankers operate for other purposes, such as general trading and arbitrage. The concept of revaluing the positions is important to manage the risk arising out of these speculative activities. To segregate the trade concepts, the input of trades requires the inclusion of trade types, which allows the system to distinguish trades into their relevant categories both for accounting and revaluing purpose.


#### 🔧 Working With

A trade FRA deal is booked either to open a fresh position or close an existing position created by previous deals. FRA Trade Deal is handled by selecting the appropriate versions within the system. Read FRA Hedge Deal for more information on the basic details required to input a FRA.DEAL .

Treasury Customer and Treasury Rate fields are used to identify a customer as a treasury customer. These fields allow the input of a treasury rate, when marketing exchange functionality is required. The Treasury Customer field holds either the value Null or No.

- By default, this field defaults the value as Null, which indicates that the counterparty is a treasury customer.

- If set as No, it is construed that the counterparty is not a treasury customer.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the value is set as No, it is mandatory for the user to input a value in the Treasury R ate field.

Input to these fields is not allowed after authorisation of the deal.

Following is an illustration of an FRA Trade Deal:

##### Marketing Exchange P&L Calculation on Settlement Date

When the market exchange profit or loss figure is posted on the trade date, it is not discounted as the settlement rate is not known upfront. If recalculation of market exchange profit or loss is required on the settlement date, that is, when the settlement rate is known, the Recalc Mkt PL field on FRA.PARAMETER is set to Yes. After authorisation, this field becomes a no change field. Mkt Ex Pl Categ and Mkt Ex Pr Categ fields within FRA.PARAMETER file holds either a Null value or relevant category codes.

The following fields are also used to display and record certain elements of the contract throughout the term of the trade:

- M kt E xch PL A mt
- M arket E xch g P rofit
- Daily Accrual Amount
- Total Accrual Amount
- Acrd Mkt E xch P rofit
- Acrd Mkt Ex P rofit in Lcy
- Mkt E xch P rofit in Lcy


##### FRA Position Management Interface

FRA application is fully integrated with Position Management (PM) module.

There are two main events in FRA that lead to an update to PM. One at the time of recording the deal in the system and the other at the time of rate fixing of the contract.

The following rules apply for the interface to the various components of the PM module:

For Trade contracts, provided the parameter option to include trade deals in PM is set, from the input of the FRA contract to the rate fix date, a projected cash flow is shown in PM Cash-flow and the same represents the Mark to Market (MTM) value of the contract. Revaluation process during each COB supplies these number to PM cash-flow, until the rate fixing event, when the estimated number is replaced by the true value.

The rate fixing date is defined on the FRA.PARAMETER table as follows:

- Foreign currency – Normally two days before settlement date
- Local currency – Same as the settlement date

The settlement amount is calculated and the resulting profit (in) or loss (out) is included in the cash flow under the settlement value date.

By default, only hedging contracts are included in PM module. However, trade deals can also be included by opting to include trade deals in PM.

The standard FX position request is performed within the accounting process, whenever entries have an impact on the foreign exchange position. This can be seen in the following:

- Foreign currency charges and commission
- Revalued amount in FCY during revaluation process
- Settlement of Profit and loss in FCY

### 1.5  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) module facilitates processing of standard Forward Rate Agreement deals.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement*, *Amount*, *Buyer*, *Contract*, *Currency*, *D*, *Date*, *FRA* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) module facilitates processing of standard Forward Rate Agreement deals.

FRA is an agreement between two parties to protect themselves against future movements in interest rates. It is a cash-settled over the counter contract, where the buyer borrows (and seller lends) a notional sum at a fixed interest rate (the FRA rate) for a specified period starting at an agreed date in the future. It is a flexible instrument that can be customised to meet the needs of both the buyer and seller. In short, a FRA is a forward-forward deposit or loan.

The parties lock in an interest rate for the stated period of time starting on a future settlement date, based on a specified notional principal amount (to calculate interest payment). For example, three to six months FRA deal at a fixed interest rate on a notional sum is entered on the trade date.

The waiting period of the contract is considered from the calculated spot date (generally T+2) to three months, and the start date of the contract commences only after three months. The maturity date of the contract is six months from the calculated spot date.

Fixing date is the date on which the prevailing interest rate for the period is determined. It is calculated for the currency contracts as follows:

- Foreign currency contracts – Two days prior to the start date
- Local currency contracts – Same day as start date

FRA effectively ends on the settlement date, which is same as start date, as there is no contractual agreement between counterparties henceforth. The contract period is one of the calculation parameters to determine the settlement amount.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Contract Rate (or FRA Rate ) | The interest rate that the two contracting parties negotiate on trade date. This rate is compared to the settlement rate during the calculation of settlement amount. It starts on the settlement (d3) date and ends on maturity date (d4). |
| Contract Period | The time between the settlement and maturity dates of the notional loan. This period can go upto 12 months. |
| Currency | The currency in which the FRA's notional amount is denominated. |
| Fixing D ate | This is the date on which the reference rate is determined, that is, the rate to which the FRA rate is compared. |
| FRA Buyer | The buyer of an FRA is the contracting party that borrows at the FRA rate (contract rate). |
| FRA Seller | The seller of an FRA is the contracting party that lends at the FRA rate (contract rate). |
| Master Agreement | Usually counterparties sign a master agreement between each other before entering into an Over the Counter (OTC) contract because huge amount of paperwork is generated and processed for every single deal without a master agreement in place. |
| Maturity Date | The date on which the notional loan is deemed to expire. |
| Notional Amount | The notional sum for which the interest rate is guaranteed and all interest calculations are based. |
| Reference Rate | The interest rate index to which the FRA rate is compared to determine the settlement amount. This is generally an IBOR-type rate index with the same duration as the FRA's contract period. For example, six months EURIBOR for an FRA in euros with a six-month contract period). |
| Settlement Amount | The amount calculated as the difference between the FRA and reference rate, as a percentage of the notional sum paid by one party to the other on the settlement date. The settlement amount is calculated after the fixing date for payment on the settlement date. |
| Settlement Date | The date on which the notional loan period (the contract period) begins and settlement amount is settled. |
| Spot Date | The market spot date applicable on the contract is usually two business days after the trade date. |
| Trade Date | The date on which the FRA is negotiated between the two counterparties. |
| Waiting Period | The period between the value date (d1) and settlement date (d3). |

FRAs are settled using cash on the settlement date. The exposure to each counterparty is determined by the interest rate differential between the market rate on settlement date and the rate specified in the FRA contract and there are no principal flows.

FRAs allow market participants to trade today at an interest rate that will be effective in the future. Thus, FRA is a tool to hedge interest rate exposure on future engagements.

The buyers of the FRA believe in locking-in a borrowing rate that protect them against a rise in interest rates. The sellers believe that obtaining a fixed lending rate protect them against a fall in interest rates. If the interest rates neither fall nor rise, there are no benefits for buyers and sellers.

The following definitions describe the terms used in this document:

PROFIT where the settlement rate is HIGHER than the FRA.DEAL contract rate.

LOSS where the settlement rate is LOWER than the FRA.DEAL contract rate.

PROFIT where the settlement rate is LOWER than the FRA.DEAL contract rate.

LOSS where the settlement rate is HIGHER than the FRA.DEAL contract rate.

The FRA application in Temenos Transact supports recording, administration and processing of FRAs. This application automates accounting, limit exposure, position updating, control and administration of trading activity and ensures efficient delivery of the related advices and payments.


##### Product Configuration

This section describes the configuration options the system offers in FRA.


###### FRA Dependency

FRA module uses the following tables:

- CUSTOMER
- ACCOUNT

These records are dependencies for FRA deals. The CUSTOMER records are necessary for any transaction, and to draw details of the counterparty. The ACCOUNT records are opened for payment and receipt of foreign currencies, settling brokerage, collecting charges and commissions.

Following are the other core dependencies tables:

- ACCOUNTING
- DELIVERIES
- LIMIT

DELIVERIES is a core Temenos Transact module, which helps in generating messages and advice for FRA transactions. The accounting entries for FRA transactions are generated during Close of Business (COB). On validation of the transaction, the system updates the position. Limits for transactions are set up before or after the input of transactions. If the limit is not set up, system creates an override message notifying the absence of a limit. On authorisation, the system automatically creates a limit for the customer for the relevant limit product.

FRA also uses other static tables, such as:

- CURRENCY
- COUNTRY
- HOLIDAY
- REGIO

Implementation of FRA module begins with configuration of various parameter tables. Below are the set of files in their respective build sequence that are required for FRA setup. Mandatory files are marked with a (*) mark.

Using this parameter users can define the following: Acceptable rate variations Spot and fixing date Timing and content of revaluation entries Default product category codes for Trade and Hedge transactions Parameter for confirmation matching Parameter for creating reports |
| 2 | MARKET.RATE.TEXT | This table allows users to define the floating rate option. The system populates user defined Floating Rate option code while populating the delivery related details. |


##### llustrating Model Products

Forward Rate Agreements are over the counter contracts between parties that determine the rate of interest to be paid on an agreed upon date in the future. The contract determines the rate to be exercised along with the duration of the contract for termination and the contract notional value. In this type of contract, only the differential amount is paid or received. The following products are available in the FRA module:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FRA Trade Buy | An FRA Trade Buy (Purchase) is a contract where the buyer is borrowing a notional sum at a fixed interest rate and for a specified period starting at an agreed date in the future. |
| 2 | FRA Trade Sell | An FRA Trade Sell (Sale) is a contract where the seller is lending a notional sum at a fixed interest rate and for a specified period starting at an agreed date in the future. |
| 3 | FRA Hedge Buy | An FRA Hedge Buy is a contract where the buyer gets into the agreement to borrow the notional amount with an aim of hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest, which is fixed at the start of the contract. |
| 4 | FRA Hedge Sell | An FRA Hedge Sell is a contract where the seller gets into the agreement to lend the notional amount with an aim hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest on it, which is fixed at the start of the contract. |

### 1.6  Rate Fixing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Rate fixing event is the second stage of input on FRA contracts. On the day of rate fixing, input the prevailing spot rate to calculate the settlement amount. The rate fixing date is generally two business days before the start date of the contract.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *FRA*, *Ref Price*, *Reference Rate*, *Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Rate fixing event is the second stage of input on FRA contracts. On the day of rate fixing, input the prevailing spot rate to calculate the settlement amount. The rate fixing date is generally two business days before the start date of the contract.

The FRA module has the functionality that allows rate fixing by grouping identical contracts in a semi or fully automatic operation, without manually reviewing each trade.


#### 🔧 Working With

The table below summarises the important event dates in FRA:

| Deal Event | LCY | FCY (if different) |
|---|---|---|
| Trade date | Today or earlier |  |
| Spot date | = Trade date | Trade date + 2 |
| Start date | Spot date + period (1) |  |
| Rate fixing date | = Start date | Start date – 2 |
| Maturity date | Start date + period (2) |  |

The two key interest rates mentioned below determines the profit or loss made in an account of the FRA deal:

- Interest rate – The rate agreed when the FRA is input
- Settlement rate – The prevailing rate on the rate fixing date

The difference between these two rates determines the Profit and Loss or settlement amount. Other interest rates used in FRA deal, such as Reference Rate is used for rate variance tolerance checking and Ref Price is used in case of hedge contracts to supply the long rate for purposes like long rate used in Position management data and for deriving the short period rate.

Rate fixing of FRA deals is done manually or through use of ST.GROUP.FIX application. The latter allows grouping of identical contracts and rate fixing is done in either semi or fully automatic manner. Fixing can be done online or using a service. Re-fixing, in cases where wrong rate is used, is also possible.

The ST.GROUP.FIX application provides an interface for the user to select all FRA trades that are to be fixed, and execute the fixing operation on authorisation. A group fixing operation is authorised before it is executed, as it involves changes to transaction data.

Various conditions are specified during the creation of group rate fixing requests. The conditions are instrument, instrument type, currency, rate fixing code and effective date along with operational parameters, such as whether a report is necessary or not. The request detects the trade (automatically) that requires a rate reset and sets the rate accordingly.

The instrument type for FRAs is either hedge or trade as defined by the FRA Type field in FRA. D EAL .

The effective date is when the new rate takes effect and not necessarily the date when the fixing operation happens. Fixing operation occurs two days before or on the same day when the new rate takes effect, depending on the currency. This is the considered as the settlement date of the FRA.

The ST.GROUP.FIX record specifies whether the FRA trade is remained in authorised or unauthorised status after the executing the fixing operation.

The rate fixing code determines which Periodic Interest rate is set to use. In FRA, it is directly linked to the PERIODIC.INTEREST table using Reference Rate field in FRA.DEAL . The user enters the same code in ST.GROUP.FIX to be used to flag the floating rate within the trades. Rates are derived from PERIODIC.INTEREST table. The key to this table is NNCCYYYYYMMDD.

10GBP20020602 allows to capture 99 individual records per currency per day. This enables individual tables for individual product types in

table. The rate considered from the PI record is from the first period (by default) and no interpolation is performed.

If it requires several requests, for example on an IMM fixing date, one record per combination of instrument or currency or rate fixing code or effective date needs to be input and authorised, and marked to be run as SERVICE.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Fix Rates (FRA)

There are no Tasks available for Rate Fixing feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

This section helps the user to understand the various enquiries and reports in Rate Fixing.


##### Enquiries and Reports

The section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports:

Rate Fixing

This enquiry fetches the list of FRA transactions performed by the Front Office Dealer. The enquiry also allows the Supervisor to perform rate fixing by entering the fixing date.

FRA Group Fix

ST.GROUP.FIX application provides the user with the interface to select FRA deals that are to be fixed and then executes the fixing operation and authorisation.

Unfixed FRA Report

This close of business report lists all the FRA deals for which the rates are yet to be fixed. The user can view the summary of FRA deals to be fixed by clicking the View Report icon corresponding to a record.

Basic Interest Rates

This enquiry displays the basic interest rate for a given currency or list of currencies.

Periodic Interest Rate

This enquiry displays the periodic interest rate for a given currency and period.

Rate fixing in next 10 days

This enquiry fetches the list of FRA deals for which the rate fixing take place in the next 10 days. The user can drilldown to the FRA deals using this enquiry.

FRA Deals Outstanding

This enquiry fetches the list of FRA deals for which the rates to be fixed. The user can drilldown to the FRA deals using this enquiry.

### 1.7  Related Deals


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The purpose of undertaking an FRA deal for hedge and trade transaction is as follows:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Hedge Txn Id*, *O/C*, *Position*, *Replacement Deal No*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The purpose of undertaking an FRA deal for hedge and trade transaction is as follows:

- To offset the interest rate risk identified
- To bridge the gap between the interest bearing assets and liabilities of the bank

- For general trading and arbitrage, thereby opening or closing a position

Thus, both hedging and trading FRA contracts may have related deals.


#### 🔧 Working With

Hedge transactions are used for hedging the risk arising out of interest bearing liabilities and assets. The user needs to note down the references of those assets and liabilities being specifically hedged by the deal undertaken and recorded. The Hedge Txn Id s field in FRA.DEAL is used for this purpose.

Trade FRAs are undertaken for either opening a new position or closing an existing position. The Position O/C flag indicates whether a particular trade opens or closes the position. The Closed FRA No specifies the FRA contract IDs which are closed by the deal being inputted. This functionality is applicable only for the deals where revaluation is performed position-wise and not deal-wise.

If an FRA replaces an earlier deal when a trade is erroneously input as a hedge; the deal must be reversed, re-input and ensure to make sure all the accounting entries are removed. In this instance, the Replacement Deal No field is used to track the original deal reference.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Related Deals feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

### 1.8  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borr...*
> 
> **Applications:** `MS.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Check Validation Limit Breach*, *Emit Business Event*, *LIMIT.TYPE*, *Pro Data Calculation*, *SUPPRESS.ACCOUNTING*, *THIRD.PARTY.EXPOSURE*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borrowers. Credit limit is one of the factors that affect the consumers' credit scores and can impact their ability to get credit in the future. A lender generally gives lower-credit limits to high-risk borrowers because they may not be able to repay the debt. Low-risk borrowers usually get higher credit limits, giving them higher flexibility to spend.

The limits are determined by banks, alternative lenders and credit card companies based on the information related to the borrower, such as

- Borrower's credit rating
- Personal income
- Loan repayment history and other factors

The line of credit is the maximum amount of money a lender allows a borrower to spend on a revolving or non-revolving credit limits.

The Limit (LI) module provides the credit limit or line of credit in Temenos Transact . All the business applications in Temenos Transact refer to the LI module for creation and maintenance of the line of credit facility applicable to the business scenario.


##### Product Configuration

Credit limits are held by customer and product. Simple limits can be defined for a single customer and single product. However, more complex limits can also be configured with multiple levels.

Limits are held by the customer at two levels:

- Individual
- Liability group

Also, limits can be held by the product as 12 levels:

- 10 levels of sub-product
- Product
- Global

Thus, an individual trade can be updated as six limits.

In this example, bank provides an unsecured loan to ABC Ltd of 3 million USD. ABC Ltd is a part of the larger group, ABC International. Bank monitors the limits at both company and group levels. Unsecured loans are a sub-product within loans and the limits are monitored at both levels. Finally, the bank sets a limitation on all business with ABC Ltd and with ABC International, and these limits are held at the global-level.

Consequently, the unsecured loan has updated six limits. If any limit is exceeded, an override is raised during the input of loan.

- LIMIT application holds the credit limits.
- LIMIT.REFERENCE application holds sub-products, products and global definitions.
- CUSTOMER application holds the customers and customer liability definitions.
- LIMIT.PARAMETER application defines the various high-level parameters regarding the application. It links contracts and accounts to LIMIT.REFERENCE .

The main limit parameters are shown in the below flowchart.

Limits can also be set to monitor the exposure against currencies, countries and industries. These limits are monitored overnight. The LIMIT application uses the parameter and product tables to define the structure of limits.

This application defines the parameters that determine the way in which the limit system operates. LIMIT.PARAMETER record can have the ID as ‘SYSTEM’. The LIMIT.PARAMETER application controls the following:

- An indicator to specify if the foreign exchange contracts must be netted before limit comparison.
- A 'number of days' to define how many days prior to Limit Expiry Date and Review Date (can be fixed in the Review Frequency field) in the LIMIT application, the approach of these events must be reported.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the first revaluation occurs and at what frequency thereafter.
- A date and cycle to indicate when a central liability report (including those liability numbers which did not move) must be produced in the back-end process.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the commodity, country and currency reports must be produced.
- A ‘number of days’, administrative Extension Days, define the maximum number of days by which the expiry date of a limit can be ’administratively’ extended before a new expiry date must be assigned to the limit.
- The LIMIT application is defined according to the specific requirements of the bank. The most important feature of this application is that it allows the bank (for each financial application) to define the precise rules applicable to an environment. In this way, the limit verification process can be established by the bank according to a bank’s own set of rules without any program maintenance.

The product group definition that allows the bank to specify the different products, (in bank’s opinion) must be part of the commodity, country and currency exposure.

Creation of Other Record IDs:

The LIMIT.PARAMETER application allows the creation of other record IDs besides SYSTEM. These record IDs can have a valid legacy application (that is, ACCOUNT, LD, MM and FOREX) as ID. The purpose of these records is to move their parametersation, which was initially done in the SYSTEM record, to new individual records for each application to improve system performance.

For example, for the ACCOUNT application, the user can create a new record, which includes all the necessary parametrisation for this particular application.

This section covers the high-level specification required for Limits (LI) module.

| 1. | LIMIT.PARAMETER | This application allows the user to define the parameter that determine the way in which LI module operates. It also allows the user to define the following: If foreign exchange contracts are to be netted. The date and frequency at which the revaluation occurs. The date and frequency at which the currency, commodity and country reports must be produced. The date and frequency at which central liability report must be produced in the back end process. Defining the frequency at which the collateral accounting service should be run. Defining the accounting type based on which entries would be booked in Limit's EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record, depending on the Balance types specified in respective Collateral Codes. |
| 2. | LIMIT.REFERENCE | This application allows the user to define the parameter, which links accounts and contracts to Limits (LI) products. In addition, it allows the user to define margin level or percentage ration between the limit amount utilised and the value of collateral available. It allows the user to define different limit amounts for contracts on different maturity dates. When the LIMIT.TYPE field is set to: Utilisation - The Limit product holds the Utilisation Limit records. Validation - The Limit product holds the Validation Limit records, which constitutes the maximum cap allowed for the underlying Utilisation Limits within a Limit structure. Standalone - The Limit product holds the Standalone Limit records, which have the same functionality as Utilisation Limit records apart from the fact that they hold no parent or child Limits. SUPPRESS.ACCOUNTING field is set to ‘Yes’ to suppress any GL accounting performed against the Limit records under the Limit product. This field accepts the input when the Limit record has nothing set in the Reference Child field. When the THIRD.PARTY.EXPOSURE field set to ‘Yes’, it marks the given Limit records under the Limit product to hold the third party exposure for their Customer(s). Any exposure created against these Limit records are excluded from the bank’s risk reports. |
| 3. | LIMIT.COMMODITY | This application allows the user to define the limits by commodity (industry type). |

Pro Data Calculation field mentions whether pro-rata calculation has to be done irrespective of manual percentage in Common Exposure Reports. Check Validation Limit Breach field indicates if breaches to validation limits have to be reported in a separate file. |
| 10. | LIMIT.NETTING.PARAM | This application allows the user to activate or deactivate the foreign exchange limit netting option, when required. |
| 11. | LI.MULTI.CUSTOMER.LIMIT.PARAMETER | This application allows the user to configure the rules for multi- customer limits without joint liability rules based on customer segments. Using this parameter, Users can configure the rules for Joint/Multi Customer Limit based on customer segment. Multi-Customer limits can be created with customers belonging to different risk groups or no group based on this parameter setup. |
| 12. | LI.TIME.CODE | This application allows the user to configure the charges based on the level of designated AA account for the respective balance types and the possibility to calculate charges per each time band amount. |

### 1.9  Interest Table


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Amt*, *Bid Rate*, *Build Fwd Rate*, *Days Since Spot*, *Int Tolerance*, *Last Wrkng Day*, *Local Routine* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the workflow of interest related reference application in Temenos Transact . The four major rates defined are as follows:

- Fixed Rate
- Floating Rate
- Periodic Rate
- Risk-free Rate


##### Fixed Rate

The fixed rate is the rate agreed with the borrower at the time of loan creation and it does not change during the life cycle of the loan. The fixed interest rate agreed with the borrower is defined in the loan contractual agreement. Floating rates and periodic rates are stored in centralised core application, so that market rate changes can be realised on all affected loans instead of the need for a manual intervention on each individual loan.


##### Floating Rate

The floating rate fluctuates according to the market movement. The frequently used floating rates, for example, base rate, prime rate, and overnight rate are defined in the BASIC.INTEREST application for each currency. The BASIC.INTEREST application stores the interest rates which are applicable across loans regardless of the loan duration. The rates in this application may be updated automatically through external feeds.

The interest conditions can be linked directly to a basic interest record in this application, rather than defining the interest rate details on each transaction record.

When a rate change takes place, only the BASIC.INTEREST record defined in this application should be updated with the new rate(s) and the effective date. This automatically updates all the transaction records, which are tied to that rate.


##### Periodic Rate

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application defines, for each currency, interest rates for any time period desired by the user for example, 10 days, 15 days, and 30 days. For each period defined by the user, both a bid and offer rate can be entered. Interest rates can also be defined by amount slabs, so a different rate can be entered for ranges from USD1 to 10,000 and between USD10,000 to 25,000.

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application is used by applications such as FOREX to default interest rates on forward contracts using the interest revaluation method or the Money Market (MM)/Lending Deposits (LD) applications to perform automatic rollovers.

The Last Wrkng Day field is set to instruct the system to check whether the current system date is the final working day of the month. If this is the case, when the rest period is defined as number of months, the system looks for the final working day of the appropriate month, rather than selecting the equivalent working day.

If February 26

is the last working day in February and having a rest period of 1M, the system finds the final working day in March, rather than simply selecting the 26

March or the nearest next working day.

It is possible to hook an API to apply rates or spreads based on user-specific criteria through the Local Routine field that enables the core routine to be overridden. Negative interest rates can also be input in the PERIODIC.INTEREST application. The Application field is used to specify the application ID(s) that can use negative interest rates.

The following screenshot shows the Bid Rate and Offer Rate fields:

It is possible to modify the Rest Period fields, Amt , Bid Rate and Offer Rate field of existing PERIODIC.INTEREST records of a past date. The use of such modified records is application dependent. Whenever a PERIODIC.INTEREST record of a past date or processing date is modified and authorised, the ID of such records are written in the PERIODIC.RATE.CHANGE application. The ID of this application is the processing date.

To create a PERIODIC.INTEREST record with interest rates expressed in number of days greater than 31D, the Rest Period field must be set with the values expressed only in days and up to three digits as shown in the below screenshot.

The system does not allow the Rest Period field to have values greater than 31D and the values expressed in months or years in the same record. If the values in months or years have to be used, then the record can hold the values expressed in days only up to 31D.


##### Risk-free Rate

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application supports Risk-Free Rates. Risk-Free Rates are overnight, backward-looking rates derived from actual market data for a given business day. They are published on each business day with a delay (that is, a rate published this business day is effective for the previous business day). These rates do not have a term structure (they are overnight rates published on each business day) and credit risk element.

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application stores overnight Risk-Free Rates in the following fields:

- Rfr Rate – Stores the overnight Risk-Free Rate for the given PERIODIC.INTEREST record.
- Rfr Date Recd – Stores the date on which the overnight Risk-Free Rate is received.

ID of a given Risk-Free Rate PERIODIC.INTEREST record holds the effective date (the date for which the rate is applicable).

When there is a Risk-Free Rate stored in a given PERIODIC.INTEREST record, the Amount , Bid Rate and Offer Rate fields are not required. The overnight Risk-Free Rates are published as a single rate with no Bid or Offer options.

The fields used for forward-looking terms are not allowed. The fields such as Rest Period , Rest Date , Days Since Spot , Build Fwd Rate , Int Tolerance , Max Int Rate and Use Last Wrkng Day are disabled accordingly.

The RFR interest calculation is performed using two different methods such as Rate Compounding and Amount Compounding depending on the setup in the relevant business application. In case of the Rate Compounding, the system calculates the average compounded rate for the period.

Results of the RFR calculation are recorded in the ST.RFR.CONTRACT.DETAILS and ST.RFR.DETAILS tables in Temenos Transact.


##### Market Rate Text

The MARKET.RATE.TEXT application contains the descriptions of tradable interest rates that are recognised by SWIFT.

Each description is used as the enrichment to the corresponding ID when it is displayed or printed during Temenos Transact processing. The Rate Text and Swift Code Words fields are used to populate the values in Tag 14 F in SWIFT MT 340, 360 and 361 messages. The Rate Text defined should be as guided by the SWIFT standards.

If the FLOATING RATE option is chosen as OTHER in the sequence C, the SWIFT standards expect the user to provide additional information in Tag 37N of MT360 and MT361 messages. Temenos Transact is enabled to auto default the additional information which includes a code word 'FROP' that is part of SWIFT.CODE.WORDS application.

### 1.10  Treasury Configuring Payment Order


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`, `NDF`, `PO`, `PP.CHANNEL`, `PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES`, `PP.CONTRACT`, `PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE`, `PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND` ... +5 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Po Ref Product*
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a generic payment order product ID for treasury settlements and map it to the Po Ref Product field in TM.PO.INTEGRATION table.
2. Create a record in PP.MSGPAYMENTTYPE table for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments.
3. Create a record in PP.NODA.LIST for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments. The Order Initiation Type field in the PO application has a specific value for the payment order originated from the Treasury applications. To know more, refer to Configuring Payment Order.
4. Create a separate PP.SOURCE record for treasury settlements.


##### Imposing Required Credit Value Date

This enables the user to impose the required credit value date passed by Treasury application on the debit value date. Hence, the statement entries for settlement amount has the appropriate value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a record in PP.CHANNEL table from where all treasury payments originate. The channel is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury payments.
2. Create a record in PP.SOURCEPRODUCTGROUP table to define source product group in Payments Hub. The source product is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury settlements.
3. Create an EB.LOOKUP record that is similar to the PP.SOURCE record. This enables to map Order Initiation Type in PP.SOURCE to the value in TM.PO.INTEGRATION .
4. In the PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE table, set the debit value date output as required credit value date. The value date in statement entry posted by TPH is same as the required credit value date passed by Treasury applications. The above steps are applicable for FX, FRA and MM. However, the user needs to create a new EB.LOOKUP record for NDF .


##### Generating Forward Entries by TPH

This enables the user to choose the parameter option at TPH level to generate forward accounting or live entries with forward value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create four new products in PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table to provide all four possibilities of treasury settlement. The following record names are products created for domestic and international payments, which TPH uses to process treasury payments: Record Name Message Type Payment Type TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 MT103 Domestic Payment TRSY.C.103.O.I-20190417 MT103 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.I-20190417 MT202 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.D-20190417 MT202 Domestic Payment
2. In the Forward Entry Flag field of PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table, set as Y. A sample record of TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 is shown in the below screenshots. (To know more, refer to the table above). To process an NDF transaction, the user needs to create four more records by setting the Originating Source and Forward E ntry Flag to NDSTLMT and N, respectively.
3. Create a new record in PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT and link it to output parameters of the determined product. This helps to identify the output channel configured in PP.CONTRACT .
4. Create a new rule in PP.CONTRACT with the PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT defined. This enables TPH to determine the output channel for the payment initiated from Treasury.
5. In the PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES table, set the Update Cash Position field as Y. The cash flow positions for payments processed through TPH is updated.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- API
- Temenos Transact Services

Collateral is the asset pledged by the customer as security for a financial facility provided by the financial institution.

- Ship
- House
- Painting
- Sculpture
- Single stamp (or an entire collection)
- Customer deposit
- Portfolio

These collateral items are revalued against the prevailing market value on a regular or ad hoc basis. A right or link to collateral items are established to cover the liabilities of the customer.

Collateral items maintained in Temenos Transact can be valued automatically.

- Deposit account
- Fixed term deposit
- All or part of customer portfolio stocks and shares


##### Product Configuration

The following table lists the module and product information for the Collateral functionality in Temenos Transact :

| Module/Product | Usage |
|---|---|
| CO | The Collateral (CO) product needs to be installed to use the basic Collateral functionality in Temenos Transact . |
| MV | The Margin Valuation (MV) product needs to be installed to configure and use the CO.VALUATION.PARAMETER application in the Advance Collateral processing. The CO product or SC product is a pre-requisite for installing the MV module. |
| CX | The Advance Collateral (CX) product needs to be installed to use the advance collateral features and derive the collateral value considering the concentration cap and currency hair-cut, as applicable to the collateral asset. The CO product and MV product are pre-requisites for installing the CX module. |
| COPOOL | The Collateral Pool (COPOOL) module enables the Corporate Collateral Pool functionality. The CO product is a pre-requisite for installing the COPOOL module. |

Configure the following parameters to use the Collateral module in Temenos Transact :

This is a company level application, which sets out high-level parameters that control the Collateral module. The parameters include:

- Maintaining the number of changes to collateral revaluation in the COLLATERAL application
- Considering account balance when deposit account is given as collateral
- Online update of cash collaterals (if required)
- Online collateral valuation (if required)
- Defining the currency and forex risk margin to cover the currency conversion risk factor
- Contract sequence routine defined in EB.API can be attached in the Contract Seq Rtn field.

The contract sequence routine instructs the system to apply a different collateral allocation order for the contracts returned, compared to the standard pro-rata allocation.

In this example, a contract sequence routine has been set up in COLLATERAL.PARAMETER , which returns the contracts in the order in which the transactions take place. The collateral amount is not allocated based on pro-rata allocation; instead, it is allocated based on the execution value for each Limit. This means that when more than one Limit is linked to the same Collateral Right , the amount assigned to each Limit is used by contracts. One Limit is not borrowed from another Limit’s assigned collateral amount. The following Limit structure has been created:

- Utilisation Limit LI0000101031 with Internal Amount = 30,000, but with an Online Limit = 22,500 based on the Execution Value of the collateral linked to the Limit.
- Utilisation Limit LI0000101032 with Internal Amount = 20,000, and an Online Limit equal to the Internal Amount ; both this and the previous Limit are linked to the same Collateral Right .
- Collateral Right COR09362S124H showing the two Utilisation Limits linked to it and the collateral to which they pertain.
- Collateral CO09362G674G showing the total Execution Value of the two Utilisation Limits and the Collateral Right Id to which they are linked:
- Collateral Allocation showing the allocated amount (that is, Execution Value ) for each of the Utilisation Limits:
- The two records in the LIMIT.TXNS application showing the contracts that utilised each Limit:

- Contract 10017194203 is disbursed for 15,000 by utilising Limit LI0000101031; given that Online Limit = 16,500, the system allocates the full amount for the transaction:
- Contract 10017194204 is disbursed for 25,000 by utilising Limit LI0000101032; given that Online Limit = 20,000, the system could have allocated a total of 21,500 for the transaction since there are still 1,500 not utilised for Limit LI0000101031; however, because of the contract sequence routine that has been initiated, the system allocates only the 20,000 assigned for this Limit:

### 2.2  Amortisation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Amortisation of interest and charges are different from amortisation of position. Normally, an Foreign Exchange (FX) forward deal impacts the currency position in the bank’s books immediately. However, if the purpose of the deal is to cover a future payable in foreign currency (for example, interest...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amortisation Cycle*, *Amortise From Date*, *Amortise Position*, *Amortise from Date*, *Fwd Int Loss Cat*, *Fwd Int Profit Cat*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Amortisation of interest and charges are different from amortisation of position. Normally, an Foreign Exchange (FX) forward deal impacts the currency position in the bank’s books immediately. However, if the purpose of the deal is to cover a future payable in foreign currency (for example, interest on a foreign currency deposit), the immediate position update distorts the dealer position book as the position amount on account of interest on Foreign Currency (FCY) deposit is accrued over a period of time.

The underlying concept is to amortise the position, on account of the FX contract (that is, build the position gradually on a given frequency, so that it off-sets the position being accrued on account of interest payable or receivable on a deposit in FCY). Thus, the impact of the position update from FX is off-set by the update from interest accrual on account of Money Market (MM) deposit or loan in FCY.


#### 🔧 Working With

If the Foreign Exchange (FX) deal done have to cover a forward interest receivable or payable, the Amortise Position field in FX application needs to be set to Yes, which amortises the position. No or Null raises the whole Position on input of the deal.

There are two methods available:

- FCY (amortisation happens only for FCY)
- BOTH (amortisation happens in both FCY and LCY)

> **⚠️ Note:** If both the currencies are foreign, amortisation cannot be performed.

Position amortisation takes place according to the frequency given in the Amortisation Cycle field. The Amortise from Date field defaults the spot date, but the user can change the value if amortisation has not already started.


##### Foreign Currency (FCY)

Using this option, only FCY amount can be amortised, and input for Amortise Position field is Y.

> **⚠️ Note:** Only STMT entries are raised to the suspense accounts.

Following is an illustration of a FX contract with Amortise Position set to Yes, Amortise from Date and Amortisation Cycle fields set with date and frequency for amortisation:

The following is a Position record of FCY before amortisation of position:

To generate the Position in FCY, the system is designed to generate the following entries according to the frequency set for amortisation:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| DR or CR | Internal Account FCY or LCY |
| CR or DR | Internal Account LCY or FCY |

Amortisation process raises the following Position accounting entries between the start and end dates of amortisation cycle. Thus, position is built gradually and not in one go as per the functionality of the amortisation of position.

In this case, the spot rate is used in accounting, which allows building the FCY position in the internal accounts. On the date of maturity of the contract, the system reverses these internal accounts. However, reversal happens at the contract rate applicable to the FX contract.

The following is a Position record of FCY after amortisation:

The difference in the spot rate and contract rate used on the above accounting entries leads to some amount left in the internal LCY (Local Currency) amount. This difference (depending on if its excess or deficit) is written off to P&L through a category entry.


##### Both

In this option, the foreign and local currency amounts can be amortised, and input for Amortise Position field is Both. In addition to the positon amortisation entries for FCY, system generates PL entries to book the difference between the spot and contract rate.

Following is an illustration of a FX contract with Amortise Position field set to Both, Amortise From Date and Amortisation Cycle fields set with date and frequency for amortisation:

The following is a Position record before amortisation of position:

According to cyclic frequency, the system posts the amortised amounts to the P&L categories. The net of the Fwd Int Profit Cat and Fwd Int Loss Cat is the exchange profit or loss, and there is no adjustment entry on maturity (as done in FCY, where Amortise Position is Yes).

The following category entries are raised for Both:

The following is the Position record for Both after amortisation:

### 2.3  Automatic Defaulting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Foreign Exchange (FX) business, especially with corporates and portfolio investors, the margin or spread applicable to their transactions is generally agreed upfront and the same varies based on the customer profile or relationship and the deal types (such as spot, forward and swap).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks


#### 📖 Introduction

In Foreign Exchange (FX) business, especially with corporates and portfolio investors, the margin or spread applicable to their transactions is generally agreed upfront and the same varies based on the customer profile or relationship and the deal types (such as spot, forward and swap).

Temenos Transact offers the functionality of identifying the customer condition group and defaulting the specified margin, automatically. This margin or spread percentage is applied to a group based on conditions or specific customer ( as agreed with the customer ) .

Margin or s pread percentage can be defined for each deal type or at granular level of c urrency and a mount, for which the FX.COMM.GROUP application is used. It is applied on the treasury rate to derive the margin p ips and then added or subtracted from the treasury rate (depending on buying or selling of base currency) to derive the final customer price.

> **⚠️ Note:** A t FX application level, the user can override the defaulted margin.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following FX spot deal shows the automatic default of margin applicable to the customer with minimum key stroke information fed on the deal.

On validation, the system identifies the Group ID to which the counterparty belongs, defaults the margin percentage accordingly by referring to FX.GROUP.CONDITION record, and derives the spot rate with the treasury rate picked up automatically.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Automatic Defaulting of FX Margin feature.

#### 📖 Introduction

Foreign Exchange (FX) module is capable of applying charges and commissions to deals. It also has the provision to apply a charge based on the delivery or deliveries. A charge can also be associated with tax and the same is handled appropriately. Charges and commission can be a standard flat amount or varying percentage on different bands or levels, as supported by FT.CHARGE.TYPE or FT.COMMISION.TYPE applications.


#### 🔧 Working With

The charge or commission code given in Foreign Exchange ( FX ) application defaults the amount of charge or commission. The user can override the defaulted value with manual input. The processing date of this amount is aligned with the value date of the scheduled delivery amount, if the charge is linked to a delivery. Else, it is processed on authorisation of the contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can provide multiple charge codes.

The below screenshot displays an FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record with flat FX charge.

The below screenshot displays an FX spot deal with standard charges applied and highlighted.

The illustration of STMT.ENTRY table reflects the treatment of charges and commissions for the respective FX Spot Deal record.

For Option contracts, which can involve partial deliveries, charges or commissions can be levied for each delivery.

### 2.5  CLS for Non-CLS Members


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The major risk in conventional settlement method is settlement risk (that is, one party delivers the required amount whereas the other party fails). The below workflow diagram helps to understand the conventional settlement of an Foreign Exchange (FX) transaction:*
> 
> **Applications:** `NETTING`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account with Bank*, *Amount Bought/Sold*, *Application ID*, *Buy/Sell Amount*, *CLS Deal*, *CLS Netting*, *CLS Settlement*, *Counterparty* ... +16 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The major risk in conventional settlement method is settlement risk (that is, one party delivers the required amount whereas the other party fails). The below workflow diagram helps to understand the conventional settlement of an Foreign Exchange (FX) transaction:

Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) is an international payment system launched in September 2002 for the settlement of FX transactions to mitigate the settlement risk. The Payment versus Payment (PVP) allows the banks to eliminate the settlement risk since the settlement by both the parties is done simultaneously. The below workflow diagram shows the settlement mechanism using PVP concept:


#### 🔧 Working With

CLS allows banks to eliminate the Foreign Exchange (FX) settlement risk. Currencies sold or bought are settled on a PVP basis – simultaneously and irrevocably, to ensure the principal of each counterparty is protected.

- FX contract with CLS.DEAL defaults to Yes.
- An Override is given, if a transaction is entered with the buy or sell value dates over the cut-off times in the FX.CLS.CPARTY tables.
- When the settlement is through CLS, the payment messages (such as MT202, MT103) and advice to receive messages (MT210) that are normally generated are suppressed.
- A copy of the deal confirmation (MT300) is used for CLS settlement. CLS nostro accounts are used instead of normal nostro accounts. Hence, a CLS Nostro needs to be identifiable.
- It is possible to book both CLS and non-CLS deals with the same counterparty but the impact on the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT and AGENCY tables needs to be considered.

The settlement of the Forex CLS trades goes through the multilateral netting settlement process, whereby, all the Forex CLS trades for a given value date and currency are netted and processed as a single settlement for the currency through the identified Nostro account for the respective currency. This multilateral trade settlement for the Forex CLS trade is handled through the NETTING application. The NETTING application is integrated with the payment order to process the payment through the Temenos Payment Hub (TPH).

Read the Payment Netting section for more information.


##### Delivery

Currently, CLS support is for a third party member and there are two methods of CLS delivery:

- In the standard SWIFT Heade r field, 103 is used to include the CLS member code. This instructs the SWIFT system to generate a T-Copy (duplicate message) to the bank CLS member.
- Alternatively, SWIFT fields 56 & 57 in MT 300 are used to identify the settlement member and a CLS message.

Support for CLS is based on local modifications, as feedback from clients indicates a mixed variety of usage. Accordingly, a few fields are added to FX to feed the relevant information to delivery.

> **⚠️ Note:** The DELIVERY module allows local mapping and population of the SWIFT Header fields and is detailed in the Delivery .


#### 📋 Tasks

A Forex CLS deal is a trade agreement between two counterparties to buy one currency against selling another at an agreed price for settlement on the spot date, called as Spot contract or at a specified future date called as Forward contract where the settlement is done through the CLS concept facilitated by an intermediary to avoid settlement risk.


##### Workflow

4. Click the Validate Icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Settlement Instruction tab to verify the details related to the settlements, which are defaulted by the system based on Standard Settlement Instructions (SSI).
6. Upon Successful validation, click the Commit icon to submit the deal for authorisation.
