### 2.6  Confirmations


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Foreign Exchange (FX), exchange of deal confirmation and matching are important, to ensure the terms and conditions agreed between the parties of the trade are same for efficient operational risk management. Different stages or activities involved with deal confirmation and matching are as follow...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Foreign Exchange (FX), exchange of deal confirmation and matching are important, to ensure the terms and conditions agreed between the parties of the trade are same for efficient operational risk management. Different stages or activities involved with deal confirmation and matching are as follows:

- Generates confirmation message and exchange with the counterparty as early as possible.
- Ensures confirmation message received from the counterparty is matched with the confirmation sent.
- Records or stamps the receipt of confirmation message from counterparty and broker in FX record.
- Generates a report by Close of Business (COB) to refer to the list of deals that awaits receipt of confirmation message (both from counterparty and broker). The report helps to follow-up with the concerned counterparty for confirmation messages.


#### 🔧 Working With

On input and authorisation of an Foreign Exchange (FX) deal, the confirmation message is generated or shared with the counterparty either in SWIFT or print format. Similarly, the counterparty generates the confirmation message and exchanges with the Temenos Transact bank. When both messages match, the stamping of the confirmation corresponding to the FX deal record is stored in the FX application.

> **⚠️ Note:** Similar to counterparty confirmation, broker confirmation receipt can also be recorded.


##### Counterparty Confirmation

The Unconfirmed Forex Deals ( FX.UNCONF.CPARTY ) enquiry fetches the list of unconfirmed deals. The user can select a particular deal record and perform the verify function, which updates the Confirm By Cparty field with the user ID, date, and time details. When the counterparty does not send any confirmation, the field is set to One Sided and the deal is excluded from the list of unconfirmed deals by counterparty report. The below screenshots show how an unconfirmed counterparty deal is confirmed by using the verify function.


##### Broker Confirmation

The Forex Deals (FX.UNCONF.BROKER) enquiry fetches the list of unconfirmed deals by the broker. The user can select a particular deal record and perform verify function, which updates the Confirm By Broker field with user ID, date, and time details. All unconfirmed broker deals are shown in the report generated in Close of Business (COB). The below screenshots shows how an unconfirmed broker deal is confirmed by using the verify function.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Verify Trade Data and Confirmation (Forex)

There are no Tasks available for Confirmations feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

This topic helps the user to view the enquiries and reports of the Confirmations feature.

This section helps the user to view the below enquiries and reports:

Auto Matched Confirmation

This enquiry lists all the Matched Confirmations (MT300). The system auto-verifies the respective contracts, whose messages are a match. It is possible to view the Matched Messages and the Forex Deal.

Broker Confirmation

This enquiry is used to verify the Broker Confirmation by the user.

This enquiry is used to verify the Counterparty confirmation of Forex Deals.

Incoming Confirmation

This enquiry lists the confirmation messages (MT300) that are sent to Temenos Transact Bank by various Banks.

- The message in Temenos Transact have their references starting with ‘R’ and ‘D’ for incoming and outgoing messages respectively.
- The messages with Match Status ‘MAT’ are the matched ones while the ones with status ‘WFM’ are waiting for Matching.
- Individual transaction can be drilled down using this enquiry.

Unmatched Confirmation

- This enquiry lists the unmatched confirmation messages in respect to outward confirmations. While doing manual matching, the user can also view the list of unmatched items in respect to inward messages.
- Using this enquiry, the user can view, check confirmation messages and perform the manual matching if they are satisfied with available information in the incoming confirmation messages.

### 2.7  Date Calculation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Value date in Foreign Exchange (FX) refers to the date on which the contractual currencies are exchanged and settled. Hence, this needs to be a common business day for both the currencies involved. FX date calculation in Temenos Transact defaults the value date in spot contracts and spot date in for...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Deal Date*, *FX Lcl Region*, *Fx Lcl Region*, *Sell*, *Spot Base Cc*, *Spot Base Ccy*, *Spot Ccy Pair*, *Spot Date* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Value date in Foreign Exchange (FX) refers to the date on which the contractual currencies are exchanged and settled. Hence, this needs to be a common business day for both the currencies involved. FX date calculation in Temenos Transact defaults the value date in spot contracts and spot date in forward contract. Additionally, it alerts the user whether the given value date is a holiday at one or both the settlement centers. The complexity in date calculation varies from low to high depending on the setup of the dealing rooms or multi-company in other centers or countries, which have different holiday setup.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the working of Date Calculation.


##### Standard Spot Date Calculation

This section describes the default operation of the system spot date calculation.This calculation takes place when FX Lcl Region and Spot Base Ccy fields are not specified in the FX.PARAMETERS record.

If the Value Date Buy or Sell is not entered in a spot deal (or first leg of a swap) or there is no Spot Date , the system attempts to default the dates. The date is calculated by adding the Spot Days or Spot Market (if spot days is not defined for a particular currency pair) from FX.PARAMETERS . This helps Deal Date to give a common working day for the two currencies involved in the deal.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local Currency | GBP | Local Country GB | Defined in COMPANY |
| Spot Market | 2 |  |  |
| System Date | 2nd July | Spot Deal | USD/GBP |

|  | Mon | Tues | Wed | Thur | Fri | Sat | Sun | Mon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| GB 00 | W | W | W | H | W | H | H | W |
| US 00 | W | W | H | W | W | H | H | W |
| Common | W | W | H | H | W | H | H | W |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local Currency | GBP | Local Country - GB | Defined in COMPANY |
| Spot Days | 1 | Spot Ccy Pair | USDCAD |
| System Date | 2nd July | Spot Deal | USD/CAD |


##### Alternative Local Currency FX Holidays

This section describes the scenario where an alternative HOLIDAY table is required for FX trading in the local currency.

A system with Local Currency as GBP is running in London, and Local Country as GB giving a local holiday table of GB00. Since the New York office also uses the system to enter trades, it should be available for them even on UK holidays (that is, the local holiday table is common working days in both the countries). Using the previous example:

|  | Mon | Tues | Wed | Thur | Fri | Sat | Sun | Mon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| GB | W | W | W | H | W | H | H | W |
| US 00 | W | W | H | W | W | H | H | W |
| Actual | W | W | W | W | W | H | H | W |

Both 4th July (holiday in US) and 5th July (holiday in UK) are working days in the system so the New York users can work on 5th July.

If an FX deal is done with GBP and USD on 2nd July (as in the previous example), the spot date results on 5th July. This date does not default in practice, as 5th July is not an actual working day in the UK (accurate date would be 6th July).

To avoid this problem, an alternative HOLIDAY table can be defined for the local currency, instead of the default HOLIDAY table (in this case GB00).

A new REGION record created (in this case GB01) for the local currency to do FX trading and a specific HOLIDAY table containing the true local holidays for this region are necessary. The region code should then be specified in the Fx Lcl Region field of FX.PARAMETERS as shown below.

Region GB01

|  | Mon | Tues | Wed | Thur | Fri | Sat | Sun | Mon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| GB 01 | W | W | W | H | W | H | H | W |

FX.PARAMETER input is shown below.

Therefore, any deal involving the local currency uses the Fx Lcl Region defined GB01 rather than the standard GB00. The following is the result using this definition on the previous deal:

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 | Column 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local Currency | GBP | Local Country | GB | (defined in COMPANY ) |
| Spot Market | 2 |  |  |  |
| System Date | 2nd July | Spot Deal | USD or GBP |  |


##### Spot Base Currency

Spot Base Currency is when some banks and markets operate with a principal that the spot dates should always fall on a working day of a particular currency. For example, if the bank wants to have USD as spot base currency, even when the deal does not involve USD currency can use the Spot Base Ccy field within FX.PARAMETERS to define the same.

Spot base currency is shown below.

The user needs to adhere to the following rules when using the above mode of date calculation:

| Deal | Description |
|---|---|
| Involves SPOT.BASE.CCY | When a deal involves Spot Base Ccy , the spot date for the non-spot base currency is determined first. If an FX Lcl Region is defined, then the same rules witnessed on the previous section is applicable. This spot date is then comparted to Spot Base Ccy holidays. If the date is a holiday in Spot Base Ccy , it is adjusted to the next common working day in both non-spot and spot base currencies. |
| Does Not Involve SPOT.BASE.CCY | A common spot date is obtained for the two currencies involved in the same way as the standard processing. If FX Lcl Region is defined, then the same rules shown above is applicable. The common date calculated is then compared to the Spot Base Cc y holidays. If the date is a holiday, it is adjusted to the next common working day for both currencies and Spot Base Ccy . |
| Both Sides are SPOT.BASE.CCY | A common working day is obtained for both currencies. The common date calculated is compared to all the Spot Base Ccy holidays. If the date is a holiday, it is adjusted to the next common date for both deal and all currencies defined in Spot Base Ccy . This method may result in a different date calculation in comparison to the standard calculation. |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 | Column 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local Currency | GBP | Local Country | GB |  |
| Spot Market | 2 | Spot Base | CCY | USD |
| System Date | 2nd July |  |  |  |

|  | Mon | Tues | Wed | Thur | Fri | Sat | Sun | Mon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| GB 00 | W | W | W | H | W | H | H | W |
| CH 00 | W | W | W | W | H | H | H | W |
| Comm | W | W | W | H | H | H | H | W |

### 2.8  Deal Sub Types


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Spot (SP) and Forward (FW) deal types can have the following sub types:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *(Depending on the Deal sub type selected)*, *BR*, *Brokerage Amount*, *Choose Forex Corporate Deal*, *Choose Forex Inter Bank Deal*, *Counterparty*, *Counterparty SSI*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Spot (SP) and Forward (FW) deal types can have the following sub types:


##### Internal (IN) Deal

An IN deal is performed internally between two dealers, and the Counterparty field represents a dealer desk and not the customer. The main objective of this deal sub type is to transfer the positions between two dealers and hence, no accounting or delivery is required. In this case, Position update for both the dealer-desks is updated for the same amount in the opposite direction.


##### Broker (BR) Deal

A BR deal is a transaction performed through a broker and the counterparty details are not known at the time of deal capture. To update the Position, using the deal sub type as BR, the deal can be captured and kept in unauthorised (INAU) status until the counterparty details are received. The deal sub type as BR has to be removed, before authorising the deal with the added counterparty details.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the working of Deal Sub Types.


##### Internal (IN) Deal

A Sales Desk Dealer can transfer the position to the Interbank Dealer using the IN deal sub type. Depending on who enters the deal in the system (that is, the Sales Desk Dealer or Interbank Dealer) the Counterparty field in FX holds either of their dealer desk ID. This is illustrated in the below deal screenshots.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Position update for both the dealers takes place for the deal amount but in the opposite direction.


##### Broker (BR) Deal

A valid record in BROKER table is required to enter the broker details for a deal.

In a BR deal sub type, the system expects broker and not counterparty details. Until the counterparty details are received and added to the deal, the contract cannot be authorised. An enquiry shows the BR deals which await counterparty details for follow-up and completion of back office processing. Once received, the deal sub type from BR is changed to None and authorised similar to a non-broker deal. The Brokerage Amount can be entered or the system allows to calculate the same based on the configuration of record in BROKER application.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Internal Forex Deal
- Execute Trade (Forex)
- Treasury Processes

Internal Deal : An internal deal is different from a standard deal. It is executed for the purpose of allowing transfers between different positions or dealer desks. There is no accounting entries, payment or advices for this type of a deal. When an internal deal for spot or forward contract is entered between two dealer desks, the system will automatically update the positions of both the dealer desks.

Broker Deal : A broker deal is struck whenever the details of the counterparty is unknown. Broker deals cannot be authorised by the system, since they do not have counterparty details. Once the details of the counterparty is known, the user should remove the BR from the deal and update the details.

Forex Private Banking Deal : These type of deals are initiated by the Private Banking. The dealer has to pick the deal and provide the exchange rates.

Single Rate Option : Single rate option is an agreement to exchange one currency for another where the delivery may take place between two specified dates of counterparty’s choice without incurring any penalty cost.

Deals Done Between Dates

Add Counterparty

So, once the details of counterparty is received from the broker, dealer has to select the trade from this enquiry and enter the counterparty details after removing BR from the deal sub type to make this trade available to back office for verification and authorisation.

### 2.9  Facility to Utilise Forex Contracts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Corporates hedge payables and receivables of their foreign currency and conversion to the local currency by entering into Forex (FX) contract with the bank’s treasury. Other departments, such as Trade Finance, Payments, and Loans utilise these contracts either fully or partially.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose Forex Corporate Deal*, *Counterparty SSI*, *Ext Settlement*, *Int Utilisation ref*, *Opt Proj Os Amt*, *Residual Amt Settl*, *SOD Maturity*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Corporates hedge payables and receivables of their foreign currency and conversion to the local currency by entering into Forex (FX) contract with the bank’s treasury. Other departments, such as Trade Finance, Payments, and Loans utilise these contracts either fully or partially.

> **⚠️ Note:** Development is involved in the transaction processing applications to enable utilisation of FX contracts.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration for the following tables:


##### FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE

FX application allows to capture deals with no settlement instructions. The blank settlement instructions indicate that Forex (FX) contracts:

- Can be utilised by external applications
- Do not have any settlement or delivery happening through FX

Also, the bank can configure utilisation details and credit limit updates through FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE .

1. FX Transaction Type .

FX Spot contracts can be partially utilised by external applications when option processing is enabled for such deals. The bank can configure spot option processing through FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE .

> **⚠️ Note:** Option processing on FX Spot contracts is enabled only for the purpose of utilisation by external applications

2. Enter the required details in the following field:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Ext Settlement | Specifies whether the settlement instructions are mandatory or not for the transaction type. If set to YES, the FX allows to successfully commit the deals without any settlement instructions. If set to NO, the settlement instructions are mandatory. |

> **⚠️ Note:** If contracts are entered with the transaction type (for which Ext Settlement is set to YES), then FX: Does not post any forward or live accounting entries Posts only the contingent accounting entries against the appropriate asset types


##### FX.PARAMETERS

The bank can configure the account, to which residual amount on value date of the contract is settled through FX.PARAMETERS .

FX Parameter .

2. Enter the required detail in the following field:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Residual Amt Settl | Holds the internal suspense account against which the residual balance in the FX contract is settled on the value date of the contract, when settlement instructions are not defined. |


#### 🔧 Working With

When a customer enters into an Forex (FX) deal with the bank’s treasury, then other applications can utilise FX contract.

When an FX contract is entered, the currency positions are generated.

Whenever the FX contract is utilised by other applications, the FX contract balance is updated real-time and details of the transaction utilising the FX contract is stored in FX application.

After utilisation, currency position generated by Forex is dropped and the corresponding AL position is raised by the Transaction Processing Application (TPA).

Option processing in FX Spot contracts allows partial utilisation of these contracts by external applications. The time option feature in FX spots is similar to the functionality in FX Forwards. Read Time Option in FX Forward Corporate Deal for more information.

Single rate spot option type allows transaction processing applications to utilise spot contracts in multiple tranches from option date until value date.

The dealer can schedule a complete delivery for residual balance on value date of the spot option contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** The facility to partially utilise an FX contract is exclusive to FX Forwards and FX Spot deals with value date set as tomorrow or spot. Cash deals are always fully utilised. Partial utilisation of FX Spot contracts is applicable only when option processing is enabled for spot contracts. Two APIs are developed to facilitate the utilisation by other transact applications. These APIs are used by other Temenos Transact applications to: Request the rate (FX Contract Rate) for processing the transaction Request the available or outstanding balance in the underlying FX contract Update the FX contract with the corresponding utilisation related information through API, after utilising the FX contract in transaction processing application (TPA)


##### Residual Balance in FX Contract

- If there is a residual balance on maturity for the FX contracts, which are entered with the transaction type (for which Ext Settlement is set to YES), then settlement happens only for the residual balance through FX application.
- The residual balance is posted to the suspense accounts defined in the Residual Amt Settl field of the FX.PARAMETERS , when SSI is not defined in the FX contract before maturity.
- If SSI is mentioned in the FX contract manually, the residual balance is settled to the SSI.


##### Projected Balance in FX

Future dated utilisations are updated as projected or predicted balance in the Opt Proj Os Amt field of FX contract.

- If SOD Maturity is set to NO, utilisations that happens today (for value dated today and future date) is updated as the predicted contract balance.
- If SOD Maturity is set to YES, the utilisation value dated today is updated in current outstanding balance.

If a customer has performed the following:

- Entered into an FX contract for a value of USD 500,000
- Settled a loan of USD 300,000 using this forward contract (yesterday)
- Requested a future dated remittance for USD 100,000

Then,

- Current outstanding balance as on today: USD 200,000
- Projected or predicted balance as of today: USD 100,000


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (Forex)
- Deal Sub Types
- Forward Contract

Facility to Utilise FX Contracts is feature in FX module that facilitates the utilisation of Forex deals booked by other transaction processing applications in Temenos Transact , such as loans, payments and trade finance.

### 2.10  Forward Contract


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The FX forward contract, an Over-the-Counter (OTC) product, is an agreement between two counterparties for buying and selling of one currency against another for delivery in the future, that is, at a date later than the spot date. The exchange rate applied is called the forward rate.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Buy/Sell Interest Rates*, *Choose Forex Corporate Deal*, *Choose Forex Inter Bank Deal*, *Forward Rate*, *Forward Rate, Revaluation Type*, *Is Deal to be Netted*, *Opt Os Rp Days*, *Send Payment* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The FX forward contract, an Over-the-Counter (OTC) product, is an agreement between two counterparties for buying and selling of one currency against another for delivery in the future, that is, at a date later than the spot date. The exchange rate applied is called the forward rate.

Generally, a forward contract has a fixed settlement date for the full contract amount. However, it is not rare to see the settlement taking place in multiple tranches over an agreed period of time but before the contract’s final value or settlement date. The system supports both types of settlements: Fixed Delivery Date and Flexible Delivery Date (time option in Temenos Transact terminology).

The time option feature allows multiple deliveries at different pre-agreed rates, which is generally applicable to FX deals undertaken with bank’s customer or corporates and not with interbank business.


#### 🔧 Working With

Forward Contract is similar to Spot Contract but with additional fields, such as Forward Rate, Revaluation Type and Buy/Sell Interest Rates . Versions for deal capture, similar to spot contracts, can be customised based on the counterparty and transaction types that distinguish between fixed delivery and flexible delivery option.

A forward contract eventually converges with spot period. However, the product category, limit reference, deal and revaluation types initially assigned do not undergo any change.


##### FX Forward Interbank Deal

When configured, the version created to capture an interbank deal has relevant fields. This makes it easy and quick for the Dealer to capture the deal done with an interbank counterparty.

The Value Date Buy and Value Date Sell fields accept the input in two ways, that is, a specific date or period such as number of days or months followed by D for calendar days, W for working days or M for months.

10D = 10 calendar days forward from spot, 10W = 10 working days forward from spot, and 6M = 6 months forward from spot.

The Forward Rate field accepts the input in two ways, an absolute rate, that is, 1.1312 or just the premium or discount in pips. When premium or discount is entered in the format of +12/-12 or +0.0012/-0.0012 pips (decimal displacement based on CURRENCY table setup) the same is converted into an absolute rate by the system by adding the spot rate to the given premium or discount.

When the settlement of contracts is subjected to netting, system defaults Y in the Is Deal to be Netted field that can be changed to N. However, the reverse is not possible. To know more, refer to NETTING application.

The Send Payment field relates to operational risk management. If the bank wants to release the payment message (MT202 or MT103) only after the deal confirmation is received and matched, then this field is initially set to Hold. Consequently, the payment messages is kept in Hold status in DE.O.HEADER , and later changed to Release once the confirmation matching requirements are fulfilled.

The Reporting tab holds the data fields that are meant for regulatory reporting according to the respective regulatory jurisdiction. Details (which defaults or user input) relating to settlement are grouped in this tab. These details consist of the customer’s pay and receive accounts, bank’s Nostro account details and counterparty’s Nostro correspondent and account details.

The Other Details tab holds the reval type selected for a contract. Unlike in spot deals where the revaluation type is only SP, a forward contract can use different methods of revaluation. Details relating to amortisation of position are also grouped here.


##### Time Option in an FX Forward Corporate Deal

The settlement of currencies, bought and sold through a forward contract is generally the full amount for a fixed date. However, in case of corporate deals it is common to allow multiple deliveries over a specified period which is referred to as time option.

The Time option in FX deal refers to the flexibility offered to the bank’s customers to deliver the contract amount in multiple tranches over a specified period and not to be mistaken for FX OTC option trades.

The system supports the following types of time options in this feature:

> **⚠️ Note:** This functionality is not required, even when the internal deals between two dealers are forward.

The buying or selling of a foreign currency, where the delivery takes place at any time between two specified dates of the customer’s choice without incurring any penalty costs. ### 2.11  FX Closing Group


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is capable of handling FX Closing Group that closes one or more open positions when a client conclude an FX contract. This functionality does not cover FX swaps and contracts of subtypes Broker (BR) and Internal (IN). The FX.CLOSING.GROUP application has the list of ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Fx Closing Group Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is capable of handling FX Closing Group that closes one or more open positions when a client conclude an FX contract. This functionality does not cover FX swaps and contracts of subtypes Broker (BR) and Internal (IN). The FX.CLOSING.GROUP application has the list of FX contract IDs, which matches with the specified counterparty and value date, and are not included in any other currency closing group or matured.


#### 🔧 Working With

When a client concludes an Foreign Exchange (FX) contract that closes one or several other open positions for the same value date, the FX module performs the following:

- Defines a closing group containing FX contracts closed against each other.
- Produces reports on a portfolio to display groups of closed FX contracts aggregated in a single line, with a corresponding realised PL figure. Other FX contracts are displayed normally.

However, this functionality does not cover FX swaps and contracts of subtypes Broker (BR) and Internal (IN). The FX.CLOSING.GROUP application is used for this purpose, which has the list of FX contract IDs that:

- Matches the specified counterparty and value date.
- Not included in any other closing group or matured.

Further, grouping of FX contracts is not allowed if there is balance in more than one currency.

> **⚠️ Note:** An FX contract cannot be reversed, if a value is given in the Fx Closing Group Id field.

In the below example, three FX contracts with open positions are grouped and Realised PL result is ascertained.

| # | Reference | Counterparty | Sub-Type | Deal Date | Value Date | Currency Bought | Currency Bought Amount | Currency Sold | Currency Sold Amount | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX1812303935 | 190051 | SP | 03 May 2018 | 07 May 2018 | GBP | 10000.00 | USD | 13500.00 | 1.35 |
| 2 | FX1812352010 | 190051 | SP | 03 May 2018 | 07 May 2018 | USD | 13,500.00 | CHF | 13500.00 | 1 |
| 3 | FX1812358047 | 190051 | SP | 03 May 2018 | 07 May 2018 | CHF | 13,500.00 | GBP | 10037.17 | 1.345 |

Between the first and second contract, the USD position is set off, and between the second and third contract, the CHF position is set off, thus, leaving with unrealised loss of GBP 37.17 for the bank.

### 2.12  FX Current Exposure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Foreign Exchange (FX) Current Exposure also known as Current Exposure (in the market), measures potential exposure of credit risk by calculating the outstanding value of the contract at current market rate and combines with potential exposure (volatility or movement) of the asset (with FX, it is cur...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Foreign Exchange (FX) Current Exposure also known as Current Exposure (in the market), measures potential exposure of credit risk by calculating the outstanding value of the contract at current market rate and combines with potential exposure (volatility or movement) of the asset (with FX, it is currencies) over the configured timeframe. Potential exposure is calculated by multiplying deal’s principal with a configured fraction.

Thus, the credit exposure for clients assessed in this method not only considers the current exposure but also adds add-on, which is the potential exposure of the asset.


##### Replacement Cost

This is the actual market value of the contract or the profit or loss when the open position is covered. Hence, if the client is in a:

- Loss – Replacement cost is positive
- Profit – Replacement cost is negative

However, when the client defaults and the deal gets cancelled, bank loses money by having to get into the market and cover the trade at current level, which is also seen as Profit at Risk.


##### Add-on

This is a defined and configured percentage of the nominal (cash transactions) or underlying (option transactions) contract amount. The percentage depends on the type and maturity of the contract, and is defined by the volatility of those asset types. In addition to FX, these calculations are applied to any asset (at present only FX forwards, the forward legs of swaps, futures and long options are covered).


#### 🔧 Working With

The FX.CURRENT.EXPOSURE application allows users to request a revaluation and report on the credit usage using the new current exposure method. It is used to perform the following:

- Enter the details of reporting method (add-on percentages configuration) to use.
- Report the usage for which customer or customers (multi-valued list of customers or ALL).

The user can run an ad-hoc revaluation on the requested customer or group of customers or whether to use the data already held in POS.TRANSACTION. Reason for the same is when the revaluation has run recently and the Mark-to-Market (MTM) value of the transactions are relatively up-to-date, there is no need to re-run the process and consume the system resources unnecessarily.

In the case when a revaluation is run, all the Foreign Exchange (FX) contracts for the counterparty or group of counterparties are revalued using the ‘Rebate’ methodology, regardless of the methodology that was initially entered for the transaction. For accounting purposes, the original methodology continues to be in use, whereas FX.CURRENT.EXPOSURE uses Rebate (RB) method of revaluation.

The profit or loss of the trade in local currency is determined, which is the current exposure (replacement value) of the trade. If there is a:

- Loss on the trade from the bank’s perspective (that is, the customer makes money on the transaction), it is negative.
- Gain on the trade from the bank’s perspective (that is, the customer loses money on the transaction), it is positive.

The user has configured add-on percentages for FX:

6MTH &

Trade at outset = Bank buys £1 million against -$1,520,000 at 1.5200, 8 months outright

Re-valued at entry rate so current exposure (replacement value) = zero

Add-on = £1 million X 1.5200 X 0.04 = $ 60,800

Utilisation = MAX ([$60,800+ $0], ZERO) = $ 60,800

Addon=£1million*1.5200*0.04=$60800

Revaluation after 3 months at 1.5300: -£1 million against +$1,530,000

Bank P/L in local ccy ($) = +$10,000 (profit of $10,000, that is, customer is losing money)

Current exposure (replacement value) = $10,000

Add-on = £1 million X 1.5300 X 0.02 = $ 30,600

Utilisation = MAX ([$30,600+ $10,000], ZERO) = $ 40,600

Trade at outset = Bank buys £1 million against -$1,520,000 at 1.5200, 6 months outright

Re-valued at entry rate so current exposure (replacement value) = zero

Add on = £1 million X 1.5200 X 0.02 = $ 30,400

Utilisation = MAX ([$30,400+ $0], ZERO) = $ 30,400

Revaluation after 1 month at 1.4800: -£1 million against +$1,480,000

Bank P/L in local ccy ($) = -$40,000 (loss of $40,000, that is, customer is making money)

Current exposure (replacement value) = -$40,000

Add on = £1 million X 1.4800 X 0.02 = $ 29,600

Utilisation = MAX ([$29,600+ (-$40,000)], ZERO) = ZERO

The system uses REVAL.ADDON.PERCEN to calculate the required add-on percentage for the product (FX), timeframe and reporting type, before applying the add-on percentage to the principal of the trade and calculating the notional utilisation.

The timeframe of the deal is calculated from the system date (today) to the maturity date of the trade. This number of days is compared to the time buckets in the REVAL.ADDON.PERCEN table to determine the add-on percentage. The deal principal is converted to local currency at the mid-rate defined in the CURRENCY table and then multiplied by the add-on percentage to find the notional add-on amount in the local currency.

An FX trade with a principal of 10 million Euros, exchange rate of 0.95, and add-on of 0.01 (1%) gives a notional utilisation of USD 0.095 million ($10 million X 0.95 X 0.01= $0.095 million).

This figure is added to the current exposure (replacement value) value obtained from the revaluation process. If the current exposure figure is negative and the add-on calculation is positive, the resultant figure is a net figure which cannot be negative, thus, the utilisation is zero.

Enquiries can access the information, collected and stored in the POS.TRANSACTION revaluation table, which can be easily setup and implemented. Each record in this table can only be entered once. Later, the record can be viewed in the See mode only. During Close of Business (COB), all authorised records are deleted and no history files exists for the records in this table as it is only for audit purpose.

Local implementation of versions ensures there is a Zero authorisation version, so that users can quickly call the routine and get total utilisation data without having to authorise the record.The fields are described in the below table:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Report Method | Defines the record in the add-on table to search for the add-on percentages. This can be any valid entry in . For example, Internal, Regulatory. |
| Customer Group | Includes any valid entry from the CUSTOMER table. Accepts either the 8-digit customer number or the customer mnemonic, a multi-value for inputting several customers. |
| Run Reval | Determines whether there is a new revaluation done using the latest FX rates or latest figures are used again (which are stored in POS.TRANSACTION for current exposure plus add-on). The default value is No. |

### 2.13  Margin Trading


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Foreign Exchange (FX) module offers the bank with Margin Trading facility to meet client’s demand for trading in different currencies. Depending on the collateral offered, clients can trade in currencies allowed within the permissible limit. The LIMIT and COLLATERAL applications cater to the setup o...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Foreign Exchange (FX) module offers the bank with Margin Trading facility to meet client’s demand for trading in different currencies. Depending on the collateral offered, clients can trade in currencies allowed within the permissible limit. The LIMIT and COLLATERAL applications cater to the setup of FX margin trading limit.

Generally, collateral can be credit balance in the account (or cash collateral) linked to a limit. The utilisation of limit happens not only at the time of initial trade but also with any potential loss incurred on customer position, thus covering the currency risk completely.


#### 🔧 Working With

The margin trading facility enables the bank’s clients to undertake trading in currencies up to a certain limit, as determined by the collateral offered. The existing COLLATERAL and LIMIT applications cater to setup such a limit. The initial and variation margin (on account of potential loss) are considered for limit utilisation to ensure effective risk management.

> **⚠️ Note:** To know how to setup a variable limit backed by collaterals, refer to the Limit or Collateral .

When the client enters into trades with the bank, the limit established is utilised in the following ways:

- Once a deal is entered, a certain percentage of the deal currency amount (bank’s buy currency) is reckoned as IM and updated to the limit utilisation amount. The calculation percentage can be a single number (for example, five percentage on the deal currency amount) or vary depending on the tenor of the contract. A user defined routine which is attached to LIMIT.REFERENCE record can also help to calculate the IM.

- During the life of the contract, Mark-to-Market (MTM) value of the deal currency varies and any potential loss to the client is accounted for and reduces the available limit amount.
- The third element that goes into limit utilisation is when the deal currency (on which the initial margin was calculated) and limit currency are not the same. The exchange rate fluctuation between the deal currency and limit currency (known as limit revaluation) impacts the limit utilisation.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Customer Sold | EUR 100,000 |
| Customer Bought | USD 106359.20 |
| Exchange Rate | 1 EUR = 1.063592 USD |
| Value Date | Spot |
| Netting Type | Multi (Netting of Buy Sell Positions in the same currency) |
| Replacement Percentage | 100% (MTM loss considered for limit update) |
| Profit. Percentage | 0% (Profit percentage netted against loss amount) |
| Recalculate Online | Yes (Whenever a new deal is done, the existing contracts also goes through online revaluation, which can be seen in LIMIT.FX.PROFIT.LOSS . However, the limit update is only done in COB)* |

### 2.14  Marketing Exchange Profit


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Treasury relies on the branches of the bank for mobilising Foreign Exchange (FX) business, and offers an incentive to them called Marketing Exchange Profit in Temenos Transact . This incentive is paid on the business mobilised from non-treasury customers, who do not have direct access to the Treasur...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Buy Local Currency Equivalent*, *Internal*, *Mkt Exch Acct Method*, *Sell Local Currency Equivalent*, *Treasury Rate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Treasury relies on the branches of the bank for mobilising Foreign Exchange (FX) business, and offers an incentive to them called Marketing Exchange Profit in Temenos Transact . This incentive is paid on the business mobilised from non-treasury customers, who do not have direct access to the Treasury department.

When the counterparty of an FX transaction is non-treasury customer, exchange happens between the Treasury and branch at one rate (treasury rate), and the branch and customer at another. The difference between the treasury and customer rate is isolated as marketing exchange profit, and passed on to the branch Profit & Loss (P&L). The currency positions raised reflect the true position on the dealer desk, that is, during transaction with non-treasury customer, the currency positions raised are at the treasury rate rather than deal rate.


#### 🔧 Working With

The relationship between treasury and other units are established easily. Any transaction processed for a non-treasury customer has exchanges between the Treasury and that department at one rate (treasury rate), and between that department and the customer at another. The difference between the two rates (that is, spread or exchange profit) is passed to the department. An initial balancing entry for the spread is passed to a suspense account at the time of the contract entry. The suspense account entry is reversed when the contract matures, effectively leaving a profit or loss on the department’s P&L category.

It is necessary to have MARKETING record in ACCOUNT.CLASS table, when using marketing exchange within FX. The category code entered in this record is used for the suspense account for dealer desk’s marketing exchange P&L.

The raised currency positions reflect the true position on the dealer desk. In other words, the local equivalent figures raised in the currency positions are at the Treasury Rate rather than the deal rate. The transaction enters the exchange position at the Treasury rate. Therefore, during the revaluation process, all profit (or loss) arising from this position (through revaluation) are allocated to Treasury.

> **⚠️ Note:** Treasury rates reflect real market rates.

In this system, the Treasury is responsible for setting the base (treasury) rates and marketing units responsible for policy on customer rates using the following:


##### Accounting

Conventionally, the market exchange in an FX contract is accounted in the below example. This method is named after Internal .

Debit – Internal Suspense Account

Credit – P&L Market Exchange

Debit – Customer Account*

Credit – Customer Account*

Credit – Suspense Account

The difference between the debit and credit customer account entries is the reversal balance of suspense account on maturity.


##### Alternative Method of Accounting

An alternative method of accounting for marketing exchange is available to make it compatible with the overall working where the Position Accounting is switched on. This method is known as P&L and works as explained below.

The Mkt Exch Acct Method field in FX.PARAMETERS is set to P&L and the system raises two category entries to post the marketing exchange profit or loss as follows:

- Debit – P&L Marketing Exchange of Treasury USD 1000
- Credit – P&L Marketing Exchange of Customer USD 1000 (Customer Marketing Department Category)

Internal is another field value in Mkt Exch Acct Method of FX.PARAMETERS , which is the conventional method of accounting where the entries are raised between the internal suspense account and P&L (as explained earlier).

The impact of P&L method on POSITION is that the LCY equivalent of the FCY is built at the contract rate and not at the treasury rate. As a result, the Buy Local Currency Equivalent and Sell Local Currency Equivalent in FX are identical until the revaluation method is Spot Revaluation (SP) and Rebate Revaluation (RB).

Since internal suspense account is not involved, reversal entries need not be posted during the maturity of the deal. Using ACCOUNT.CLASS , one or two P&L category codes are defined for marketing exchange depending on whether the credit and debit goes to one or different category codes.

### 2.15  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is designed to meet the needs of dealing operations in the Foreign Exchange Market.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cus Margin Default*, *FX Commission Group ID*, *FX Group Cond ID*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is designed to meet the needs of dealing operations in the Foreign Exchange Market.

The module offers comprehensive treasury solution starting from the deal capture in the front office to deal processing in back office, covering a wide range of FX products. The module covers entire deal life cycle of FX transactions including features such as recording of limited orders, online limit checking, position updating, revaluation of positions, accounting, brokerage, generation of SWIFT confirmations, payments and print advices. In addition, the module also helps generate reports for audit and risk management.

The above image illustrates spot, forward and swap deal types and its associated transaction types supported by the system, which caters to the business needs of Treasury.

Using FX module, a dealer can directly input a deal in the system with key elements, such as currencies, amount, rate, value date and counter-party. This avoids the need for hand-written deal tickets and ensures the real-time update of positions and risk, that is, counterparty’s liability or exposure, exchange position and daily foreign exchange movements reflects the dealer’s system inputted deal.

All elements of FX transactions have default values, except the key information that the dealer provides. Thus, for any given counterparty, payment methods and instructions are loaded automatically from user definable tables. If required, the back office user can confirm or exceptionally amend the deals.

The ability to arrive at intelligent defaults also has another benefit. For example, in a swap, all the default information on the second leg is derived from the first leg. Thus, dealer’s input of information is reduced to the minimum.

After the dealer provides their inputs, the deal slips are printed for the back-office. At the authorisation stage, the system invokes the following:

- Generating and delivering confirmations
- Passing any accounting entries such as brokerage, commissions and charges, and issue of any required pay or receive instructions

Otherwise, there are overnight processes that involve eventual settlement, revaluation and accruals, and exception or maturity reporting.

The FX application is supplied with initial input of the contract details with a few of them requiring any changes during remaining life cycle. Such changes, if any, are generally limited to settlement related. The brokerage calculation and processing of brokerage is handled by using BROKER application.


##### Product Configuration

This section describes the configuration options the system offers in FX.


##### FX Build Sequence

Implementation of FX module begins with configuration of various parameter tables.

The following list of files are required for FX main setup, and the mandatory files are suffixed with an *. The dependency tables are marked and stated alongside the parameter tables in their build sequence.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters consists of the following:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX.PARAMETERS | The rules that determined the Foreign Exchange (FX) transactions are defined in the following files: Classifies spot and forward contracts, according to local central bank and internal reporting rules. Defines the spot default value date. Uses the OFS.SOURCE ID present in this field to perform FX.BULK.ORDER . Uses the version ID present in this field as VERSION to populate or create FX BULK DEAL master records. Defines default category code for spot, forward and swap transactions. Defines the precious metal currency codes, hence, any number of currency codes can be defined. Conditions under which deals are entered with split value dates. Indicators show if Profit & Loss (P&L) and EXCHADS entries are booked when revaluation of forward and spot contracts takes place. Creates rounding rule for transactions. The Cus Margin Default field determines if the FX Group Cond ID corresponding to a customer is defined in a FX contract or not (subjected to the existence of the condition priority setup in FX margin). The values accepted are Yes, No and None. If set as Yes, the FX Group Cond ID defaults from SEC.ACC.MASTER ( SAM ). If it is not available in SAM , it defaults from CUSTOMER.CHARGE . If set as No or None, the FX Group Cond ID does not default from SAM or CUSTOMER.CHARGE . However, the user can still define the margin percentage manually (together with treasury rate) and derive the customer rate in FX deal. |
| 2 | FX.POS.TYPE | Assigns profit centre to the trading position, which can be amended as desired. |
| 3 | FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE | Classifies the deal types. A record in this application can control the default value for category codes, revaluation types, and allows delivery and types of options processing. The existing records can be amended and new records can be created. |
| 4 | FX.GEN.CONDITION | Identifies a specific group of customers, which can be cross-related to the group condition table, to define conditions applicable to that group. The groups are determined based on customer details such as sector and target. The criteria used and their priority are specified in the Condition Priority file in the record whose ID is FX.MARGIN. |
| 5 | FX.GROUP.CONDITION | Defines the spread or margin percentage for a specific customer, group of customers or default group. When a group customer is defined, the FX Gen Condition record needs to exist before any associated group condition is specified. For an individual customer, the ID is C , whereas, the default group ID is generally assigned as either 99 or 999. |
| 6 | FX.COMM.GROUP | Defines spread or margin based on currency, and the amount that falls in a range and is used in FX contracts. The FX Commission Group ID field in SAM is used in FX.BULK.ORDER application, and a reference to SAM is used in FX.GROUP.CONDITION . Hence, the margin is given in absolute terms or referred to FX Commission Group ID (based on which the margin is applied in an FX deal). |


##### Illustrating Model Products

The following products are available in the FX module:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX Spot | FX Spot is a contract of buying or selling a currency, commodity or security for immediate settlement (payment and delivery) on the spot date at a spot Rprice. |
| 2 | FX Forward | FX Forward is a contract of buying and selling an asset or a currency at a predetermined spot rate at a specified date in the future (which is greater than the spot date). The predetermined rate is called as the Forward Rate. |
| 3 | FX Swap | FX Swap is an agreement between counterparties to exchange currency. The agreement involves swapping of principal and interest payments between two different currencies. |
| 4 | Precious Metal Deal | Precious Metal Deals involve trading in various precious metals such as gold, silver, palladium, platinum and so on, in spot, forward or swap rates depending on the types of deals entered. |
| 5 | Single-rate Option | Single-Rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two specified dates at customer’s choice without incurring any penalty cost. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. |
| 6 | Multi-rate Option | Multi-rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two different option dates with different rates. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. In this, the applied rate depends on the period delivery. |
| 7 | Internal Deals | Internal Deals allow transfers between different positions or dealer desks. Hence, there is no need for accounting entries, payments, advices and so on. The system automatically updates the position, when an internal forex spot or a forward deal is entered. |
| 8 | Broker Deal | Broker Deals are entered when the counterparty is not known. The user needs to enter BR as sub-type and associated brokers deals. Once the counterparty name is known, BR is removed and the counterparty details are entered in the deal. |
| 9 | NDF Vanilla Deal | Non Deliverable Forward (NDF) Vanilla Deals is an hedging strategy, where parties in the contract agree to settle the profit or loss prior to the expiration date of the contract. A vanilla NDF transaction has an agreed rate fixing date, which is two working days before the settlement date. |
| 10 | NDF Exotic Deal | An Exotic NDF Deal allows in setting the fixing date as any date before the vanilla date in the tenure of the transaction. The fixing profit is discounted, if the NDF is fixed and settled early. The discount amount is amortised from the settlement date to the value date of the NDF. |

### 2.16  Netting

Netting in Foreign Exchange (FX) refers to grouping of transactions (which satisfies the grouping condition), and making or receiving payment for the ne...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Application ID*, *Buy/Sell Amount*, *CLS Deal*, *Counterparty*, *Creating Netting*, *Currency Bought*, *Currency Sold*, *Currency to be Netted* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

NETTING is a core functionality in Temenos Transact . It includes offsetting the value of multiple payments due to be exchange between two parties. Netting in Foreign Exchange (FX) refers to grouping of transactions (which satisfies the grouping condition), and making or receiving payment for the net amount. The grouping of transactions is based on Currency, Counterparty and Value Date. Accounting entries are consolidated for grouped transactions and raised against a suspense account instead of nostro account. On settlement date, the Suspense account is reversed and an entry for the net amount is posted to customer or nostro account.


#### 🔧 Working With

The bank creates a NETTING.AGREEMENT record for each customer who agreed for netting. This holds the following details:

- Counterparty and currencies eligible for netting.

- Number of days ahead from current date, which is used as the selection criteria in CREATE.NETTING .

> **⚠️ Note:** If the value is not given, CREATE.NETTING automatically builds netting groups with two working days ahead.

In the below illustration, a netting agreement is created for customer 100473 with GBP and USD currencies subjected to netting, and a valid period between 16th March 2018 to 16th March 2019. The transactions subsequent to the NETTING.AGREEMENT are listed below:

On authorisation of the records, NETTING.ENTRY records get generated for the above transactions as illustrated below:

Using the CREATE.NETTING application, the netting entries that are generated contract-wise on authorisation of the contracts, are subjected to netting, and a consolidated entry is raised between the suspense and the customer or nostro account.

> **⚠️ Note:** Creating a record in this table can be done either manually or automatically.

After executing the Close of Business (COB), NETTING records are generated in IHLD status.

On authorisation of NETTING records, the net payment gets released and netting reference gets attached to the respective NETTING.ENTRY records, along with generating the STMT.ENTRY .


#### 📋 Tasks

Netting is a core application in Temenos Transact . It involves offsetting the value of multiple payment dues that are to be exchanged between two parties. Netting in Forex refers to grouping of transactions that satisfy a given grouping condition and making or receiving payment for the net amount.

Create Forex Netting : A netting record can be created using this option by grouping the transactions, which are covered by a Netting Agreement. For Forex transaction, the grouping can be done on Currency, Counterparty and Value Date. Accounting entries are consolidated for grouped transactions.

Create Netting Payment : (FX) transactions covered by a netting agreement are sent to the Netting Entry application for netting of payments. For such transactions, system will raise accounting entries to suspend account instead of Nostro accounts.

For the grouped payment based on grouping in the Create Netting application, a record is created in Hold status. This record can be maintained to add settlement details, confirmation details and individual payment can be dropped from the net payment, if required.

3. Enter values in the following fields: Counterparty Currency to be Netted Value Date Application ID

1. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Deal Date Currency Bought Currency Sold Buy/Sell Amount Spot Date Spot Rate CLS Deal

1. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
2. Upon successful validation, click the Commit icon to submit the record.

Users can perform the following actions using the Create Netting Payments tab: Input – Enter values for Netting Agreed On, Netting Confirmed with and Account with Bank fields of any Netting Payment on the list. Authorise – Authorise a Netting Payment. Delete – Delete a Netting Payment record from the list. View - View details of any Netting Payment record on the list.

### 2.17  Order Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

>

#### 📖 Introduction

The FX module has two types of FX orders that are serviced by the following applications:


##### FX.BULK.ORDER

This application enables an Account Officer to request the purchase and sale of currencies on behalf of several clients, in a single order for the same currency and value date. When authorised, an FX.ORDER record is generated in IHLD (on hold) status.

The Treasury dealer takes ownership of the same and makes use of the record to capture market side deal details and customer side rate and spread. After authorising the FX.ORDER record and running the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE, the FX master deal for the market side deal is generated in INAU (unauthorised) status. After authorising the master FX deal and running the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE again, the child deals for the customer side are generated.


##### FX.LIM.ORDER

This application enables recording a customer order to buy or sell currencies at a desired rate and for a specified value date. Validity time of the order can be specified, after which the order expires. There are different order types designed to meet the customer requirements.

| Order Types | Description |
|---|---|
| Single Order | For recording a one-time order to buy or sell a currency against another. |
| One Cancels Other | For recording two orders, generally for buy and sell, and upon execution of one order, the other one cancels. |
| If Done | For recording two orders and the second order is valid only when the first order is executed. |
| Revolving Order | For executing an order multiple times. |

The application also works as an interface between the Treasury Dealer and other business units of the bank. Exchange rate request for a transaction can be raised using this application. In response, the Treasury Dealer provides the rate which can then be applied to the transaction by the requesting business unit. This process can be fully automated, if the transaction application is enabled to interact with the application using APIs. This functionality is known as internal rate request.

The below image shows the working of an internal rate request from Temenos Payment Suite (TPS).

Thus, the end-to-end processing of recording several customer orders, interbank or internal deal details and generating the FX deals for both interbank or internal and customers are achieved effortlessly.


##### FX Limit Orders

The following are the two distinct functionalities in FX Limit Orders:

1. Using the FX.LIM.ORDER application, the Relationship Managers record requests from their clients who wants to buy or sell foreign currency at a desired rate for a specified value date.

One of the bank’s customer intends to buy GBP 15,000 against USD for value date spot at 1.30, and the order is valid until Good Till Cancellation (GTC) with order type as Single.

The Ord Item Status is Open and Order Status is Active.

2. The Treasury Dealer monitors these orders for execution, unless they are cancelled or expired.

3. When order is executed, the counter currency amount and certain other details are updated on the record, as shown in the below screenshot. The order is executed by setting Execute Order as Yes, and inputting the rate in the Exec Rate field.

The FX Contract ID gets assigned to the particular LIM Order with the help of OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE.

The Ord Item Status is Executed and Order Status is Done.

The rate at which the FX.LIM.ORDER is executed, is not stored in the contract but the USD equivalent is arrived at 19,500 = (15,000 * 1.30)

The executed orders lead to the creation of intended FX deals automatically, if the service is auto enabled. Depending on the number of authorisers set for the version and configuration used for creating FX deal, the record is created in INAU or Authorised status.

The FX.LIM.ORDER record ID is stored in the FX deal created.

The Lim Order Type field distinguishes between a normal customer Lim order and an internal rate request. The fields applicable for a normal customer Lim order may not be applicable for an internal rate request such as limit reference, settlement account details, and deal types (other than spot).

The internal rate request is meant for transactions with current value date (today) and not for booking any spot or forward contracts (in case of Customer Lim orders). The internal rate request functionality aids the user in a workflow where another Temenos Transact or external application needs an exchange rate from the treasury department in a semi or fully automated manner. If such workflow is expected to be a Straight Through Processing (STP), an interface between the requesting transaction processing application and FX.LIM.ORDER application needs to be established.

If Treasury Front Office uses the Temenos Transact system, the rate request appears on the Dealer menu and the Dealer provides the rate for the same. After authorising the record, the rate requesting application can view the rate and apply it to the transaction for which the rate request is made.

Treasury Dealer provides the rate, and the rate requesting application is intimated when an interface is established.

If the bank’s treasury uses a third party system, an interface between their treasury system and Temenos Transact facilitates an automated processing.

### 2.18  Position Transfer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The foreign currency positions that are raised in a company due to transactions or contracts, are transferred to a particular company daily to avoid exposing the branches to revaluation profit or loss.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCOUNT.CLASS`, `COMPANY`, `FX.POSITION.TRANSFER`, `FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM`, `FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.SELECT`, `POS.MVMT.TODAY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *@ID*, *Consol Comp*, *Credit Txn Code*, *Debit Txn Code*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The foreign currency positions that are raised in a company due to transactions or contracts, are transferred to a particular company daily to avoid exposing the branches to revaluation profit or loss.

Position transfer is dependent on the branch company that is defined in FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM . To transfer the currency position, the position file is used as the base file, thus raising accounting entries at the branch, and transferring the positions through Treasury. The debit and credit accounts used in the accounting entries are internal accounts, and the categories for these internal accounts are specified using the ACCOUNT.CLASS application.

Accounting Rules

When the position is transferred from one company to the designated company, corresponding accounting entries are created in both the companies. This ensures that the currency positions match the foreign currency asset and liabilities.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following configurations are available for the Position Transfer functionality.


##### Configuring theFX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAMApplication

This application holds the branch IDs for which the position entries are removed and shown against the treasury branch. If a branch does not require position transfer, it can be excluded by not defining it in the parameter application.

The table below details the field description and validations of the FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM application.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| @ID | Holds the name of the company from where the position needs to be transferred. It must be a valid branch ID. |
| Consol Comp | Holds the name of the company to where the position needs to be transferred and must be a valid record in the COMPANY application. It must be a valid branch under the same lead company. |
| Credit Txn Code | Holds the credit transaction code. |
| Debit Txn Code | Holds the debit transaction code. |

The below screenshot is an example of a record that can be modified based on the user’s requirements.

The records in FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM need to be created for the respective branches or companies from where the position needs to be transferred as shown in the above screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

After creating records in FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM , create internal accounts in the local currency for the suspense account in ACCOUNT.CLASS . Every branch or company must have an internal account for its local currency (local currency of the main or treasury branch), and the currencies for which an FT or FX transaction is done. These internal accounts must have an entry in the main or treasury branch to where all the positions are transferred.

The below screenshot is an example of an internal account, which can vary based on the user’s requirements.

The position record showing the status after COB, is shown in the below screenshot.

The US0010100 entries that are nullified and moved against entry US0010001 in the Consol Comp field, are shown in the below screenshot.


###### Describing the Subroutines in theFX.POSITION.TRANSFERApplication

The description and property specifications of the FX.POSITION.TRANSFER application are given in the table below.

| Property Specification | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Multi-threaded batch routine |
| Attached To | BNK/FX.POSITION.TRANSFER |
| Attached As | Batch job |
| Dependency | NA |
| Description | Transferring the position of the companies that are parameterized in the Consol Comp field in FX.POSITION.TRANSFER.PARAM . |

Selects the POS.MVMT.TODAY application with @ID as BRANCH.ID Builds the Key list. FX.POSITION.TRANSFER Uses the Key supplied from the SELECT routine. Fetches the internal account category for the account from the U-BRPOSCR, U-BRPOSDR, U-HOPOSCR and U-HOPOSDR records in ACCOUNT.CLASS . ### 2.19  Position Updating


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Currency Position defines the transactions undertaken for buying and selling different currencies, which are grouped by Company ID , Currency Market , Position Type , Currency Pair , Dealer Desk and Value Date to calculate the net amount bought or sold. Hence, the net open amount in a Foreign Curren...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *AL Position*, *Company ID*, *Currency Market*, *Currency Pair*, *Dealer Desk*, *Dealer ID*, *Forward Position*, *Position Type* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Currency Position defines the transactions undertaken for buying and selling different currencies, which are grouped by Company ID , Currency Market , Position Type , Currency Pair , Dealer Desk and Value Date to calculate the net amount bought or sold. Hence, the net open amount in a Foreign Currency (FCY) is called Position, which can be long (over bought) or short (over sold).

The long position is denoted by a negative (-) sign in line with core accounting standards in Temenos Transact . However, enquiries catering to display Position amounts, can change the sign from negative to positive and positive to negative.

Real time update to POSITION record or Position ACCOUNT is key to currency risk management. Real time update to a currency position record supports dealer’s actions to manage the risk. Revaluation of Position or Mark-to-market (MTM) helps the Dealer to manage the position by taking profit or stopping the loss.

Similar to other applications in Temenos Transact , Foreign Exchange (FX) also updates the POSITION table and ACCOUNT in real time (that is, during the deal capture). Using an ACCOUNT to post the Position amounts is part of Position Accounting concept, which is in addition to the core POSITION keeping mechanism. Option to select Position Accounting is available in CONSOLIDATE.COND table and for further information, refer to Financial Accounting user guide.

Temenos Transact uses POSITION table for keeping track of Currency Positions. Each update to POSITION table is backed by an entry in POS.MVMT.TODAY table with essential details. The record ID in POSITION record consists of Company ID , Currency Market , Position Type , Dealer ID , Currency Pair and Value Date (such as GB00100011TRF3GBPUSD20180501).


#### 🔧 Working With

An Foreign Exchange (FX) contract is essentially an agreement to buy or sell one currency against another at an agreed rate and date. Hence, an update to Position in the currencies of the trade is crucial for monitoring the Net Open position soon after the deal is done. Position update is a system activity.

On input of an FX contract, system creates two records in POSITION table, one each for the two currencies of the deal, which can be seen in the below example.

An Unauthorised FX Spot contract

The respective POSITION records for each currency of the deal.

The system also updates POS.MVMT.TODAY table, which is similar to a STMT.ENTRY for an account. A Position Movements Today (POS.MVMT.TODAY) enquiry allows the user to view the movements in the Position for a given currency and dealer, as shown in the below screenshots.

In addition to the POSITION table, an FX contract also updates the POS.TRANSACTION table. The record ID corresponds to the FX deal suffixed by 1. This table supports the revaluation and accounting process by storing the revaluation details for each contract.

During the Close of Business (COB) of FX deal maturity date, the Position representing the FX deal is merged with the Position for Asset & Liability (AL).

If Position Accounting is turned on, suspense accounts are created for each currency against Local Currency (LCY) and reverse based on Company ID , Dealer Desk and so on. Similar to an Account Statement, the Position Entries Detail (POS.STMT.ENT) enquiry displays the position movements for a given currency pair and dealer desk.

The STMT.ENTRY table displays the entries for the FX spot contract inputted.

The POS.STMT.ENT enquiry is applicable for both the currencies. There are several other enquiries used to view the POSITION data and among them is Currency Position (FX.OPEN.ALL.SUMM) enquiry as shown in the below screenshot.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| AL Position | Currency-wise net position on account of the Foreign Currency Assets and Liabilities. |
| Spot Position | Currency-wise net position on account of transactions or contracts whose maturity date is less than or equal to spot date. |
| Forward Position | Currency-wise net position on account of transactions or contracts whose maturity date is greater than the spot date. |
| Unauth AL Position | Currency-wise net position on account of transactions which are left unauthorised and EOD process is performed. |


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Position Updating feature.

FX Position Report

This COB report prints the FX Position Sheet . The position is listed by currency and Currency Market. The following details are printed in the report, such as, Split of the Position for Asset and Liability, Spot, Forward and Totals along with Local Equivalent.
