### 2.20  Post Trade Events


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An FX contract has a pre-determined exchange rate and settlement date for the full contract amount. However, there could be instances where the delivery under a forward contract may take place before the settlement date, or delivery may not take place at all.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Partial Delv*, *Assoc FX Ref*, *Assoc FX ref*, *Canc Buy Amt*, *Canc Buy Date*, *Canc Pl Acc Ccy*, *Canc Pl Account*, *Canc Pl Amt* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An FX contract has a pre-determined exchange rate and settlement date for the full contract amount. However, there could be instances where the delivery under a forward contract may take place before the settlement date, or delivery may not take place at all.

If the underlying transaction is likely to take place after the maturity of the forward or spot contract that is already booked, a customer may seek an extension of the contract. Such requests for cancellation or extension can be made by the customer on or before the maturity of the forward contract. The bank generally agrees to these variations, provided the customer agrees to bear the loss if any, the bank may have to sustain on account of these variations.

Since all such requests happen after trade processing has taken place, these activities are termed as ‘Post-trade events’. There are three types of Post-trade events possible for an FX Forward contract.

- Early Delivery
- Cancellation
- Extension/Rollover

These events are further classified to indicate if the post-trade processing is for the complete or partial amount. The SWIFT guidelines have defined specific codes for each of these post-trade activities, based on which customer advices are generated. The following image provides the classification of the codes.

The following table provides the details of the codes.

| Short Code | Name | Definition | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAMT | Early delivery | Trade will be settled early. | Full Early Delivery User creates a delivery tranche with complete contract balance and uses this code to indicate that the client has fully delivered the contract before maturity. The outstanding balance on the contract is updated as zero and the contract matures after authorization. |
| PEAM | Partial early delivery | Trade will be partially settled early. | Partial Early Delivery User creates a delivery tranche with partial amount available and uses this code to indicate that the client has delivered partial amount before the maturity date. The outstanding amount is reduced by the amount delivered. The contract does not mature until value date, as there is pending amount. |
| PRUR | Partial unwind rollover | Part of the trade will be settled on its original date and the remainder will rollover. | Partial Delivery and Partial Rollover on Due Date Partial amount is delivered on the maturity date and rest will be rolled over to an extended value date. The contract can be rolled over any time before the contract matures. |
| PRUW | Partial unwind | Part of the trade will not be settled. | Partial Cancellation Partial amount on the contract is cancelled and the outstanding or remaining amount is reduced by the cancelled amount. The contract will be in ‘live’ status until the value date for the settlement of outstanding amount. |
| ROLL | Rollover | Rollover of a previous trade. | Rolled Over Contract Marker The current trade is an extended trade and is linked to a cancelled trade. |
| UNWD | Unwind | Trade will not be settled. | Full Cancellation The complete contract amount is cancelled and there is no outstanding balance on the trade. |
| UNWR | Unwind rollover | Original trade will not settle on its original date and will be rolled over. | Full Rollover The complete contract amount is cancelled on the original trade and a new trade is booked with an extended value date for the same amount. |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To enable the processing of FX cancellation or extensions, new fields are added to the FX.PARAMETERS and FOREX applications. The user should configure these tables for correct cancellation rate and cancellation profit or loss calculation and accounting.


##### FX.PARAMETERS

To enable the processing of FX cancellation or extension in FX.PARAMETERS , perform the following steps.

1. FX Parameter .
2. Enter the required detail in the following field: Field Description CANC.PROFIT.CAT Identifies the Profit/Loss category, used for posting the cancellation profits.


##### FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE

To enable the processing of FX cancellation or extension in FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE , perform the following steps.

1. FX Transaction Type .
2. Enter the required detail in the following field: Field Description CANC.RATE.ROU A placeholder to link the customised cancellation rate determination routine.


#### 🔧 Working With

Post-trade events can be carried out on either Spot or Forward FX option contracts. The bank can cancel, deliver, or extend an FX option contract, either on or before the value date.


##### Early Delivery

To support a client’s request for an early delivery of the complete contract amount before the agreed-upon value date of the deal, FX allows the user to,

- Specify Trade Event Type as EAMT.
- Schedule complete delivery of the contract on or before its value date.

Once the user schedules the delivery of the complete contract amount with the settlement date, any outstanding amount on the deal is reduced to zero and the contract is matured upon authorization.

The following figure shows an example of a complete early delivery of an FX contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the user does not schedule the complete contract amount with Trade Event Type set to EAMT, the system raises a validation error to warn the user. Early delivery charge calculation is currently not supported.


##### Partial Early Delivery

The client may request for partial delivery of the contract amount before the agreed-upon value date of the deal for an FX option contract. In such cases, the bank may allow for the required amount to be delivered by scheduling a ‘drawdown’ for settlement date using option processing functionality as explained below.

Partial amount on the contract, as specified, will be delivered when Trade Event Type is set to PEAM. Once the user schedules the delivery of partial contract amount with the settlement date, the outstanding amount on the deal is reduced to the extent of the scheduled amount.

The following figure shows an example of partial early delivery of an FX contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the user schedules the complete contract amount with Trade Event Type set to PEAM, the system raises a validation error to warn the user. Partial early delivery can be performed on single rate option contracts only when Allow Partial Delv is set to Yes in FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE . In addition, multiple partial deliveries can be performed on such contracts.


##### Cancellation

During the deal life cycle of an FX contract, the client or customer of the bank may request for a cancellation of the FX Forward/Spot option contract for various purposes. Such requests for cancellation can be made by the customer on or before the maturity of the contract.

When the contract is unwound upon client’s request, the bank can levy the cancellation charges (financial loss or financial gain) on the client or retain the same.

FX option contract allows the user to provide cancellation instructions as part of the delivery tranche. Any revaluation entries and charges posted on the contract until the cancellation date remains intact even if the contract is completely unwound. In other words, the contract is not completely reversed. Instead, the cancellation of the deal affects only those activities from the cancellation date.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can specify cancellation instructions on an FX contract only upon the authorization of trade.

The user should enter the required details in the following fields.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Trade Event Type | Holds SWIFT codes for post trade events. The values are: UNWD - Complete amount on the contract is cancelled and there will be zero outstanding amount. PRUW - Partial amount, is cancelled and the outstanding deal amount is reduced to the extent of cancellation amount. |
| Canc Buy Date | Specifies the cancellation date of the bought currency. The date can be the same as Canc Sell Date or different in case of a split value date scenario. The cancellation buy date is always the current system date. |
| Canc Buy Amt | Specifies the amount of the bought currency to be cancelled. This amount is the full outstanding amount of the trade. |
| Canc Rate | Allows the usage of custom routines to derive the cancellation rate. The standard routine (model) calculates the indicative cancellation rate by deriving the forward rate or taking the spot rate based on the cancellation date (early or due date). The user can override the defaulted value, if required. |
| Canc Sell Date | Specifies the cancellation date of the sold currency. The date can be the same as Canc Buy Date or different in case of a split value date scenario. The cancellation sell date is always the current system date. |
| Canc Sell Amt | Specifies the amount of the sold currency to be cancelled. This amount is the full outstanding amount of the trade. |


###### Cancellation Charge Details

When the client requests the bank for cancellation of an FX deal, the bank agrees to cancel the deal, provided the client bears any cancellation charges due to the variation of exchange rates.

The user should enter the required cancellation charge related details in the contract.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Canc Pl Account | Specifies the charge account to be used while debiting or crediting the cancellation loss or profit. |
| Canc Pl Acc Ccy | Specifies the currency of the cancellation profit or loss settlement account. |
| Canc Pl Type | Specifies the charge type to be used to calculate cancellation charges. If input, the charge type must exist on FT.CHARGE.TYPE or FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record. |
| Canc Pl Amt | Specifies the charge amount entered or calculated, based on the charge type defined. |
| Canc Profit Pass | Specifies whether the cancellation profit will be passed on to the customer or retained by the bank. Y - Resulting profit upon cancellation of the contract is passed on to the client. N - Resulting profit upon cancellation is not passed on to the client. |

When the user validates the deal, system calculates the cancellation rate based on the custom routine defined in FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE .

- If cancellation is done on the value date of the FX contract, routine defaults the prevailing spot rate of the contract.
- If cancellation is done prior to the value date of the contract, routine defaults the cancellation forward rate till the value date of the contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** Forward premium/discount is derived from the FORWARD.RATES table. If the Reva Within Sp is set to Yes in REVALUATION.PARAMETER , the cancellation rate is derived from the FORWARD.RATES table for the period within spot day definition.

| Base Currency | Cancellation PL | Canc. rate | Profit or Loss to bank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Currency Bought | (Contract rate – Cancellation rate) * Amount Buy in base currency | No | Loss |
| Currency Sold | (Contract rate – Cancellation rate) * Amount Buy in base currency * (-1) | No | Profit |
| Currency Bought | (Contract rate – Cancellation rate) * Amount Buy in base currency | Yes | Profit |
| Currency Sold | (Contract rate – Cancellation rate) * Amount Buy in base currency * (-1) | Yes | Loss |


##### Complete Cancellation

Upon client’s request, the bank can completely cancel an FX contract on or before the value date with Trade Event Type set to UNWD. The following are the possible types of cancellation. The cancellation charges result in profit or loss to the bank in cases of complete cancellation on or before the maturity date.


###### Complete Cancellation on Maturity Date

When the client requests for cancellation, the dealer specifies the complete contract amount in the cancellation amount field of the option or non-option currency, and Trade Event Type is set to UNWD.

- Cancellation amount of non-option currency is calculated based on the option rate and cancellation amount of the option currency.
- Cancellation date is specified as the current day’s date.
- Upon validation, cancellation rate is defaulted as the prevailing spot rate, which the user can manually override.

Charge details including charge type and amount are specified by the dealer. Once the cancellation instructions are provided, the outstanding amount on the contract is reduced to zero as the contract is completely cancelled.

The following figures show the FX contract and the corresponding positions prior to cancellation.

The following figure shows the FX contract upon cancellation.

> **⚠️ Note:** Complete cancellation is not allowed on partially delivered contracts. Future dated cancellations are not allowed. Cancellation cannot be performed on the same date when Sod Mat is set to YES. Cancellation processing is always performed during EOD maturity.

On commit, Forward option currency positions are reversed for the entire contract balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** Revaluation and charge entries that were raised up to the cancellation date are not reversed upon cancellation.

Upon authorization of the contract:

- The counterparty credit limits are reinstated for the complete cancellation amount.
- Accounting entries are reversed for the complete contract amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** Counterparty credit limits do not reflect the cancellation charges.

The previous off-balance sheet entries are reversed for the entire contract balance. RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY for the cancellation amount is raised for FXOPTBUY/FXOPTSELL asset type as follows.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| FXOPTBUY | 10000 | CAN |
| FXOPTSELL | 12000 | CAN |

Since cancellation charges result in a profit to the bank, the accounting entries are generated to credit customer account and debit P&L category. Cancellation charges are passed on to the client when Canc Profit Pass field is set to Yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** When cancellation charges result in a profit to the bank and Canc Profit Pass is set to No, resulting profit is not passed on to the client and accounting entries are suppressed.

Consider the same FX contract to have resulted in a loss to the bank. Then, the accounting entries are generated to debit customer account and credit P&L category.


###### Complete Cancellation Prior to Maturity Date

The complete cancellation workflow before the value date is similar to the case described above (cancellation on maturity date). However, here the cancellation rate is the forward rate calculated from the cancellation date to value date.


##### Partial Cancellation

Upon the client’s request, the bank can partially cancel an FX contract on or before the value date with Trade Event Type set to PRUW. The cancellation charges result in profit or loss to the bank in cases of partial cancellation on or before the maturity date.


###### Partial Cancellation on Maturity Date

When the client requests for cancellation, the dealer specifies the partial amount in the Canc Buy Amt / Canc Sell Amt field of the option or non-option currency, and Trade Event Type is set to PRUW. Cancellation date is specified as the current day’s date. Upon validation, the cancellation rate is defaulted as the prevailing spot rate, which the user can manually override.

> **⚠️ Note:** Cancellation amount cannot exceed or equal the outstanding contract amount in the option currency. Complete cancellation is not allowed when Trade Event Type is set to PRUW.

Charge details including charge type and amount are specified by the dealer. Once the cancellation instructions are provided, outstanding amount on the contract is reduced to the extent of the cancellation amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** Partial cancellation of an FX contract can be performed only once during the life of a contract. System raises a validation for multiple events of PRUW or PRUR on a single FX contract.

The following figures show the FX contract and positions raised prior to cancellation.

The following figures show the FX contract, upon cancellation.

On commit, Forward option currency positions are reversed for the cancelled amount as shown below.

Upon authorization of the contract, the counterparty credit limits are reinstated to the extent of cancellation amount. Accounting entries are reversed for the partial contract amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** The revaluation of the FX contract is done for the outstanding balance of the contract post cancellation. Cancellation profit and loss is calculated only to the extent of cancellation amount and not on the entire contract balance.

Since cancellation charges result in a loss to the bank, the accounting entries are generated to debit customer account and credit P&L category.


###### Partial Cancellation Prior to Maturity Date

The partial cancellation workflow before the value date is similar to the case described above (partial cancellation on maturity date). However, here the cancellation rate is the forward rate calculated from the cancellation date to value date.

> **⚠️ Note:** Cancellation instructions cannot be amended by the user, after authorization of the deal.


##### Rollover

Upon client’s request, the bank can extend the value date of an FX contract on or before the current value date. Extension can be for a complete or partial contract amount. The process of extension consists of cancellation of an FX contract, followed by rebooking the new deal for the cancelled amount.


###### Complete Rollover On or Before Maturity Date

When the client requests for a complete rollover of an FX option contract before the value date, the dealer specifies the complete contract amount in the cancellation amount field of the option or non-option currency, and Trade Event Type is set to UNWR. Cancellation date is specified as the current day’s date and cancellation rate is defaulted as forward rate (including forward premium).

Charge details including charge type and amount are specified by the dealer. Once the cancellation instructions are provided, the outstanding amount on the contract is reduced to zero. The cancelled contract follows a similar process to complete cancellation, to generate positions and accounting entries. The complete contract balance is reversed.

Rebooked contract is booked for the entire contract balance of the cancelled contract with the extended value date given by the user and Trade Event Type set to ROLL. The Assoc FX Ref field maintains the link between cancelled contract and extended contract. Cancellation PL, generated due to cancellation of the original contract is defaulted onto the rebooked contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** User has the flexibility to rebook the cancelled contract at a later point in time. An FX contract does not allow multiple tranches with ROLL trade event type.

When an FX contract is rolled over on the maturity date, the workflow is similar to complete cancellation on maturity date for the cancelled contract (with cancellation rate defaulted as prevailing spot rate). The rolled over contract is booked for the extended value date, as required.


###### Partial Rollover On or Before Maturity Date

When the customer requests for partial rollover of an FX option contract on the value date, the dealer specifies the partial contract amount in the cancellation amount field of the option or non-option currency, and Trade Event Type is set to PRUR. Cancellation date is specified as the current day’s date and cancellation rate is defaulted as prevailing spot rate.

> **⚠️ Note:** Multiple partial rollovers are not allowed on a single FX contract. The remaining or outstanding amount on the original contract is expected to be settled with the counterparty.

Charge details including charge type and amount are specified by the dealer. Once the cancellation instructions are provided, the outstanding amount on the contract is reduced to the extent of the cancelled amount specified. The cancelled contract follows a similar process to partial amount cancellation, in order to generate positions and accounting entries. The partial contract balance is reversed.

The contract amount which was cancelled is rolled over on to the new contract with the extended value date given by the user and Trade Event Type set to ROLL. The Assoc FX ref field maintains the link between the cancelled contract and extended contract. Cancellation PL, generated due to cancellation of the original contract, is defaulted onto the rebooked contract.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Currency Bought | USD |  |  |
| Currency Sold | GBP | Cancel Amount Buy | 3900 USD |
| Amt. Bought | 13000 | Cancel Rate | 1.315 |
| Amt. Sold | 10000 | Cancel Amount Sell | 3000 GBP |
| Forward Rate | 1.3 | Cancellation charge in base ccy | 45 GBP |
| Base Currency | GBP | Charge PL Ccy | CHF |
| Option Currency | GBP | Cancellation PL in charge ccy | 53.37 |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Cancellation (Forex)
- Execute Delivery (Forex)
- Execute Rollover (Forex)

Post-trade events are early delivery, cancellation and rollover of forex option deals. Using this enquiry, the user can perform the following post-trade events:

- Full Delivery
- Partial Delivery
- Full Cancellation
- Partial Cancellation
- Full Rollover and
- Partial Rollover


##### Workflow

In Post-trade Events feature, the user can perform the following operations:

To capture the full cancellation, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Full Cancellation option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Cancellation tab, enter values in the following fields: Cancel Buy or Sell Date Cancel Amount Buy or Sell (Entire Deal Amount to be inputted) Cancel P & L Type Cancel Profit Pass Cancel P & L Account
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To capture the partial cancellation, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Partial Cancellation option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Cancellation tab, enter values in the following fields: Cancel Buy or Sell Date Cancel Amount Buy or Sell (Partial Deal Amount to be inputted) Cancel P & L Type Cancel Profit Pass Cancel P & L Account
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To capture the full rollover, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Full Rollover option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Cancellation tab, enter values in the following fields: Cancel Buy or Sell Date Cancel Amount Buy or Sell Cancel P & L Type Cancel Profit Pass Cancel P & L Account
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.
6. Enter deal details for rollover contract.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the rolled over deal.

To capture the partial rollover, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Partial Rollover option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Cancellation tab, enter values in the following fields: Cancel Buy or Sell Date Cancel Amount Buy or Sell Cancel P & L Type Cancel Profit Pass Cancel P & L Account
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to Submit the deal.
6. Enter deal details for rollover contract.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the rolled over deal.

To execute the full deliver, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Full Delivery option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
4. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To execute the partial deliver, follow the steps below:

1. Post Trade .
2. Select the Partial Delivery option from the drop-down corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Settlements tab, enter values in the following fields: Settlement Amount for Sell (or) Settlement Amount for Buy
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To capture the cancellation settlement account, follow the steps below:

1. Check Cancellation Settlement Account .
2. Select the Amend icon corresponding to a deal.
3. In the Settlement tab, enter values in the following fields: Cancel P&L Account Cancel PL Lcy
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

### 2.21  Precious Metal Trade


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Foreign Exchange (FX) module allows trading and delivery of precious metals. Metals are setup as part of the CURRENCY table, and following are some of the precious metals and their respective ISO currency code:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose Forex Inter Bank Deal*, *Setlmnt Acct for CCY bought*, *Setlmnt Acct for CCY sold*

#### 📖 Introduction

Foreign Exchange (FX) module allows trading and delivery of precious metals. Metals are setup as part of the CURRENCY table, and following are some of the precious metals and their respective ISO currency code:

| Metal | ISO Code |
|---|---|
| Gold | XAU |
| Palladium | XPD |
| Platinum | XPT |
| Silver | XAG |

Precious Metal Trades are recorded on the same FX Deal Capture page used for currency trade but with a few additional trade terms and conditions. During SWIFT confirmations, delivery and transfer of precious metals, the system is enabled to generate the following:

- MT 600 for deal confirmation
- MT 604 for delivery or transfer
- MT 605 for advice to receive

> **⚠️ Note:** FX Trades cannot be booked with cross metal trades, that is, both sides being metal in Temenos Transact .


#### 🔧 Working With

Similar to versions created for currency trades with spot, forward, and swap deal types, versions are created for precious metals with additional fields that enables the dealer to easily capture deals in the system. Position update, revaluation, and accounting are similar to normal FX currency trades.

For example, a precious metal trade to purchase Gold.

For example, a precious metal trade to sell Gold.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (Forex)

The Forex ( FX ) application allows the user to enter the Forex Spot or Forward transactions on precious metals, such as, Gold, Silver, and so on. These metals are traded in terms of their quantity.

To create a Metal Trade, perform the following steps:

3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields:

1. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
2. Upon successful validation, click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To capture a Settlement Instruction, follow the below steps:

2. Click the Input Settlement details icon corresponding to a Forex Deal record.
3. Enter values in the required fields.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

Forex authorisation is a process of authorising a forex deal by the Treasury supervisor.

To authorise a Forex Deal, follow the below steps:

1. Forex Authorisation .
2. Click the Authorise icon corresponding to a Forex Deal record.
3. Verify the deal details and then click the Authorise icon to complete the authorisation process.

To reverse a forex deal, follow the below steps:

1. Reverse Forex Deal .
2. Click the Reverse icon corresponding to a forex deal record.
3. Review the deal details.

To modify an unauthorised forex deal, follow the below steps:

To delete an unauthorised forex deal, follow the below steps:

3. Review the deal details.
4. Click the Delete icon to submit the deal for deletion.

### 2.22  Revaluation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Foreign Exchange (FX) module provides daily revaluation of the FX position, which produces daily profit or loss for each dealer or group of dealers. The revaluation types are classified based on the treatment of exchange profit or loss during the lifecycle of the deal in Cost-to-Cover and Amorti...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *(EUR)*, *(GBP)*, *(Suspense*, *(USD)*, *)*, *,*, *.*, *= Sell Local Currency Equivalent* ... +78 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Foreign Exchange (FX) module provides daily revaluation of the FX position, which produces daily profit or loss for each dealer or group of dealers. The revaluation types are classified based on the treatment of exchange profit or loss during the lifecycle of the deal in Cost-to-Cover and Amortisation methods. The following are the types of revaluation methods:

| Method | Types |
|---|---|
| Cost-to-Cover | Spot Revaluation (SP) |
| Rebate (RB) |  |
| Amortisation | Interest (IN) |
| Interest Hedged (IH) |  |
| Straight Line (SL) |  |
| Straight Line Funding (SF) |  |

There are several enquiries and reports generated in Close of Business (COB) processing to show the revaluation details.


#### 🔧 Working With

Revaluation assesses the daily position of Foreign Exchange (FX) for each dealer or group of dealers.

- Spot Position is revalued by using Spot Revaluation (SP) method.
- Forward Position is revalued either on a Rebate (RB) basis (that is, cost-to-cover the position today) or interest straight-line, interest hedged basis or straight funding basis (that is, amortisation of the apparent exchange profit or loss during the life cycle of the deal).

The forward premium or discount in an FX Swap can also be treated as interest income or expense and amortised over the deal period. These parameters allow applying rebate revaluation method to currency positions arising from non-FX applications such as, Swaps (SW), Securities (SC) and Funds Transfer (FT) (provided the latter two modules are set to value dated accounting).

> **⚠️ Note:** The Rebate (RH) Revaluation module, according to the value defined in the REVALUATION.PARAMETER table, interpolates rates to the actual deal value date (that is, it interpolates a rate between the known rates for the closest dates before and after a given date).


##### Revaluation Rate

Similar to Asset and Liability revaluation, FX revaluation processing uses the Reval Rate field (if defined) for a particular currency. This is applied to positions that relate to both on and off balance sheet assets and liabilities. All types of revaluation uses the following:

- Reval Rate field, if populated.
- Mid Reval Rate field, if left blank.

The RB revaluation type uses the Mid Reval Rate field by default. However, the system can be configured to refer to Reval Rate field in the CURRENCY table (if populated) for calculating the revaluation rate, if the Reval Rate field is set as Yes in REVALUATION.PARAMETER .


##### Setting-up of Revaluation Parameters

Revaluation is controlled using a set of parameters defined on the REVALUATION.PARAMETER file. While spot deals invariably go with Spot (SP) method, in case of forward deals or forward leg of a swap deal, the option to choose a particular revaluation type, that is RB or IN, SL, IH, SF is available at the FX application.

As seen in the above screenshots, for each of the revaluation type the necessary parameter values are defined. Revaluation process refers to these parameter values corresponding to the revaluation type applicable for each contract.


##### Principles of Contract Revaluation

This section explains and illustrates the revaluation process which is part of the End-of-Day (EOD) processing relating to FX module.

This highlights both spot and forward revaluation process and illustrates the different revaluation methods applicable in forward contracts.

| Field | Currency | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Currency and Amount Bought | EUR | 1,000,000.00 |
| Rate of Exchange |  | 1.1280 |
| Currency and Amount Sold | USD | 1,128,000.00 |
| Value Date |  | Spot |
| Dealer Desk |  | 1 |
| Spot LCY Amount | USD | 1,128,000.00 |
| Buy LCY Amount | USD | -1,128,000.00 |
| Sell LCY Amount | USD | 1,128,000.00 |


##### Forward Contract Revaluation

The revaluation process allows the following methods for revaluation of forward contracts:

- Rebate (Mark-to-Market)
- Amortisation (Premium or discount treated as interest income or loss)

Based on the setup in REVALUATION.PARAMETER file, the revaluation process considers either the Mid Reval Rate or Reval Rate in the CURRENCY table, together with the FORWARD.RATES . However, this depends on the revaluation type opted at contract level.

An example is given for each one of these methods.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| SPOT EUR or USD | 1.13 |
| SPOT GBP or EUR | 1.17 |
| FWD 3MTH EUR or USD | 0.0040 |
| FWD 3MTH GBP or EUR | 0.0030 |

| Field | Currency | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Currency and Amount Bought | EUR | 1,000,000.00 |
| Spot Rate |  | 1.13 |
| Rate of Exchange |  | 1.1340 |
| Currency and Amount Sold ( LCY) | USD | 1,134,000.00 |
| Value Date |  | 3 Months |
| Dealer Desk |  | 1 |
| Revaluation Type |  | SL |
| Spot Lcy Amt | USD | 1,130,000.00 |
| Buy Local Currency Equivalent | USD | -1,130,000.00 |
| Sell Local Currency Equivalent | USD | 1,134,000.00 |

| Field | Currency | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Currency and Amount Bought | EUR | 1,000,000.00 |
| Spot Rate |  | 1.13 |

| Currency and Amount Sold | USD | 1,134,000.00 |

The local currency amount of the contract generates the local currency value in the corresponding Buy Local Currency Equivalent and Sell Local Currency Equivalent , that is,

- If Amount Bought = Local currency, then Amount Bought = Buy Local Currency Equivalent
- If Amount Sold = Local currency, then Amount Sold = Sell Local Currency Equivalent

The foreign currency amount of the contract is converted at the contract spot rate to generate the local currency value in its corresponding Buy Local Currency Equivalent and Sell Local Currency Equivalent .

The base amount of the contract is converted at the CURRENCY table middle rate of the base currency to generate the local currency value in its corresponding Buy Local Currency Equivalent or Sell Local Currency Equivalent .

The other foreign currency amount of the contract is converted at the contract spot rate and the Mid Reval Rate of the base currency in CURRENCY table to generate the local currency value in its corresponding Buy Local Currency Equivalent or Sell Local Currency Equivalent .

These spot local currency values are also used to update the FX position, once the deal is successfully validated.

After the validation of the two deals, the position file looks similar to the straight line method.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 | Column 5 | Column 6 | Column 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| For | - | EUR | 1,000,000.00 | + | USD | 1,134,000.00 |
| Against | + | USD | 1,134,000.00 | - | EUR | 1,000,000.00 |
| Local Equiv | - | USD | 1,130,000.00 | + | USD | 1,134,000.00 |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 | Column 5 | Column 6 | Column 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| For | - | GBP | 1,000,000.00 | + | EUR | 1,170,000.00 |
| Against | + | EUR | 1,170,000.00 | - | GBP | 1,000,000.00 |
| Local Equiv | - | USD | 1,325,000.00 | + | USD | 1,323,867.52 |


###### Dealer Desk 02

In the interest revaluation method, the difference between Buy Local Currency Equivalent and Sell Local Currency Equivalent is also isolated as a Profit and Loss amount at the start of the contract. However, this reserve is now amortised between reserve accounts offset by two Profit and Loss entries as follows:

- A credit to interest received exchange for the currency bought.

- A debit to interest paid exchange for the currency sold.

The net between the two profit and loss entries represent exactly the amount booked in a reserve account, and also the single accrual amount booked in the straight line revaluation method. The two daily profit and loss entries correspond exactly to one day's interest on the amount bought and sold by using the interest rates generated in the contract record.

> **⚠️ Note:** Signs follow the accounting conventions.

During COB, assuming the deals are fully authorised, the position in each foreign currency is revalued at spot rate against the local currency. Spot rates are used for revaluation during the complete life of these two contracts (explained earlier), as the FX position is also entered with spot rates. The revaluation process is identical to the one explained in the SPOT REVALUATION. The same revaluation rates and accounting entries are produced.

When the spot date is crossed, an additional process takes place namely the accruals on the local currency difference. These accruals continue till the value date of the contract (three months in the example), and the daily accrual amount is calculated as follows:

For the Currency Bought

That is, in the example deal 1 (FCY), (1,000,000 * 0.328826087) / 36000 = 9.13

When the contract involves local currency, the foreign currency accrual amount is always converted at the contract forward rate (1.1340 in our case). The daily accrual in local currency is USD 10.35.

In the example deal 2 (FCY),

(1,000,000.00 GBP x 0. 73438000 )/36 500 = GBP 20.12

When the contract does not involve the local currency of the country, the base currency accrual amount is always converted at the CURRENCY table Reval Rate (1.325).

The daily accrual in local currency is USD 26.66.

For the Currency Sold

In the example Deal 1 (LCY)

(1,134,000 * 1.708888888) / 36000 = 53.83

In the example Deal 2 (FCY)

(1,169 , 000 .00 * 0.391103507 )/ 360 00 = 12.70

When the contract does not involve the local currency of the country, the non-base currency accrual amount is always converted at the contract forward rate and the CURRENCY table reval rate of the base currency.

In this case, the rate is 1.325/1.1690 = 1.129.

The equivalent local currency accrual is 12.70* 1.129 = USD 14.34.

The system generates the following accruals accounting entries:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Deal 1 |  |
| C R Reserve Account | USD 43.48 |
| C R Interest Received Exchange | USD 10.35 |
| D R Interest Paid Exchange | USD 53.83 |
| Deal 2 |  |
| DR Interest Received Exchange | USD 12.32 |
| C R Reserve Account | USD 26.66 |
| D R Interest Paid Exchange | USD 14.64 |

When the value date of the contract is reached, both contracts are liquidated and relevant entries are passed to Customer, Nostro or Internal account. Similarly, as described for the straight line revaluation method, one supplementary statement entry is generated (that is, the liquidation of the Res account, which was used for the accruals). This supplementary entry also allows the transfer of the FX position to the Asset or Liability position on the value date of the contract with movements balancing in local currency.

|  | FCY | LCY |
|---|---|---|
| Deal 1 |  |  |
| D R Nostro or Customer Account | EUR -1000000 | USD -1,130,000.00 |
| D R Reserve A ccount (Suspense account ) |  | USD -4,000 |
| C R Nostro or Customer account |  | USD 1,134,000.00 |
| Deal 2 |  |  |
| DR Nostro 1,000,000 GBP | GBP - 1000000 | USD -1,325,000.00 |
| CR Nostro 1,173,000.00 EUR | EUR 1,169,000 | USD 1,323,867.52 |
| CR Reserve Account ( Suspense account) |  | USD 1,132.48 |

As illustrated, the FX transaction is posted to the settlement accounts on value date with its original values ( Buy Local Currency Equivalent and Sell Local Currency Equivalent of the contract), and henceforth value date is revalued within the asset or liability revaluation process.

##### Posting Only Unrealised Losses

Booking of unrealised revaluation profit is optional. This option can be set by using the Book Profits field.

- If set as Yes, both unrealised profit and loss is posted.
- If not set, only unrealised losses is booked.


##### Revaluation at Deal Level and Net Present Value

Based on the guidelines of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), users can book the revaluation profit or loss for the deal as a unit at the present value by setting up REVALUATION.PARAMETER as shown below:

If the Ifrs Revalue field is set as Yes, the re-valuation profit or loss is booked at deal level after discounting the profit or loss to the present value. The discounting rate is obtained from the PERIODIC.INTEREST table key defined in the Ifrs Disc Rate Key field.

To know more, refer to the Revaluation in IFRS .


##### Accounting Rules in Revaluation

The accounting rules in revaluation are illustrated with two examples as given below:

Example 1

| Currency | GBP | EUR | USD |
|---|---|---|---|
| GBP | NA | 1.18 | 1.33 |
| EUR | 0.85 | NA | 1.13 |
| USD | 0.75 | 0.89 | NA |

| Currency | GBP | EUR | USD |
|---|---|---|---|

| P&L | 50 | 50 | Reserve | -50 | -50 |
| P&L | 50 | 50 | Reserve | -50 | -50 |


##### Revaluation - IFRS

Due to regulatory requirements, according to the International Financial Reporting Standards IFRS, some users may calculate the re-valuation profit or loss on FX and NDF deals at deal level rather than at currency level and at the present value.

Temenos Transact provides this when the IFRS Revalue field in REVALUATION.PARAMETER is set as Yes. The system calculates the deal level profit or loss by netting the re-valuation profit or loss of each leg in local currency and then discounts the net amount. The discounting rate is obtained from the PERIODIC.INTEREST record for the key defined in the IFRS Disc Rate Key field in the REVALUATION.PARAMETER file. If direct rate is not available for the value date of the deal, the discount rate is interpolated.

|  | On Input | After Revaluation |  | LCY Equivalent |  | Currency | FCY Amount | Initial | Re-valued | Profit or Loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy Leg | CAD | -1000000.00 | -702619.16 | -710613.37 | 7994.21 | Profit |  |  |  |  |
| Sell Leg | INR | 40000000.00 | 702619.16 | 656492.73 | 46126.43 | Profit |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  | Deal Profit | 54120.64 |  |  |  |  |  |

The revaluation profit or loss is booked to the Profit Loss account at the net present value. The net present value is arrived at by discounting the deal level profit or loss at the appropriate discount rate for the period from the spot date (to the run date) to the value date of the deal.

- If the value date of the deal falls within the spot period for the currency pair, then no discounting is done.
- If the value date falls within one year from the spot date for the currency pair, discounting is done under the Simple method.
- If the value date falls after one year from the spot date for the currency pair, discounting is done under the Compound Method.

The spot date for the currency pair is calculated as on-run date, and the year is always calendar year.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| r | The rate of interest from the PERIODIC.INTEREST table. |
| n | The number of days, the value date is from the spot date (as on-run date and 365 is the basis). The basis is applicable to the local currency. |

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| REVAULATION.NPV.DETS | Gives leg-wise revaluation figures (for the date and upto the date) and discounted NPV of the revaluation (for the date and up to the date). |
| REVALUATION.NPV.DEAL | Gives deal-wise netted revaluation figures (for the date and up to the date) and discounted NPV of the revaluation (for the date and up to the date). |

### 2.23  Spot Contract


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A Foreign Exchange (FX) Spot contract is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) product. It is an agreement between two parties to buy one currency against selling another at an agreed price for settlement on the spot date. Spot date is usually two common business days of the two currencies of the contract from ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose Forex Inter Bank Deal*, *Spot Days*, *Spot Internal*, *Spot Market*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A Foreign Exchange (FX) Spot contract is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) product. It is an agreement between two parties to buy one currency against selling another at an agreed price for settlement on the spot date. Spot date is usually two common business days of the two currencies of the contract from the trade date, unless a longer period is customary or required in the local market. The exchange rate at which the transaction is executed, is called the spot exchange rate.

An FX deal is undertaken to buy a foreign currency against the local currency or another foreign currency (known as Cross Currency deal).

The following are the variants of a spot deal based on the value date:

The value or settlement date of the currencies bought and sold is same as the trade date known as value today or CASH deal.

The value or settlement date of the currencies bought and sold is for the next common working day of the two currencies, after the trade date is known as TOM deal.

The value or settlement date is two common business days (extended up to fourteen calendar days after the trade date), unless made shorter as required in the local market.

The spot date for Canadian Dollar or CAD spot is one business day.


#### 🔧 Working With

The examples below outlines the main components of a spot deal. The data fields vary depending on whether the deal is performed with an interbank counterparty or a corporate customer of the bank. The amount of information required is limited, and the versions are tailored for interbank and corporate deals separately. The versions are customized to assist the dealer in entering the deals based on the counterparty and types of deals. The following are an illustrative list of such versions:

- Spot interbank - Direct
- Spot interbank - Broker
- Spot corporate
- Spot private individuals

| Values | Description |
|---|---|
| T | Today |
| TO | Tomorrow |
| S or Null | Spot |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (Forex)

Spot deal or transaction is a contract of buying or selling a currency, commodity or security for immediate settlement (payment and delivery) on the spot date (which is two business days after the trade date).

The exchange rate applied is called as a spot rate. Forex trade by a bank with another bank is termed as Inter Bank Trade, whereas, the same performed with a customer is termed a normal Foreign Exchange Trade.

### 2.24  Swap Contract


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *FX swap contract involves a simultaneous purchase and sale of one currency for another with two different value dates (usually, spot to forward but forward to forward is also possible). Different exchange rates applied to the spot (first or near) and forward (second or far) legs reflect the interest...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Choose Forex Inter Bank Deal*, *Customer Rate*, *Exchange Profit*, *FWD FWD Swap*, *Forward Rate*, *GBP*, *GBP 1Mio* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

FX swap contract involves a simultaneous purchase and sale of one currency for another with two different value dates (usually, spot to forward but forward to forward is also possible). Different exchange rates applied to the spot (first or near) and forward (second or far) legs reflect the interest rates differential of the contract currencies known as premium or discount. Both spot and forward transactions are usually, but not necessarily, done with the same counterparty. The FX application maintains the link between the spot and forward deals, although they are handled as two separate transactions.

The short-term swaps, such as Overnight (ON), Tom-Next (TN) and Spot-Next (SN) are widely used swap transactions for funding and rollover of positions and the same are supported by the system. The following are the types of swap contracts:

| Types of Contracts | Description |
|---|---|
| Spot-Forward | A swap transaction with near leg having a spot value date and far leg have a value date greater than the spot value date. |
| Forward-Forward | Both the near and far legs have a forward value date. |
| Even | The swap base currency amount in near leg remains the same in the far leg. |
| Uneven | The swap base currency amount in first and second legs is not the same, which is the case generally in investment swap. |


#### 🔧 Working With

As mentioned earlier, FX swap is a simultaneous purchase and sale of identical amount of one currency for another with two different value dates. The starting point on the first leg and swap period determines the variants of swap contracts as:

- Overnight (ON) Swap, Tomorrow Next (TN) Swap, Spot Next (SN) Swap.
- In Spot-Forward Swap, the first leg is spot and subsequent leg is forward.

Spot next, spot one week, spot 6 months and so on.

- In Forward-Forward Swap, both the legs are forward.

3 months over 6 months, 3 months over 12 months and so on.


##### Spot-Forward Swap

The first leg has a spot value date and the second or far leg has a forward value date.

The below screenshot shows the first leg of swap that buys EUR and sells USD in spot

The first leg of the swap contract is similar to a spot deal. The Swap Base CCY field allows the user to select one of the two currencies and its amount in the first leg to be constant in the second of the swap deal. Depending on the purpose for which the swap deal is undertaken, the defaulted amount in the second leg can either be retained or modified. To know more on how the defaulted swap base currency amount is retained in the second leg, refer to Second Leg of a Swap .

The below screenshot shows the second leg of swap that sells EUR and buys USD in forward three months.

The swap period in the above transaction is three months and the swap premium is 12 Pips (Forward rate minus spot rate). Until the first leg is matured, both legs are considered as one unit and any amendment to any one of the legs will have to pass through both the legs. Once the first leg is matured, the second leg becomes an independent record similar to a forward outright contract.

The swap base currency amount in both the legs of the swap is identical according to the above example.

If the bank needs the Swap Base Currency amount defaulted in the second leg of the swap to be different from the first leg, the user can modify it. The below example has different Swap Base Currency amounts in the first and second legs.

In the below second leg of the swap screenshot, the Swap Base Currency amount of the first and second leg are different. Also, the system selects Y in the Uneven Swap field.


##### Forward-Forward Swap

Unlike in Spot-Forward contract, the first leg also has a forward value date, hence, it is called Forward-Forward Swap. In order to capture a forward-forward swap deal, the FWD FWD Swap field has to be marked as Yes, so the fields relevant for this type of swap deal are available for input.

> **⚠️ Note:** A deal input version for entering a Forward-Forward Swap can be configured to default the field to Yes.

The following are the screenshots of an FX Forward-Forward deal with even swap base currency amount:

The Forward Rate field allows user inputs, and Value Date Buy and Value Date Sell fields allow a forward value date.

The first leg rate defaults in the second leg ( Leg1 Rate field).

The difference between Leg1 Rate and Forward Rate represents the swap points. The user can also enter the swap points (applicable for customer FX deals versions) in the Forward Rate field in the following format:

- If the swap points are 25 Pips discount, the same is given as -25 (based on the quotation Pips in non-base currency record this number is converted to decimal displacement). The system applies the discount Pips to Leg1 Rate to derive the Forward Rate applicable for the second leg.
- If the swap points are +25 premium, then the same is converted to +0.0025 (assuming the Quotation Pips field in CURRENCY record for the non-base currency has a value 4).

Revaluation type opted for the first leg is defaulted to the second leg, which cannot be changed. Except the SF method of revaluation, all other types of revaluation methods are allowed. Amortisation of interest element representing the forward premium or discount is performed leg-wise (that is) the interest element worked out is based on the spot and forward rates for each leg individually.

Similar to spot-forward swap, margin percentage is not allowed on the first leg since the margin is generally applied on the contract as a whole and not on individual legs. The difference between the Treasury Rate and Customer Rate is considered as Exchange Profit (Non-treasury customer related fields are available on the version that supports corporate deals).

The following are the screenshots of an FX Forward-Forward deal with uneven swap base currency amount:

The Swap Base Currency is GBP and Amount is GBP 1Mio .

The same amount defaults in the second leg. The defaulted swap base currency amount is modified to book an uneven swap, as required.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (Forex)

A Forex Swap is an agreement to exchange the identical principal amounts of one currency for another with two different value dates. It is the exchange of a currency at spot rate with an agreement to reverse the contract with ideal amount of currency at a future date and at a specified forward rate.

### 2.25  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borr...*
> 
> **Applications:** `MS.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Check Validation Limit Breach*, *Emit Business Event*, *LIMIT.TYPE*, *Pro Data Calculation*, *SUPPRESS.ACCOUNTING*, *THIRD.PARTY.EXPOSURE*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borrowers. Credit limit is one of the factors that affect the consumers' credit scores and can impact their ability to get credit in the future. A lender generally gives lower-credit limits to high-risk borrowers because they may not be able to repay the debt. Low-risk borrowers usually get higher credit limits, giving them higher flexibility to spend.

The limits are determined by banks, alternative lenders and credit card companies based on the information related to the borrower, such as

- Borrower's credit rating
- Personal income
- Loan repayment history and other factors

The line of credit is the maximum amount of money a lender allows a borrower to spend on a revolving or non-revolving credit limits.

The Limit (LI) module provides the credit limit or line of credit in Temenos Transact . All the business applications in Temenos Transact refer to the LI module for creation and maintenance of the line of credit facility applicable to the business scenario.


##### Product Configuration

Credit limits are held by customer and product. Simple limits can be defined for a single customer and single product. However, more complex limits can also be configured with multiple levels.

Limits are held by the customer at two levels:

- Individual
- Liability group

Also, limits can be held by the product as 12 levels:

- 10 levels of sub-product
- Product
- Global

Thus, an individual trade can be updated as six limits.

In this example, bank provides an unsecured loan to ABC Ltd of 3 million USD. ABC Ltd is a part of the larger group, ABC International. Bank monitors the limits at both company and group levels. Unsecured loans are a sub-product within loans and the limits are monitored at both levels. Finally, the bank sets a limitation on all business with ABC Ltd and with ABC International, and these limits are held at the global-level.

Consequently, the unsecured loan has updated six limits. If any limit is exceeded, an override is raised during the input of loan.

- LIMIT application holds the credit limits.
- LIMIT.REFERENCE application holds sub-products, products and global definitions.
- CUSTOMER application holds the customers and customer liability definitions.
- LIMIT.PARAMETER application defines the various high-level parameters regarding the application. It links contracts and accounts to LIMIT.REFERENCE .

The main limit parameters are shown in the below flowchart.

Limits can also be set to monitor the exposure against currencies, countries and industries. These limits are monitored overnight. The LIMIT application uses the parameter and product tables to define the structure of limits.

This application defines the parameters that determine the way in which the limit system operates. LIMIT.PARAMETER record can have the ID as ‘SYSTEM’. The LIMIT.PARAMETER application controls the following:

- An indicator to specify if the foreign exchange contracts must be netted before limit comparison.
- A 'number of days' to define how many days prior to Limit Expiry Date and Review Date (can be fixed in the Review Frequency field) in the LIMIT application, the approach of these events must be reported.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the first revaluation occurs and at what frequency thereafter.
- A date and cycle to indicate when a central liability report (including those liability numbers which did not move) must be produced in the back-end process.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the commodity, country and currency reports must be produced.
- A ‘number of days’, administrative Extension Days, define the maximum number of days by which the expiry date of a limit can be ’administratively’ extended before a new expiry date must be assigned to the limit.
- The LIMIT application is defined according to the specific requirements of the bank. The most important feature of this application is that it allows the bank (for each financial application) to define the precise rules applicable to an environment. In this way, the limit verification process can be established by the bank according to a bank’s own set of rules without any program maintenance.

The product group definition that allows the bank to specify the different products, (in bank’s opinion) must be part of the commodity, country and currency exposure.

Creation of Other Record IDs:

The LIMIT.PARAMETER application allows the creation of other record IDs besides SYSTEM. These record IDs can have a valid legacy application (that is, ACCOUNT, LD, MM and FOREX) as ID. The purpose of these records is to move their parametersation, which was initially done in the SYSTEM record, to new individual records for each application to improve system performance.

For example, for the ACCOUNT application, the user can create a new record, which includes all the necessary parametrisation for this particular application.


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Limit related tables.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| creditLimits.createLimitParameter.limitParameterCreated | Event to create limit parameter |
| creditLimits.updateLimitParameter.limitParameterUpdated | Event to amend limit parameter |
| creditLimits.createProduct.productCreated | Event to create limit product |
| creditLimits.createUtilisationProduct.utilisationProductCreated | Event to create utilisation limit product |
| creditLimits.createValidationProduct.validationProductCreated | Event to create validation limit product |
| creditLimits.createIntradayProduct.intradayProductCreated | Event to create intraday limit product |
| creditLimits.createReservationProduct.reservationProductCreated | Event to create reservation limit product |
| creditLimits.updateLimitProduct.productUpdated | Event to amend limit product |
| creditLimits.updateIntradayProduct.intradayProductUpdated | Event to amend intraday limit product |
| creditLimits.cancelLimitProduct.productCancelled | Event to cancel limit product |
| creditLimits.createSecuredLimit.securedLimitCreated | Event to create secured limit |
| creditLimits.createUnsecuredLimit.unsecuredLimitCreated | Event to create unsecured limit |
| creditLimits.createGroupSecuredLimit.groupSecuredLimitCreated | Event to create secured group limit |
| creditLimits.createGroupUnsecuredLimit.groupUnsecuredLimitCreated | Event to create unsecured group limit |
| creditLimits.createReportingLimits.customerReportingLimitsCreated | Event to create reporting credit limit |
| creditLimits.updateIntradayLimit.intradayLimitUpdated | Event to amend intraday credit limit |
| creditLimits.createReservationLimit.reservationLimitCreated | Event to create reservation limit |
| creditLimits.limitExpiryDueDate.expiryDue | Event for limit expiry due date |
| creditLimits.limitExpiryFailure.expiryFailed | Event for limit expiry failure |
| creditLimits.limitReviewDate.reviewDateReached | Event to review limit on review date |
| creditLimits.limitReviewDueDate.reviewDue | Event to review limit |
| creditLimits.updateLimit.limitUpdated | Event to amend limit |
| creditLimits.updateLimitAmount.limitAmountUpdated | Event to update limit amounts |
| creditLimits.updateLimitAvailability.limitAvailabilityUpdated | Event to update limit availability |
| creditLimits.updateExpiryDate.limitExpiryDateUpdated | Event to update expiry date of limit |
| creditLimits.reportLimitIncrease.limitIncreased | Event to increase limit schedule |
| creditLimits.reportLimitDecrease.limitDecreased | Event to decrease limit schedule |
| creditLimits.reportLimitExpiry.limitExpired | Event to indicate limit expiry |
| creditLimits.reportLimitBreach.validationLimitBreached | Event to validate limit breach |
| creditLimits.cancelLimit.limitCancelled | Event to cancel limit |
| creditLimits.updateExposure | Transaction command event for exposure update |
| creditLimits.updateExposure.exposureUpdated | Event to update exposure in the limit |
| creditLimits.deleteExposure | Transaction command event for exposure delete |
| creditLimits.delinkContract | Event to be emitted when limit is delinked from contract |
| creditLimits.delinkContract.contractDelinked | Event to delink contract from the limit |
| creditLimits.recordContractClosure | Event to be emitted when contract is linked to limit closed |
| creditLimits.recordContractClosure.contractClosed | Event for limit contract closure |
| creditLimits.recordContractLink | Event to be emitted for the limit and contract link |
| creditLimits.recordContractLink.contractRecorded | Event to link contract to the limit |
| creditLimits.updateContractLimit | Event to be emitted to update limit property linked with contract |
| creditLimits.updateContractLimit.contractLimitUpdated | Event to update limit in limit contract |
| creditLimits.updateContractOwners | Event to be emitted when customer changes the contract linked to limit |
| creditLimits.updateContractOwners.contractOwnersUpdated | Event to update owner in limit contract |
| creditLimits.updateContractProperties | Event to be emitted when there is a change in contract linked to limit |
| creditLimits.updateContractProperties.contractDetailsUpdated | Event to update limit contract properties |
| creditLimits.updateContractTerm | Event to be emitted when there is a change in contract term |

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The System Tables user guide explains the Customer and related reference tables and the Core Reference tables.

- Customer and related reference tables – This includes the following: The customer application and associated static tables. The customer centric functionalities.
- Core Reference tables – This includes core tables that act as reference for transaction processing as listed below: Country and related tables (like REGION , HOLIDAY and DATES ) Currency Category Interest related tables (like Accrual Parameter, Interest Basis, Basic Interest and Periodic Interest) Charge related tables Tax related tables Card Management tables Cheque Management tables Treasury and Settlements related tables Other Core Reference Tables


#### Product Configuration

The following system-wide applications help in grouping the customers and defining rules for the group based on the business purposes, like defining customer group specific charges and tax.

- CONDITION.PRIORITY
- XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION, where XXX refers to the business application.
- APPL.GEN.CONDITION


##### Condition Priority

The purpose of the CONDITION.PRIORITY application is to specify, for certain applications, which data elements in other reference applications can be specified to determine condition groups. CONDITION.PRIORITY records can be created with the following IDs:

- ACCOUNT
- FIDUCIARY
- FUNDS.TRANSFER
- FX.MARGIN
- LETTER.OF.CREDIT
- SC.MANAGEMENT
- SC.SAFEKEEPING
- SC.TRADING
- STATEMENT
- TAX
- POR.TRANSACTION

CONDITION.PRIORITY is a CUS level application. Records of this application can be shared between companies, which share the same customer company, or there could be company-specific CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a Company Code in the ID.

For the

application, it is possible to have a specific record for the Company DE0010001 with the ID ACCOUNT-DE0010001.

The (parameters) records without a Company ID suffixed is applicable to the Master Customer Company (specified as Customer Company in the COMPANY application) as well as to Companies that do not have their own CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

An existing CONDITION.PRIORITY record cannot be modified. However, it is possible to specify parameters that are applicable in future (after the COB processing on a specified date, which can be either the processing date or any future date) by creating CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a date after the company code in the ID.

The record with ID ’ACCOUNT--20040702’ (with a null Company ID for the customer company) is applicable to the Master Customer Company and the record with ID ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001-20040702’ is applicable to the Company DE0010001, both records to be effective after the COB processing on 2nd July 2004. The date specified can either be the processing date or it could be a future date.

It is possible to specify the priority items (fields) using the Priority Item field. This is a multi-valued field which defines the order in which fields are used, when matching conditions against values specified in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

- Fields from CUSTOMER application can be specified in all CONDITION.PRIORITY records.
- Fields from ACCOUNT application can be specified only in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to ACCOUNT or STATEMENT.
- Fields from SEC.ACC.MASTER can be specified only in the three CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to Wealth application (with IDs SC.MANAGEMENT, SC.SAFEKEEPING and SC.TRADING).

The priority items specified in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records are defaulted as the field names in the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

While determining the condition groups of applications, the priority of the data items (specified as Priority Item ) is determined by their relative position in the CONDITION.PRIORITY record.

For each priority item specified in CONDITION.PRIORITY , users can also specify a validation, which ensures that a value entered for a priority item (in XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications) exists as a record ID in another table. This can also be used to display an enrichment when the value is entered.

In the

record for

, the

CATEGORY’ can have a validation specified in the

DESCRIPTION’. In this case, when a value for the CATEGORY is entered in

, the value entered should be a valid record ID in the

application, and the value of the

field in that

record will be displayed as an enrichment.


##### Parameters and Rules for Groups

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications provide the parameters to calculate the default groups for some applications. The priority data items, which are used in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION tables, are defaulted from the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications and the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records from which the priority data items are defaulted are listed below:

| XXX.GEN.CONDITION Applications | CONDITION.PRIORITY record ID from which priority data items are defaulted |
|---|---|
| ACCT.GEN.CONDITION | ACCOUNT |
| FD.GEN.CONDITION | FIDUCIARY |
| FT.GEN.CONDITION | FUNDS.TRANSFER |
| LC.GEN.CONDITION | LETTER.OF.CREDIT |
| SCPM.GEN.CONDITION | SC.MANAGEMENT |
| SCSK.GEN.CONDITION | SC.SAFEKEEPING |
| SCTR.GEN.CONDITION | SC.TRADING |
| STMT.GEN.CONDITION | STATEMENT |
| TAX.GEN.CONDITION | TAX |
| FX.GEN.CONDITION | FX.MARGIN |
| PP.GEN.CONDITION | POR.TRANSACTION |

The parameters specified in FD.GEN.CONDITION , FT.GEN.CONDITION , LC.GEN.CONDITION , SCPM.GEN.CONDITION , SCSK.GEN.CONDITION , SCTR.GEN.CONDITION , TAX.GEN.CONDITION , and PP.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the condition groups in the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application.

The parameters specified in ACCT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the account group ( Condition Group ) in ACCOUNT , while those specified in STMT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the frequency in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT .

For each XXX.GEN.CONDITION application, there is a corresponding XXX.GROUP.CONDITION application (except for STMT.GEN.CONDITION ) to define the various parameters for each group. The following XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications exist:

- ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION
- FD.GROUP.CONDITION
- FT.GROUP.CONDITION
- LC.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION
- TAX.TYPE.CONDITION
- FX.GROUP.CONDITION

All the XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications referred here are of the FTD level, which may be company specific or shared between companies depending on the configuration of Default Finan Com or Spcl Fin File fields in the COMPANY record.

If the FTD type files for the Company DE0010001 are unique, then the

records for the Company DE0010001 can have the data items defaulted from the

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001’ if that record exists, else from the default

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT’.

While defining CONDITION.PRIORITY records to be applicable in future, it is possible to specify which XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records need to be retained, by specifying their IDs in the Gen Cond Keep and Group Cond Keep fields respectively. During COB processing on the specified date, these XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are automatically modified with priority data items applicable for the new structure, by retaining existing priority data items and their values. New priority data items are updated with null values.

Further, in conjunction with dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records, it is also possible to specify dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records, which can become effective in future. Such XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are defined by suffixing a hyphen with a date (either processing date or a future date) in the ID. Priority data items in these records are defaulted from the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records. These record IDs must not be defined as retention record IDs in the Gen Cond Keep field of CONDITION.PRIORITY .

After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

Those XXX.GEN.CONDITION records that are not included in the Gen Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record or those records that do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION record are dropped after the COB processing on the specified date.

With the exceptions described below, future dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION can be created with an ID of the format ‘xxx-Date’, provided the ID is not already specified in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record. After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

There is an exception to the above referred functionality (which existed before the CONDITION.PRIORITY application has been enhanced to accept dated records). The ID format of the SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION and SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION applications is ‘xxx.date’ (both parts mandatory and connected by a dot) to allow definition of parameters, which applies on various dates. The first part of the ID is validated against the first part of the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records. When the records in these applications are entered, there is no validation against the CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records whose IDs are not included in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record, or which do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION record (suffixed to the ID with a hyphen and date), will be dropped after the COB processing on the specified date. However, customer-specific XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records with ID format as ‘C-Customer ID’ is not dropped after COB processing.

For Payments, the parameters and conditions applicable for a group of customers is defined in PP.CLIENT.CONDITIONRECORD application. Please read Introduction to Client Conditions for more details.


##### Parameter to Default Groups UsingTemenos TransactRoutine

The APPL.GEN.CONDITION application is used to define group conditions for contracts based on a combination of decisions and calls to locally developed subroutines. For example, it allows specific tax codes to be applied to particular types of contract for particular types of customer.

There is one record per application for which many sets of group conditions can be defined. User must ensure that multiple set of groups are defined correctly, as the first set of conditions that pass the validation checks result in that contract group code being applied.

A Temenos Transact subroutine, APPL.GRP.CONDITION can be called to evaluate the current contract record using relevant APPL.GEN.CONDITON . It returns the first group code where all decision checks evaluate to true.

The MM.MONEY.MARKET and LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSIT applications call the evaluation routine automatically. Other applications can call the evaluation routine from VERSION routines to update local reference fields with the relevant group code.

The subroutine processes these decisions and updates the Contract Group field in the application record whenever the contract is changed. If changes to the contract cause the conditions to break, then a new Contract Group code is generated, which results in a different tax code being applied. A default group code can be defined as the last group code without associated conditions, if required. TAX.TYPE.CONDITION allows the Contract Group code to be linked to the allocation of specific tax codes.
