### 2.27  Treasury Settlement


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Application*, *Autoroute Bank*, *BROKER*, *Bic Code*, *Effective Date*, *GB Notes*, *Last Eff Change*, *Nostro Acct No* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the workflow of the treasury and settlement related reference applications in Temenos Transact .


##### Nostro Account

The NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application defines the nostro account records by currency and identifies, which account is the default nostro for each function of each application within the specified currency.

FT OT transactions use account 20753, FX uses 23752 and all others transactions use account 20656.

The various NOSTRO.ACCOUNT records can be recorded for each application. The definition of NOSTRO.ACCOUNT records within this application eliminates the need to enter the same details each time for each transaction processed by various applications of Temenos Transact .

> **⚠️ Note:** FOREX allows fast input of alternate nostro account values by entering A, B and C and so on. These relate directly to the first, second, third and so on, values entered.

- Future Dated Nostro Account Details Banks change their Nostro correspondents periodically. They are notified in advance when these changes happen and it is possible to capture these changes within the system, allowing the system to provide the correct nostro account details based on a settlement date. Once the effective date of a record is reached, the system makes this the current record and writes previous records to history during the online phase of COB. A record is entered into the system with the ID as effective date added as a suffix to the record (as shown in the below screenshot). The Effective Date field is used to hold a list of effective dated records within the system on the current record. GB Notes field is used to add comments. The last date and time, an effective date record updated is held in Last Eff Change field. The Effective Date and GB Notes fields are updated in the current record (as shown in the below screenshot), when effective and future dated records are created:


##### Agency

The AGENCY application contains the settlement details for major customers and all banks irrespective of whether there is any business connection. The details include any arrangements, account relationships and where possible, the agent’s correspondent bankers for specific currencies. This information is entered centrally to supply automatic routing instructions for remittances or cover to all banks and customers with whom the bank has numerous dealings. This eliminates the need to re-enter the details at transaction level. It allows full advantage to be taken of electronic delivery facilities by providing automatically, the settlement agents for remittances or cover involved in outward payments.

The absence of agent's correspondent banker’s information in this application forces the user to enter these details each time at the time of transaction. Any nostro account defined in this application is for information only and is not used as a default nostro by the transaction processing, which always uses the details from the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application.

Record details can be setup on this application using two different ID formats, either the customer number or the Bic Code field prefixed with SW- in DE.BIC application.

- Customer Number The basic details of these banks and major customers must first be defined in the CUSTOMER application before the creation of the AGENCY details is allowed. Having created a CUSTOMER record, which is a bank, it is advisable to create an AGENCY record with the same ID and all available auto routing details.
- Bic Code The AGENCY records can be created for the BIC code with all the auto routing details. The input of this record is similar to that of the record created by using the customer number ID. The exceptions being that the input are not allowed for Nostro Acct No , Our Ext Acc No and Their Acct No fields. In the AGENCY application, the BIC codes are pre-fixed by ‘SW-’ and should have 14 characters (including ‘SW-’). The Bic Code should be a valid SWIFT code and can exist in the DE.BIC application. The DE.BIC application is loaded from the BIC address directory file and this is supplied by SWIFT. Refer the DE.BIC section, for more details. If the Validate Bic field in the DE.BIC.PARAMETER application must be set to YES, then upon inputting a BIC code (an SW- record) Temenos Transact validates the ID against the DE.BIC records. If the field is set to NO, then AGENCY accepts any SW- codes as long as they are in the correct format.
- Multiple Agency Records for Settlement

> **⚠️ Note:** There is an informal linkage between records, which comes into effect when the system is working out the full settlement path for a customer.

The auto routing bank ( Autoroute Bank field) is defined for the counterparty in the AGENCY application. The auto routing bank must exist in the AGENCY application and the input can be in BIC or customer number. If the Application field is FX or FT, the Autoroute Bank field is defined as a BIC.

The below screenshot shows SWIFT BIC codes used in AGENCY for the Autoroute Bank field.

The AGENCY for a counterparty has the Autoroute Bank field value as the correspondent bank BIC for a specific currency. If the correspondent bank has the payment routing arrangement with another intermediary bank for the currency, then the BIC or customer number of the intermediary bank can be set as correspondent bank BIC in Autoroute Bank.

An example of auto routing arrangement is shown in the following screenshots:

- The counterparty record (100129) in AGENCY has Autoroute Bank as SW-BFWTES01 (correspondent bank BIC).
- The correspondent bank BIC (SW-BFWTES01) has the routing arrangement through the intermediary bank (Autoroute Bank) as SW-BFWTES02.
- The Intermediary bank has the Autoroute Bank defined as the same BIC, indicating that there is no further routing.

Future Dated Settlement Instructions

Temenos Transact can capture future dated standard settlement instructions, if required. This allows the bank to update the correspondent banking details in advance of the effective date, allowing the system to provide the correct settlement instructions based on a settlement date.

Once the effective date of a record is reached, the system makes this the current record and writes the previous records to HISTORY table during the online phase of COB.

A record is entered into the system with the effective date added as a suffix to the record’s ID. For example, 140048-20091224 (as shown below) or SW-CITIUS33-20091224’.

The future dated record for customer is shown in the below screenshot.

The future dated record for BIC is shown in the below screenshot.

The Effective Date field is used to hold a list of effective dated records within the system on the current record. The GB Notes field is used to add comments. The last date and time, an effective dated record was updated, is held in Last Eff Change field in the current record.

The below screenshots demonstrate the Effective Date and GB Notes are updated in the current record, when effective and future dated records are created:

The current record with the Effective Date and GB Notes fields are shown in the below screenshot.

The future dated record with the Effective Date and GB Notes fields are shown in the below screenshot.


##### Broker

The BROKER application is used to define the banks' authorised brokers. The following screenshot shows the field details in BROKER application:

- Payment Instructions

The first section of the BROKER application is used to specify the broker's payment instructions as follows:

- Currencies in which the broker accepts payment
- The default transaction code for brokerage entries
- The account to which the brokerage funds are to be transferred.

This account may be defined in two ways:

1. The default specifies an internal account number, which consists of: The payment currency The category specified in the ACCOUNT.CLASS record The BROKER and the sub-division code specified in the BROKER record. The actual internal account number is not shown on the record.
2. The second method of account definition is the specification of a Temenos Transact account, which must be a customer account that belongs to the BROKER . One account may be defined for each payment currency. Calculation Parameters

The second section of BROKER application is used to determine the different brokerage rates applicable to specific deal types. During the deal input stages for the valid applications, if a broker code is entered, then the details of this application are obtained to default and the brokerage amount for the deal. Certain aspects of the deal are matched to the parameters on this application to define a deal type. Each deal type is defined using the following parameters:

- System ID
- Category
- Time

The System ID is used to define the application. At present, valid products are Money Market, Loans and Deposits, Letter of Credit, Drawings, Fiduciaries and Forward Rate Agreements. Category is used to match the product category of the deal. Time is defined as the number of days from the start date to the maturity date. Once a match has been found for the deal type, the currency of the deal is matched with a list of currencies on the BROKER record. Then, whether the customer of the deal is a bank or a non-bank, a rate or FT.CHARGE.TYPE or FT.COMMISSION.TYPE is returned on which the brokerage calculation is based.


##### Position Type

The FX.POS.TYPE application is used to split the position and accounting of the bank into logical divisions. In particular, the usage of this application is mandatory when using a GAAP or IFRS financial reporting. Although prefixed by FX, this application is commonly used in Temenos Transact and is referred to by CATEGORY, ACCOUNT and many accounting or position parameter files.

When used for GAAP reporting, it is recommended that the two digit ID is set to the same ID used by the country (that is, IN for India, GB for the UK, CH for Switzerland and so on). The TR record is the original and default record used by Temenos Transact must be present. The IF record is used for IFRS reporting and must be present, if IFRS reporting is required.

In normal usage, the ID of the application is used but for contingent and self-balancing, an extended ID identifier is needed.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is recommended that the following style of values is followed:

- For P/L add the PL prefix to the position type. For example, PLIF.
- For Contingent P/L add CP prefix to the position type. For example, CPIF.
- For self-balancing P/L add CB prefix to the position type. For example, CBIF.

Otherwise, by default it is achieved, by taking the first character of the ID and adding 'P' for contingents and 'B' for self-balancing. Alternatively, the user can define their own values of up to four digits for each of these.

> **⚠️ Note:** There is a system control RE.PL.PREFIXES table, which stores a cross-reference of all the prefixes that prevents the duplication of any user or system defined values.


##### Deal Method

The FX.DEAL.METHOD application is used by the main dealing or lending applications to record how the deal was booked. It is used mainly for advices and reports, and is entered in the BROKER field on the relevant applications.

#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a generic payment order product ID for treasury settlements and map it to the Po Ref Product field in TM.PO.INTEGRATION table.
2. Create a record in PP.MSGPAYMENTTYPE table for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments.
3. Create a record in PP.NODA.LIST for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments. The Order Initiation Type field in the PO application has a specific value for the payment order originated from the Treasury applications. To know more, refer to Configuring Payment Order.
4. Create a separate PP.SOURCE record for treasury settlements.


##### Imposing Required Credit Value Date

This enables the user to impose the required credit value date passed by Treasury application on the debit value date. Hence, the statement entries for settlement amount has the appropriate value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a record in PP.CHANNEL table from where all treasury payments originate. The channel is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury payments.
2. Create a record in PP.SOURCEPRODUCTGROUP table to define source product group in Payments Hub. The source product is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury settlements.
3. Create an EB.LOOKUP record that is similar to the PP.SOURCE record. This enables to map Order Initiation Type in PP.SOURCE to the value in TM.PO.INTEGRATION .
4. In the PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE table, set the debit value date output as required credit value date. The value date in statement entry posted by TPH is same as the required credit value date passed by Treasury applications. The above steps are applicable for FX, FRA and MM. However, the user needs to create a new EB.LOOKUP record for NDF .


##### Generating Forward Entries by TPH

This enables the user to choose the parameter option at TPH level to generate forward accounting or live entries with forward value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create four new products in PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table to provide all four possibilities of treasury settlement. The following record names are products created for domestic and international payments, which TPH uses to process treasury payments: Record Name Message Type Payment Type TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 MT103 Domestic Payment TRSY.C.103.O.I-20190417 MT103 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.I-20190417 MT202 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.D-20190417 MT202 Domestic Payment
2. In the Forward Entry Flag field of PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table, set as Y. A sample record of TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 is shown in the below screenshots. (To know more, refer to the table above). To process an NDF transaction, the user needs to create four more records by setting the Originating Source and Forward E ntry Flag to NDSTLMT and N, respectively.
3. Create a new record in PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT and link it to output parameters of the determined product. This helps to identify the output channel configured in PP.CONTRACT .
4. Create a new rule in PP.CONTRACT with the PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT defined. This enables TPH to determine the output channel for the payment initiated from Treasury.
5. In the PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES table, set the Update Cash Position field as Y. The cash flow positions for payments processed through TPH is updated.

#### 📖 Introduction

Banks and financial institutions analyse and make decisions based on comprehensive data sets. Consequently, Data Integration is a crucial process for the following reasons.

- Operational Efficiency: By integrating data, banks can streamline their processes, reduce redundancies, and improve overall efficiency. This can lead to cost savings and faster service delivery.
- Risk Management: Integrated data systems enable better risk assessment and management. Banks can quickly identify potential risks and take proactive measures to mitigate them.
- Regulatory Compliance: Data integration helps banks comply with regulatory requirements by ensuring that all necessary data is accurately captured and easily accessible for reporting purposes.
- Enhanced Decision Making: With integrated data, banks can leverage advanced analytics and AI to make more informed decisions. This can lead to better strategic planning and improved business outcomes.

The precise set of messages required to implement an intraday liquidity dashboard for regulatory reporting depends on the specific requirements from the national regulator(s) to which a financial institution reports. The Intraday Liquidity Management (ILM) module can be used to prepare reports for intra day liquidity risk management purposes internally.


##### Data Collection

This section explains the various ways and approaches banks follow to collect data as required by the regulators.

Some regulators have implemented a broad regulatory intraday liquidity framework, which obligates banks to provide evidence that they manage their intraday liquidity in real-time. This requires data to be collected and saved by the banks in real-time at transactional level and can be retrieved for audit purposes.

Banks can collect transaction data retrospectively which is required for regulatory reporting of the tools (as defined in the BCBS paper). In this case, the data must be collected at transactional level with a confirmation of the time at which the debit or the credit entry has affected the liquidity position.

In this approach, banks need not produce a regulatory reporting based on time-stamped information at transactional level but according to a pre-agreed time interval. Debit and credit confirmations can be delivered by the service providers either through batch reporting sent at a maximum time interval of 15 minutes or through transactional reporting providing the accurate time stamping information.


##### Data Integration in ILM

Temenos ILM relays near real-time data to update the liquidity position. Static tables are used to store fixed reference data or integrated data from multiple sources in ILM for monitoring and managing liquidity positions. The static tables that must be configured for integrating data in ILM are,

Liquidity Events ( IL.EVENT ) act as an initial point of interaction between the Transact Liquidity module and external entities. These touch points are crucial for facilitating communication and data exchange through messages and use the static data configuration to create liquidity events in real time. IL.EVENT records support multiple identifiers from various source systems. The liquidity events created capture liquidity movements, which are consolidated into different cash positions.

Open Financial Service (OFS) is an interface that allows Temenos Transact to process transaction and query requests. Every interaction with IL.EVENT takes place through OFS to create a liquidity event and update downstream tables.

The below flowchart depicts the data flow in ILM.


##### Messages Supported in ILM

Financial institutions use SWIFT messages to exchange information about financial transactions securely. They are relayed as liquidity events from various source systems. The below image depicts the various types of SWIFT messages supported by the ILM module.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the system configurations to manage intraday liquidity events. The following fields in IL.PARAMETER must be defined to configure data integration in Intraday Liquidity Management (ILM).

- Event Version - To define the valid IL.EVENT version using which the automatic (STP) event records are created.
- OFS Source Event - To define the OFS record for creating events automatically (STP) from the messages.
- Transaction Version - To define the valid IL.TRANSACTION version using which the automatic (STP) transaction records are created or updated.

Read the IL.PARAMETER user guide for more information on the parameterisation of ILM.

For mapping ISO200022 messages the opening elements alone must be specified. This field applies various symbols for different purposes like, ':' - Used as a conditional statement. For tag1PCRD:tag2, if tag1's value is PCRD, then tag2's values are retrieved. '[]' - Used when a field has multiple values from various tags. In decreasing order, priority drops. If Message Tag contains [tag1][tag2], there are two possible values in the corresponding field, from tag1 and tag2 each. Since the priority is in descending order; if tag 1 has no value, the system enters only tag 2's value in Event Field . '+' – Used when a field must store values from multiple tags. If Message Tag contains [tag1]+[tag2], the field stores the values of both tag1 and tag2, delimited by '/'. That is, the system enters tag1/tag2 values in Event Field . |

#### 🔧 Working With

Once the static tables are configured, the system captures the IL.EVENT from various source systems and maps them to IL.TRANSACTION . This section explains how events are captured and mapped to transactions.


##### Capturing Events

A liquidity event ( IL.EVENT ) is a message or data feed for receipts, payments, and statement messages received from various source systems such as SWIFT, Core Banking System, Treasury Management System, and Payment Hub. Such liquidity events happen on a real-time 24/7 basis; hence, the Intraday Liquidity Management (ILM) solution receives and processes them in near real-time.

All the receipts, payments, and statements messages received from various sources such as SWIFT or any third-party system are recorded as events to be used to create transactions in ILM. IL.EVENT allows users to view, create, update, or delete events. An event can be created manually or automatically through STP.

Multiple events can create or update a single transaction record and link the events with the transaction record based on a matching key.

- Events ( IL.EVENT ) to Transaction ( IL.TRANSACTION ) is a many-to-one relationship.
- Events ( IL.EVENT ) to Account Daily Balance ( IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL ) is one-to-one relationship.

The events created here are processed in downstream dynamic tables IL.TRANSACTION and IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL based on the value of Event Type for processing the liquidity positions.

##### Mapping Event to Transaction

The Matching Key decides the logic based on which the transaction is updated using IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE . The screenshot below shows the matching key formed in IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION .

IL.EVENT created either manually or through STP can generate or update IL.TRANSACTION ( Event Type should be set as Transaction).

> **⚠️ Note:** While creating an event manually, IL.EVENT defaults Event Type with Transaction. However, the user can change it.

The liquidity events currently support the following SWIFT messages for updating IL.TRANSACTION .

- ISO15022 - MT103, MT202, MT210, MT900, MT910, MT942, MT940, and MT950.
- ISO20022 – pacs.008, pacs.009, camt.057, camt.054, camt.052, and camt.053.

The statement messages like camt.052, camt.053, MT942, MT940, and MT950 are bifurcated into ‘n’ number of IL.EVENT records with Event Type as Transaction based on the number of transactions available in the statement. The above message-based validations are incorporated in IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION to maintain data integrity.

Here, X messages refer to the ISO15022 and ISO20022 messages listed above.


##### Importing Events from Source Systems

This section explains the various source systems from where the events can be imported.

Temenos Payments interacts with many Transact applications, external bank host systems, clearings, and payment gateways to successfully process a payment request and send outward payment messages to the recipient. TPH as a source system imports MT103, pacs.08, MT202, and pacs.009 into ILM.

> **⚠️ Note:** As a prerequisite, configure PP.STATUS.ACTION and PP.PROGRAM.CHARACTERISTIC as mentioned in configuring TPH section.

- Once the payment messages are generated from TPH, the user must set the below services to AUTO. XXX/PAYMENT.STPFLOW.HEAVY XXX/PP.INTERFACE.UPDATE XXX/SWIFT.OUT.LISTENER XXX/PAYMENT.STPFLOW.HEAVY XXX/INTEGRATION.SERVICE
- The system updates Status of the payment messages to 999.
- When the user runs the OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE service, the system creates the IL.EVENT records for TPH-generated messages based on IL.MSG.EVENT.MAP .

EB.FILE.UPLOAD (as a source system) imports all the liquidity messages supported by ILM. It is used when a non-Temenos system sends data to Temenos Transact. This alternative system follows standard OFS syntax to upload information, but this requires an understanding of the OFS syntax, which may or may not be practical.

For file upload, the source system does not need to understand the Temenos Transact syntax. It takes the onus of the source system for mapping and passes that to Temenos Transact, where core functionality such as version can be used to handle data upload. Read Using File Upload for more information on the file upload functionality.

> **⚠️ Note:** As a prerequisite, configure the EB.FILE.UPLOAD.PARAM as mentioned in Configuring EB.FILE.UPLOAD.PARAM section.

The user can use the template provided to update the CSV files with the relevant information. The user must be aware of the column position of each field and its message-based validation in IL.EVENT . Click here to download a sample CSV template.

Follow the below procedure to import events through csv.

1. Select Upload Type as IL.EVENT.UPLOAD in EB.FILE.UPLOAD .
2. Upload the required CSV file in File Name .
3. Authorise the record and run the XXX/T24.UPLOAD.PROCESS service.

By default, the first row acts as the header ID. However, the user can configure the header ID position.

- If an error occurs in the header ID, then all the remaining rows are not processed to create IL.EVENT .
- If the header ID is processed and an error occurs in either of the remaining rows, all the other rows (except the erroneous one) are processed to create IL.EVENT .

The events that are created successfully update IL.TRANSACTION .

The Delivery (DE) module manages the flow of all messages from Temenos Transact, such as confirmations, payments, and advices which enables the user to control formatting and language of presentation. Messages are generated automatically, as soon as the transaction is complete or when a scheduled event occurs. ILM imports MT210 and camt.057 messages generated by the Delivery module.

Read the Working with Generic Delivery Interface section for more information on adding a new interface through the generic delivery interface.

> **⚠️ Note:** As a prerequisite, configure DE.MESSAGE and DE.INTERFACE as mentioned in the Configuring DE Layer section.

Once the receipt messages are generated from DE, the user can import the following messages.

The user can run the below services,

- XXX/SWIFTXML.OUT
- XXX/XMLISO.OUT
- XXX/INTEGRATION SERVICE

The system updates DE.DELIVERY.REQUEST.LISTENER and updates the status ( Dispositon ) of DE.O.HEADER from Unformatted to Ofs Formatted.

The user can run the XXX/SWIFT.OUT service. Then the system updates the status ( Disposition ) of DE.O.HEADER from Unformatted to Formatted as shown below.


##### Updating Transactions

The Transaction table ( IL.TRANSACTION ) contains details of various transactions generated through different events like receipts, payments, and statements from a source system for various entities in ILM.

The receipts, payments, and statements messages received from SWIFT are MT103, MT202, pacs.008, pacs.009, MT210, camt.057, MT900, MT910, camt.054, MT940, MT942, MT950, camt.052, and camt.053.

A transaction can be created manually or automatically through STP and can be matched automatically or manually by the user. The transactions created in IL.TRANSACTION are processed in downstream dynamic tables IL.BALANCE.MVMT and IL.TIME.BASED.BAL for processing the liquidity positions when the cash positions are updated as actuals.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Event Ref No | Holds the @ID of IL.EVENT , representing the different events associated with the transaction. It updates the latest event ID of a transaction. |
| Comm Ref No | Holds the transaction reference number imported from the SWIFT ISO MX messages. It is a common reference for the various events of a deal and the same is associated with the transaction. |
| Transaction Type | Holds the transaction type information with which the latest event record is associated. |
| Transaction Status | Holds the status of an IL transaction which is used to update the status change of a transaction through its life cycle based on the associated events. |
| Source System | Holds the information of source system which is updated from the associated events. |
| Beneficiary | Holds the beneficiary details which is updated from the associated events or input manually from the SWIFT or MX messages |
| Account ID | Holds the account ID corresponding to clearing channels or NOSTRO which is updated from the associated events. |
| Account Name | Holds the account name that represents the clearing channel or NOSTRO which is updated from the associated events. |
| Currency | Holds the currency Code from the associated events or input manually from the SWIFT or MX messages. |
| Amount | Holds the Amount derived from the associated events or input manually from the SWIFT or MX messages. |
| Value Date | Holds the value date derived from the associated events or input manually from the SWIFT or MX messages. |
| Reporting Time | Holds the reporting time details derived from the associated events or input manually. For STP Event creation - If the values are present then the respective values from events are converted to one of the below formats and stored in this field. For Manual creation - The user can enter the time in the specified format. If not present, then the value of Tran Date And Time is converted to one of the below formats and stored in this field. Allowed formats are, . For example, 20240828T12:10 . For example, 20240828T12:10+ or 20240828T12:10-. 20240828T12:10+1. |
| Msg Type | Holds various MT and MX message types for selection from IL.MESSAGE . It cannot be changed by the user when Auto Completion is set to Yes. It is changeable only when Auto Completion is set to No and can be changed only to succeeding messages. MT103/202/pacs.008/pacs.009 (EP) to MT900/camt.054 with debit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with debit indicator(AP) or to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with debit indicator (SP). MT210/camt.057 (ER) to MT910/camt.054 with credit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with credit indicator (AR) or to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator (SR). MT900/camt.054 with debit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with debit indicator (AP) to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with debit indicator (SP). MT910/camt.054 with credit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with credit indicator (AR) to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator (SR). Read the Working with Position Management User Guide for configurations of Transaction Type , Trans Status , Matching Status , and Cash Pos Type for each message. |
| Dealer | Holds dealer information of the associated event records. |
| Product | Holds the product information of the associated event records. |
| Business Unit | Holds the business unit information of the associated event records. |
| Entity | Holds the entity information of the associated event records. |
| Country | Holds the country information of the associated event records. |
| Manual Transaction | Holds a flag value specifying (defaulted by the system) if the transaction was created manually or automatically. Allowed values are, Yes – When the user creates the transaction manually. No – When the system creates the transaction even if events are created manually or automatically. |
| Dr Cr Indic | Holds the debit or credit indication of camt.054, camt.052, camt.053, MT942, MT940, and MT950 messages. |
| Related Reference | In case of auto-updated events, this field holds the value of related reference derived from tag 21 from SWIFT or its equivalent MX message. In case of manual events, the user must input the appropriate reference. |
| Matching Status | Holds the matching status updated by the integrated reconciliation engine for the different lifecycles of a deal. The lookup values are, None - Matching Status is not applicable for Transaction Type . Matched - Underlying Transaction Type is matched by reconciliation engine. Not matched - Underlying Transaction Type is not matched by reconciliation engine. |
| Cash Position Type | Holds the different cash position types from IL.CASH.POS.TYPE . |
| Tran Date and Time | Holds the date and time when the transaction record was created. This field updates the date and time for the first commit stage of the transaction only. |
| Auto Completion | Holds an indicator for transaction completion either by, the system (automatically) or the user (manually). This is based on the operations performed on message type and its related mandatory fields which update the Transaction Type , Trans Status , Matching Status , and Cash Pos Type respectively. This field holds the following values, Yes - The underlying transaction is completed automatically by the system. No - The underlying transaction is manually completed by the user amendment. |
| Matching Key | Holds the logic based on which transaction is updated using IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE . If the system finds an exact match for the matching key in transaction, then the system raises an error. If the system does not find an exact match for matching key in transaction, then a transaction is created or updated accordingly. The format for Matching Key is . |
| Tran Outs Liq Hrs | Holds a flag value indicating the transactions received after end-of-day statement messages (MT940/MT950/camt.053) or after Liq Mon Hrs . The allowed values are Yes and No. It is flagged as yes in following cases. If end-of-day statement is received for the current day, then it considers all transactions (MT900/MT910/camt.054/MT942/camt.052) received after it, until the next day’s opening time of Liq Mon Hrs . If end-of-day statement is not received or received after Liq Mon Hrs , it considers the time frame between Liq Mon Hrs of current and next day. |
| Input Date Time | Holds the date and time for each commit stage of transaction. |

Manual Event amendment is a process of making changes to a manually created event by user after authorisation of the same. To amend a manual event, follow the below steps.

1. Amend Manual .
2. Click the Amend icon corresponding to an event record.

#### 📖 Introduction

Monitoring account balance movements involves tracking the inflows and outflows of funds to maintain accurate records and ensure proper reconciliation of balances.

Here are some key points to understand about the liquidity movements of accounts:

- Transactions : Every transaction, whether a deposit, withdrawal, or transfer, affects the account balances. These are recorded in the bank's ledger.
- Reconciliation : Regular reconciliation is essential to ensure that the account balances match the balances in the statements provided by the correspondent bank. This process helps to identify and resolve discrepancies promptly.
- Currency Fluctuations : Nostro accounts deal with foreign currencies, so exchange rate fluctuations can impact liquidity. Banks need to account for these changes to maintain accurate records.
- Reporting : Banks generate regular reports on the liquidity movements of accounts to provide transparency and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.
- Automation : Many banks use automated systems to track and reconcile account transactions, which reduces errors and improves efficiency.


##### Managing Liquidity Information

The ILM solution provides essential liquidity management information required by a liquidity manager throughout the day. The system is upgraded to capture and store liquidity information in various tables such as Account Daily Balances, Balance Movement Information, and Time-Based Balance Information.

This data is sourced from the ISO15022 statement messages, including MT940 (Customer Statement Message), MT950 (Statement Message), MT941 (Balance Report), MT942 (Interim Transaction Report), or equivalent ISO20022 statement messages such as camt.052 (BankToCustomerAccountReport) and camt.053 (BankToCustomerStatement). These messages are received daily from the Account Servicing Institution according to the bank's Service Level Agreements (SLA) with the nostro correspondent.

#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration options, the system offers to manage the events of intraday liquidity solution.


##### Parameterization

The Liq Mon Hrs field in IL.PARAMETER is used to configure the bank's liquidity monitoring hours by determining the creation time of the first and last records of IL.TIME.BASED.BAL based on configuration. This denotes the start and end times of the intraday position graph in the Liquidity Officer User Agent. Read the Liquidity User Agent User Guide for more information.

The Liq Mon Hrs field should be configured so that the End of Day (EOD) statement is also processed within the liquidity monitoring time period. For example, if a bank has an SLA with its nostro correspondent to receive the EOD statement at 5:00 PM daily, the Liq Mon Hrs field should be configured as X:00 - 5:30 PM, where X:00 represents the opening liquidity hours.

The Time Freq Bal field determines the frequency at which IL.TIME.BASED.BAL records should be created within the configured liquidity monitoring hours. Read the IL.PARAMETER section for more information on the parameterization of intraday liquidity management.


##### Balance Type

The balance information from statements or receipts is important in intraday liquidity management as it allows the bank to understand the liquidity position of the accounts. The IL.BALANCE.TYPE table stores the different balance types used in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table to process incoming statements and reports such as MT940, MT950, MT941, camt.052, and camt.053. Based on these records, the debit or credit balance amounts are classified and updated as opening, intraday, and closing balances in the account daily balances.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Balance Type Description | Holds the description of the balance type. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Temenos has released the configuration data for the IL.BALANCE.TYPE static table. The Intraday Liquidity Management functionality relies on this data.

##### Event to Transaction and Event to Balance Mapping

The IL.EVENT and IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL tables are facilitated with above message-based validations to maintain data integrity. The user can generate or update IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL using events from both manually and through Straight through Processing (STP) in IL.EVENT .

Set the Event Type field to 'Balance' to update the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table.

While creating an event manually, IL.EVENT defaults the Event Type field to 'Transaction'. The user can change the Event Type to 'Balance' to update the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table.

The liquidity events support the following SWIFT messages for updating the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table:

- ISO15022: MT941, MT940, MT950
- ISO20022: camt.052, camt.053

Read the Mapping Event to Transaction section for more information.

##### Account Daily Balances

IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL is a system-updated table that records various balances updated by the incoming statements and reports such as MT940, MT950, MT941, camt.052, and camt.053, based on the IL.BALANCE.TYPE for a given account at a specific date and time in the intraday liquidity management solution.

Effective management of these balances is crucial to ensure that financial institutions can meet their obligations promptly, thereby maintaining stability within the financial system. The table is continuously updated with the current day's data upon receiving relevant statements or reports. Once the COB operations are performed and the statements or reports for the subsequent day start arriving, the previous day's record are replaced with the new balance values. However, the prior record is archived in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL.HIST table.

The below table lists the fields in IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Number | Hold the account ID for which different balances are updated based on the statement message type at a particular time of the day. |
| Currency | Holds the currency of the account for which different balances are updated. |
| Balance Type | Holds different balance types from the records of IL.BALANCE.TYPE . The system updates the balances based on the balance types configured in the IL.MESSAGE table. |
| Opening Balance | Holds the opening balance of the account when the Balance Type field is set as ‘OPE’. |
| Open Bal Entry | Holds the debit or credit indication of the opening balance. |
| Available Balance | Holds the available balance of the account based on the Balance Type with the below logic: Acts as the Closing Available Balance when the message type is MT940/MT950/camt.053 with the Balance Type field set as ‘CLO’. Acts as the Intraday Available Balance when the message type is MT941/camt.052 with the Balance Type field set as ‘INT’. |
| Avail Bal Entry | Holds the debit or credit indication of the Available Balance field based on the Balance Type . |
| Booked Balance | Holds the booked balance of the account based on the Balance Type with the below logic: Acts as the Closing Available Balance when the message type is MT940/MT950/camt.053 with the Balance Type field set as ‘CLO’. Acts as the Intraday Available Balance when the message type is MT941/camt.052 with the Balance Type field set as ‘INT’. |
| Book Bal Entry | Holds the debit or credit indication of the Booked Balance field based on the Balance Type . |
| Statement Message Type | Holds the statement message type that has updated the balances for an account on a particular day. |
| Statement Number | Holds the statement-sequence number of the message type that has updated the balances. |
| Statement Time Stamp | Holds the time stamp of the statement message type that has updated the balances at a given time. |
| Event Reference Number | Holds the latest IL.EVENT record Id that has updated the balances for an account on a particular day. |

The below screen shows the fields in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table.


##### Balance Movements

Regularly monitoring balance movements can detect unauthorised transactions and reduce fraud risk. Reconciling account balances with external statements (bank statements) helps identify discrepancies and maintain financial record integrity.

IL.BALANCE.MVMT is a system updated table that stores the total debit and credit entries along with balance movements for a given account on a particular date and time for the intraday liquidity management solution. It includes additional details such as actual balance, intraday balance, closing balance, and suspense balances.

The feed for the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table is from the IL.TRANSACTION table for the following message types:

- MT900
- MT910
- MT942
- camt.054
- camt.052

The feed for the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table is also from IL.TRANSACTION with the following message types only when Trans Status is updated as 'Statement not matched'.

- MT940
- MT950
- camt.053

The table also receives updates from IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL when statement balances are updated through the following message types:

- MT940
- MT950
- MT941
- camt.053
- camt.052

Records received for the current day are stored in this table. When COB is performed and balances or transactions for the next day are received, the previous record is replaced by a new record. The previous day's record is then moved to the IL.BALANCE.MVMT.HIST table.

The below table lists the fields in IL.BALANCE.MVMT .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Number | Holds the account ID for which the debit and credit movements are updated on a particular date. |
| Currency | Holds the currency of the account for which the credit and debit movements are updated on a particular date. |
| Opening Balance | Holds the opening balance of the account on a particular day. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Adj Act Bal value of the previous day record in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field as zero. This field is also updated when MT940/MT950/camt.053/MT941/camt.052 messages are received for the current day. |
| Ttl Credit Mvmt | Holds the sum of the total credit amount of an account during the day. |
| Ttl Credit Entries | Holds the total number of credit entries updated from IL.TRANSACTION with the following message types and the transaction status set as SN (Statement Not matched) received for the day: MT910 or camt.054 with credit indicator MT942 with credit indicator MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator |
| Ttl Debit Mvmt | Holds the sum of the total debit amount of an account during the day. |
| Ttl Debit Entries | Holds the total number of debit entries from IL.TRANSACTION with the following message types and the transaction status set as SN (Statement Not matched) received for the day: MT910 or camt.054 with Debit indicator MT942 with Debit indicator MT940/MT950/camt.053 with Debit indicator |
| Ttl Actual Balance | Holds the actual balance of the account at a particular time in the day. |
| Intraday Balance | Holds the latest intraday balance updated through statement messages on a particular day. |
| Intra Bal Time | Holds the time at which the latest intraday balance is updated through the statement messages on a particular day. |
| Susp Intra Bal | Holds the difference in balance, after the intraday balance information is received through statement messages (MT941 or camt.052). This field is updates in the below sequence: For first intraday hit the Susp Intra Bal is the difference between the Intraday Balance and Ttl Actual Balance fields. For remaining instances of nth intraday hit, all the Susp Act Bal fields (n-1,n-2… multivalue) are first calculated. Susp Intra Bal for the nth instance is then calculated as a difference between the Intraday Balance at the nth instance and the SusP Act Bal (n-1 multivalue). Susp Intra Bal (n-1,n-2,… multivalues )are maintained the same for multiple instances of the intraday hit. |
| Susp Act Bal | Holds the value after adjusting the total actual balance with the suspense intraday balance and the suspense EOD balance at a particular time in the day. |
| Susp Open Bal | Holds the difference between the opening balance updated through the statement message (MT950, MT940, or camt.053) and the calculated opening balance for the current day. |
| Net Bal Diff | Holds the net balance difference based on the number of intraday statement hits and EOD hit at a particular time of the day. |
| Adj Act Bal | Holds the latest values from the nth multivalue of the Susp Act Bal field at a particular time of the day. |
| Transaction ID | Holds the latest IL.TRANSACTION ID reference that has updated the balances for an account at a particular time of the day. |
| Time Indication | Holds the time indication information that was updated in IL.TRANSACTION for the following message types: MT900, MT910, or camt.054 with debit-credit indicator MT942, camt.052 with debit-credit indicator MT940, MT950, camt.053 with debit-credit indicator |
| Closing Booked Bal | Holds the closing balance of an account on a particular day updated through the statement messages (MT940, MT950, and camt.053). |
| Susp EOD Bal | Holds the difference in the balance after the EOD balance information is received through statement messages (MT940, MT950, or camt.053). This field is updated in the below sequence: All the Susp Act Bal (n-1,n-2… multivalue) fields are calculated. Once the Susp Act Bal is calculated the Susp EOD Bal is calculated using the below formula, The nth Susp Act Bal multivalue field is calculated based on the EOD statement hit. |
| EOD Bal Time | Holds the time at which the EOD balance was updated through the statement messages (MT940, MT950, or camt.053) on a particular day. |

The below screen shows the fields in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table.


##### Time Based Balances

Understanding how balances change over time provides valuable insights into the financial health of a business, aiding in the identification of trends and the making of informed decisions. Monitoring time-based balance movements is crucial for effective cash flow management, ensuring sufficient funds to meet obligations and invest in opportunities. Accurate tracking and reporting of balance movements are essential for compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements.

The IL.TIME.BASED.BAL table is an updated system table that records all debit and credit movements for a given account within specific time periods throughout the day, as part of the intraday liquidity management solution.

The number of records generated in this table corresponds to the time period or frequency configured in IL.PARAMETER . The IL.TIME.BASED.BAL table feeds data from the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table by consolidating the transactions based on the time bands configured in IL.PARAMETER . This table consistently stores records for the current day when balance or transaction hits are received. Upon running COB and receiving the subsequent day's balance or transaction data, the previous day's records are purged, and new records are created for the current day based on balance and transaction hits recorded in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. The below chart illustrates the activities under IL.EVENT .

The below table lists the fields in IL.TIME.BASED.BAL .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Number | Holds the account ID for which the debit and credit movements are updated at a particular time period based on the frequency set in IL.PARAMETER . |
| Currency | Holds the currency of the account for which the credit and debit movements are updated. |
| Time Band | Updates the time at which the record is created based on parameter setup on time interval. |
| Opening Balance | Holds the opening balance of the account on a particular day. |
| Intraday Balance | Holds the latest intraday balance updated through the statement messages on a particular day. |
| Pre Time Act Balance | Holds the actual balance of the previous record created at a particular time period. |
| Ttl Credit Amount | Holds the sum of the total credit amount of an account during the day within the time band. |
| Ttl Debit Amount | Holds the sum of the total debit amount of an account during the day within the time band. |
| Susp Act Bal | Holds the actual balance after adjusting the value with the suspense intraday balance within the time band. |
| Ttl Actual Balance | Holds the actual balance of the account at a particular time band in a day. The value for the Ttl Act Bal field is fetched from Susp Act Bal until the record for which the intraday nth hit is recorded at the first instance. From the second instance, the value is the difference between the Susp Act Bal and Susp Intra Bal nth multivalue field values, until the record for which the intraday n+1th hit is recorded at the first instance. |
| Transaction ID | Holds the latest IL.TRANSACTION record Id that has updated the balances for an account at a particular time within the time band. |
| Time Indication | Holds the time indication information that was updated in IL.TRANSACTION for the following message types within the time band: MT900, MT910, or camt.054 with debit-credit indicator MT942 or camt.052 with debit-credit indicator MT940, MT950, or camt.053 with debit-credit indicator |
| Susp Open Bal | Holds the difference between the opening balance updated through the statement message (MT941, MT950, MT940, camt.052, or camt.053) and the calculated opening balance for the current day. |
| Susp Intra Bal.1 | Defaults the value from the Susp Intra Bal field of IL.BALANCE.MVMT whenever there is an intraday hit. |
| Intra Bal Time 1 | Holds the time at which the latest intraday balance is updated through the statement messages on a particular day. |
| Adj Act Bal | Holds the precise actual balance after adjusting the value with the suspense intraday balance and the suspense end of day balance within the time band. |
| Susp EOD Bal | Holds the difference in balance after the EOD balance information is received through the statement messages (MT940, MT950, or camt.053). |
| EOD Bal Time | Holds the time at which the EOD balance was updated through the statement messages on a particular day. |
| Closing Booked Bal | Holds the closing balance of the account updated through the statement messages (MT940,MT950, and camt.053) on a particular day. |

#### 📖 Introduction

Liquidity Monitoring involves detailed analysis of the size and timing of payment inflow and outflow. An institution must have a system in place which has the capacity to measure the expected gross liquidity inflows and outflows, anticipate the intraday timing of these flows wherever possible, and forecast the range of potential net funding shortfalls that might arise at different points during the day.

Intraday liquidity management is a key element of the bank’s overall liquidity management framework, ensuring efficient control and optimization of the available funds throughout the trading day. Its primary aim is to ensure that a bank has adequate liquidity to meet short-term payment obligations and respond to unforeseen financial demands, essential for financial stability, regulatory compliance, and seamless transaction processing.

Regulatory frameworks such as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), require banks to implement monitoring tools for intraday liquidity management. These tools provide quantitative measures and controls, including compliance with obligations such as:

- Monitoring the real-time cash position across accounts and currencies to meet payment and settlement obligations.
- Managing and reporting the liquidity position across branches, business units, and legal entities.
- Building historical information to support intraday liquidity modeling, liquidity forecasting, and liquidity risk analytics.

The Liquidity Officer (LQUSER1) User Agent, developed using the Temenos Explorer framework, is designed to address the needs of international treasury operations in a modern banking environment. This monitoring tool ensures that the bank maintains sufficient liquidity positions for nostro accounts, enabling seamless customer services while minimising costs, mitigating risks, and adhering to regulatory requirements.

Read the Liquidity Officer User Agent guide for more information on the components of the Liquidity UA.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Read the Configuring Liquidity Management section for more information on configuring liquidity monitoring.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how the Liquidity Officer UA feeds data for the Intraday Positions, Projections, and Cashflow screens. Read the Liquidity User Agent User Guide for more information on the components of Liquidity User Agent.


##### Intraday Positions

Intraday liquidity refers to the availability of funds required by a financial institution to meet its obligations during a single trading day. It is crucial in banking and financial markets to ensure a seamless functioning of the payment and settlement processes.

The Intraday Positions screen displays the real-time intraday positions of a nostro account within the liquidity monitoring hours in a line graph format as shown below.

The recorded line series in this screen is based on the records from the IL.TIMEBASED.BAL table, updated according to the frequency configured in the Time Freq Bal and Liq Mon Hrs fields in IL.PARAMETER for an account in a day. Read the Time Based Balance section for more information on the function of IL.TIMEBASED.BAL table.


##### Projections

Liquidity cash flow projections forecast an organization’s cash inflows and outflows over a specific period to ensure adequate liquidity for meeting obligations and managing financial risks. These projections help in planning, identifying potential cash shortfalls, and optimizing the use of surplus funds.

The Projections screen provides the liquidity officer with the options to project that day’s positions and transaction details within the monitoring hours as shown below.

The feed for the bar graph in projection screen is from the IL.API.CASH.POS.SUM.1.0.0 enquiry, which calculates the projected liquidity of a particular account for each day using the below formula.

Where,

- Actual cash position is the summation of the transaction amounts in the IL.TRANSACTION records for which the Cash Pos Type field is updated as ‘Actual’.
- Expected cash position is the summation of the transaction amounts in the IL.TRANSACTION records for which Cash Pos Type field is updated as ‘Expected’.
- Opening balance is the projected liquidity position for the previous day.

> **⚠️ Note:** Only the projected liquidity calculated for the current day has its opening balance value fetched from the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table either from the current day record’s Opening Balance field or the previous day record’s Closing Balance field based on availability.

The feed for table in the Projections screen is from the IL.TRANSACTION table which contains the transaction details while the closing balance value corresponds to the projected liquidity position for a particular day.

Read the Transaction section for more information on the functions of the IL.TRANSACTION table.


##### Cash Flow by Account

The Cash Flow By Account screen displays the details of the cash flow movements for the selected account. The user can view the cashflows of an account for today (T) or the day before (T-1) as shown below.

The feed for the table in the Cash Flow By Account screen is from the IL.API.CASHFLOW.ACCOUNT.1.0.0 enquiry, which fetches the transaction details from IL.TRANSACTION and the closing balance details from IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL for a particular account.


##### Cash Flow by Currency

The Cash Flow By Currency screen displays the details of the cash flow movements for the selected currency. It also displays a table that contains the account-wise cash movements for the selected currency. The user can view the cashflows of a currency for today (T) or the day before (T-1) as shown below.

The feed for the table in the Cash Flow By Currency screen is from the IL.API.BALANCE.MVMT.1.0.0 enquiry, which fetches the balance movement details for a particular account. The feed for bar chart is from the IL.API.CASHFLOW.CURRENCY.1.0.0 enquiry, which consolidates the balance movements of the accounts based on different currencies.


##### Cash Flow by Country

The Cash Flow By Country screen displays the details of the consolidated cash flow movements for all the accounts in different currencies. The amounts are converted based on the exchange rate of valuation currency selected by the user from the Valuation Currency drop-down. The user can view the cashflows of a country for today (T) or the day before (T-1). This screen has two views - chart and table. The chart view is the default option.

Below is the chart view of Cash Flow By Country screen.

Below is the table view of the Cash Flow By Country screen.

The feed for the table or chart in this screen is from the IL.API.CASHFLOW.CURRENCY.1.0.0 enquiry, which fetches the balance movement details for a particular account and converts it based on the exchange rate with the selected valuation currency. The total balances widget summates the converted balance values for different currencies against the selected valuation currency.

#### 📖 Introduction

Following the failure of many banks to adequately measure, manage, and control their liquidity risk in September 2008, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) issued its Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (the Sound Principles). These guidelines provide banks with best practices for managing liquidity risk and collateral. Principle 8 of the Sound Principles specifically addresses intraday liquidity risk, stating:

“A bank should actively manage its intraday liquidity positions and risks to meet payment and settlement obligations on a timely basis under both normal and stressed conditions and thus contribute to the smooth functioning of payment and settlement systems”

Intraday liquidity management plays a crucial role in banking operations, ensuring the efficient control and optimisation of available funds throughout the trading day. As the demand for instant payments increases, the response from financial institutions, particularly Treasury, must be swift and effective. The regulatory pressure, lessons learned from recent bank failures, and the need to optimise liquidity buffers have made intraday liquidity management a critical element in modern banking.


##### ILM in Transact

The Intraday Liquidity Management (ILM) module in Transact is designed to support Treasury liquidity operations, focusing on the efficient control and optimisation of available funds throughout the trading day. It offers a comprehensive liquidity management solution with the primary aim to ensure a bank has adequate liquidity to meet short-term payment obligations and proactively respond to unforeseen financial demands. Thereby it enhances financial stability, regulatory compliance, and seamless transaction processing.

This module features a sophisticated and user-friendly Liquidity User Agent, offering a smarter and more intuitive approach to managing liquidity insights. With customizable views, the user can:

- Switch between split and full-screen modes for easy access to the key liquidity information.
- Personalise the display by showing or hiding columns and applying smart filters, allowing them to focus on the most relevant data.
- Drill down to view the actual cashflows contributing to the liquidity position on a particular day.

This feature helps banks monitor and control their overall liquidity positions in real-time, ensuring efficient control and management of multi-currency liquidity assets across the nostro accounts. The system also forecasts the projected liquidity based on the expected and actual cash positions. The user agent can be seamlessly integrated with an existing third-party system.

The intended audience of this module are as follows:

| Role | Function |
|---|---|
| Liquidity Officer | Manages the organization’s liquidity position, ensuring that it has enough cash and easily liquidated assets to meet its short-term obligations |
| IT Personnel of the bank or financial institution | Maintains computing infrastructure and upgrades of computer applications |


##### Product Configuration

This section explains the configurations required to set up the ILM system.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Days Post Value Date | Holds the number of days after the value date for an Event and Transaction to be removed from the live IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION tables and to be written to the respective history files. |
| Event Version | Specifies the valid IL.EVENT version. The user can define the IL.EVENT version using which the automatic event records are created. |
| OFS Source Event | The OFS.SOURCE ID present in this field is used to create events automatically from the messages. |
| Transaction Version | Specifies the valid IL.TRANSACTION version. The user can define the IL.TRANSACTION version using which the automatic transaction records are created or updated. |
| Liq Mon Hrs | Based on the value configured here, the first and last records of IL.TIME.BASED.BAL are created which denotes the start and end time of the intraday position graph. . It should be configured in such a way that EOD statement is also processed within the time period. Consider a bank that has an SLA with its nostro correspondent to receive the EOD statement at YY:MM Hrs on a daily basis. This field should be configured as XX:MM - ZZ:MM, where XX:MM are the opening liquidity hours and ZZ:MM are the closing liquidity hours which should be greater than receiving time of the EOD statement (YY:MM) Hrs. |
| Time Freq Bal | Specifies the frequency in which IL.TIME.BASED.BAL records should be created within the Liq Mon Hrs configured. |
| Ext Reconciliation | Specifies if the intraday liquidity system is integrated with an external reconciliation engine. Allowed values are Yes and No . |
| Mode | Specifies the mode of Intraday Liquidity Management. Allowed values are: Standalone: The Intraday Liquidity solution is integrated with an external payment system, liquidity management system, or treasury management system which acts as the source system. Embedded: The Intraday Liquidity solution is integrated with the in-house Temenos payment system and other modules of Temenos which act as the source system. The system currently supports only the Embedded mode. |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| GB Entity Description | Specifies the number of days after the value date, for the event and transaction to be removed from the live IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION tables and written to the respective history file. |
| Entity Name | Holds the name of the entity. |
| Geo Block | Holds the geographic block of the entity. |
| Base Currency | Holds the local currency of the entity in ISO currency code. |
| Country | Holds the country code of the entity. |
| Entity BIC | Holds the BIC of the entity which is then used in the SWIFT messages. |
| Master Entity | Indicates if the entity is the master entity where the consolidated liquidity is monitored. Only one master entity is allowed. |
| Parent Entity | Specifies the parent entity to which the liquidity is consolidated. This establishes the parent-child hierarchy of the entities. |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Description | Holds the description of the nostro account. |
| Account Name | Specifies the name of the nostro account. |
| Balance Rollover | Defines whether the closing balance of the account will be rolled over to the next day. Allowed values are: Y: The system rolls over the closing balance of the current day as the opening balance for the next day during COB processing. N: The system does not rollover the closing balance of the current day as the opening balance for the next day. Instead, it takes zero as the opening balance during COB processing until the system receives the account statement message (from an account servicing institution) to pick the opening balance. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table with the Adj Act Bal value of the previous day record in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field as zero in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. |
| Correspondent BIC | Holds the BIC of the correspondent or the account servicing institution which is required mainly for account lookup during SWIFT message processing. |
| Correspondent Name | Specifies the name of the correspondent bank or the account servicing institution. |
| Currency | Holds the ISO currency code of the account record involved in transactions. |
| Display Name | Holds the display name of the nostro account. |
| Entity | Indicates the entity in which the account record is created. |
| External Account number | Indicates the actual account number assigned to the account owner by the account servicing institution. The account ID can be in IBAN or non-IBAN account format. The system uses this ID to identify or lookup the account during SWIFT or MX message processing. |
| Primary Nostro | Indicates if the account created or used is considered as the primary nostro. |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Srcsys Name | Holds the name of the source system. |
| GB Srcsys Description | Holds the description of the source system. |
| Output Channel | Holds the output channel that would be referred while importing the messages from TPH. This is a dropdown field. |
| Direction | Holds the direction of the message which is intended to be imported from TPH to IL solution. Allowed values are: O - Outgoing I - Incoming R – Redirect B - Book |
| Message Type | Holds various MT and MX message types for selection from the IL.MESSAGE . This is a dropdown field. |


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level specifications required for ILM.

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| IL.PARAMETER | The IL.PARAMETER table defines the rules by which the ILM system operates allowing the users to pass through a stored procedure with a single parameter table. This is achieved without modifying the underlying code by having complex business logic within a single routine, making it easier to manage and execute. The configurations done here are used in the downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT , IL.TRANSACTION , IL.BALANCE.MVMT , and IL.TIME.BASED.BAL for processing the liquidity positions and balances based on the accounts. |
| IL.ENTITY | The IL.ENTITY table stores details of the entities which refers to a distinct unit that has its own legal and operational identity to perform the business functions for liquidity monitoring. It also allows the user to set up parent-child entity relationships, which are used to represent the hierarchical structures of the bank. This helps in monitoring the liquidity at an individual level or the overall liquidity at a lead entity level within the liquidity management solution. The entity configured here is used in downstream static tables like IL.ACCOUNT and IL.BUSINESS.UNIT , along with the dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity based on the entity. |
| IL.ACCOUNT | The IL.ACCOUNT table contains the nostro accounts for which intraday liquidity is to be monitored. Liquidity management in nostro accounts involves ensuring there are sufficient funds available to meet the bank's transaction needs. This requires careful monitoring of receipts, payments, and obligations to avoid overdrafts and optimize cash flow. Effective liquidity management helps banks maintain appropriate balances and improve their overall capital management framework. The accounts configured here are used in downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity positions and balances based on the accounts. |
| IL.SOURCESYS | A source system is an authoritative data source where core data elements are maintained and cash flow transactions originate. It relays all the liquidity-related SWIFT messages to Transact for processing it within the intraday liquidity solution. This solution is integrated with in-house modules such as TPH , DE , and EB.FILE.UPLOAD which acts as the source system and has the ability to integrate with any external source system to process the liquidity-related SWIFT messages. The source system configured here is used in downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity based on the source system. |

The below table lists the products of the Intra Day Liquidity Management module.

Hence, the ILM solution subscribes to such events and processes them in near real-time. An event can be created manually or automatically through STP. |
| Liquidity Transaction | A liquidity transaction contains the details generated through different events, such as receipts, payments, statements, and SWIFT messages from a source system for various entities in a liquidity management solution.​ A Transaction can be created manually or automatically through STP.​ It can also be automatically matched or manually matched by the user. Event to Transaction is a many-to-one relation. |
| Liquidity Balance Movements | Liquidity Balance Movements represent the Opening Balances, Intraday Balances, and Closing Balances on the account. Wherever possible, the balance movements are generated automatically from the bank's source systems such as the Core Banking System, Ledger Systems, Payment Hubs, and Treasury Management Systems. |

#### 📖 Introduction

A bank's liquidity position refers to the cash and cash equivalents it holds at a given time. This is crucial to meet short-term obligations and smooth operation. Key points about the cash positions in a bank include:

- Banks monitor their liquidity (often daily) ensuring they have enough liquidity to manage the cash inflows and outflows, and to adjust their holdings of liquidity assets accordingly.
- Regulatory authorities require banks to maintain a minimum liquidity level to meet the withdrawal demands and other short-term obligations.
- Effective cash flow management forecasts future needs and ensures sufficient liquid assets are available, considering unexpected events.
- Liquidity cash positions reflect expected, actual, and projected cash balances from the cash flow transactions. ILM is designed to integrate with the external reconciliation systems to compute accurate liquidity positions.

##### Transaction Mapping Rule

Maintaining a strong liquidity position is crucial for a bank's financial health, ensuring it can cover immediate liabilities like customer withdrawals and operational expenses.

The IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE table stores rule mappings for cash position aggregation in the intraday liquidity management system. These rules update the Cash Position Type , Trans Status , Matching Status , and Transaction Types in the downstream dynamic IL.TRANSACTION table.

The below table lists the fields in IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE .

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| GB Description | Holds the description of IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE . |
| Cash Position Type | Stores the different cash position types from the IL.CASH.POS.TYPE table. |
| Compared with 1.1 | Stores the different transaction types from the IL.TRANSACTION.TYPE table that must be compared with the record created in this table. |
| Operand 1.1 | Holds the operand used for mapping in this table. |
| Transaction Status.1.1 | Stores the transaction status from the IL.TRANSSTATUS table. |
| Matching Status.1.1 | Holds the matching status updated by the integrated reconciliation engine for different life cycles of a deal. |

The below screen shows the fields in the IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE table.

> **⚠️ Note:** The configuration data for the IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE static table are released by Temenos, and the functionality of the Intraday Liquidity Management depends on this data.


#### 🔧 Working With

Events serve as the entry point into the ILM boundary. The comparison in the ILM Boundary is based on the following metrics:

- Transaction type
- Value Date
- Amount
- Currency
- Common Ref No

The Matching Key field determines the logic for updating a IL.TRANSACTION using IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE .

- If the system finds an exact match for the matching key in IL.TRANSACTION , the IL.EVENT is marked as not processed.
- If the system does not find an exact match for the matching key in IL.TRANSACTION , the IL.EVENT is marked as processed, and a transaction is updated or created accordingly.

The format for the matching key is: TransType*TransRefNo*Ccy*Amount*ValueDate.

The below screenshot shows the Mapping Key formed in the IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION tables.

The following statuses and types are updated in a transaction based on IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE :

- Matching Status
- Transaction Type
- Transaction Status
- Message Types
- Cash Position Type (only in IL.TRANSACTION )

The IL.MESSAGE table includes records that are released with the corresponding transaction types and balance types configured.

The ILM solution includes the below comparison logic within IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE that uses comparison metrics to create a matching key.

Based on the intraday liquidity management logic, the cash position type is updated to ‘Actuals’ or ‘Expected’. These cash position types are used to calculate the cash position summary and projected liquidity for a day, enabling the Liquidity UA to monitor the overall liquidity.

The below screenshot illustrates the liquidity workflow for receipts by updating the cash positions in ILM.

The below screenshot illustrates the liquidity workflow for payments by updating the cash positions in ILM.
