### 4.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is designed to meet the needs of dealing operations in the Foreign Exchange Market.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cus Margin Default*, *FX Commission Group ID*, *FX Group Cond ID*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Foreign Exchange (FX) module is designed to meet the needs of dealing operations in the Foreign Exchange Market.

The module offers comprehensive treasury solution starting from the deal capture in the front office to deal processing in back office, covering a wide range of FX products. The module covers entire deal life cycle of FX transactions including features such as recording of limited orders, online limit checking, position updating, revaluation of positions, accounting, brokerage, generation of SWIFT confirmations, payments and print advices. In addition, the module also helps generate reports for audit and risk management.

The above image illustrates spot, forward and swap deal types and its associated transaction types supported by the system, which caters to the business needs of Treasury.

Using FX module, a dealer can directly input a deal in the system with key elements, such as currencies, amount, rate, value date and counter-party. This avoids the need for hand-written deal tickets and ensures the real-time update of positions and risk, that is, counterparty’s liability or exposure, exchange position and daily foreign exchange movements reflects the dealer’s system inputted deal.

All elements of FX transactions have default values, except the key information that the dealer provides. Thus, for any given counterparty, payment methods and instructions are loaded automatically from user definable tables. If required, the back office user can confirm or exceptionally amend the deals.

The ability to arrive at intelligent defaults also has another benefit. For example, in a swap, all the default information on the second leg is derived from the first leg. Thus, dealer’s input of information is reduced to the minimum.

After the dealer provides their inputs, the deal slips are printed for the back-office. At the authorisation stage, the system invokes the following:

- Generating and delivering confirmations
- Passing any accounting entries such as brokerage, commissions and charges, and issue of any required pay or receive instructions

Otherwise, there are overnight processes that involve eventual settlement, revaluation and accruals, and exception or maturity reporting.

The FX application is supplied with initial input of the contract details with a few of them requiring any changes during remaining life cycle. Such changes, if any, are generally limited to settlement related. The brokerage calculation and processing of brokerage is handled by using BROKER application.


##### Product Configuration

This section describes the configuration options the system offers in FX.


##### FX Build Sequence

Implementation of FX module begins with configuration of various parameter tables.

The following list of files are required for FX main setup, and the mandatory files are suffixed with an *. The dependency tables are marked and stated alongside the parameter tables in their build sequence.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters consists of the following:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX.PARAMETERS | The rules that determined the Foreign Exchange (FX) transactions are defined in the following files: Classifies spot and forward contracts, according to local central bank and internal reporting rules. Defines the spot default value date. Uses the OFS.SOURCE ID present in this field to perform FX.BULK.ORDER . Uses the version ID present in this field as VERSION to populate or create FX BULK DEAL master records. Defines default category code for spot, forward and swap transactions. Defines the precious metal currency codes, hence, any number of currency codes can be defined. Conditions under which deals are entered with split value dates. Indicators show if Profit & Loss (P&L) and EXCHADS entries are booked when revaluation of forward and spot contracts takes place. Creates rounding rule for transactions. The Cus Margin Default field determines if the FX Group Cond ID corresponding to a customer is defined in a FX contract or not (subjected to the existence of the condition priority setup in FX margin). The values accepted are Yes, No and None. If set as Yes, the FX Group Cond ID defaults from SEC.ACC.MASTER ( SAM ). If it is not available in SAM , it defaults from CUSTOMER.CHARGE . If set as No or None, the FX Group Cond ID does not default from SAM or CUSTOMER.CHARGE . However, the user can still define the margin percentage manually (together with treasury rate) and derive the customer rate in FX deal. |
| 2 | FX.POS.TYPE | Assigns profit centre to the trading position, which can be amended as desired. |
| 3 | FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE | Classifies the deal types. A record in this application can control the default value for category codes, revaluation types, and allows delivery and types of options processing. The existing records can be amended and new records can be created. |
| 4 | FX.GEN.CONDITION | Identifies a specific group of customers, which can be cross-related to the group condition table, to define conditions applicable to that group. The groups are determined based on customer details such as sector and target. The criteria used and their priority are specified in the Condition Priority file in the record whose ID is FX.MARGIN. |
| 5 | FX.GROUP.CONDITION | Defines the spread or margin percentage for a specific customer, group of customers or default group. When a group customer is defined, the FX Gen Condition record needs to exist before any associated group condition is specified. For an individual customer, the ID is C , whereas, the default group ID is generally assigned as either 99 or 999. |
| 6 | FX.COMM.GROUP | Defines spread or margin based on currency, and the amount that falls in a range and is used in FX contracts. The FX Commission Group ID field in SAM is used in FX.BULK.ORDER application, and a reference to SAM is used in FX.GROUP.CONDITION . Hence, the margin is given in absolute terms or referred to FX Commission Group ID (based on which the margin is applied in an FX deal). |


##### Illustrating Model Products

The following products are available in the FX module:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX Spot | FX Spot is a contract of buying or selling a currency, commodity or security for immediate settlement (payment and delivery) on the spot date at a spot Rprice. |
| 2 | FX Forward | FX Forward is a contract of buying and selling an asset or a currency at a predetermined spot rate at a specified date in the future (which is greater than the spot date). The predetermined rate is called as the Forward Rate. |
| 3 | FX Swap | FX Swap is an agreement between counterparties to exchange currency. The agreement involves swapping of principal and interest payments between two different currencies. |
| 4 | Precious Metal Deal | Precious Metal Deals involve trading in various precious metals such as gold, silver, palladium, platinum and so on, in spot, forward or swap rates depending on the types of deals entered. |
| 5 | Single-rate Option | Single-Rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two specified dates at customer’s choice without incurring any penalty cost. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. |
| 6 | Multi-rate Option | Multi-rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two different option dates with different rates. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. In this, the applied rate depends on the period delivery. |
| 7 | Internal Deals | Internal Deals allow transfers between different positions or dealer desks. Hence, there is no need for accounting entries, payments, advices and so on. The system automatically updates the position, when an internal forex spot or a forward deal is entered. |
| 8 | Broker Deal | Broker Deals are entered when the counterparty is not known. The user needs to enter BR as sub-type and associated brokers deals. Once the counterparty name is known, BR is removed and the counterparty details are entered in the deal. |
| 9 | NDF Vanilla Deal | Non Deliverable Forward (NDF) Vanilla Deals is an hedging strategy, where parties in the contract agree to settle the profit or loss prior to the expiration date of the contract. A vanilla NDF transaction has an agreed rate fixing date, which is two working days before the settlement date. |
| 10 | NDF Exotic Deal | An Exotic NDF Deal allows in setting the fixing date as any date before the vanilla date in the tenure of the transaction. The fixing profit is discounted, if the NDF is fixed and settled early. The discount amount is amortised from the settlement date to the value date of the NDF. |

### 4.2  Backvalue and Prematured Contracts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Money Market (MM) module supports premature and back-value dated maturity to the contracts. The maturity date of the MM deal can be changed to the current date (today) or back value date. The processing of deal is through a service, instead of waiting for Close of Business (COB) processing.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Matured Online*, *Maturity Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Money Market (MM) module supports premature and back-value dated maturity to the contracts. The maturity date of the MM deal can be changed to the current date (today) or back value date. The processing of deal is through a service, instead of waiting for Close of Business (COB) processing.


#### 🔧 Working With

A fully back valued contract has both value date and maturity date less than today (that is, less than the system date). In premature contracts, the user changes the original maturity date to an early date including a back date. If the user inputs a deal with a Maturity Date as today or yesterday (that is, a fully back valued deal), or changes the Maturity Date of an existing deal to a date that is today or yesterday (that is, a premature deal), the system sets the Matured Online field to Yes. The deal is then processed within the day (online), instead of Close of Business (If the TSA.SERVICE for MM.ONLINE.MATURITY is running as described in MM services). This denotes the accounting entries, accruals and interest payments are created within the day, instead of at Close of Business (COB).

Temenos Transact calculates the interest payable or receivable on the contract, and credit or debit of relevant customer and PL accounts. This denotes the funds that are credited or debited from customer accounts are available the same day. If funds are not available, the system generates appropriate records in the PD.PAYMENT.DUE application, which takes the responsibility for the past due payment. In premature contracts, adjustments to the accrual and interest amounts are made to cancel accruals from the new maturity date to today.

All general ledger movements are posted to the Central Reporting Base (CRB) at the end of the day. The LIMIT updates are made within the day. Although, fully back valued deals do not affect revolving limits, the deal principal is deducted from non-revolving limits (wherever appropriate). In regards to Delivery for fully back valued contracts, Temenos Transact does not make automatic payments (that is, there are no MT102/202/210 SWIFT messages). The bank needs to take care of the delivery of fully back valued deals manually. For premature contracts, Temenos Transact makes SWIFT payments as usual.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Back Value and Premature Contracts feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Back Value and Premature Contracts feature.

### 4.4  Call Notice Taking Deal Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Call or notice taking is a contract with maturity on Call or a Notice term. Maturity is 0 days for a call and notice but can be 1 to 14 days (however, the system allows up to 999 days). The rate of interest can be fixed or floating, and the interest can be liquidated or deferred on the due date. Pri...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Contract Type*, *Counterparty*, *Interest Rate*, *Mature*, *Mature at*, *Mature at SOD*, *Negative Interest*, *OD* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Call or notice taking is a contract with maturity on Call or a Notice term. Maturity is 0 days for a call and notice but can be 1 to 14 days (however, the system allows up to 999 days). The rate of interest can be fixed or floating, and the interest can be liquidated or deferred on the due date. Principal repayment can be bullet or partial. Rollover is not allowed on call or notice contracts. However, the rollover functionality is used to record a change in the interest rate (fixed) from a date that coincides with the interest due date.


#### 🔧 Working With

Apart from the maturity terms and interest related processing, the functionality between fixed maturity taking deals and call or notice taking deals, almost remains the same. The illustration below explains how call or notice taking are inputted using fixed or floating interest rate. A call or notice contract eventually converts into a fixed maturity contract on fixing the maturity date.

The interest rate types handled within the module are fixed, floating and none. When fixed interest rate is static throughout the life of the contract or for a given interest period, floating rate varies throughout the life of the contract. The type ‘None’ denotes the contract does not have an interest rate, which is the case with Sundry payable or receivable type of contracts.

Fixed rate of interest is keyed in manually or defaulted from Periodic Interest rate key while applying a spread.

The module supports both positive and negative rates of interest.

- To use negative interest rate, the Negative Interest field in MM is set to Yes. This does not allow the users to input the fields related to tax and liquidation mode. Negative interest capitalisation is allowed for Money Market (MM) contracts.
- In the absence of negative interest rate field set to Yes, if the floating rate moves into negative territory during the course of contract life time, system considers the interest rate as zero.

The MM supports various accrual methods, such as First Day, Last Day and Both:

- In the First Day accrual method (default), the accrual is performed on the first day of the value date of the contract.
- In the Last Day accrual method, the last day of the interest period is considered for accrual while, skipping the first day in the interest calculation period.
- Both day accrual denotes one-day additional accrual, asboth first and last day are included in the accrual.

To know more, refer to the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table.

The MM module provides an alert in the form of an override message to prevent any incorrect interest rate keyed in capturing the deal. The inputted interest rate is verified against the Periodic Interest rate key 01 of the respective currency as part of the check. If the variance is greater than the given percentage in PERIODIC.INTEREST rate table or as mentioned in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS (if the former is not available), the system performs a tolerance check and raises an override message.

Spread refers to the basis points either added or subtracted to or from the floating or periodic rate of interest to arrive at the contract rate. When the given spread needs to be subtracted a minus sign precedes the value given.

The example below illustrates the way how all or notice takings are inputted using fixed and floating interest rate.

The Interest Spread is included in the fixed interest rate during the e input of Interest Rate field and the Spread is not separately updated. However, if the interest rate is fetched from a PI key it is possible to add or subtract a spread from it.

The Mature at SOD field on MM.MONEY.MARKET stands for mature MM deals at the SOD. MM deals can be matured at the start of the day, so the customer has access to the funds from a deposit and can avail a loan at the start of the day maturity.

This field can store one of the following values:

- ‘Yes’ for the maturity of the deals at the SOD processing
- ‘No’ for the maturity of the deals to be executed at the Close of Business.

There are two ways to apply value in this field:

- In the first way, the user picks a category code. The MM routine uses this category code to read the value of Mature a t S OD field in the LMM.ADVICES parameter file.
- In the second way, the user can override this value by selecting or inputting a Yes or No within the transaction as shown below:

Maturity will be 0 days for a call, and 1 to 999 days for notice contracts. This maturity generally happens during the COB on the maturity date, that is, the accounts show the updated balances on the next day. However, it is possible to set the maturity to run during the SOD as part of the previous day's COB, that is, accounts show updated balances on the day of maturity. This option is allowed by the Mature a t S OD field. A similar field on LMM.ADVICES is used to default values into this field.

If a contract is set to mature in COB processing and if the bank decides to mature it online, it can run the MM.ONLINE.MAT service. If the counterparty wants to renew the contract before maturity, it is possible to roll over or extend the period of the existing contract rather than having to set up a new deal for the new arrangement.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (Money Market)
- Call or Notice Placement
- Fixed Placement

A Call or Notice Taking is a contract to borrow a fixed amount of money in a specific currency, which is returned over a Call or Notice. Interest rate of these contracts can be either fixed or floating, where the users should specify the frequency of interest payment.

The rate of interest can be fixed or floating, which means, it can accommodate even negative interest rate. Principal repayment ...*

#### 📖 Introduction

Call or notice placement is a loan contract with maturity on call or notice term. Maturity is zero days for a call and notice but can be 1 to 999 days for notice contract. The rate of interest can be fixed or floating, which means, it can accommodate even negative interest rate. Principal repayment can be bullet or partial, whereas rollover is not allowed on call or notice contracts.


#### 🔧 Working With

Apart from the maturity terms, the differences between fixed maturity placement deals and call or notice placement deals remain the same. The illustration below explains how to input call or notice placements using fixed or floating interest rate.

The interest rate types handled within the module are fixed, floating and none. Fixed interest rate is static throughout the life of the contract or for a given interest period, the floating rate varies throughout the life of the contract. The type ‘None’ denotes the contract does not have an interest rate, which is the case with sundry payable or receivable type of contracts.

Fixed rate of interest can either be keyed in manually or defaulted from periodic interest rate key. Periodic interest key also considers a spread (if given) to populate the fixed rate. The module supports both positive and negative rates of interest. To use negative interest rate, the Negative Interest field in MM is set to Yes. If the Negative Interest field is set to Yes, the user cannot enter values in the fields related to tax and liquidation mode. Negative interest capitalisation is allowed for Money Market (MM) contracts. In the absence of negative rate field set to Yes, if the floating rate moves into negative territory during the course of contract life time, system considers the interest rate as zero.

| Accrual Method | Description |
|---|---|
| First day (default) | Performs accrual on the first day of the value date of the contract. |
| Last day | Considers the last day of the interest period for accrual while skipping the first day in the interest calculation period. |
| Both day | Denotes one-day additional accrual, as both first and last day are included in the accrual. |

The MM module provides an alert in the form of an override message to prevent any incorrect interest rate keyed during the deal capture. The inputted interest rate is verified against the periodic interest rate key 01 of the respective currency as part of the check. If the variance is greater than the given percentage in PERIODIC.INTEREST rate table or as mentioned in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS (if the former is not available), the system performs a tolerance check and raises an override message.

The example below illustrates how call or notice placements are inputted using fixed and floating interest rate.

The interest spread is included in the fixed interest rate during manual input of the Interest Rate field and therefore the Spread is not separately given or allowed. However, if the fixed rate of interest is fetched from PI record, it is possible to apply spread to derive the contract rate.

The floating rate is referred to BASIC.INTEREST table and a spread can be applied on the same.

Observe the Spread field with a value of 0.25 percentage, which is added to the floating rate of 0.549% to get the final rate of 0.799% and this is considered in the interest amount calculated.

The Mature a t S OD field in MM.MONEY.MARKET stands for mature MM deals at the Start of Day (SOD). MM deals can be matured at the start of the day, so the customer accounts are updated with the funds from contracts that matured during SOD processing.

This field can store one of the following values:

- ‘Yes’ for the maturity of the deals at the SOD processing
- ‘No’ for the maturity of the deals to be processed at the COB

There are two ways to apply value to this field:

- In the first way, the user picks a category code and the MM routine uses this category code to read the value of a Mature at SOD field on the LMM.ADVICES parameter file.
- In the second way, user can override this value by selecting or entering Yes or No within the transaction as shown below:

Maturity is 0 days for a call, and 1 to 999 days for notice contracts. This maturity generally happens during COB on the maturity date, that is, accounts show the updated balances on the next day. However, it is possible to set the maturity to run during the SOD as part of the previous day's COB, that is, accounts show updated balances on the day of maturity. This option is allowed by the Mature a t S OD field. A similar field on LMM.ADVICES is used to default values into this field.

If a contract is set to mature in COB processing and if the bank decides to mature it online, it can run the MM.ONLINE.MAT service. If the counterparty wants to renew the contract before maturity, it is possible to roll over or extend the maturity period of the existing contract rather than having to setup a new deal for the new arrangement.

#### 📖 Introduction

Money Market (MM) module supports confirmation of the MM deals. Confirmation is a process of getting all the details of the contract validated by the counterparty to the client. A deal, when confirmed to be correct, can be verified and confirmed within the system, which allows the settlement of the deal on maturity.


#### 🔧 Working With

Recording the receipt of a deal confirmation message from the counterparty and having verified the correctness of the deal details (within the MM record) is important in two aspects:

- Managing the operational risk arising from human errors.
- Ensuring the deal amounts and settlement date are correct before making the settlement.

When the back office receives the deal confirmation message and is satisfied with the accuracy, the user performs the verify function to stamp the MM record with the user ID, date and time stamp details. This function helps in releasing the payment with the backing of the confirmation received from counterparty. Additionally, follows-up with counterparties, from whom confirmation messages need to be received. The following screenshots illustrates the process of confirming a deal.

#### 📖 Introduction

The Money Market (MM) module is capable of handling fees and commissions applicable to the deals. The MM product uses the core tables (that is, FT.CHARGE.TYPE and FT.COMMISSION.TYPE ) to process fees and commissions on its transactions. On inputting the charge key in the contract, the system retrieves and displays the details of charges for the user to accept or override. A charge collected can be taken to P&L in one go or amortised over the deal period or user specified time period.


#### 🔧 Working With

The standard FT.CHARGE.TYPE and FT.COMMISSION.TYPE tables define the conditions related to fees and commission to apply on the transactions. The below illustration shows, how a charge related to MM deal is defined on FT.COMMISSION.TYPE table and is reflected on the transaction.

The user can amortise the charges or commissions associated with the contract by configuring the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record. They can also define a minimum charge amount eligible for amortisation in the Accrual Min Amt field. The amortisation process for charge or commission begins from the value date of the contract. The period for amortisation can be the period between the value date and maturity date. However, the user can also define the amortisation period in the Amortisn Period field in the FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record.

If the user gives an amortisation period that exceeds the maturity date of the contract, then the maturity date is considered as the end date for amortisation. The below screenshot illustrates a sample with Amortisn Period field updated in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE .

Rollover of a fixed maturity contract does not affect the amortisation process of an existing charge. A new charge entered after the maturity date extends through a rollover and is amortised based on the new maturity date. If the fixed maturity contract is closed prematurely, the system recalculates the amortisation amount and raises an adjustment entry.

In call and notice contracts, charges or commissions are not amortised and posted to P&L directly, as there are no maturity date for these types of contracts. However, a charge entered after the maturity date is fixed is amortised similar to a fixed maturity contract. The facility to define the amortisation period through Amortisn Period does not cover call or notice contracts. The details of amortisation are recorded in EB.ACCRUAL according to the example given below.

### 4.8  Fixed Placement Deal Processing

#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed placement is a contract with a fixed maturity term. The maturity date is the date on which the deal is liquidated, along with principal and interest. The rate of interest can be fixed or floating. Principal repayment can be bullet or partial, and rollover can be manual or automatic.


#### 🔧 Working With

The fixed placement deal is similar to fixed taking deal, except placement is an asset while taking is a liability. Tax feature does not apply to placement deals is another difference. The initial and final cash flow directions would be opposite. Similar to a taking, periodic interest liquidation is possible by defining a frequency. Interest rate, floating or fixed, with or without spread is possible. The illustration below is for a fixed maturity placement with fixed rate of interest.

As mentioned earlier, the interest rate types used within the module are fixed, floating and none. While fixed interest rate is static throughout the life of the contract or for a given interest period, floating rate varies throughout the life of the contract. The type ‘None’ denotes that the contract does not have an interest rate, which is the case with sundry payable or receivable type of contracts.

Fixed rate of interest can either be input manually or defaulted from periodic interest rate key while also applying a spread. During rollovers, the new rate of interest can be keyed in manually or derived from periodic interest key while applying a spread, if any.

The module supports both positive and negative rates of interest. To use negative interest rate, the Negative Interest field in MM is set to Yes. If the Negative Interest field is set to Yes, the user cannot enter values in the fields related to tax and liquidation mode. Negative interest capitalisation is allowed for Money Market (MM) contracts. In the absence of negative interest rate field set to Yes, if the floating rate moves into negative territory during the course of contract life time, system considers the interest rate as zero.

The MM module supports various accual methods, such as First Day, Last Day and Both.

- On the First Day accrual method (default), the accrual is performed on the first day of the value date of the contract.
- On the Last Day accrual method, the last day of the interest period is considered for accrual while, skipping the first day in the interest calculation period.
- Both day accrual denotes one-day additional accrual, as both first and last day are included in the accrual.

To know more, refer to the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table.

The MM module provides an alert in the form of an override message to prevent any incorrect interest rate keyed-in capturing the deal. The inputted interest rate is verified against the periodic interest rate key 01 of the respective currency as part of the check. If the variance is greater than the given percentage in PERIODIC.INTEREST rate table or as mentioned in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS (if the former is not available), the system performs a tolerance check and raises an override message.

The interest rate from the PERIODIC . INTEREST table for fixed-rate contracts is fetched by using the Periodic Interest Key field.

This rate is linked to the principal amount of the contract and the term of the deal, if amount banding is set up for the selected PERIODIC.INTEREST table. The Interest Rate field is left blank, and all relevant dates and amounts are entered before the input of Periodic Interest Key , which fetches the Interest Rate from PERIODIC.INTEREST table. After updating, the enrichment of the interest key indicates the derived rate, together with a maturity date and amount, the band used to derive the rate. The same steps are followed to derive the New Interest Rate in the case of a rollover.

When the rollover details are setup for manual or automatic rollover, the user can derive the new interest rate from the relevant PERIODIC . INTEREST table or use the new fixed interest rate that is inputted. Interest spread can also be given in this scenario.

This section describes the following:

The fixed interest rate is derived from the PERIODIC.INTEREST table by mentioning the PI key in the Periodic Interest Key field in MM application. It is possible to define interest spread in such cases, which can either be added or subtracted accordingly. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PERIODIC.INTEREST and the defined spread. The logic to fetch the rate considers the contract’s interest period, currency and amount. Where there is no exact term point corresponding to the period for which the rate is required, system does interpolation.

Modification either in spread or PI interest key (during INAU or authorised status) requires the user to clear the Interest Rate field to allow the system to recalculate the rate. Below is the fixed rate type of MM contract with Interest Rate updated as 1.682869 after the summation of the values 1.02869 in Periodic Interest Key and 0.80 in Interest Spread fields.

Input is allowed in the Interest Spread field, when Periodic Interest Key is defined. Together with the spread and the rate fetched from PERIODIC.INTEREST table, the contract rate is derived.

Temenos Transact accepts input in both Interest Spread and New Intt Spread , and the value of the New Intt Spread field is considered for next period’s interest calculations. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PI and defined spread.

Temenos Transact accepts input in both Interest Spread and New Intt Spread . The value of the New Interest Rate field is considered for next period’s interest calculations, provided Rollover Interest Rate is defined with P S. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PI and defined spread.

> **⚠️ Note:** This functionality is limited to contracts entered either during first input or amendments. The existing logic remains unchanged for 'Manual Rollovers without PI key' and 'Auto Rollovers'.

The Mature a t S OD field in MM.MONEY.MARKET stands for mature MM deals at the SOD. MM deals can be matured at the SOD, so that customer has access to the funds from a deposit and can avail a loan at the SOD maturity.

This field can store one of the following values:

- 'Yes' for the maturity of the deals at the SOD processing
- 'No' for the maturity of the deals to be executed at COB

There are two ways to apply value to this field:

- In the first way, the user picks a category code. The MM routine uses this category code to read the value of Mature a t S OD field in the LMM.ADVICES parameter file.
- In the second way, the user can override this value by selecting or entering Yes or a No within the transaction as shown below.

The MM module allows the use of a TAX code through Tax Interest Key and Tax Interest Type fields to be applied to the interest element on deposits. While the input in a Tax Interest Key field is a Tax code, the input in a Tax Interest Type depends on the group codes created. Users can input multiple instances of TAX code or TAX type. Accounting entries are raised separately for each of the tax amount. Following are the conditions and rates that can be applied to this tax:

- The APPL.GEN.CONDITION system table is used to define a series of conditions and calls to locally developed subroutines, which determines a contract group code that automatically updates the Contract Group field whenever the contract is changed.
- The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION system table allows to define contract group codes about tax types and specific tax codes.
- The tax type together with the contract group code are used to determine a specific interest tax code for the contract. If changes to the contract result in a different contract group code being generated, then a new tax code gets is applied as per the conditions set.

If there are no rollover instructions given, a fixed maturity placement or taking contract matures on the maturity date. Temenos Transact sends out maturity notices accordingly, in advance of maturity and generates the appropriate movements for the principal and interest, to deliver funds to the agreed accounts. This maturity generally happens during the COB on the maturity date, that is, accounts show the updated balances on the next day. However, it is possible to set the maturity to run during the SOD as part of the previous day's COB, that is, the accounts show updated balances on the day of maturity. This option is allowed by the Mature a t S OD field. A similar field on LMM.ADVICES is used to default values into this field.

If a contract was set to mature in COB processing and if the bank decides to mature it online, it can run the MM.ONLINE.MAT service. If the counterparty wants to renew the contract before maturity, it is possible to roll over or extend the period of the existing contract rather than having to setup a new deal for the new arrangement.

#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed taking is a contract with a fixed maturity term. The maturity date is the date on which the deal is liquidated along with principal and interest. The rate of interest can be fixed/periodic or floating, and interest can be capitalised with the principal along with the rollover event. Principal repayment can be bullet or partial. Rollover can be manual or automatic with or without interest capitalisation.


#### 🔧 Working With

Except for the maturity and interest payment terms, there is no difference between fixed maturity taking deals and call or notice taking deals, as far as post deal processing is concerned. As stated, a call or notice taking deal gets converted to a fixed maturity contract once the maturity date is fixed, at some point of time. The illustration below explains how a fixed maturity taking is inputted using fixed or floating interest rate.

The interest rate types handled within the module are fixed, floating, and none.

- Fixed interest rate is static throughout the life of the contract or for a given interest period.
- Floating rate varies throughout the life of the contract.
- None denotes the contract does not have an interest rate, which is the case with Sundry payable or receivable type of contracts.

Fixed rate of interest is keyed in manually or defaulted from periodic interest rate key. During rollovers, the new rate of interest is keyed in manually or derived from periodic interest key along with spread (if any). The module supports both positive and negative rates of interest. To use negative interest rate, the Negative Interest field in MM is set to Yes. If the Negative Interest field is set to Yes, the user cannot input any values in the fields related to tax and liquidation mode. Negative interest capitalisation is allowed for Money Market (MM) contracts.. In the absence of negative rate field set to Yes’ if the floating rate moves into negative territory during the course of contract life time, system considers the interest rate as zero.

The MM module supports various accrual methods, such as First Day, Last Day and Both.

- On the First Day accrual method (default), the accrual is performed on the first day of the value date of the contract.
- On the Last day accrual method, the last day of the interest period is considered for accrual while skipping the first day in the interest calculation period.
- Both day accrual denotes one-day additional accrual, as both first and last day are included in the accrual.

To know more, refer to the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table.

MM module provides an alert in the form of an override message to prevent any incorrect interest rate keyed during the deal capture. The inputted interest rate is verified against the periodic interest rate key 01 of the respective currency as part of the check and if the variance is greater than the given percentage in PERIODIC.INTEREST rate table or as mentioned in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS (if the former is not available), the system performs a tolerance check and raises an override message.

The interest rate from the PERIODIC . INTEREST table for fixed-rate contracts is derived by using the Periodic Interest Key field.

This rate is linked to the principal amount of the contract and the term of the deal, if amount banding is setup for the selected PERIODIC INTEREST table. The Interest Rate field is left blank, and all relevant dates and amounts are entered before the input of Periodic Interest Key , which derives the Interest Rate from PERIODIC INTEREST table. After updation, the Interest Rate can be modified, and the enrichment of the interest key indicates the derived rate (together with a maturity date) and amount the band used to derive the rate. The same steps are followed to derive the New Interest Rate in the case of a rollover.

When the rollover details are setup for manual or automatic rollover, the user can derive the new interest rate from the relevant PERIODIC . INTEREST table or use the new interest rate (fixed) that is inputted.

This section describes the following:

The fixed interest rate is derived from the PI table by mentioning the PI key in the Periodic Interest Key field in MM application. It helps to define interest spread in such cases, which can either be added or subtracted accordingly. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PI and the defined spread. Modification in spread or PI interest key (during INAU or authorised status) requires the user to clear the Interest Rate field to allow the system to recalculate the rate. Below is the fixed rate type of MM contract with Interest Rate updated as 1.6365 after the summation of the values 0.8365 in Periodic Interest Key field and 0.80 in Spread field.

Input is allowed in the Spread field, when either Auto Rollover is set or Periodic Interest Key is defined. In this case, the derived interest rate includes the defined spread.

Temenos Transact accepts input in both Spread and New Intt Spread . Value of the New Intt Spread field is considered for next period’s interest calculations. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PI and defined spread.

Temenos Transact accepts input in both Spread and New Intt Spread . Value of the New Interest Rate field is considered for next period’s interest calculation, if Rollover Interest Rate is defined with P S. The resultant interest rate is the summation of the derived rate from PI and defined spread.

> **⚠️ Note:** This functionality is limited to contracts entered either during first input or amendments. The existing logic remains unchanged for 'Manual Rollovers without PI key' and 'Auto Rollovers'.

The Mature a t S OD field in MM.MONEY.MARKET stands for mature MM deals at the SOD. MM deals can be matured at the SOD, so the customer has access to the funds from a deposit and can avail a loan at the SOD maturity.

This field can store one of the following values:

- Yes for the maturity of the deals at SOD processing.
- No for the maturity of the deals to be executed at the COB.

There are two ways to apply value to this field:

- In the first way, the user picks a category code. The MM routine uses this category code to read the value of Mature a t S OD field in the LMM.ADVICES parameter file.
- In the second way, the user can override this value by selecting or entering a Yes or a No within the transaction as shown below:

MM allows the use of a Tax code through Tax Interest Key and Tax Interest Type fields to be applied to the interest element on deposits. While the input in a Tax Interest Key field is a Tax code, the input in a Tax Interest Type depends on the group codes created. Users can input multiple instances of TAX code or TAX type. Accounting entries are raised separately for each of the tax amounts. Following are the conditions and rates applied to this tax:

- The APPL.GEN.CONDITION system table is used to define a series of conditions and calls to locally developed subroutines, which determines a contract group code that automatically updates the Contract Group field whenever the contract is changed.

Defining a generic tax type in TAX is possible as opposed to the specific tax code.

- The TAX.TYPE.CONDITION system table allows to define contract group codes about tax types and specific tax codes.

The tax type together with the contract group code are used to determine a specific interest tax code for the contract. If changes to the contract result in generating a different contract group code, then a new tax code is created.

If there are no rollover instructions given, a fixed maturity placement or taking contract automatically matures on the maturity date. Temenos Transact sends out maturity notices accordingly, in advance of maturity, and generates the appropriate movements for the principal and interest, to deliver funds to the agreed accounts. This maturity generally happens during the COB on the maturity date, that is, accounts show the updated balances on the next day. However, it is possible to set the maturity to run during the SOD as part of the previous day's COB, that is, the accounts show updated balances on the day of maturity. This option is allowed by the Mature at SOD field. A similar field on LMM.ADVICES is used to default values into this field.

If a contract was set to mature in COB processing and if the bank decides to mature it online, it can run the MM.ONLINE.MAT service. If the counterparty wants to renew the contract before maturity, it is possible to roll over or extend the period of the existing contract rather than having to setup a new deal for the new arrangement.

### 4.10  Maturity and Rollover


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *MM module allows for extension of the maturity period of a fixed maturity contract using the rollover feature (automatic or manual). Along with rollover, it is possible to capitalise the interest amount net of taxes. New interest rate or spread is applied to the extended period to take effect on the...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Capitalise*, *Auto Rollover*, *Auto Rollover Term*, *Final Maturity Date*, *Periodic Interest Key*, *Rollover*, *Spread*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

MM module allows for extension of the maturity period of a fixed maturity contract using the rollover feature (automatic or manual). Along with rollover, it is possible to capitalise the interest amount net of taxes. New interest rate or spread is applied to the extended period to take effect on the rollover date, or periodic interest rate with a spread can be used. Rollover confirmation details through swift or print message are shared with the counterparty or customer, ahead of the rollover event.


#### 🔧 Working With

Rollover feature offers both manual and automatic extension of the maturity period of a fixed maturity contract. Manual rollover is performed in two ways:

Extends the maturity date of the contract along with changes in interest rate and principal movement but does not handle interest capitalisation.

Allows all of the above along with capitalisation of interest, where, the interest amount is subjected to tax and only the net interest amount is capitalised or paid according to the option chosen.

- Auto Rollover , Auto Capitalise and Auto Rollover Term fields in MM application caters to the automatic rollover functionality.
- The Final Maturity Date field denotes a date after which the auto rollover of the contract is suspended or stopped.
- In every auto rollover event, it is possible for interest payout or captilisation of interest.
- Rate reset during auto rollover is possible using a Periodic Interest Key .

When the rollover details are entered, the interest amount for the next period (in the case of a rollover with interest settlement) or new interest amount for the current period (in the case of maturity date extension) is calculated and stored in the deal. It can also store the new principal amount, including any capitalised interest amount. MM contracts can be rolled over during the maturity delivery period. During this period, input is allowed in the Rollover and Spread fields but with override messages generated (which indicates that payment is already sent). Position Management is updated to show both the details of the current period (interest amount, end date, rolled principal etc.) along with new maturity and the interest amount due after the rollover advice is generated ahead of the rollover date. Similarly, forward account movements are posted for the next interest period to ensure Nostro cashflow is accurate.

Additional information stored in the deal reflects the current interest period start and end date, and the original value and maturity date at contract input. The initial value date may be entered, while entering into the contract initially, and may be earlier than the actual value date, which may be the case when a deal is taken over from an existing system. This information is used in the detailed Central Reporting Base (CRB) reports, and is additionally used in CONSOL.KEY for MM to determine the initial maturity period. Any of the date fields can be used to determine the initial period for reporting. This allows the contract period to remain constant when a rollover takes place, rather than being reported with a longer term.

Contract Term – 3 months

Rollover instructions – Automatic rollover for every three months with interest rate reset.

Interest processing – Interest to be paid during a rollover or to be capitalised.

Final Maturity Date – Two years from the date of initial deposit.

In the above scenario, roll over happens in a contract every three months with interest rate reset for an effective period of two years until the contract matures (similar to any other contract). According to the instruction, the interest amount is either paid out or capitalised.

### 4.11  Merging Contracts at Maturity


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Merging one contract with another contract at maturity, which has the same counterparty, category, currency and maturity is possible. Merging is associated with the maturity of secondary contract and the rollover of primary deal with a separate principal increase event.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Final Maturity Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Merging one contract with another contract at maturity, which has the same counterparty, category, currency and maturity is possible. Merging is associated with the maturity of secondary contract and the rollover of primary deal with a separate principal increase event.


#### 🔧 Working With

Merging contracts at maturity is when one contract is setup to be rolled over, with the principal and interest amounts from other maturing contracts merged into it through a principal increase event on rollover. The merge contracts shall have the same counterparty, category, currency and maturity. The merging happens when the secondary contracts mature and primary deal rolls over. The merged amounts is recorded as a separate principal increase. If there is also a standard principal increase on the primary deal, then two principal increase events are recorded. A MERGEMM record in ACCOUNT.CLASS is defined and suspense accounts is setup for all relevant currencies.

The example shows that a primary contract is set to roll over with a principal increase, and to merge principal from a secondary deal of the same counterparty due to mature on the rollover date. The secondary contracts to be merged into the primary contract, needs to have their principal and liquidation accounts defined as internal merge suspense account.

Input a deposit of GBP 10,000 for four months at a fixed interest of 5% for a counterparty. Mark the liquidation account as internal account meant for Money Market (MM) merger.

Input a deposit of GBP 10,000 for four months at a floating interest rate for the same counterparty (similar to secondary contract). The screenshots below shows how the primary contract is setup, and secondary deal is merged with the primary contact using the command line.

> **⚠️ Note:** To derive amount banded periodic interest rate, enter all amount-related information.

Additionally, the user can merge contract setup using the automatic rollover to Final Maturity Date . The merging information is entered during the final interest period, when the rollover details are setup automatically on the primary contract. The Final Maturity Date is extended on the primary contract, and the secondary contracts is left to mature.

### 4.12  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Money Market (MM) module enables the Treasury department to support deal capture and administration of the standard product types used in the interbank Money Market. This section is designed to help the Temenos Transact users to understand the application features, navigation and the functionali...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Fair Value Margin Key*, *Fair Value Rate Key*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Money Market (MM) module enables the Treasury department to support deal capture and administration of the standard product types used in the interbank Money Market. This section is designed to help the Temenos Transact users to understand the application features, navigation and the functionalities related to MM module. The intended audience of this module are as follows:

| Role | Function |
|---|---|
| Dealer | Executes deals with counterparty and records the deal details in the system |
| Treasury Back office personnel | Ensures authorisation, confirmation, settlement of payments |
| Risk Manager | Enforces and monitors risk limits |
| IT Personnel of bank or financial institution | Maintains computing infrastructure and upgrades of computer applications |

Certain features specific to retail deposit and loan products are, generally, not applicable in interbank MM business. Therefore, it is essential that the functions and features of MM module are relevant to the standard interbank MM business.

The processing within the module is straightforward but flexible. Although MM module primarily supports taking and placement of contracts, it also offers a range of advanced features, such as auto rollover, contract merger, period interest payments, etc.

The below workflow diagram provides a view of the functional landscape of the MM module in Temenos Transact . It shows the products covered and features supported by the module. The brokerage calculation and processing is available in the BROKER application.

The MM module supports the following main products:

| Product | Description |
|---|---|
| Taking (Deposit) | Taking (also known as a deposit) is a contract between two financial organisations, mainly banks or financial institutions, where one bank or financial institution borrows money from the other bank or financial institution. The terms and conditions of taking could vary, such as fixed term or call or notice basis with a fixed or floating interest rate linked to a base rate using a key. |
| Sundry Deposit (Payable) | Sundry Deposit is a simple one-time deposit without interest, on a fixed or call basis. The purpose is to allow the bank to record amounts due to clients, without having to pay any interest. |
| Placement (Loan) | Placement (also known as Loan) is a contract between two financial organisations, mainly banks or financial institutions, where one bank or financial institution lends money to the other bank or financial institution. The terms and conditions of placement could vary, such as fixed term or call, notice basis with a fixed or floating interest rate linked to a base rate using a key. |
| Sundry Loan (Receivable) | Accounts receivable is a simple one-time loan, without interest on a fixed or call basis. The purpose is to allow the bank to record amounts or miscellaneous items due from clients without having to pay any interest. |

The key contractual terms are as following:

Fixed Term contracts, both taking and placement, shall have a fixed term or period to determine the maturity date. These contracts can be entered by using the fixed and floating rate of interest. A fixed rate can be referenced to PERIODIC.INTEREST table and floating rate to BASIC.INTEREST table.

Call or Notice contracts do not have a term or period, so the maturity date is not known until both parties agree to liquidate the contract. These contracts have on-call or on-notice (generally from 1 to 14 days, and could vary based on different markets) periods to determine the maturity date. These contracts allow fixed and floating rate of interest to the contractual terms.

Every MM contract has two parts: principal and interest. The maturity of the contracts determines the treatment of principal and interest components in the module as follows:

The principal is the contractual amount, which needs to be repaid or received on maturity depending on the underlying of the contract. The principal can be increased or decreased during the life of the contract. This happens in both fixed maturity as well as call or notice contracts.

In a call or Notice contract, the repayment of the principal can be bullet (one-shot) or early partial or total repayment. Rollover is not allowed on a call or notice contract.

Interest is the resultant monetary value arising from a placement or taking of the principal amount. Interest is always in arrears, and no interest is paid or received on sundry deposit or accounts receivable contracts.

Term contracts allow fixed, floating and periodic rate of Interest. Interest schedule defines the interim interest payment date and frequency cycle for future interest payout until maturity. Capitalisation of interest (addition to the principal) is possible along with rollover of the contract. Rollover is either manual or auto.

Call or notice contract allows fixed and floating rate of Interest. The due date and frequency at which the interest is paid or received is according to the contract terms. Interest payment can be liquidated or deferred on the interest due date.


##### Product Configuration

The MM deals are processed based on the below parameter files, which are also shared by Loans and Deposits (L&D) module:

The processing of MM transaction is handled by using the below three applications, after setting up all the required parameter information:

- MM.MONEY.MARKET for input and maintenance of placements and deposits.
- MM.PAYMENT.ENTRY for early partial or full repayments.
- MM.RECEIPT.ENTRY for early partial or full receipts.

Although the products supported by the MM module and L&D module are different, the basic accounting and delivery requirements are similar.


##### Illustrating Model Products

The following products are available in the MM module:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Call or Notice Placement | To lend a fixed amount of money in a specific currency, where the tenure of the contract ends based on call or number of days of notice. The frequency of interest payment needs to be specified, which can be fixed or floating. |
| 2 | Fixed Maturity Placement | To lend a fixed amount of money in a specific currency to the counterparty. The length of the tenure is fixed at the time of agreement. Interest rate on the contract value can be fixed or floating. |
| 3 | Call or Notice Taking | To borrow a fixed amount of money in a specific currency where the tenure of the contract ends based on Call or Number of days of Notice. The frequency of interest payment needs to be specified, which can be fixed or floating. |
| 4 | Fixed Maturity Taking | To borrow a fixed amount of money in a fixed currency. The length of the tenure is fixed at the time of agreement. Interest rate on the contract value can be fixed or floating. |


#### 📊 Outputs

The MM module is an integral part of management information for the production of comprehensive general reports and enquiries including:

| Enquiry | Description |
|---|---|
| Cash Flow | PM.CAS enquiry shows daily analysis of net inflows and outflows along with cumulative balance. |
| Liquidity Position | PM.GAP enquiry shows the future amounts placed and taken, and the average and break-even rate of a particular currency represented by different time band buckets (as defined on PM.CALENDAR). It also displays the future interest movements. |
| Nostro Position | NOSTRO.POSITION enquiry shows the current and forward positions of the Nostro accounts by currency. |
| Interest Rate Exposure | PM.IRE enquiry shows the asset and liability by maturity with average rate, calculation of the break-even rate for each period and cumulative balance. |
| Interest Rate Sensitivity | PM.INT enquiry shows the effect of profit and loss on increasing the interest rates in series of 25 basis points. |

To know more, refer to Position Management (PM) and Foreign Exchange (FX) . There are also MM specific reports that includes:

- All contracts maturing in the next N days

The list is in maturity date order and has necessary details, such as contract reference number, customer name, currency, principal and interest amount, liquidation accounts for principal and interest and type of contract.

- Deliveries for the next N days

The list is in payment value date order, and under each value date heading appears the remittance accounts to which payments are to be made. Provision is made to display the beneficiary bank together with the name of the final beneficiary of the funds in question.

- Contracts with broker confirmation not received.

- Contracts with counterparty confirmation received.

- Contracts with payment instructions received.

Activity Report

- Contracts that have activities today (including MM contracts), which are authorised.

Exception Log Report

- Contracts that are not authorised, (including MM contracts) starting from initial input or changes.

- The enquiry provides the basis to view the contract progress.

The Fair Value Rate Key and Fair Value Margin Key fields are linked to the PERIODIC.INTEREST table. Entering a value in these fields provides the default value for the fields with the same name on the LD and MM contracts (the CATEGORY matches the ID of the transaction that defaults from LMM.ADVICES ). These fields are overridden at the contract level and can be used for reporting purpose.

### 4.13  Periodic Interest Payment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Fixed maturity contract allows payment of interest on a regular periodic basis. The frequency in which the payout is made can be defined within the contract. In addition, it is possible to define the frequency of the payment on rollover of the contract.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Interest Schedule Date*, *Special Interest Method*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed maturity contract allows payment of interest on a regular periodic basis. The frequency in which the payout is made can be defined within the contract. In addition, it is possible to define the frequency of the payment on rollover of the contract.


#### 🔧 Working With

Fixed maturity contracts allow payment of interest on a periodic basis. Make a frequency based interest settlement by defining a frequency in the Interest Schedule Date field in MM application. Several frequency options are available, such as daily, weekly, monthly or user defined frequency. To include the interest for the last day of the first interest payment, the Special Interest Method field in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS is set to Yes. The total interest payment remains the same with the one without Special Interest Method set to Yes. The difference is only one day more in the first interest payment and one day less in the last.

The user has the option at contract level to override the special method of interest calculation by inputting Yes or No in the Special Interest Method field. By default, the value on the field is Null. If the contract has a flag, auto or manual rollover with interest settlement, then an interest settlement event will be effective on the rollover date.

> **⚠️ Note:** The periodic interest payment feature is not applicable where the interest is sought to be capitalized on rollover.

There are no Tasks available for Periodic Interest Payment feature.

### 4.14  Principal Movement


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An increase or decrease of initial principal amount, during the life of the contract is a common business requirement in MM transactions. MM module allows for Principal Increase (PI) or Principal Decrease (PD) at any time during the life of the contract. The effective date for PI or PD event can be ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Incr Eff Date*, *Prin Increase*, *Principal Inc or Dec*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An increase or decrease of initial principal amount, during the life of the contract is a common business requirement in MM transactions. MM module allows for Principal Increase (PI) or Principal Decrease (PD) at any time during the life of the contract. The effective date for PI or PD event can be today, back dated or future dated. In addition to the Principal Inc or Dec field in MM application, which allows principal increase or decrease, MM.PAYMENT.ENTRY and MM.RECE I PT.ENTRY are two applications within MM module that facilitate principal increase and decrease. The PI or PD can be a regular input to the deal or associated with a rollover event.


#### 🔧 Working With

MM module allows for principal increase or decrease at any time during the life of the contract.


##### Principal Increase (PI)

PI can be a regular input to the deal using the Principal Inc or Dec field or associated with a rollover event.

The effective date of the principal amount can be today, backdated or future dated, which is used in conjunction with Incr Eff Date field. On reaching this, the system automatically handles principal movement on the existing contract, together with appropriate recalculation of the total interest amount due on the contract. When a backdated PI is introduced, it does not lead to recalculation of interest for the already paid interest or capitalized interest during the period. The treatment remains the same even for rolled over contracts. Adjusting the effective date for PI can be performed by keying in the number of days to be adjusted in the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM application. To know more, refer to the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table.


##### Principal Decrease (PD)

PD can be a regular input to the deal using the Principal Inc or Dec field or associated with a rollover event. A negative sign before the amount in Prin Increase field denotes a PD.

The effective date of the principal amount can be today, backdated or future dated, which is used in conjunction with Incr Eff Date field. On reaching this, the system automatically handles principal movement on the existing contract, together with appropriate recalculation of the total interest amount due on the contract. When a backdated PD is introduced, it does not lead to recalculation of interest for the already paid interest or capitalized interest during the period. The treatment remains the same even for rolled over contracts. Adjusting the effective date for PD can be performed by keying in the number of days to be adjusted in the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM application. To know more, refer to the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table.

The PD event is handled through MM.PAYMENT.ENTRY and MM.RECEIPT.ENTRY applications.

- The MM.PAYMENT.ENTRY application is used for all liability types of contracts, that is, deposits (except fiduciary deposits) and payment entries can be either automatic or manual.
- The MM.RECEIPT.ENTRY application is used for all asset types of contracts, that is, placements or loans (except fiduciary placements) and receipt entries can be either automatic or manual.

> **⚠️ Note:** During auto or manual rollover process of MM contracts with capitalisation of negative interest rate, the contract is liquidated or matured before the date in FINAL.MATURITY specified in the contract, when capitalised negative interest makes the Principal zero or negative.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Principal Movement feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Principal Movement feature.

### 4.15  RFR Linked Placement or Taking


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The MM.MONEY.MARKET application has the capability to capture and process overnight Risk-Free Rates (RFR) money market transactions and migrate the existing (L)IBOR transactions to RFR. It now supports Risk-Free Rate flooring options for Daily, Average and Total (all-in) floor types and performs amo...*
> 
> **Applications:** `LMM.INSTALL.CONS`, `MM`, `MM.MONEY.MARKET`, `MONEY.MARKET`, `PERIODIC.INTEREST`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose MM Deal*, *Interest Rate Type*, *Negative Rates*, *RF*, *RFR*, *RFR Calc Method*, *Rfr Calc Method*, *Rfr Convention*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The MM.MONEY.MARKET application has the capability to capture and process overnight Risk-Free Rates (RFR) money market transactions and migrate the existing (L)IBOR transactions to RFR. It now supports Risk-Free Rate flooring options for Daily, Average and Total (all-in) floor types and performs amount compounding in addition to the rate compounding of RFRs.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To enable the processing of Risk-Free Rates (RFR) in the MM module, new fields are added to LMM.INSTALL.CONDS and MONEY.MARKET applications. The user has to configure the RFR-related fields in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS for correct rate calculation, according to the bank’s preferences.


##### LMM.INSTALL.CONDS

LMM Install Conds .

2. Configure the following RFR fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Rfr Convention | Market convention for rate compounding or averaging The MM application follows Lookback methodology. |
| Rfr Lookback Type | Type of Lookback method applied for rate compounding or averaging. It has the following types for rate calculations: Narrow Definition – Uses the original interest period day count with lookback rate. For example, if Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Friday’s weight (three days) to the Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift – Uses the original day count of the lookback rate. For example, if Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Wednesday’s weight (one day) to the Wednesday’s rate. |
| Rfr Calc Method | Calculation methods for RFR averaging are: Compound Simple Amount NCCR |
| Rfr Spread Treatment | Spread treatment methods during the RFR averaging are: Spread-Inclusive - Uses the spread within the averaging calculation along with daily rates. Spread-Exclusive - Adds the spread separately after RFR averaging is done. |
| Rfr Period Day Count | Treatment of the last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It allows the following values: Full - Last RFR with day weightage, which is applicable for the full interest period. Today - Last RFR with its original day weightage, which is applicable till the current business day. |
| Rfr Decimals | Rounding value applied for RFR |


#### 🔧 Working With

The new fields introduced in LMM.INSTALL.CONS are available in MONEY.MARKET application, which enables the dealer to process RFR linked Money Market (MM) contracts.

Capture MM Deals .

2. To input a RFR linked MM placement or taking, perform the following:

- In the Interest Rate Type field, select ‘Floating’.
- In the RFR Key field (which has the RFR), enter the rate key.

3. Define the market convention and calculation method for averaging RFR in the Rfr Convention and Rfr Calc Method fields.

4. Define the number of lookback days for RFR calculations in the RFR Lookback Days field.

> **⚠️ Note:** The spread treatment method enables the user to include or exclude the contractual spread from the rate averaging.

The following are the additional fields introduced in MM application:

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Key | PERIODIC.INTEREST record key that has the RFR. |
| RF Rate | Stores the compounded Risk-Free Rate. This is a system updated field. |
| RFR Lookback Days | Number of lookback days considered for RFR calculations. |

The MM application follows the Lookback methodology to arrive at the RFR applicable for interest period. Hence, each business day the contract receives a new rate for the interest period. The accrual amounts for each working day are calculated based on the new rate.

The LMM.ACCOUNT.BALANCES table stores the accrual ladder for the current interest period with the amount accrued and rate applied for each accrual cycle. Average RFR changes every business day, once a new rate is available.

The below screenshot shows the interest rate changes in LMM.ACCOUNT.BALANCES , due to new RFR published for each business day.


##### Amount Compounding of Money Market Contracts using RFRs

The RFR Calc Method field is set as Amount to input RFR linked MM placement or taking with amount compounding.

When amount compounding is selected, the system calculates interest accruals using the daily RFRs published by the central banks. It multiplies the daily overnight RFR with the sum of outstanding principal and the unpaid accrued RFR interest.

The amount compounding method uses various methods for each spread treatment, while calculating interest accruals:

- Spread-Inclusive – Derives the amount compounding using the rate and spread (as a single value) as returned by term rate routine.
- Spread-Exclusive - The rate follows compounding calculation (the balance follows compounding using the daily RFR) while the spread follows simple interest calculation.


##### Non-Cumulative Rate Compounding

The Rfr Calc Method field in the MM.MONEY.MARKET application is set as NCCR to enter the RFR-linked money market (MM) placement or taking contracts with Non-Cumulative Rate Compounding.

The NCCR method applies a calculated compounded interest factor based on the difference between the ‘Cumulative Compounded Effective Rate’ for that given day and the previous day to arrive at a daily compounded accrual.

Calculating the NCCR involves three steps:

1. Annualised Cumulative compounded Rate (ACR) is calculated with existing Transact functionality for compounded average RFRs.
2. Unannualized Cumulative compounded Rate (UCR) is derived using the rate from Step 1 is unannualized by multiplying with the business day convention - the number of calendar days in the interest period divided by the market convention for quoting the number of days in the year.
3. The UCR for that given business day from Step 2 is subtracted from the UCR of the previous business day and multiplied with the market convention for quoting the number of days in a year, divided by the day count for the given business day. The result is NCCR.


##### Risk-Free Rate Flooring

The Negative Rates field in the MM.MONEY.MARKET application is enhanced to offer Daily Floor and Average Floor options in addition to the existing Yes and No options.

The Negative Rates field has the following options:

- Yes - Allows negative rates and does not allow RFR flooring.
- No - Applies total (all-in) RFR flooring, that is, when the average RFR plus the spread are below the floor value, the system floors the total rate to the floor value. The existing functionality is preserved for rates different from RFRs
- Daily Floor - Applies a floor on the RFRs published each business day before averaging them and applying spread whenever the daily RFRs are below the floor value
- Average Floor - Applies a floor on the average RFRs whenever the average RFRs are below the floor value. This option is not applicable for Spread-Inclusive margin treatment.

The flooring happens at the central rate calculation engine level. The MM module consumes the rates.


##### Cash Flow Projection

The forward accounting entries and cash flow projections are based on the last available average RFR.

The below screenshot shows the changes in interest amount forward entry, due to new RFR published for each business day.


##### MM Confirmation

SWIFT messages related to deal confirmation (MT320 and MT330) for RFR contracts has zero interest rate and amount. This is because the final rate applicable for the interest period is not available at contract initiation. During contract maturity, the final rate applicable is available and the maturity confirmation (MT320 and MT330) for RFR contracts has the actual interest rate.


##### Migration of Existing MM Contracts from (L)IBOR to RFR

To migrate existing contracts from (L)IBOR to RFRs, the user needs to perform the following:

- Specify the rate key with RFR rates in the RFR Key field.
- Define a new spread for migrated contract in the Interest Spread field, as (L)IBOR is not equal to RFRs.

#### 📖 Introduction

MM module supports setting up different rounding rules for rounding off interest, commission, charges and fees.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Rounding Rule field accepts any value defined in EB.ROUNDING.RULE , and based on this setting system rounds the interest calculation accordingly. The rounding rule for MM module is specified in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS file.

In the EB.ROUNDING.RULE application, other rounding types are also defined. Rounding rules are defined in the Rounding Type field within each record. The rule that is set on LMM.INSTALL.CONDS defaults into the MM.MONEY.MARKET application. However, modifying this, results in generating an override message to the user notifying about the change.
