### 7.4  Margin Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The margin accounts in Temenos Transact records any margin calls when required.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Clean Price*, *Dirty Price*, *Principal Amount 1*, *Principal Amount 2*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The margin accounts in Temenos Transact records any margin calls when required.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration content for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section briefs on how to set the margin rate for REPO contracts and also describes the procedure for handling margin calls.


##### Margin Accounts

The user can either define the required account or use the memo account. The account postings defined is used for establishing various accounts in SEC.ACC.MASTER records in differing currencies may be used (if required). The margin calls are usually made in the reference currency. If the currency of the security does not have an account specified in the margin portfolio, the first account defined is used as the default account.


##### Initial Margins

The Sc Init Mgn Rte field in REPO allows the user to select the margin rate to be applied for each security or multiple securities that are entered. This field becomes active only if the Trans Type field is set to Security. The values of the Sc Init Mgn Method field is Standard or Gmra and this field defaults to the Standard option for margin processing.

The Init Margin Rate field indicates the initial margin related to the cash amount entered in the Principal Amount 1 field. This field is populated only if the value in the Trans Type field is Cash and is a no input field, if the Trans Type field is set to Security.

The normal market requirement for a buyer is that the collateral is always slightly higher (for example, by 5%) than the cash loan. Then in this case, the Sc Init Mgn Method field is set to Standard.

If the user has selected the REPO security type and the amount of nominal, Temenos Transact defaults the Clean Price and Dirty Price fields This information is then populated in the Principal Amount 1 field. However, if the user has populated the Sc Init Mgn Rte the amount displayed in the Principal Amount 1 field is reduced by the new calculation method. The Sc Init Mgn Rte displays the percentage amount of the margin, (for example, 5%). Then, Temenos Transact calculates the new principal amount as follows:

Cash amount = market value of security x margin

= Nominal x dirty price x margin

= 1,000,000 x 96 x 0.95

= 912,000

The buyer has demanded a 5% haircut, meaning they intend to transfer cash, which is 5 % less than the market value of the security.

Temenos Transact realises the calculation to derive at the correct cash amount and multiplies the nominal of security by (0.95) and not 5%. Thus, reducing the nominal amount by 5 %, the reduced amount is multiplied by the current dirty price to equal the financing amount. This allows the user to enter the correct amount of percentage, to ensure that the correct figures are transferred to the confirmation. The information in the Sc Init Mgn Rte field is used to generate the MM.MONEY.MARKET child contract. The initial margin does not require additional entries as the cash received or lent is reduced to reflect the margin amount. The cash deposit continues to accrue interest at the current REPO rate in the normal way. The total amount repayable at maturity is calculated at the reduced cash amount. The additional margin calls (if any) are booked in the normal way to the customer margin portfolio account.

The second option of GMRA indicates that the margin calculation is to be expressed as:

Cash amount= market value of security x margin

= Nominal x dirty price x margin

= 1,000,000 x 96 x (1 /1.05)

= 914,285.71

In this method, Temenos Transact uses the clean price stored in the SECURITY.MASTER record and accrued coupon interest on the security (if any) thus deriving the dirty price. The final cash proceeds are calculated against the dirty price and the initial margin is deducted in accordance with the haircut method selected by the user.


##### Margin Call Valuation

The counterparty margin portfolio is updated by the REPO application, which is used as the basis for the margin processing. If the same counterparty is involved in both REPO and RESO transactions with the bank, where two margin portfolios are required to record the transactions separately.

The SC.VAL.REPO enquiry performs a valuation of the margin portfolio. Based on this information, the bank decides whether to make a margin call or to expect one from the counterparty of the REPO contract. Since all REPO and RESO contracts are recorded in different portfolios, the margin valuation enquiry must be run only over the RESO portfolios to indicate the counterparties for additional cash margins. The other party decides whether the bank needs to pay additional margin in respect of a REPO. The user may however run the enquiry for both REPO and RESO portfolios (if required). The SC.VAL.REPO enquiry allows the bank to view the margin call as either a net REPO or RESO position, derived using all contracts with a given counter party.

The margin calls are made with regard to the following options:

- Change in the principal amount - cash margin calls
- Change in the number of nominal or
- Substitution of the security with or without a change in nominal along with a margin call.

The last two options are referred as security based margin calls.


##### Margin Calls Settled in Cash

The user must enter the amount by which the principal is to be increased or decreased in the Prin Increase field, to affect a cash margin call. This field allows input only in an authorised record. This field accepts a negative value to obtain a decrease in the original principal.

If the Principal Increase field has a value, the Mgn Call Eff Date and Send Payment fields are available for input. The Mgn Call Eff Date field indicates the date on which the margin call is effective. The effective date must fall between the value defined in the Value Date and Maturity Date fields. The user may input a back valued date , if the date falls between the Value Date and the Maturity Date of the contract.

The Mgn Call Eff Date field is mandatory, if the Principal Increase field has a value, or if a change is made to the New Sec Code or New Nominals fields in an authorised record.

The Send Payment field determines whether any delivery message is sent for the change in the principal. If this field is set to Yes, the delivery instructions are generated to pay or receive cash. The default value for this field is No.

When a cash based margin call is made using the Principal Increase field to increase or decrease the principal, the change in the REPO interest due to the change in the principal is displayed in the Principal Increase Interest field.

If the Mgn Call Eff Date field has a future date, the revised principal due to the margin call is displayed in the Proj Cash Amt field. During the Close of Business (COB) operation on the date specified in the Mgn Call Eff Date field, the value in the Principal Amount 1 field gets revised to reflect the margin call and the value in the Proj Cash Amt field is cleared. The Principal Amount 2 field is calculated based on the new value in the Principal Amount 1 field.

The accounting entries are adjusted accordingly with the correct SWIFT messages for receipt of cash (MT210) or payment of cash (MT202 or MT100 or MT103). The values in the Fwd Settlement and Fwd Price fields are recalculated, with the option to override at input level. The investment rate is restricted to the original REPO rate specified at the initiation of the contract. The accrual of interest at the rate of interest for the REPO contract defined in the Repo Rate field occurs on the revised principal following the date in the Mgn Call Eff Date field.


##### Margin Calls Settled in Securities

The user can replace the security with one of the higher values or increasing the nominal to effect margin calls in Securities. If any change is made to the values in the New Sec Code or New Nominal fields, the Mgn Call Eff Date and the Mgn Deliv Instr fields are available for input. These fields are mandatory for a margin call settled in securities. The Mgn Deliv Instr field accept only the instructions that do not entail any payment.

If the margin call is made by changing the number of nominals, the delivery instructions for the movement of securities are generated for the difference between the old value and the new value in the New Nominal field.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for REPO - Margin Processing feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Repo margin is the difference between the market value of the security used as collateral and value of the loan.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below list of enquiries and reports:

Repo Variation Margin

Repo transactions are listed in this enquiry and reflects the margin adjustments to monitor margin calls on portfolio basis for all REPO Transactions, over and above the margin maintenance amount.

Reso Variation Margin

Reverse REPO (RESO) transactions are listed in this enquiry and reflects the margin adjustments to monitor margin calls on portfolio basis for all Reverse repo Transactions, over and above the margin maintenance amount.


##### SWIFT Messages

NA


##### Advices

NA


##### Alerts

NA

The repurchase agreement (REPO) is a short-term agreement between two parties in which one party sells the security at a price to the other party with an agreement to repurchase the security at a fixed time and price.


##### Product Configuration

The configuration of REPO module is explained in detail in the following sections.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Repo Margin Suf | Indicates the suffix for the repo counterparty margin portfolio. The value in this field determines the portfolios used for the reporting of REPO, stock or borrow lending contracts. |
| Rp Mrgn | Indicates the description of the Repo Margin Suf field. |
| Reso Margin Suf | Indicates the suffix for the reverse repo counterparty margin portfolio. The value in this field determines the portfolios used for the reporting of RESO contracts. |
| Rs Mrgn | Indicates the description of the Reso Margin Suf field. |
| Init Mrgn Booking | Indicates the initial margin of a REPO contract, which undervalues the securities involved to cover the risk of the adverse movement of the securities, which may arise before a margin call. The values are: Notional - Included in the margin portfolio valuation None – Display-only. |
| Repo Limit Update | Indicates whether the limit for a REPO contract is regarded as a LOAN or DEPOSIT. |
| Days Post Maturity | Indicates the number of days after maturity the contract remains in the live table. After this period expires, the matured contract is moved to the history table during the COB processing. The SBL contracts with zero nominal are moved to history after a specified period. However, if the contract is amended prior to this date, the nominal is increased to a non-zero value. The contract remains in the LIVE table until the specified time, as the nominal is again reduced to zero and the number of days specified is exceeded after restarting the day’s count. Once a contract is moved to the HISTORY table, it is not possible to restore the contract to a live contract. The contacts with zero nominal are not included in calculating corporate action for the stock concerned, unless there is an outstanding settlement. |
| Calculation Link | Indicates the default copied into each REPO record as it is created and determines if there are links between certain fields during the creation of the REPO contract. |
| Auto Calc Nominal | Indicates the cash amount entered in Principal Amount and any initial margin and calculates the amount of nominal required to exceed the cash amount if this field is set to Yes and the Trans Type field is set to Cash. This field is mandatory if the Calculation Link field is set to Yes. |
| Update Sc Pos Sod | Indicates that the REPO contract generates the near leg SECURITY.TRANSFER record immediately on authorising the contract regardless of the value date if this field is set to Yes. .In addition, this field updates the SECURITY.POSITION because of the far leg of the SECURITY.TRANSFER , at the SOD of the maturity date instead of the COB of the maturity date as occurred so far. This is a display-only field |
| Process Repo Sod | Indicates if the forward dated REPO contracts become LIVE and the maturity of the REPO contracts. The contracts can be processed either the SOD or COB. The values are Null, Fwd To Live, Maturity or Both. If this field is set to Null, the transactions turn live or mature at COB. This field enables selective process of the contracts becoming live or maturing at SOD. If the Update Sc Pos Sod field is set to Yes, this field accepts only the values Maturity or Both. |
| Ent Cpn Susp | Indicates if the RESO entries are posted to this specific account for corporate actions. This field allows the user to change the Account No field in the ENTITLEMENT record for the RESO positions. |
| Split Debit Cpn | Indicates if the cash entries relating to REPO contracts are posted to separate Nostro account. This process is enabled if the Account field is updated for the REPO application in the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT record. The NOSTRO.ACCOUNT record must be entered in the security currency of the DIARY. |
| Ac Block Clos Updt | Indicates if the Ac Block Closure from the REPO application is automatically updated for field New Cu Acct No in REPO. If this field is set to No, updates are not made and the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE application closes the accounts in live REPO contracts. |
| Accrue Fee | Indicates the fee that accrues until the contract matures for fixed term or until closed out for open trades, if this field is set to Yes. If value date is selected in charge frequency, the default is not to accrue. The fee amount posted on the repo contract accrues on a daily basis with the initial fee based on the current market value of the contract. After the first day, fee needs to be calculated based on the price stored on the SECURITY.MASTER and a COB should be run with the SECURITY.MASTER price being changed prior to the COB to ensure the accrual amount is correct. |
| Stp | Allows auto STP creation of the opposite SBL Internal Trade, if this field is set to Yes. This field can be set to Yes or left blank. |
| Fee Refund | Indicates the required refund of the fees, if the fee was taken on value date. For a fixed term contract the user can early mature the trade, if required. This is a Yes or No field. |

This application holds the records, which control the processing of the REPO contracts. Each REPO contract must have a valid REPO.TYPE entered.

- REPO.TYPE configuration as loan (REPO) or deposit (reverse REPO).
- Product category used ( CATEGORY record).
- Suffix for the margin portfolios.
- Definition of the customer REPO.
- Category of the suspense accounts for customer REPOs ( CATEGORY record).
- Transaction type used for the customer REPOs ( SC.TRANS.TYPE record).
- Default delivery instructions.
- Type of the REPO contract.
- Definition of the Effective Rate field
- The Link field links the opposite internal REPO.TYPE to allow auto creation of opposite trade.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Effective Rate field indicates if the interest rate in REPO is expressed as a nominal interest rate or an effective rate (EIR). If this field is set to Yes, the REPO accruals are based on an effective rate.

A margin portfolio must be setup for any counter party used in the REPO contracts. This portfolio is used to run the valuations to determine whether a margin call is due or is to be expected.

Read the Securities User Guide for more information on setting the portfolio ( SEC.ACC.MASTER ) application. The suffix used to define the margin portfolio must match with the suffix defined in the REPO.TYPE record. If the bank performs both REPO and RESO transactions with any given counterparty, the user needs to open one portfolio for each operation.

The underlying CUSTOMER.SECURITY record for the REPO counterparty must have the value Customer in the Customer Type field before the user can successfully open the new portfolio.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Interface To | Requirement |
| RP | For REPO contracts |
| RS | For RESO contracts |
| RPM | If Init Mrgn Booking is set to Notional on REPO.PARAMETER required for REPO. |
| RSM | If Init Mrgn Booking is set to Notional on REPO.PARAMETER required for RESO. |
| RPC | For customer REPO contracts |
| RSC | For customer RESO contracts |

The SUB.ASSET.TYPE records are required to record the securities that are on hold or loan status as part of the REPO and RESO contracts.

The user must configure a SUB.ASSET.TYPE for each of the ASSET.TYPE records created in the previous section.

This record provides additional details for the REPO agreement type.

The Description field indicates the free format description of the Repo Agreement Type field.

Both legs of the REPO contracts are often transacted under one agreement. The PSA agreement is used in the US, while in Europe the PSA/ISMA General Master REPO Agreement (GMRA) is the standard agreement used.

The standard agreement types must be defined in this record and referenced to the REPO contract, to avoid defining complex narrative of the contract used for delivery purposes. If required, additional conditions may be specified in the contract, or if the contract is not subjected to a standard agreement type.

The REPO agreements can be tracked with the DOCUMENT.MANAGEMENT application. The REPO module can be linked to this application for the user to produce an override or stop the trading with new counterparty, until the full legal documentation is received and agreed.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters for Repurchase Agreements are explained below:

System level parameter for processing REPO deals are defined in this application, which holds the following details:

- A Valid portfolio suffixes for the counterparty margin portfolio
- The Booking method of initial margin
- The limit update treatment for REPO deals
- The number of days post maturity when contracts are moved to history
- Processing of REPO deal at start of the day

REPO deals are usually transacted under an agreement. PSA agreement type is used in the US and PSA/ISMA general master REPO agreement are used in Europe. Standard agreement types should be entered into this application, and referenced on the REPO contract in the field agreement type.

Definition of all types of REPO contracts allowed in the system are defined in this application. It contains details such as category code, transaction index, default delivery, deal type etc.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Following products are available under REPO module.

| S.No | Product Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | REPO | A REPO is an agreement of sale and repurchase of a security. The securities are sold to the counterparty at a fixed price and the seller has a commitment to repurchase those securities at a pre-agreed price at a fixed point of time in the future. The price difference can be seen as the interest to deposit and maybe defined as a cash price or as a repo rate. |
| 2 | Reverse REPO(RESO) | A RESO is an agreement of purchase and re-sale of a security, which is also a converse of a REPO agreement. The securities are purchased at a fixed price and the buyer has the commitment to re-sale those securities at a pre-agreed price at a future date. The price difference can be seen as interest to the loan and maybe defined as price. |
| 3 | Sell-Buy Back | A sell or buy back is an agreement of a spot sale and a forward repurchase of a security. This is different from REPO agreement as the sale and purchase are treated as two separate legs. Hence, an agreement is not required. |
| 4 | Buy-Sell Back | A buy or sell back is an agreement of a spot purchase and a forward sale of a security. This is different to REPO agreement as the purchase and sale are treated as two separate legs. Hence, an agreement is not required. |

#### 📖 Introduction

REPO is short form of sale and repurchase agreement. It is essentially a transaction whereby two parties involved agree to perform two deals as a package. The first deal is a purchase (or sale) of a security, often a government bond, for delivery straight away (the exact settlement date varies according to the market convention for the security involved). The second deal is a reversal of the first deal, it is the settlement on some future date.

It is understood that the first deal is reversed, it is clear that both parties intend the transfer of securities (in one direction) and the transfer of cash (in the other direction) to be temporary rather than permanent. Therefore, the transaction is equivalent to a loan of securities in one direction and a loan of cash in the other.

The REPO is structured, so that the economic benefit of owning the securities, income and capital gains or losses, remains with their original owner. These are the driving factors behind the REPO market, all REPO’s are driven by either:

- The need to lend or borrow cash, which is collateralised by securities or
- The need to borrow specific securities

The prices for both the original sale and the repurchase are agreed at the outset. The difference between the two prices are calculated to be equivalent to the cost of borrowing secured money.

- For lenders of cash, a REPO has the advantage of double security. If counterparty defaults, they can rely on the collateral. Therefore, they can verify the creditworthiness of both the counterparty and the issuer of the collateral.
- For borrowers of cash, an advantage to make use of an investment in their portfolio to borrow funds either more cheaply or in a case where they would not normally be able to borrow at all.

A REPO is defined as an initial sale of securities followed by a subsequent repurchase. A reverse REPO is the opposite case, where an initial purchase of securities followed by a subsequent re-sale. As there are two parties involved in a REPO contract to perform the opposite transactions, one of the party performs a REPO while the other party performs a reverse REPO. The term REPO is based on the securities side of the deal and not the Money Market (MM), therefore if the dealer is selling securities (seller)/borrowing cash (buyer) the deal is REPO. And, if the dealer is purchasing securities (buyer)/lending cash (seller) the deal is reverse REPO.

Temenos Transact supports a wide variety of REPO and RESO type of transactions, such as:

- Bond REPO
- Gilt REPO
- Equity REPO
- Bilateral REPO
- Trilateral REPO
- Cross currency REPO
- Open REPOs
- Intra-day REPO
- Buy/Sell Back
- Sell/Buy Back
- Stock borrow/Lending

Temenos Transact also, provides the options such as:

- Multiple securities (classic security driven contracts only on delivery against payment trades)
- Substitution of securities
- PSA/ISMA or GMRA agreements
- REPO contracts on behalf of a customer (customer REPOs)

The REPO application enables the cash side as well as the security side of a REPO or RESO transaction to be booked. The input of the security side is not mandatory, if a trilateral REPO or RESO is specified (because it is quite possible that the securities as collateral may not be known at the time of the deal).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about entering a REPO Contract and its Accounting in detail.


##### Entering a REPO Contract

The REPO application is used to enter, modify and process the REPO contracts.

The table below shows the description of the fields that are available in the REPO application.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| REPO Type | Determines the type of REPO contract to be entered. It must be a valid record in the REPO .TYPE application. |
| Counterparty | Initiates the REPO contract when this field is blank. It must be a valid record on the CUSTOMER and CUSTOMER.SECURITY applications. |
| Currency | Indicates the currency of the REPO contract. It must be a valid record in the CURRENCY application. |
| Business Centre | Determine the working days for a specific country. It must be a valid record in the COUNTRY application. |
| Trade Date | Indicates the date on which the trade was agreed. It defaults to the current date. |
| Value Date | Indicates the date on which the contract becomes active |
| Maturity Date | Indicates the date on which the REPO contract matures. If the value in the REPO Type is set to Open REPO, it allows a value of 0 (zero), which can be changed to a valid maturity date. |
| Principal Amount 1 | Specifies the total amount of the contract on the near leg. |
| Principal Amount 2 | Specifies the total amount of the contract on the far leg |
| Interest Basis | Specifies the interest basis which is used for calculating interest. It allows entry of A-F and S (for special allows the user to modify the REPO Interest field) from the INTEREST.BASIS application (read comments below this table for more information). |
| REPO Rate | Sets the rate at which the REPO accrues the interest during the life of the contract. It is used to calculate the Principa l Amount 2 field. A negative REPO rate can be entered if required. |
| Product Category | Defaults the value from the REPO .TYPE record but may be changed manually in which case it must be a valid record in the CATEGORY application |
| Agreement Type | Specifies the agreement type that adheres to both legs of the contract. It must be a valid record in the REPO .AGREEMENT.TYPE application. |
| Condition | Accepts free format text. In this field, special conditions that apply to this contract are entered. |
| Limit Reference | Defaults the value from the LIMIT.REFERENCE application |
| Deal Type | Indicates the type of deal represented by this contract: Bilateral - Involves two parties. Trilateral - Involves three parties. |
| Prin Increase | Makes a margin call in cash. The amount of cash to be received or paid out for purposes of margin must be entered in this field. The margin call is effective from the date mentioned in the Mgn Call Eff Date field. After this, the field is made null. |
| Prin Increase Int | Displays the change in the REPO interest on account of the change in the principal resulting from a cash margin call. This is a no input field. |
| Mgn Call Eff Date | Holds the date on which the margin call comes into effect. The effective date must fall between the Value Date and the Maturity Date of the contract. The user may input a back valued date provided it falls between the Value Date and the Maturity Date of the contract. The Mgn Call Eff Date field becomes mandatory, if there is a value in the Pri Increase field, or a change made to the New Sec Code or New Nominals fields in an authorised record. |
| Send Payment | Determines whether any delivery message is to be sent for the change in the principal. If this field is set to YES, delivery instructions are generated to pay or receive cash. The default value for this field is NO. |
| Proj Cash Amt | Displays the revised principal on account of the margin call in the Proj Cash Amt field till the margin call takes effect, If the value in the Mgn Call Eff Date is a future date |
| New Sec Code | Determines the security that is used in the REPO contract. Once the record is authorised, if this field is changed it effects a substitution. |
| New Nominal | Determines the amount of the security that is traded in this REPO contract |
| Clean Price | Defaults the value from the Last Price field in the SECURITY.MASTER record. It can be manually changed in which case the values in the Gross Amount and Dirty Price fields are recalculated. |
| Gross Amount | Holds the gross amount of the REPO contract |
| Dirty Price | Holds the price which includes the Accrued Int Amt |
| Accrued Int Amt | Holds the accrued coupon interest. The parameters for this calculation are set in the SECURITY.MASTER record. |
| New Depo | Specifies the depository where the security is held |
| Sub Account | Specifies a sub-account for the depository entered in the New Depo field. It must be configured in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. |
| New Cu Acct No | Defaults the value from either the Margin Portfolio (for regular REPO) or Cust Portfolio (for Customer REPO) fields in the SECURITY.ACC.MASTER record. This field can be modified manually. |
| Sc Init Mgn Rte | Populates the Sc Init Mgn Amt field. It is available only when the Trans Type field is set to SECURITY and is a percentage used to undervalue the securities. |
| Sc Init Mgn Amt | Populates when data is entered in the Sc Init Mgn Rte field |
| Total Settlemnt.1 | Holds the total near leg settlement for the security |
| REPO Interest | Holds the interest to be charged for this security on this contract |
| Fwd Settlemnt | Holds the total far leg settlement for the security |
| Fwd Price | Holds the price that is used for the far leg settlement of the security |
| Cpn Invst Rate | Applies only to buy sell back and sell buy back contracts. It defaults the value from the Repo Rate field and is used to calculate the Cpn Invst Amt . |
| Bnd Rnd Meth | Stores the rounding of method, If the Sc Bond Rounding field is used in the rounding of interest calculations |
| Fx Rate | Defaults the exchange rate from the currency table, where the REPO transaction differs from the security currency. However, the user has the option of changing the rate that has been defaulted. |
| Mgn Deliv Instr | Allows input when a margin call is to be settled in securities. The delivery instructions must always signify a transfer of securities without any associated payment. |
| Supp Delivery | Controls the SWIFT delivery for a complete or partial change in security (substitution). This field in the security multi-value set and has the option YES or NO, Whereas NO is the default value. |
| Newcu Br Xrate | Maps to the Funds Transfer field when making a cash only margin call through the FUNDS.TRANSFER application. | Margin Portfolio | Specifies the portfolio to be used for valuations for non-customer REPO contracts |
| Init Margin Rate | Populates the Init Margin Amt field and is available only when the Trans Type is set to CASH and if a percentage is used to undervalue the securities |
| Drawdown Account | Indicates the account across which movements of cash is effected upon the value date of the contract |
| Prin Liq Acct | Identifies the account number where entries are made for the reimbursement of the principal at liquidation or maturity date |
| Prin Ben Bank 1 | Identifies the beneficiary bank that is to be used for the principal amount of a REPO contract at maturity or for a reverse REPO contract. It draws down when the customer has requested for external delivery of the proceeds of the transaction. |

| Mature At Sod | Specifies whether REPO must mature at the SOD of the maturity date. It is defaulted to YES, if the Process REPO Sod field in the REPO .PARAMETER application is set to either MATURITY or BOTH. The value in this field is mapped to the Mature At Sod field in the child MM.MONEY.MARKET contract. |
| Country Risk | Assists the asset management module, while determining risk analysis |
| Group Status | Determines if the REPO transaction must be considered for the netting of delivery Instructions. The below values are the available settings for this field: YES NO and NULL For INTERNAL or SBL trades (as set in Rt Deal Type ) this field defaults to NO and cannot be set to NET. |
| Br Agent | Determines the agent (DEAG, DEI1, DEI2..., REAG,REI1,REI2...) in MT540-MT543 messages and forms associated sub value with Br Agent Ac field. This field provides information on instructions to the depository. |
| Br Agent Ac | Determines the agent (DEAG, DEI1, DEI2..., REAG,REI1,REI2...) in MT540-MT543 messages and forms associated sub value with Br Agent field. This field provides information on instructions to the depository. |
| Counterparty Depo | Records which depository the counterparty is using. Any input to this field is mapped to the Broker Depo field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER record.This field is used to create settlement instructions for the clearing systems which has been setup within the Securities module of any particular bank. The value in the Br Def Depo field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the counterparty, is defaulted in this field provided the depo mentioned in the New Depo field has been setup in the SC.CLEARING.SYSTEM application. |
| Cpty Sec Depo Ac | Records which account number of the depository the counterparty is using. Any input to this field is mapped to the Br Sec Depot Ac field in the SECURITY.TRANSFER record. This field is used to create settlement instructions for clearing systems which has been setup within the Securities module of any particular bank. If The value in the Br Sec Depot Ac field in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY record of the counterparty, is defaulted in this field, provided the depo mentioned in the Counterparty Depo field has been setup in the SC.CLEARING.SYSTEM application. |
| Negative Rate | Defaults to YES, If the value in the Repo Rate field is negative. If the interest rate in the Repo Rate field is positive this field is set to NO. The value in this field is mapped to the Negative Rate field in the MM.MONEY.MARKET application. It is a no-input field. |
| Pset | Determines the place of settlement in MT540-MT543 messages |
| Cancel Mat Call | Cancels an unsettled margin call or maturity instructions.If a margin call was the last action, the associated SECURITY.TRANSFER or FUNDS.TRANSFER contracts are reversed. Whereas, this cannot be cancelled using this field, if a cash margin call has been through the MM.MONEY.MARKET application. If the last action was an entry of a maturity date for an open REPO, the maturity date is reset to 0.It can be YES, only if the last action was either the entry of a maturity date for an open contract or a cash or security margin call. Also, they cannot be cancelled, if the maturing SECURITY.TRANSFER records are generated. |
| Ft Trans Type | Maps to the Transaction Type field in the FUNDS.TRANSFER application. This is used while making a cash margin call using the FUNDS.TRANSFER application. |
| Activity Code | Holds the activity code(s) of the event(s) taking place. This is a multi-value field. |
| Activity Date | Holds the date(s) the activity(s) is or are scheduled for. This is a multi-value field. |
| Mapping Key | Holds the mapping key(s) associated with the message(s) being produced. This is a multi-value field. |
| Msg Ref | Holds reference number(s) of the message(s) produced and returned by APPLICATION.HANDOFF |
| Init Margin Amt | Populates only if the Trans Type is set to CASH and the Init Margin Rate field is set. This is the amount of initial margin that is related to the cash amount entered in the Principal Amount 1 field. |
| Margin Port Suffix | Defaults the value from the REPO .TYPE record. This is the suffix that is used to create the key for the margin portfolio. |
| Broker No | Defaults to the Broker Depo or Counterparty field, for customer REPO |
| Transaction Index | Defaults the value from the REPO .TYPE record |
| Transfer Charges | Ensures that there are no charges on the underlying SECURITY.TRANSFER deals. The transfer of securities under the REPO application are without charge. |
| Delivery Instr | Defaults the value from the REPO .TYPE record, although it can be overwritten with a valid entry in the SC.DEL.INSTR application |
| Sc Trans Type | Defines the transfer type that is used to include a security in the REPO contract and is dependent on the Transaction Index of the REPO .TYPE application used by the transaction. If the REPO contract is a reverse REPO - the Transaction Index , field which uses the transfer type TRI, is set to LOAN. If the REPO contract is REPO - the Transaction Index field, which uses the transfer type TRO, is set to DEPOSIT. |
| Sc Rev Trans Type | Defines the transfer type that is used to remove a security from the REPO contract and is dependant on the Transaction Index of the REPO .TYPE application used by the transaction. If the REPO contract is a reverse REPO - the Transaction Index , field which uses the transfer type TRO, is set to LOAN. If the REPO contract is REPO - the Transaction Index field, which uses the transfer type TRI, is set to DEPOSIT. |
| Interest Amount | Holds the total amount of REPO interest to be charged on this contract |
| Mm Int Basis | Assumes that the same value as the Interest Basis field and is mapped through to the MM.MONEY.MARKET contract |
| Mm Contract Id | Raises a MM.MONEY.MARKET deal, for the cash side of the REPO contract. The key to this deal is held in this field. |
| St Contract Id | Raises a SECURITY.TRANSFER deal for each security detailed on the REPO contract, in order to process the security side of the REPO contract |
| St Reverse Id | Raises a SECURITY.TRANSFER deal for each security detailed on the REPO contract, in order to process the security side of the REPO contract. When a substitution of securities is effected, a SECURITY.TRANSFER deal is raised to back out any securities that have been substituted. When the substitution is authorised, the keys to these contracts are held in this field. |
| St History Id | Raises a SECURITY.TRANSFER deal for each security detailed on the REPO contract, in order to process the security side of the REPO contract. When a substitution of securities is effected, the original transaction references for the SECURITY.TRANSFER deals are held in this field. The transaction references held in this field are no longer a part of the REPO contract and are held purely for information purposes. |
| St Unau Cont Id | Raises SECURITY.TRANSFER deals to effect the movement of the securities, when securities are defined in the REPO contract. The keys to of the SECURITY.TRANSFER deals, whose changes to the security information by the REPO contract are unauthorised, are held in this field. |
| St Unau Rev Id | Raises a SECURITY.TRANSFER deal to back out any securities that have been substituted, when a substitution of securities is effected. When the substitution is unauthorised, the keys to these contracts are held in this field. |
| Contract Status | Holds the current status of the REPO contract, as a three letter code INI - When the value date is in the future, but the delivery instructions for the near leg transfer of securities is issued based on the settings in the REPO .PARAMETER application. FWD - The contract is yet to reach value date. CUR - The contract is current, that is, between value date and maturity date. MAI - Where the maturity date is not reached, but the delivery instructions for the far leg for transfer of securities have been issued based on the settings in the REPO .PARAMETER application. LIQ - The contract has matured. |
| Ft Locref Name | Indicates the name of any local reference field setup in the FUNDS.TRANSFER application. This field forms part of an associated multi-value set along with the Ft Locref Data field. |
| Ft Locref Data | Accepts input of any data that the user may want to input in the local reference field setup in the FUNDS.TRANSFER application. The name of the local reference field appears in the Ft Locref Name field. This field forms part of an associated multi-value set along with the Ft Locref Name field. |
| Ft Margin Id | Contains a multi-valued list of keys of the authorised FUNDS.TRANSFER contracts relating to cash margin calls. This field is used only for cash margin calls when the Generate Ft field in the REPO .TYPE application is set to YES. |
| Rt Deal Type | Populates automatically upon entering a value in the Deal Type field. It contains the value in the Deal Type field in REPO .TYPE application. |
| Cash Hold Settle | Controls cash updates in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. This field allows input of either YES or NO. This field is editable, only if the Actual Settlement field is set to YES and Settle Method is set to US in the SC.PARAMETER record and if the Generate FT field in the REPO .TYPE application is set to YES. If this field is YES, the cash accounting uses the actual settlement. If REPO transaction with Cash Hold Settle field set to YES is authorised, the system creates a SC.SETTLEMENT record from the corresponding SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction. |
| Sec Hold Settle | Control the stock updates in the SC.SETTLEMENT application. This field allows the input of YES or NO. This field is editable, only if the Actual Settlement field is set to YES and Settle Method is set to US in the SC.PARAMETER record and if the Generate FT field in the REPO .TYPE application is set to YES. If REPO transaction with Sec Hold Settle field set to YES is authorised, the system creates a SC.SETTLEMENT record from the corresponding SECURITY.TRANSFER transaction. |
| Cust Act Susp Cat | Captures the suspense amount of the customer. This field is used as a category reference for the customer. The value is picked up from the SC.PARAMETER which holds a similar field in it. The values are defaulted from the SC.PARAMETER fields. The value in this field must be a valid entry in CATEGORY . |
| Brok Act Susp Cat | Captures the suspense amount of the broker. This field is used as a category reference for the broker. The value is picked up from the SC.PARAMETER application, which holds a similar field in it. The values are defaulted from the SC.PARAMETER fields. The value in this field must be a valid entry in CATEGORY . |
| Misc Act Susp Cat | Captures the miscellaneous suspense amount. The value is picked up from the SC.PARAMETER application, which holds a similar field in it. The values are defaulted from the SC.PARAMETER fields. The value in this field must be a valid entry in CATEGORY . |
| Auto Cust Sett | Enables the automatic settlement of the nominal and cash to the customers who have contractual agreements with the bank. This value is defaulted to YES, if the Auto Cust Sett field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY file is set to YES. The automatic settlement can be turned off at transaction level, though it has been turned on in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. If the Auto Cust Sett field is NULL in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application, this field is defaulted to NO. This field is editable, only if Cash Hold Settle or Sec Hold Settle is set to YES. If Bank Portfolio is a dealer book and the Cash Hold Settle or Sec Hold Settle fields are set to YES this field must be set to YES. This field allows only YES, NO or NULL. Where, NULL is equivalent to NO. |
| Auto Brok Sett | Enables the automatic settlement of the nominal and cash to the brokers who have contractual agreements with the bank. This value is defaulted to YES, if the Auto brok Sett field in CUSTOMER.SECURITY file is set to YES. The automatic settlement can be turned off at transaction level, though it has been turned on in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application. If the Auto brok Sett field is NULL in the CUSTOMER.SECURITY application, this field is defaulted to NO. This field is editable, only if Cash Hold Settle or Sec Hold Settle is set to YES. If Bank Portfolio is a dealer book and the Cash Hold Settle or Sec Hold Settle fields are set to YES this field must be set to YES. This field allows only YES, NO or NULL. Where, NULL is equivalent to NO. |
| Intraday Trade | Indicates intra-day REPO deal with same maturity day. System allows both Value date and Repurchase date to be the same. The Start Time and End Time fields are enabled only if this field is set to Yes |
| Start Time | Holds the start time of the REPO intra-day deal. The time format must be HH:MM:SS |
| End Time | Holds the settlement time of the REPO intra-day deal. The input in the End Time field is only allowed when the Start Time field has a value. This field is not mandatory, If set to No , the system calculates interest amount for one full day If set to Yes, the system calculates the duration of the intra-day deal. The time format must be HH:MM:SS |
| Duration | Indicates the duration of the contract in minutes. The system automatically updates this field based on the value in the Start Time and End Time field. The value in this field is rounded “up” to the nearest value |
| Sys Int Amt | Holds the interest amount of the Intra-day Repo contract |

The REPO application enables the user to automatically re-fix long term REPOs, on a re-fixing date. Re-fixing is a process, where the deal rate changes to a new value, during the life of a REPO. It occurs in a specified period, which is known as the start of REPO.

The user can link the term trade to a periodic interest table (which holds sufficient logic to handle interpolation of rates), using a valid PI key. The Pi Int Key field holds a unique identification number and indicates if the REPO contract is a floating rate trade or a fixed rate REPO.

When a floating rate contract is created, value date gets defaulted in the Rate Ch Date field. If PI key is not defined, this field becomes NULL. If PI key is defined, this field defaults to the current date. The spread is captured from the Int Spread field, which acts as a modifier of the interest rate. It derives the interest rate from the periodic interest table. This rate is used for overall rate and REPO interest calculations. If it is positive, the spread is added and if it is negative, the spread is subtracted to arrive at the REPO rate.

> **⚠️ Note:** Interest rate derived from the periodic interest key is adjusted with the value in the Int Spread field and updated in the Repo Rate field. The Repo Rate is then linked to the value in the Interest Rate field, in the generated child MM.

The Rate Selection field determines the rate from the PERIODIC.INTEREST table. The following are the two options allowed:

- BID (bid rate)
- OFFER (offer rate)

When BID is selected, the bid rate is picked and when OFFER is selected, offer rate is picked for REPO rate calculation. The PERIODIC.INTEREST application is shown in the below screenshot.

The Rate Selection field picks the rate from PERIODIC.INTEREST . The next rate change is applied to the contract based on the value specified in the Next Rate Ch Date field. If the field is left blank, the frequency specified in the Int Term field is returned and defaulted. The value in the Int Term field is then populated in the Rate Ch Date field. The user can input the value for only new contracts and subsequent updates are done by the Rp Online Job.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Next Rate Ch Date value must be greater than the Value Date / Rate Ch Date / Today fields and lesser than the Maturity Date field.

If the Maturity Date falls before the Next Rate Ch Date , the system replaces the Next Rate Ch Date with the Maturity Date . The accrued interest is capitalised (added to principal), if the Cap Int field is set to YES and whenever the contract is rolled in the child MM contract. If the Cap Int is set to NO, the accrued interest is paid and a new interest is calculated in the Principal Amount 1 field at a new rate, for the next interest period. The Auto Rollover field is a no input field and gets defaulted to Y, when the Rate Ch Date field holds a value.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Pi Int Key is null, the Int Term, Int Spread, Rate Selection and Next Rate Ch Date fields are not editable.

The Maturity Date field is mapped to the Final Maturity Date field, in the child MM contract. When the Rate Ch Date field populates a date, the REPO Interest field automatically generates a value using REPO rate and term as Rate Ch Date until the Next Rate Ch Date . The Principal Amount 2 field remains blank, until the rate is fixed for the final period. The principal amount is calculated only when Next Rate Ch Date is equal to Maturity Date . The Fwd Settlemnt and Fwd Price fields remain static and get updated only when the final rate fixing takes place. The Fwd Settlemnt amount is same as the Principal Amount 2 amount.

When the REPO contract is created, the user needs to run COB till the contract reaches its maturity date. For all the subsequent rate change dates that are crossed (while reaching the maturity date), the user can expect a change in the REPO rate of the contract, this is based on the PI table. The user can either roll the interest accrued during the fixed period or settle the interest accrued. The MM.MONEY.MARKET application is shown in the below screenshot.

The MM.MONEY.MARKET application allows the user to capture a floating rate deal. The logic associated with this type of transaction is replicated in the REPO application with the required fields and mapped to the underlying child MM.MONEY.MARKET contract, generated through the CMM.

The underlying MM.MONEY.MARKET contract is a fixed type, in which maturity date is fixing date and final maturity date is maturity date. Here, the Auto Rollover field is set to Yes. This update of the REPO Rate on REPO contract is performed as part of online stage of batch processing.

When the Interest Basis used is S, the Repo Interest field is editable and the user can change the default value. The input value is compared with the default value,

- If the changed value exceeds 5 % of the default value, an error message is displayed.
- If the variance is greater than 1% but below 5%, then an override message is displayed.
- If the variance is less than 1 %, no warning is displayed.

When the Interest Basis is set to S, the value in the Principal Amount 2 field (if any) is cleared. If the user modifies the value in the Repo Interest field, the Principal Amount 2 is recalculated. If the user does not change the value in the REPO Interest field after changing the Interest Basis to S, the Principal Amount 2 is recalculated upon validating of the record.

The Accrued Int Amt field allows the user to override the default value that is populated from SECURITY.MASTER . This gives greater flexibility when a predefined interest basis does not equate to the exact amount of interest, required for settlement. The existing calculation formulas are maintained such that, the revised amount is reflected in the Total Settlemnt.1 field.

Any difference observed between the accrued interest calculated from the SECURITY.MASTER record and the Accrued Int Amt entered manually, requires manual intervention. The Interest Basis S is not be allowed for open REPOs.

The exchange rate to be used for such transactions is displayed in the Fx Rate field. The rate defaults from the currency table, however the user has the option to change the rate defaulted by the system. With the calculation link set to Yes, once the foreign exchange amount is calculated, the cash or security is automatically populated in the corresponding field.

There are two types of REPO or Reso contracts - bilateral and trilateral. The two versions that are supplied with the REPO application allows these two types of transaction.

- REPO, BREPOinp defaults Bilateral into the Deal Type field and the Third Party field is not displayed.
- REPO, TREPOinp defaults Trilateral into the Deal Type field and displays the Third Party field.
- A third type of contract is the customer contract. The majority of such contracts are Reso.
- REPO, CREPOinp defaults Bilateral into the Deal Type field and displays the relevant customer fields, hiding the bank fields.

When a REPO trade is done, securities move out from the Bank Portfolio to the Margin Portfolio of the Counterparty . In a Reso, securities flow into the Margin Portfolio from the portfolio of the Counterparty , which is usually not maintained by the bank. For the forward leg of a REPO transaction, the SECURITY.TRANSFER record is created on the Value Date or n number of days before the Value Date , depending on the value of n that has been set in either the Days Delivery field of the REPO transaction or Days Prior Event field in the RP-0140 record in the EB . ACTIVITY application.

The value in the Days Delivery field in the REPO transaction is prioritised over any value set in the Days Prior Event field in the RP-0140 record in the EB.ACTIVITY application. The SECURITY.POSITION gets updated upon authorising the SECURITY.TRANSFER record (the authorisation happens automatically when the REPO transaction is authorised). If the Update Sc Pos Sod field in the REPO .PARAMETER application is set to YES, the processing of the SECURITY.TRANSFER application and the update of the SECURITY.POSITION file takes place as explained below.

The SECURITY.TRANSFER application and the resulting SECURITY.POSITION records pertaining to the forward leg of the REPO transaction are created immediately upon authorising the REPO transaction, regardless of the Value Date or the values in either the Days Delivery field of the REPO transaction or Days Prior Event field in the RP-0140 record in the EB.ACTIVITY application.

The SECURITY.TRANSFER record pertaining to the maturity leg of the REPO transaction is created as per the Value Date or n number of days before the Value Date depending on the value of n that has been set in either the Days Delivery field of the REPO transaction or Days Prior Event field in the RP-0140 record in the EB.ACTIVITY application. The value in the Days Delivery field in the REPO transaction takes priority over any value set in the Days Prior Event field in the RP-0140 record in the EB.ACTIVITY application. However, the SECURITY.POSITION record is not updated until the maturity date. The purpose of generating the SECURITY.TRANSFER record is to only produce the related delivery messages.

Since the SECURITY.TRANSFER record is created (but SECURITY.POSITIONS are updated only on the maturity date of the REPO), it is necessary to maintain a list of security transfer IDs for which the position needs to be updated. To do this, a live file RP.SCTR.SCHEDULES is maintained. The ID of the records in this file is the date. The system records the IDs of all the SECURITY.TRANSFER records for which the position needs to be updated on a particular date.

If the user inputs a negative interest rate in the Repo Rate field, it changes the figures that are calculated and defaulted in the Principal Amount 2 field. The negative REPO rate calculation is shown in the below screenshot.

The cash management postings to the Nostro account are also changed in line with negative rate characteristics. The maturing interest that initially was a deposit, is now listed as a debit on the Nostro account, as the interest is negative. Conversely, a deposit is reflected as a credit on the Nostro account.

| Rp Cash Xch | Indicates the exchange rate used between the security currency and the local currency |
| Rp Net Lcy | Indicates the REPO net cash amount in the local currency |


##### Accounting

Accounting is available for view through enquires at unauthorised stage. If the value date for the accounting is greater than the bank date the accounting is generated as forward entries. A COB job like Cob Sc Group Trades Accounting , deletes the forward entries and raises a real accounting entry, when the value date is reached.

A short sale of securities can be linked to a REPO transaction, upon booking the securities delivered in a short sale, posted as a liability and backed by a borrow in REPO transaction. The result of the assessment that is based on the type of REPO, is recorded in balance sheet accounts. The main idea is to book the deal which is done using securities received as collateral from counterparty and deliver to other counterparty in short sale.

The Repo Reference field in the SEC.TRADE application allows the user to give the REPO ID in the trade. Immediately after the REPO deal is entered, the system raises entries for the principal amount in the categories mentioned in the REPO .TYPE application. A short sale trade is done subsequently with the REPO ID linked to it and if there is any difference in the price between SEC.TRADE and REPO , it goes to PL category mentioned in the REPO .TYPE application.

An instance of a short sale backed by a REPO is shown below. It also illustrates the entries when there is a difference in price between REPO and SEC.TRADE .

The above five highlighted fields in the REPO .TYPE application, accept the internal account category codes. If the REPO transaction is input for this REPO .TYPE and the transaction index is LOAN, the following accounting entries are raised from the REPO .

The DR and CR categories are defined in the Srt Cr Cat and the Srt Col Cat fields, to the extent of Principal Amount 1 .

The Rp Reference field in the SEC.TRADE application within the customer multi-value set is used to capture the REPO contract ID. Once the SEC.TRADE record is committed, additional entries are raised from SEC.TRADE to the category defined in the Srt Cr Cat and Srt Col Cat fields of the underlying REPO .TYPE record. If the price of the REPO contract and the SEC.TRADE transaction are different, the additional entries are raised to the extent of the profit or loss realised in the transaction. It is to be raised to the categories defined in the Srt Loss Cat or Srt Pr Cat (based on the loss or profit respectively) and Srt Com Cat fields.

A Repo is a Sale and Repurchase agreement, where the securities are sold to a counterparty at a fixed price. The seller has a commitment to repurchase the securities at a predetermined price at a fixed point of time in the future. The price difference are therefore Interest to deposit (or loan if reverse repo) and maybe defined as cash price (the buy back amount) or as a rate.


##### Workflow

The user can process the REPO Contract by using the below workflow:

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Capture Repo Deals . |
| Capture Repo Deals | Select the Repo option from the Choose Repo Deal field drop-down and click the Launch icon. |
| Repurchase Agreement | In the Repurchase Agreement tab, enter values in the following mandatory fields: Trade Date Issue Date Repurchase Date Agreement Click the Security Assignment tab and enter values in the following fields: Own Book Portfolio Security Code Nominal Click the Settlements tab, enter settlements details, such as, the Drawdown account and Liquidation account for Principal and Interest amount. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal. |

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Capture Repo Deals . |
| Capture Repo Deals | Select the Reverse Repo option from the Choose Repo Deal field drop-down and click the Launch icon. |
| Reverse Repo Agreement | In the Reverse Repo Agreement tab, enter values in the following mandatory fields: Trade Date Issue Date Repurchase Date Agreement Click the Security Assignment tab and enter values in the following fields: Own Book Portfolio Security Code Nominal Click the Settlements tab, enter settlements details, such as the Drawdown account and Liquidation account for Principal and Interest amount. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal. |

This enquiry allows the user to verify, authorise or delete the Repo deals booked by the Dealer.

To authorise a Repo deal, follow the below steps:

### 7.7  Stock Borrow or Lending


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact has the ability to process the stock borrow lending transactions for customer and own book positions.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrual Amt*, *Accrual Date*, *Accrue Fee*, *Actual Settlement*, *Auto Brok Sett*, *Auto Cust Sett*, *Auto Cust Settle*, *Bank Portfolio* ... +60 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact has the ability to process the stock borrow lending transactions for customer and own book positions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following fields are configured in the SC.PARAMETER application to control the contractual and actual processing of stock borrow and lending in the REPO application.

- The Actual Settlement field and its associated setup fields
- The Settle Method field


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the process of stock borrow or lending feature in Temenos Transact .


##### Illustrating Main Trade Flow

If the customer 1 sells short 100 IBM shares through the SEC.TRADE application, the option is required to cover this position through a borrow rather than a closeout through a further SEC.TRADE .

- Market trade 1 - borrow 100 shares
- Internal trade 2 - lend 100 shares to customer 1
- Both trade 1 and 2 go through wash book as a control. That is, trades 1 and 2 are two-sided: Trade 1 (T1) - Borrow to wash with an external counterparty or a broker Trade 2 (T2) - Lend to an internal customer with portfolio as a counterparty or a broker
- T1 and T2 are independent transactions. There may be multiple T1s against multiple T2s. However, there is direct link is not available within the system. Manual control ensures that the positions borrowed offset the positions lent, that is, the control account (wash position) must be at 0. The booking of a T2 is not dependent on the booking of a T1 and vice versa.

If the details in the above example are used, the user needs to cover customer 1 short position. The flow of the required trades are as follows:

The customer position is not moved as a result of T2, that is, the customer position remain short (with a borrowed position), if they are short and to be covered by the borrow.

Trade 1 produces an agent or a depository instruction in MT540 or MT542 format. Generally, this is an Free of payment (FOP), but this may also be a Delivery versus payment (DVP) transaction.

Depository messaging is not required for T2 as this is an internal trade and the user can only switch between the security positions wash - customer.

The T2 booking details not only hold the customer details, but also hold the portfolio (where long and short portfolios are held for the customers) details.

> **⚠️ Note:** There is link between T1 and T2.

A customer may return 100 shares on T2 and another customer may borrow 100 with another T2. There is no requirement for a return T1. In this case, the positions may not necessarily be net out, whereas, they may be maintained as a pending position between T2 and T1.

Customer X returns 100 and customer Y borrows 60. The own book or wash control account has 40 positions, which are manually closed by the users through T1 or T2 transactions.

As all depository messaging are at T1, the T1 trades move the stocks. Typically, the traded borrows and loans always offset. The wash control portfolio indicates the differences due to the presence of a position. However, there may be settlement differences, which are monitored through normal settlement procedures. These differences arise if T1 is unsettled, although T2 has been settled contractually or actually (using Auto Cus Settle). In case of multiple borrows making up a borrowed position, T2 returns are received with instructions that, which position must be returned.


##### Entering a Stock Borrow Lend Contract

The fields related to stock borrow or lending (SBL) contract in the REPO application are explained in the below table.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Br Account No | Allows the account postings of the required SBL transaction in conjunction with the amended Br Account No field. |
| New Cu Acct No | Controls the account postings for SBL transactions in conjunction with the amended Br Account No field. This functionality is controlled by the following field settings in the REPO.TYPE application: Deal Type - Internal or Stock Borrow Lend Generate FT Transaction - Yes After the user makes these changes, the postings of the required accounting entries are made. The accounting entries to be populated in this field are linked to the portfolio used on the contract and are specified in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application. This field allows all account types and is not restricted to NOSTRO accounts. The updation of this field is controlled by the specific Deal Type used in conjunction with the settings in the SEC.ACC.MASTER application and the account specified in the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application. |
| Drawdown Account , Prin Liq Acct and Int Liq Acct | If the Generate FT Transaction field in the REPO.TYPE application is set to Yes, these fields become display only fields. |
| Bank Portfolio | Allows the user to define a bank portfolio (own book) or a customer portfolio. |
| Margin Portfolio | Holds the default standard portfolio (-1), which defaults from the Counterparty field. This functionality is driven by the REPO.TYPE application and is available only for internal trades. Also, this functionality is required to ensure if the Security Position of the bank is updated correctly. |
| Group Status | Allows no input in this field and the value is defaulted to No, if the value in the Deal Type field is either Internal or Stock Borrow Lend in the REPO.TYPE application. |
