### 8.5  Currency Interest Rate Swap Deal Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A currency interest rate swap is similar to interest rate swap, where two streams of interest payments to be exchanged are in different currencies. In addition, exchange and re-exchange of principal amount happens at the beginning and end of the deal between the counterparties. Interest rates can be...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose Swap Deals*, *Liquidation Mode*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A currency interest rate swap is similar to interest rate swap, where two streams of interest payments to be exchanged are in different currencies. In addition, exchange and re-exchange of principal amount happens at the beginning and end of the deal between the counterparties. Interest rates can be fixed or floating. The interest payment schedules can be generated from a frequency or manually defined. The principal amount can vary during the life of the swap, according to the user definable payment schedule.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Swap contract captures the customer ID, swap type, dealer details, trade date, maturity date, asset and liability legs. The asset and liability side of the contracts are captured in separate tabs. Additionally, settlement instructions are captured along with the contract input.

An illustration of currency interest rate swap, when inputting and validating a record is shown below:

An illustration of swap schedules (for both asset and liabilities leg) built for the above transaction is as follows:


##### Interest Rate Schema

SWAP module supports the following interest rate variations:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Fixed Rate | The interest rate is fixed at the time of the contract input. This is applicable throughout the life of the contract. However, specifying the Rate Reset (RR) schedule enables to change the rate on an individual contract basis. |
| Floating Rate | The interest rate is reset based on a frequency, usually the period falling between 1 and 12 months. It uses a Periodic Interest (PI) rate key for the appropriate floating rate. 03LIBOR to differentiate it from the fixed rate. A spread can be applied to the rate before the interest calculation. Cap and/or floor rates can also be specified to check the applied interest rate for any errors (CAP and FLOOR options are different and are not supported in SWAP module). |

The module also supports the following interest rate or amounts and the downstream processing:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Negative Rate | Negative interest rates can be in any of the forms of fixed rate and floating rate with or without spread. This can be defined in Negative Rates field in the SWAP application. This is a no change field, which defaults to Null and is similar to No. Liquidation Mode field is set to Automatic to allow negative rates. The user cannot input negative rates for Annuity Payments (AP) schedules. |
| Fixed Interest Amount | The interest amount can be fixed by specifying an Interest Payment (IP) schedule with an associated amount. This is useful when there is a requirement to maintain the same interest amount for every interest period throughout the life of the contract. |


##### Interest Day Basis

The interest day basis C (366/366), C2 (366/366) and D (360/366), in addition to the regular market basis are available in the Temenos Transact Swap module.

The interest calculations differ when the calculation period falls as part of a non-leap year and leap year. It also differs when the year period exists between C (known as the ISDA method) and C2 (known as the AFB method).

- For the C calculation – The period is broken down into actual years.
- For the C2 calculation – The year starts at the maturity date and works backwards.

If February 29 exists in that period then it counts it as 366 days, otherwise, it is 365. If the period lasts more than a year, subsequent calculations are made for each yearly period.

| C | C2 |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of days | Days in year | Interest | Number of days | Days in year | Interest |
| 10 | 365 | 315.07 | 91 | 366 | 2859.29 |
| 81 | 366 | 2545.08 | - | - | - |
| Total Interest | 2860.15 | Total Interest | 2859.29 |  |  |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Execute Trade (SWAP)
- Interest Rate Swap Deal Processing
- Treasury Processes

It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of interest payments over a period of time and or to lock in a profit or minimise the loss to offset a Loan or Deposit contract on bank book.


##### Workflow

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

To enter a Currency Interest Rate Swap Hedge deal, perform the following steps:

1. Capture Swap Deals .
2. Select the CIRS Hedge Deal option from the Choose Swap Deals field drop-down and then click the Launch icon.
3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Principal Account with Bank Account Address Agreement Maturity Date
4. Click the Settlement tab and enter settlement details.
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

To enter a Currency Interest Rate Swap Trade deal, perform the following steps:

1. Capture Swap Deals .
2. Select the CIRS Trade Deal option from the Choose Swap Deals field drop-down and then click the Launch icon.
3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Principal Account with Bank Account Address Agreement Maturity Date
4. Click the Settlement tab and enter settlement details.
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon to submit the deal.

### 8.6  Day Convention and Adjustment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The day convention feature determines the processing of schedules that fall on non-working or non-business days. The module supports Preceding, Following and Modified Following day conventions, which are applicable on the following schedules:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The day convention feature determines the processing of schedules that fall on non-working or non-business days. The module supports Preceding, Following and Modified Following day conventions, which are applicable on the following schedules:

- Principal Exchange (PX)
- Principal Re-Exchange (RX)
- Interest Payment (IP)
- Principal Increase (PI)
- Principal Decrease (PD)
- Rate Reset (RR)

| Day Convention | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Preceding | If the schedule date falls on a non-business day, the processing of the schedule is adjusted to the preceding business day. |
| Following | If the schedule date falls on a non-business day, the processing of the schedule is adjusted to the following business day. |
| Modified Following | Similar to Following but with an exception given below: If the adjusted following business day falls over to next month, then it works same as preceding. |

The module also supports date adjustment methods (Value and Period), which determines the period for interest amount calculation.

| Date Adjustment | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Value | The interest amount for the original period remains unchanged, though the interest schedule is processed either earlier or later. |
| Period | The interest amount is recalculated in accordance with the reduced or extended period because of the applied day convention. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the working of day convention and adjustment.


##### Day Convention Methods

The SWAP module supports the below day convention methods and are applicable for Principal Exchange (PX), Principal Re-Exchange (RX), Interest Payment (IP), Principal Increase (PI), Principal Decrease (PD) and Rate Reset (RR) schedules. The user can enter day convention in SWAP application.

If a particular schedule date for processing falls on a non-working day, it is processed on the preceding business day.

If a particular schedule date for processing falls on a non-working day, it is processed on the next business day.

If a particular schedule date for processing falls on a non-working day and with the day convention set as ‘Following’, the processing date is modified to preceding day (when the next business day falls in the following month).


##### Adjustment Methods

The module also supports the following date adjustment methods. The user can enter the date adjustment in SWAP application.

The interest period or effective date of the schedule remains unchanged even if there is a change in the settlement or processing date due to applicability of the day convention.

If the interest payment schedule is due on 31st of March (which happens to be a non-business day in the respective currency), the processing date moves to next business day because of the applicability of day convention. However, the interest period is considered only until 31st March.

The period for calculation of interest also changes in line with the processing or settlement date according to the day convention. As mentioned in the above example, the interest period is considered until the next business day in line with the settlement date.


##### Payment Netting

When exchange of interest payments are in the same currency and with the same settlement date, the option to net the payments is available.

- If the amount net is payable, the payment message is generated.
- If the amount net is receivable, an advice to receive a message is generated.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Day Convention and Adjustment feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Day Convention and Adjustment feature.

### 8.7  Deposit Deal Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The deposit product is a single leg transaction where the principal is involved. The interest is due to or from the client in arrears, depending on positive or negative rate of interest. Interest rates can be fixed or floating. The interest payment schedules can be generated from a fixed frequency o...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Liquidation Mode*, *Negative Rates*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The deposit product is a single leg transaction where the principal is involved. The interest is due to or from the client in arrears, depending on positive or negative rate of interest. Interest rates can be fixed or floating. The interest payment schedules can be generated from a fixed frequency or manually defined. The principal amount varies during the life of borrowing, according to the user definable payment schedule (accreting or amortisation).


#### 🔧 Working With

The deposit contract captures the customer ID, swap type, dealer details, trade date, maturity date and liability leg. A separate tab facilitates capturing of liability side details of the contract and settlement instructions or details.

An illustration of deposit, when inputting and validating a record is as follows:

An illustration of Swap Schedule (SWAP.SCHEDULE) enquiry for the above swap contract is as follows:


##### Interest Rate Schema

SWAP module supports the following interest rate variations:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Fixed Rate | The interest rate (also known as Swap Rate) is fixed at the time of the contract input, which is applicable throughout the life of the contract. However, specifying the Rate Reset (RR) schedule enables to change the rate on an individual contract basis. |
| Floating Rate | The interest rate is reset, based on a frequency (usually the period falling between 1 to 12 months). It uses a Periodic Interest (PI) rate key for the appropriate floating rate. For example, 03LIBOR, for rate resetting as per the given frequency and to differentiate it from the fixed rate. A spread can be applied to the rate before the interest calculation. Cap and/or floor rates can also be specified to check the applied interest rate for any errors (CAP and FLOOR options are different and are not supported under SWAP module). |

The module also supports the following interest rates or amounts and the downstream processing:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Negative Rate | Negative interest rates can be in the form of fixed and floating rate with or without spread or interest amounts. This can be defined in Negative Rates field in the SWAP application. This is a no change field, which defaults to Null and is similar to No. The Liquidation Mode field is set to Automatic to allow negative rates. The user cannot input negative rates for Annuity Payments (AP) schedules. |
| Fixed Interest Amount | The interest amount can be fixed by specifying an Interest Payment (IP) schedule with an associated amount. This is useful when there is a requirement to maintain the same interest amount for every interest period throughout the life of the contract. |


##### Interest Day Basis

The interest day basis C (366/366), C2 (366/366) and D (360/366), in addition to the regular market basis are available in the Temenos Transact SWAP module.

The interest calculations differ when the calculation period falls as part of a non-leap year and leap year. It also differs when the year period exists between C (known as the ISDA method) and C2 (known as the AFB method).

- For the C calculation – The period is broken down into actual years.
- For the C2 calculation – The year starts at the maturity date and works backwards.

If February 29 exists in that period, then it counts it as 366 days, otherwise, it is 365. If the period lasts more than a year, subsequent calculations are made for each yearly period.

| C | C2 | Number of days | Days in year | Interest | Number of days | Days in year | Interest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 365 | 315.07 | 91 | 366 | 2859.29 |  |  |
| 81 | 366 | 2545.08 | - | - | - |  |  |
| Total Interest | 2860.15 | Total Interest | 2859.29 |  |  |  |  |

- Execute Trade (SWAP)

### 8.8  Future Schedules


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *All future life cycle events of a swap transaction are recorded and stored in a file.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Asset Date Frequency*, *Asset Interest Set Date*, *Liab*, *Liability Interest Set Date*, *Liablity Inter*, *Notional*, *e*, *i* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

All future life cycle events of a swap transaction are recorded and stored in a file.

SWAP.SCHEDULES is a live file that records data of the unprocessed schedules for a swap contract falling on different schedule date. The recorded data includes the activity triggered from a Delivery viewpoint. When a swap contract is amended, the SWAP.SCHEDULES table record for the contract is deleted and rebuilt. When the schedule is processed, the related SWAP.SCHEDULES table record is removed.

An extensive set of SWAP.SCHEDULE.TYPE records are released with the Temenos Transact SWAP module. These give the flexibility and capability to meet many requirements of a Swap transaction.


#### 🔧 Working With

All schedules are processed online and at Close of Business (COB), except for Interest Payment (IP) and Annuity Payment (AP) schedules, which are due today. In the latter case, these schedules are only processed at COB.

Following are the standard schedule types available in Temenos Transact and the rules surrounding input of different schedule types:

PX is a one off schedule in which no amount or rate is allowed. The principal amount remains Notional with Yes in SWAP.BALANCES , until PX schedule is processed on the contract. With PX event specified on the contract, the Notional field in SWAP.BALANCES file is set to No.

These variations are allowed in swap contract:

- PX at start and Re-exchange Principal (RX) at maturity on both asset and liability sides
- No PX or RX
- PX and RX on asset side only (exceptional as warning is displayed)
- PX and RX on liability side only (exceptional as warning is displayed)

Interest amount is mandatory, if neither rate nor rate key is specified on the contract. This schedule performs final accrual and corrects the interest amount (if required).

Multiple IP schedules are allowed provided there is no frequency attached to them. These schedules can also have associated amounts.

Lead Lag Settlements

The settlement date of interest amounts for swaps can lead or lag behind the interest period end date by several days, including working days.

Swaps (IRS) allow settlement dates that differ from the period end dates. For each interest period, users are allowed to define the actual settlement date for each leg. This can differ from the period end date, while settlement amounts remain the same pertaining to that interest period.

The Asset Interest Set Date and Liab i lity Interest Set Date are required to store interest settlement date corresponding to the interest period.

A value is entered in the Asset Interest Set Date or Liablity Inter e st Set Date , when the Asset Date Frequency or Date or Frequency has a single date (for example, 20160915) and not when it has a frequency (for example, 20160915M0315).

The value input cannot be backdated, and needs to meet the following criteria:

- Be a standard Temenos Transact date
- Greater than the contract value date
- Greater than interest period end date and interest settlement date of any prior interest schedule
- Lesser than interest period end date and interest settlement date of any later interest schedule

If a settlement date is specified that is not a working day according to the relevant business centres, an override is generated.

> **⚠️ Note:** If a date is specified in Asset Interest Set Date or Liability Interest Set Date for an interest period, it overrides the settlement date implied by Asset Date Frequency or Date or Frequency. It is not necessary to specify Asset Interest Set Date or Liability Interest Set Date for an interest period and it is acceptable to override for some interest periods but not for others. The Asset Interest Set Date or Liability Interest Set Date cannot be modified by any date rules specified in Adjustment in both asset and liability leg.

In RR schedule, amount cannot be entered and schedule is not processed until a rate is entered. The schedule updates current rate on the contract and rate fields in the SWAP.BALANCES record.

| Deal | PI | PIN |
|---|---|---|
| Swap with Principal Exchange (PX and Principal Re-Exchange RX) | The increase causes actual movements of cash across Nostro and customer accounts | Causes cash movement |
| Swap without Principal Exchange (PX and Principal Re-Exchange RX) | The increase is notional and there are no movements of cash | No cash movement |

| Deal | PD | PDN |
|---|---|---|
| Swap with Principal Exchange (PX and Principal Re-Exchange (RX | The decrease causes actual movements of cash across nostro and customer accounts | Causes cash movement |
| Swap without Principal Exchange (PX and Principal Re-Exchange (RX | The decrease is notional – there are no movements of cash | No cash movement |

- Amount is mandatory and no rate is allowed in PM schedule.
- Amount is always payable regardless of asset or liability leg.

- Amount is mandatory and no rate is allowed in RV schedule.
- Amount is always receivable regardless of asset or liability leg.

- An RX schedule is to re-exchange the principal at the end of contract duration.
- The RX schedule is not allowed, if neither PX nor Issue Price (IS) is previously defined.
- It is a one-off schedule and no amount or rate is allowed.
- It re-exchanges the principal outstanding on the SWAP.BALANCES record and changes either asset or liability status to MAT.
- If there is a PX schedule, presence of RX schedule is mandatory.

It is a one-off schedule and it must have either amount or rate specified. Similar to PX schedule, even IS schedule requires Notional field in SWAP.BALANCES to be set as No. It is similar to the drawdown issue price in Loans and Deposits. The issue price is expressed as a percentage (0-500) of the nominal or flat amount. It can be below or above 100% of the nominal amount. The final drawdown issue price is the net of any charges and/or fees.

The AP schedule is similar to the annuity in mortgage. It uses the standard repayment calculation routine to work out a theoretical repayment amount. If amount is not entered, the theoretical amount is used. Otherwise, the amount entered needs to be greater than or equal to the theoretical amount.

A PX schedule is specified at the beginning of the contract to generate the principal movement. Otherwise, the principal remains Notional.

There are no Tasks available for Future Schedules feature.

Swap Schedules

This enquiry fetches the details of schedules for a specific swap contract. To launch this enquiry, the transaction reference number is a mandatory criteria.

### 8.9  Group Fixing or Floating Rate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The SWAP module provides the functionality to perform fixing up of floating rates. Group fixing is grouped into a semi or fully automatic operation, without the need to manually review each trade.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ST.EOD.GROUP.FIX`, `ST.GROUP.FIX`, `ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMATER`, `ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Refixing*, *As Rr Process Date*, *Asset Current Rate*, *Currency*, *Effective Date*, *Error Log*, *Fixing List*, *Fixing Rate* ... +16 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The SWAP module provides the functionality to perform fixing up of floating rates. Group fixing is grouped into a semi or fully automatic operation, without the need to manually review each trade.

ST.GROUP.FIX application helps consolidate swap trades that matches the user specified parameters for group fixing operation.

A record needs to be created in ST.GROUP.FIX application for each rate fixing operation. This record contains the criteria to group the contracts which are due for fixing the rate. Based on an option, the rate fixing takes place immediately or using an online service, whenever required.


#### 🔧 Working With

Trades matching certain user-specified parameters are fixed using the ST.GROUP.FIX application. This application allows the group fixing (also known as Rate Reset) operation to be run intraday through a service, and rerun with another rate. For example, in cases, where wrong rates are used.

The ST.GROUP.FIX application provides an interface for the user to select the swap trades to be fixed and execute the fixing operation on authorisation. A group fixing operation must be authorised for execution, as it involves changes to the transactional data.

When creating group rate fixing requests, various parameters are specified (For example, instrument, instrument type, currency, rate fixing code and effective date) along with operational parameters (For example, whether a report is necessary). This application automatically detects trades that require a rate reset and sets the rate accordingly.

When a spread rate is defined, the fixing operation adds this to the fixing rate to derive the actual fixing rate. This is needed for cases where a coupon with a floating rate is fixed, such as LIB3M + 0.5%.

The fixing operation creates an individual Rate Reset (RR) schedule record for each effective date with the fixing rate (which includes the spread component, if defined for that trade).

If a frequency code is input in the RR Schedule Date field, the fixing program creates the next RR schedule, after advancing the date to be that of the next reset date as determined by the frequency.

| Schedule | Date | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| RR | 20181228M0328 | 5.4% |

In SWAP application Liability Current Rate (or alternatively Asset Current Rate ) field is updated with the new rate of 5.4%. An example of ST.GROUP.FIX is shown below:

The instrument type defines the application, for example, SWAP or FRA .

The effective date is the date on which the new rate takes effect. This is not necessarily the date on which the fixing operation happens. Typically, fixing occurs two days before or on the day the new rate takes effect, depending on the currency.

The ST.GROUP.FIX record specifies whether the swap trade becomes authorised or unauthorised after execution of fixing operation.

The rate fixing code determines which PERIODIC.INTEREST rate set to use. The link to the PERIODIC.INTEREST table is handled using MARKET.RATE.TEXT record in Floating Interest field of either asset or liability side. The rate fixing code represents the MARKET.RATE.TEXT key. The same code must be input in ST.GROUP.FIX and is used to flag the floating rate within the trades.

Rates are derived from PERIODIC.INTEREST . The key to this table is NNCCYYYYYMMDD. For example, 10GBP20181202 allows up to 99 individual records which are captured per currency per day. This enables individual tables for individual products. The respective PI record key is fetched along with the fixing rate based on the configurations in ST.GROUP.FIX . The user has the option of manually amending the PI key that is defaulted, if required. The system throws an error stating 'Only PI records respective to the currency and rate code selected is allowed' when PI record changed by the user different from the currency and rate code selected in multi-value set of ST.GROUP.FIX . If a different dated PI record for the given currency and rate code input in ST.GROUP.FIX is selected by user from the effective date input, an override is thrown that 'Different dated PI record is selected for the given currency and rate code'. PI record Key and Fixing Rate field gets updated only when instrument is Swap. Upon committing the record, the rate fixing is done for the respective deals.

When an unfixed leg is due for fixing, the SWAP application downloads the rate from the source rate file and automatically updates the swap transaction record with the relevant rate. Reports provide details of the performed fixing operations and encountered errors, if any.

If several requests are required on an IMM fixing date, one record per combination of instrument or currency or rate fixing code or effective date needs to be input and authorised, and marked to be run as Service.

A detailed explanation of the fields in ST.GROUP.FIX are as follows:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Instrument | Defines the application (for example, SWAP ). |
| Type | Subtype within SWAP group. This can be any type defined in the SWAP.TYPE application. |
| Currency | Currency to be fixed. Only one currency can be specified. |
| PI Int Key | Descriptor for the rate set supplying the fixing rates. In SWAP , this is the value in MARKET.RATE.TEXT . |
| Rate Selection | Uses mid or bid-offer rate from the rate table. Allowed values are: Middle – The fixing process calculates and uses the mid-rate between the Bid and Offer rates as defined in the rate table. Bid-offer – The fixing process uses either Bid or Offer as appropriate for the deal type (asset legs uses the offer, liability legs use the bid). |
| Effective Date | Date on which the new rate takes effect. For the SWAP application, This is the date in Rr Schedule Date or Rr Process Date . This date represents the Rr Schedule Date field when the Processed Date Fixing field in ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMETER is set to No. This date represents the Rr Process Date field when Processed Date Fixing field in ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMATER is set to Yes. When the service is run, ST.GROUP.FIX records are processed in the sequential order in which they were created by matching the respective Rr Process Date field. Refer to Processed Rate Reset Date Fixing Logic for further information. For FRA application, this date represents the settlement date and not the fixing date. |
| Timing | Specifies when the operation is executed. Allowed values are: Wid (executed immediately after the ST.GROUP.FIX record is authorised) Service (rate fixing for the groups defined takes place only on running the service ST.EOD.GROUP.FIX ). |
| Allow Refixing | The fixing operation overwrites rates for trades that are already fixed (manually or automatically). Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Fixing List | Decides whether the list of trades fixed is required for the user to view a list of trades about to be fixed. Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Error Log | Decides whether the process should write to the log. Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Trade Status | Decides whether a fixed trade goes directly to authorised or unauthorised status. Allowed values are: AUTH – Trade is authorised. WAIT– Trade is not authorised. |
| Last Run Date | The date, status (started or completed) and number of errors (if completed). The system controls and updates this field. |
| Pl Record Key | Allows the user to verify the PI record referred for Rate fixing and to alter Pl Record Key when necessary. When the user does not enter the PI record key, the system defaults to the existing PI record with the currency and rate code for the effective date specified. If no PI record exists for the effective date, the system loops and searches for an existing PI record by reducing one calendar day from Today. The system throws an override when a different dated PI record is selected by the user for the given effective date. It is an associated multi-value field of TYPE. |
| Fixing Rate | Allows the user to verify the rates defaulted from PI table based on the Pl Record Key field confirmed by the user. The system defaults the rates based on rate selection field (middle or bid offer) and would be referred to the Swap records for rate fixing by ST.GROUP.FIX service. It is an associated multi-value field of TYPE. |

> **⚠️ Note:** The fixing logic is handled in the Processed Date Fixing field of ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMETER which acts as a parameter switch between the existing logic and the new processed date fixing logic. Refer Configurations section of Group Fixing of Floating Rate feature for more information.


##### Group Fixing of Floating Leg through Service

Rate fixing for the groups defined takes place on running the service ST.EOD.GROUP.FIX . The below steps are followed to execute group fixing of floating leg through Service:

- The Timing field in ST.GROUP.FIX table is set to Service.
- Service mentioned needs to be initiated.

### 8.10  Interest Rate Swap Deal Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An interest rate swap is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of interest payments over a period of time. This does not involve exchange of principal, hence, the interest is calculated on the notional principal amount in the same currency. Interest rates can be fixed or floati...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Choose Swap Deals*, *Liquidation Mode*, *Maturity Payment Date*, *Negative Rates*, *Principal*, *Trade Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An interest rate swap is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of interest payments over a period of time. This does not involve exchange of principal, hence, the interest is calculated on the notional principal amount in the same currency. Interest rates can be fixed or floating, and the interest payment schedules can be generated from a given frequency or manually defined. The notional principal amount can vary during the life of the swap according to the user definable payment schedule.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration options the system offers in Interest Rate Swap.

- Interest rate swap deal processing is handled by selecting the appropriate input version within the system.
- The Product category code is hardcoded and must be in the range 20000 and 49999 to be applied on the swap contracts. SWAP.TYPE has the definitions of all swap contract types and product category codes related to them. Swap trade type (Trade or Hedge) is defined in the Trade Type field within the deal.
- SWAP.AGREEMENT.TYPE file stores different types of agreements used in swap contracts. For example, ISDA, BBAIRS, MASTER, etc. Every contract is linked to an agreement type.
- SWAP.PARAMETER holds system level parameters for processing of swap transactions. SYSTEM record within SWAP.PARAMETER file consists of income accrual categories, expenses accrual categories, additional data (such as, transaction code to use on net payments, date and frequency of accruals and categories of upfront allocation of P&L). Maturity Payment Date field in SWAP application defaults from SWAP.PARAMETER with an option to override.
- SWAP.ACTIVITY records define the activity that produces delivery output. These activities relate to specific events given as follows: During the life of the contract Whenever delivery output is generated using S WAP module
- The activity code of the relevant advice is recorded on the contract.
- SWAP.ADVICES controls the output of the delivery messages for SWAP.ACTIVITY .
- SWAP.ADVICES record is linked with another SWAP.ADVICES record to customise the output by defining multiple message types, print formats, and deal slips.
- All the fields related to swap revaluation are grouped in a single SYSTEM record of SWAP.REVAL.PARAMETER table.

> **⚠️ Note:** To know more on the parameter tables, refer to Configuration section.


#### 🔧 Working With

The swap contract captures the customer ID, swap type, dealer desk ID, trade date, maturity date, and asset and liability legs. The asset and liability side of the contracts are captured in separate tabs. Settlement instructions are captured along with the contract input.

An illustration of how the swap schedules of both asset and liabilities leg built for the above transaction is given below:


##### Interest Rate Schema

The following interest rate options are supported in S WAP module:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Fixed Rate | The interest rate (also known as swap rate), is fixed at the time of the contract input. This is applicable throughout the life of the contract. However, by specifying the Rate Reset (RR) schedule, the rate can be changed on an individual contract basis. |
| Floating Rate | The interest rate is reset based on a frequency, usually the period falling between 1 and 12 months. A periodic interest rate key for the appropriate floating rate is used. 03LIBOR, for rate resetting as per the given frequency. A spread can be applied to the rate before the interest calculation. Cap and/or floor rates can also be specified to check the applied interest rate for errors (CAP and FLOOR options are different and are not supported in SWAP module). |

The module also supports the following interest rate or amounts and the downstream processing:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Negative Rate | Negative interest rates can be in any of the forms of fixed rate, floating rate with or without spread. This can be defined in Negative Rates field in the SWAP application. This is a no change field which defaults to Null and this is same as No. To allow negative rates, the Liquidation Mode field should be set to automatic. The user cannot input negative rates for Annuity Payments (AP) schedules. |
| Fixed Interest Amount | The interest amount can be fixed by specifying an Interest Payment (IP) schedule with an associated amount. This is useful when there is a requirement to maintain the same interest amount for every interest period throughout the life of the contract. |


##### Interest Day Basis

The interest day basis C (366/366), C2 (366/366) and D (360/366), in addition to the regular market basis are available in the Temenos Transact SWAP module.

Interest calculations differ when the calculation period falls as part of a non-leap year and leap year. It also differs when the year period exists between C (known as the ISDA method) and C2 (known as the AFB method).

- For the C calculation – The period is broken down into actual years.
- For the C2 calculation – The year starts at the maturity date and works backwards.

If February 29 exists in that period then it counts it as 366 days, otherwise, it is 365. If the period lasts more than a year, subsequent calculations are made for each yearly period.

| C | C2 |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of days | Days in year | Interest | Number of days | Days in year | Interest |
| 10 | 365 | 315.07 | 91 | 366 | 2859.29 |
| 81 | 366 | 2545.08 | - | - | - |
| Total Interest | 2860.15 | Total Interest | 2859.29 |  |  |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Treasury Processes
- Current Interest Rate Swap Deal Processing (Task)

Interest Rate Swap – Hedge

It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of interest payments over a period of time and or to lock in a profit or minimise the loss to offset a loan or deposit contract on bank book.

Interest Rate Swap – Trade

It is an agreement between two counterparties. To exchange streams of interest payments over a period of time is called as Interest Rate Swap. It does not involve the exchange of principal. The interest is calculated on the notional amount. The interest rates can be fixed or floating and the payment schedules are either generated from a frequency or can be manually defined. A trade deal is a speculative transaction without an underlying asset.

#### 📖 Introduction

The loan product is a single leg transaction for extending credit to a client or counterparty with interest being charged in arrears. Interest rates can be fixed or floating, and the interest payment schedules can be generated from a frequency or manually defined. The principal amount can vary during the life of the loan according to the user definable payment schedule (Accrediting or Amortisation). The user can expect repayment based on equitable monthly or quarterly instalments through Annuity Payment (AP) schedules. However, currently the annuity schedules work only with fixed rate of interest.


#### 🔧 Working With

The loan contract captures the customer ID, swap type (loan type), dealer details, trade date, maturity date and asset leg. The details of the asset side of the contract are captured in a separate tab. Settlement instructions are also captured along with the contract input.

The loan repayment can be amortised through equated instalments using Annuity Payment (AP) schedules. However, this works only if the rate of interest is fixed.

##### Interest Rate Schema

The SWAP module supports the following interest rate options:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Fixed Rate | The interest rate is fixed at the time of the contract input, which is applicable throughout the life of the contract. However, by specifying the Rate Reset (RR) schedule, the rate can be changed on an individual contract basis. |
| Floating Rate | The interest rate is reset based on a frequency, usually the period falling between 1 to 12 months. It uses a PI rate key for the appropriate floating rate. 03LIBOR to differentiate it from the fixed rate. A spread can be applied to the rate before the interest calculation. Cap and/or floor rates can also be specified to check the applied interest rate for any errors (CAP and FLOOR options are different and are not supported in SWAP module). |

The module also supports the following interest rate or amounts, and the downstream processing:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Negative Rate | Negative interest rates can be in any of the forms of fixed rate and floating rate with or without spread or interest amounts. This is defined in Negative Rates field in the SWAP application. This is a no change field, which defaults to Null and is similar to No. To allow negative rates, the Liquidation Mode field should be set to Automatic. The user cannot input negative rates for AP schedules. |
| Fixed Interest Amount | The interest amount can be fixed by specifying an Interest Payment (IP) schedule with an associated amount. This is useful when there is a requirement to maintain the same interest amount for every interest period throughout the life of the contract. |

The interest day basis C (366/366), C2 (366/366) and D (360/366), in addition to the regular market ones are available in the Temenos Transact SWAP module.

The interest calculations differ when the calculation period falls as part of a non-leap year and leap year. It also differs when the year period exists between C (known as the ISDA method) and C2 (known as the AFB method).

- For the C calculation – The period is broken down into actual years.
- For the C2 calculation – The year starts at the maturity date and works backwards.

If February 29 exists in that period then it counts it as 366 days, otherwise, it is 365. If the period lasts more than a year, subsequent calculations are made for each yearly period.

| C | C2 |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of Days | Days in year | Interest | Number of days | Days in year | Interest |
| 10 | 365 | 315.07 | 91 | 366 | 2859.29 |
| 81 | 366 | 2545.08 | - | - | - |

### 8.12  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Interest Rate Swap module helps the users of Temenos Transact system to acquaint themselves with the application features, navigation and the functionality.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services
- Swap

The Interest Rate Swap module helps the users of Temenos Transact system to acquaint themselves with the application features, navigation and the functionality.

This module is intended to the following users or user roles:

| Role | Function |
|---|---|
| Dealer | Executes deals with counterparty and records the deal details in the system |
| Treasury Back office personnel | Ensures authorisation, confirmation and settlement of payments |
| Risk Manager | Enforces and monitors risk limits |
| IT personnel of bank/financial institution | Maintains computing infrastructure and upgrades the computer applications |

An interest rate swap is a forward contract in which one stream of future interest payments is exchanged for another, based on a specified principal amount. Interest rate swaps involve exchange of a fixed interest rate for a floating rate (or vice versa), to do one of the following:

- Reduce or increase exposure to fluctuations in interest rates
- Obtain a marginally lower interest rate than would have been possible without swap

The Temenos Transact SWAP module supports the recording and administration of both Interest Rate Swaps (IRS) and Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CIRS). It also supports ‘single-leg’ contract types (asset or liability), which are essentially loans or deposits. Additionally, Swaps are incorporated into the Limits, Accounting, Delivery and Position Management modules of Temenos Transact .

The details supporting the swap transaction are held in a single contract. Transaction details stored include the following:

- Counterparty
- Notional principals
- Interest rates
- Schedules for both Swap Legs (interest or premium future payment details - cash flows)
- Payment instructions

All future events, such as Principal Exchange, Interest Payment, Rate Reset, etc., are recorded in SWAP.SCHEDULES and the current and previously processed schedule details are stored in SWAP.BALANCES file. The Temenos Transact SWAP module supports the following products:

| Product | Description |
|---|---|
| Vanilla Swap | The exchange of a fixed rate for a floating rate is undertaken. The notional principal is constant throughout the life of the contract |
| Currency Interest Rate Swap | The principal is either notional or exchanged but in different currencies |
| Amortizing Swap | The principal is amortized over the life of the contract |
| Accreting Swap | The principal is increased over the life of the contract |
| Roller-Coaster Swap | The principal is subjected to increase and decrease during the life cycle |
| Balloon Swap | A smaller portion of the principal amount is amortized while a larger amount is retained until the end of the contract |
| Basis Swap | Both legs of the swap involve a floating rate instead of fixed vs floating as seen on the vanilla swap |
| Risk-Free Rate Swaps | RFR swaps with Lookback and Lockout RFR market conventions in addition to Plain Arrears and Rest Cut-Off. It also enables the user to delay the actual interest payment and generate payment messages when the final RFR is available in the system. |


##### Product Configuration

This section describes the configuration options the system offers in Interest Rate Swap.

A swap contract input page has the following sections:

- Contract details
- Asset details including schedules
- Liability details including schedules
- Settlement instructions

Most of the fields have default values except for the key elements, such as counterparty, maturity date, agreement type, currencies, fixed interest rate, floating rate index, principal amounts etc. Schedules are entered directly in the contract by using the schedule types, dates, frequencies, amounts and rates. This simplifies the input of a relatively complex swap contract.

All schedules are processed online and at COB, with the exception of the IP and AP schedules, which are due for today. In the latter case, they are processed only at COB.

At input and commit stage, the system checks and updates the credit limits of the customer and Position Management.

At the authorisation stage, the system generates all the necessary accounting entries for various types of schedules including charges and fee, CRF entries, and SWIFT or print trade confirmation messages.

Broker or Customer confirmation is performed using the verify function, and when the contract are confirmed, it is stamped with the terminal number, operator name, time and date. The type of confirmation required is specified as a prefix to the contract number (which is ignored for other functions) with either CU for customer confirmations or BR for broker confirmations.

By using the versions Swap, Customer and Swap, Broker and the default enquiry supplied with these versions, the appropriate prefix is automatically appended to the contract number.

The Temenos Transact SWAP module classifies the deal into IRS, CIRS, Loan and Deposit contracts.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameters consists of the following:

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Swap Parameters | This table allows the users to define the system lever parameter for processing of Swap contracts. The record ID of this table is 'SYSTEM'. User can also update parameter values for Days post maturity, Maturity Date, Defer online position update and Defer online schedule update. |
| 2 | Swap Reval Parameter | This table allows the user to parameterize the Swap Revaluation setup. The record ID of this table is 'SYSTEM' and consists of parameter values for PL Category, Revaluation Credit Code, Debit Code and setup related to Asset & Liability Short and Long rates selection, Zero coupon rate selection, NPV forward rate, NPV accrual adjustment. |
| 3 | Swap Type Record | This file contains the definition of all types of Swap contracts allowed on the system. It contains details such as Category Codes for Booking Revaluation Entries, Accounting (ON/OFF Balance sheet) and Revaluation Method. |
| 4 | Swap Agreement Type | This file stores the types of agreements that are used in Swap contracts. Each swap contract has to be linked to an agreement type, based on which the validations are performed. The user can modify an existing record and as well create new records. |
| 5 | Swap Activity Record | This file allows the user to define and control the delivery output for Swap module. The records in this file define all the activities that produce delivery outputs. These activities relate to specific events during the life of the contract. If required, the delivery pertaining to each of these events can be produced prior to the event itself. In this case, the number of days in advance of the event that the advices are produced is defined in this file. |
| 6 | Market Rate Text | This table defines descriptions of tradable interest rates that are recognised by SWIFT. The key of the periodic interest table corresponding to the rate described is linked in this file. Floating interest rates defined in Swap Contracts are must also be linked to this file. |


##### llustrating Model Products

Following products are available under Swap module:

| S.No | Products | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest Rate Swap - Trade | Interest Rate Swap is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange the streams of Interest payments over a period of time. It does not involve the exchange of Principal, and the interests are calculated on the notional amount. The interest rates can be fixed or floating and the payment schedules are either generated from a frequency or can be manually defined. A Trade deal is a speculative transaction without an underlying asset. |
| 2 | Interest Rate Swap - Hedge | It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of Interest payments over a period of time and or to lock in a profit or minimize the loss to offset a Loan or Deposit contract on bank book. |
| 3 | Currency Interest Rate Swap - Trade | It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange the streams of Interest payments in different currencies over a period of time. Additionally, the principal amount can be exchanged between the counterparties at the beginning and end of the deal. Interest rates can be fixed or floating. The payment schedules can either be generated from a frequency or defined manually. |
| 4 | Currency Interest Rate Swap - Hedge | It is an agreement between the counterparties to exchange the streams of interest payment in different currencies over a period of time, mainly to lock in a profit (or minimize the loss) to offset a Loan or Deposit contract on banks book. |

The following enquiries are available in the SWAP application:

| SWAP.OVERDUE.REP | Contracts overdue for rate fixing |

% Swap, Customer and % Swap, Broker are the two additional enquiries that list contracts awaiting customer or broker confirmation. These enquiries are invoked by default from the Versions, Swap Customer and Swap Broker. When these enquiries select a contract, the Verify function is used to stamp the contract as confirmed, and the appropriate prefix is automatically appended to the selected contract number.

### 8.13  Past Due


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Past Due P rocessing (PD) module allows the users to monitor and control overdue amounts receivable by bank from loans or derivative instruments (such as Swap ) .*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Liquidation Mode*, *Overdue Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Past Due P rocessing (PD) module allows the users to monitor and control overdue amounts receivable by bank from loans or derivative instruments (such as Swap ) .

The Liquidation Mode field in SWAP application acts as a link to PD module, when the value is given as Semiautomatic or Manual. If the amount is due from the customer (but the account does not have any balance) and Liquidation Mode is set to Manual or Semiautomatic, the overdue amount moves to PD module for monitoring and ageing process. To know more, refer to the user guide in PAST DUE module.

The SWAP module links to the PD module, similar to other modules, such as MG , MM and LD . Only the asset side of the SWAP is used to construct the corresponding PD.PAYMENT.DUE contract.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following two fields are available in the SWAP application:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Liquidation Mode | Identifies how to handle overdue payments. The default for all contracts is Automatic but can be changed to Manual to invoke Past Due Processing. |
| Overdue Status | Identifies the status of the underlying PD.PAYMENT.DUE contract (GRA, PDO, NAB, WOF, CUR and so on) This is a no input field.. |

The following rules apply:

- If the PD.PAYMENT.DUE product is not defined for the current company or only the liability side is specified, then the only allowed setting is Automatic.
- If the Overdue Status is not ‘CUR’ or ‘WOF’, automatic is not allowed.
- If Overdue Status is not set to ‘CUR’ or Null, Principal Increase (PI) is not allowed on the asset side.

In a swap transaction, the interest amount due on the asset side is debited to the customer’s current account, which does not have sufficient balances. If Liquidation Mode is set to Semiautomatic, the account cannot be debited when there is no credit balance. Therefore, the due amount is monitored by PAST DUE module as shown in the following screen shots:

Record in PD.PAYMENT.DUE table

Swap is essentially an interest rate derivative instrument. It is used to hedge the interest rate risk arising out of the asset and liability maturity mismatch. Position Management (PM) using PM.GAP enquiry helps in identifying and managing the maturity gaps. When the gaps are closed using swap transactions, the PM.GAP should include the swap transaction data as well, to provide up to date information.

The Temenos Transact SWAP module is fully interfaced with the Temenos Transact PM module. The PM enquiries are updated as soon as the transactions are input.

#### 📖 Introduction

A schedule represents an event which can have financial or non-financial impact. It is important to update those processed schedules or events in a file, which shall be the basis for certain purposes. The SWAP.BALANCES file records all financial movements and balance details of a particular swap contract (including all balance information, principal outstanding, rates, accruals, past schedules and charge details). Both current and historical details are maintained, which enables the system to control and record all financial transactions. This file also holds important data relating to interest accruals, foreign currency position and equivalent Local Currency (LCY) amount. Queries related to historical events work on this file.


#### 🔧 Working With

Two SWAP.BALANCES records (asset and liability) are created whenever a swap contract is entered in the system, and remained until the contract is Live. The record Id is made up of contract number followed by leg identifier that is Asset (A) or Liability (L).

For example, SW1810762356.A and SW1810762356.L

> **Purpose:** *The SWAP application has the capability to capture and process overnight Risk-Free Rate ( RFR) swap transaction s and migrate the existing (L)IBOR transactions to RFR. It now supports Risk-Free Rate flooring options for Daily, Average and Total (all-in) floor types.*

#### 📖 Introduction

The SWAP application has the capability to capture and process overnight Risk-Free Rate ( RFR) swap transaction s and migrate the existing (L)IBOR transactions to RFR. It now supports Risk-Free Rate flooring options for Daily, Average and Total (all-in) floor types.

The SWAP application can process RFR swaps with Lookback and Lockout RFR market conventions in addition to Plain Arrears and Rest Cut-Off. It also enables the user to delay the actual interest payment and generate payment messages when the final RFR is available in the system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describe the configuration required for the processing of Risk-Free Rate (RF R) in the SWAP module by adding new fields to SWAP.PARAMETER , SWAP.REVAL.PARAMETER , SWAP.TYPE and SWAP . The bank has to configure the RFR fields in SWAP.PARAMETER , however, it is optional for SWAP.REVAL.PARAMETER and SWAP.TYPE .


##### SWAP.PARAMETER

The configuration on SWAP.PARAMETER is required for the correct rate calculation, according to bank’s preferences.

Swap Parameter .

2. Configure the following RFR fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Rounding | R ounding rules for RFR ( default ed on SWAP level ) |
| RFR Period Day Count | Treatment of last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It a llow s the following values: Full - L ast RFR with day weightage , which is applicable for the remaining period Today - L ast RFR with its original day weightage , which is applicable till the current business day |
| Rfr Paymt Dely Categ | Defines the suspense account category code for parking the interest amount during the delay payment period. |


##### SWAP.REVAL.PARAMETER

Swap Revaluation Parameter .

2. Configure the following fields (optional):

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Coupon Rate | Coupon curve used to determin e the discount factors for revaluation of Overnight Index Swaps ( OIS ) contracts |
| RFR Zero Rate | C urve with zero rates for the revaluation of OIS contracts |


##### SWAP.TYPE

Swap Type Record .

2. Configure the following fields (optional):

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Convention | Identifies the market convention used for rate averaging. The allowed values for swaps are: Plain Arrears – Indicates the daily averaging of RFRs Reset Cut-Off – Indicates the daily simple averaging of RFRs with last N days set as cut-off days. This uses the last RFR available in the averaging Lookback – Indicates the daily averaging of historical RFRs with a lag of N days set as lookback days to arrive at the average rate applicable for a given interest period Lockout – Indicates the daily compound averaging of RFRs with last N days set as lockout days. This uses the last RFR available in the averaging |
| RFR Lookback Type | Identifies the type of lookback method to be applied for rate compounding or averaging. There are two types of lookback methods: Narrow Definition – Original interest period day count is used with lookback rate for rate calculations. Example: If Wednesday’s rate is used for Friday, then apply Friday’s weight, that is, three days to Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift – Original day count of the lookback rate is used for rate calculations. Example: If Wednesday’s rate is used for Friday, then apply the Wednesday’s weight, that is, one day to Wednesday’s rate. |
| RFR Lookback Days | Identifies the number of lookback days to be considered for RFR calculations. |
| RFR Calc Method | C alculation method for RFR averaging: Compound Simple |
| RFR Spread Method | S pread treatment method during the RFR averaging: Spread-Inclusive - Spread is taken within the averaging calculation along with the daily rates Spread-Exclusive - S pread is added separately after RFR averaging is done |
| RFR Cut -O ff Days | C rystallisation period (Number of business days prior to period end date when rate referencing stops and last available RFR is used for the remaining days) for the reset cut-off market c onvention |
| RFR Payment Delay | Identifies whether the payment on the given interest period can be delayed by N days |
| RFR Rounding | Defaults from SWAP.PARAMETER and overrid es on SWAP.TYPE |


#### 🔧 Working With

RFR Swap Deals .

2. Select a risk- free rate key in the Floating Interest field.

3. Define values in the Lb Rfr Convention and Lb Rfr Calc Method fields for averaging RFR for an interest period.

- For Reset Cut-Off and Lockout market conventions, the SWAP module has an option to define the number of cut-off days for which the same rate is applied to calculate the interest.
- For Lookback market conventions, the SWAP module has an option to define the Lookback days and Lookback Type to be applied on the contract.

4. In the Lb Rfr Spread Treatment Method field,define whether the contractual spread needs to be included or excluded from the rate averaging.

> **⚠️ Note:** RFRs are backward looking and published with a delay .

5. Contract receives a new rate for each business day, which is applicable for the previous business day.The accrual amounts for each working day are re-calculated and updated, once a new rate is available.

6. The SWAP.BALANCES table stores the accrual ladder for the current interest period with the amount accrued and rate applied for each accrual cycle. The a verage RFR change s every business day , once a new rate is available.

The below screenshot shows the change in Interest Rate field of SWAP.BALANCES , as new RFR is published for each business day.

> **⚠️ Note:** Forward accounting entries and cash flow projections are based on the last average RFR that is available .


##### Pre-termination and Rate Correction of RFR Swap Contracts

A bank can perform a rate correction or pre-terminate an RFR swap contract during the current interest period resulting in updated or zeroed interest amount on the asset and liability legs of an RFR Swap contract contract on any day, including IP, IP+1, and DP dates.

The user can initiate the rate correction by providing a rate (other than zero) in the As Rf Rate and Lb Rf Rate fields in both the asset and liability legs of the RFR swap contract.

The screenshot below shows the post-rate correction values.

The rates provided in the As Rf Rate and Lb Rf Rate fields is the final risk-free rate applicable for the current interest period, where the interest accrual amount and total interest amount are re-calculated and updated in the record in SWAP.BALANCES application for both the legs.

The final rate is applied in the As Current Rate and Lb Current Rate fields of the contract to ensure the mapping in various delivery messages are in line with the final rate.

The user can pre-terminate an existing RFR swap contract by defining the value in the As Rf Rate and Lb Rf Rate fields as zero in both the asset and liability legs of the contract. The Maturity Date , As Date Freq and Lb Date Freq fields, are amended to the current date.

To enable the full unwinding of interest rate swaps during the delay payment (DP) period, the system must check the following:

- The final RFR rate ( Dp Final Rate in SWAP.BALANCES is set as Yes) is available for the RFR Swap deal.
- The effective date is set as the current date and the rates for the current period are passed as 0 (that is RF.RATE for the RFR leg and RR for the fixed leg should be given as 0, along with the effective date as current date). If the rate is passed as 0, the system allows to unwind the deal online, else the system continues to raise the ‘Defined IP frequency is not allowed as there exists Delay payment for the similar dates’ error.
- The Dp Final Rate field is updated either through the SW.ONLINE.DELAY.PAYMENT online service or during COB.
- The SW.ONLINE.MATURITY service runs in the background, which picks this deal, processes the DP schedule by moving the amount from the suspense account to the customer account and marks the contract as matured. If the online service is not triggered, then this deal is processed at the maturity date.

The contract is matured and interest accrued for the current interest period is zeroed for both asset and liability legs after the contract is authorised by the Treasury supervisor. The updated interest rate and interest amount are reflected in the record in the SWAP.BALANCES application.


##### RFR Online Maturity

The user can delay the payments by using the Rfr Payment Delay field, as the final rate is calculated at the end of the interest period. Additionally, mature the swap contracts online by using the Rfr Online Maturity field and running the SW.ONLINE.MATURITY service.


##### Swap Advices

This generates the SWIFT messages relat ed to Rate Reset (MT362) , when:

- Final rate for a leg is available in a given interest period.
- C onfirmation messages (MT360 and MT361) have the name of the benchmark and not the actual rate

The b elow screenshot shows the configuration of SWAP.ADVICES for 202 (Payment).

Similarly, include the MT362 message in SWAP.ADVICES of 210 (Advice to Receive) and 105 (Interest Payment).


##### Payment Delay

For plain arrears market convention with payment delay, the Delay Payment (DP) schedule is automatically created by the system to handle the delayed interest payment and delivery messages.

The system checks if the final Risk-Free Rate (RFR) applicable for the interest period is available in the system during each COB. Based on the RFRs availability, the system generates the payment or receipt advice and rate reset advice.

Interest accruals are adjusted based on the final RFR SWAP during the delay payment period, which is, Rfr Payment Delay days from the interest payment date. The actual interest payment is delayed using the suspense accounts with the category code configured in the Rfr Paymt Dely Categ field in SWAP.PARAMETER .

The screenshot below shows the SWAP contract with payment delay.

The screenshot below shows the accounting entries for parking the interest amount in the internal suspense account during the delay payment period.

The SWAP.BALANCES table is automatically updated with the Delay Payment (DP) schedule details as shown in the screenshot below.

The system can generate payment messages and rate reset advices when the final rate is available in the system.

The SWAP.BALANCES table is updated when final rate is available in the system.

Using the SW.ONLINE.DELAY.PAYMENT service, users can trigger the generation of payment or receipt message and rate reset advice online, when the final rate is entered. The interest payment however is done at the end of the delay payment period.


##### RFR Netting Payment

The Net Payments field in the SWAP application is set to Yes for Risk-Free Rate (RFR) Swap contracts with a payment delay defined, the system delays the payment of the non-RFR leg based on the delay payment days specified in the contract.

Following are the steps in the RFR netting payment process:

1. Enter an RFR-swap contract with the payment delay days specified in the Rfr Payment Delay field of the RFR leg(s) of the contract. The Net Payment field is set to Yes in the SWAP application. The value specified in the Lb Date Frequency field is December 28 and field value for the Lb Rfr Payment Delay field is 1 day as shown in the below screenshot.
2. Once the Interest Payment (IP) schedule date is reached, the Net Pay Val Dt field is adjusted according to the specified payment delay days as shown in the below screenshot.
3. The system adjusts the date to December 31 (originally December 28) after considering the holiday and delay days. The Net Amount field in the Swap contract is updated with net pay amount or net receive amount derived from netting of the asset and liability legs of the contract. In the above case, the activity is updated as advice to receive for the asset leg due to the netting between the two legs.


##### Payment Delay for Fixed Leg

A swap deal is entered with Rfr Fixed Dp as Yes. Based on the value in Rfr Fixed Dp , DP schedules are created for the fixed leg only when corresponding floating side with delay payment is specified. It is not applicable for float vs float deals. The different functionalities with Rfr Fixed Dp and Net Payments are shown below.

| Net Payments | Rfr Fixed Dp | Functionality |  |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | Yes | Fixed leg follows DP settlement if the IP frequency matches or does not match the floating leg. | Floating leg follows DP |
| Yes | Yes |  |  |
| Yes | No | Fixed leg follows IP settlement if the IP frequency does not match the floating leg. |  |
| Fixed leg follows DP settlement if the IP frequency matches the floating leg. |  |  |  |
| No | No | Fixed leg follows IP settlement if the IP frequency matches or does not match the floating leg. |  |

For fixed leg, the system sets Dp Final Rate and Dp Msg Generated as Yes (in the assumption that the rate is fixed and a message for the same is generated in prior) and stores the current interest amount in Dp Payment Amt and delay payment date in Dp Payment Dt in the SWAP.BALANCES application. On fixed IP date COB, the system posts the settlement amount to the suspense account and swap schedules are built for DP with IP+2 date. On DP date COB, the system processes the DP schedule and posts the entries to the customer account. The system postpones the entries to the DP date and generates the message for fixed leg and RFR leg. The message generation is based on final rate availability.


##### Risk-Free Rate Flooring

The Negative Rates field in the SWAP application is enhanced to offer Daily Floor and Average Floor options in addition to the existing Yes and No options.

The Negative Rates field has the following options:

- Yes - Allows negative rates and does not allow RFR flooring.
- No - Performs total (all-in) RFR flooring, that is, when the average RFR plus the spread are below the floor value, the system floors the total rate to the floor value. The existing functionality is preserved for rates different from RFRs
- Daily Floor - Applies a floor on the RFRs published each business day before averaging them and applying spread whenever the daily RFRs are below the floor value
- Average Floor - Applies a floor on the average RFRs whenever the average RFRs are below the floor value. This option is not applicable for Spread-Inclusive margin treatment.

The As Floor Rate and Lb Floor Rate fields are used to define the floor value for the asset and liability legs, respectively depending on which leg has the RFR benchmarks. The floor value is the rate below which the RFR’s are not allowed to go for the given contract.

The flooring happens at the central rate calculation engine level. The SWAP module consumes the rates.


##### Migration of Existing Swap Contracts

A n additional field ( Rfr Adj Spread ) is available t o migrate existing co ntracts from (L)IBOR to RFR . This enables the user to specify the percentage change in the spread of a migrated contract , as (L)IBOR is not equal to RFRs.

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

3. Enter values in the following mandatory fields: Counterparty Principal Currency Maturity Date Agreement RFR fields Account with Bank Account Address

### 8.17  Swap Revaluation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *After 2008 financial crisis, financial disclosure requirements have made swap valuation an important topic. Swap (Interest Rate or Currency Interest Rate Swaps) has an initial value as Zero. Changing market interest rate and time causes the swap to have a positive or negative value.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Coupon Curve Rate*, *Floating Interest*, *Fwd Rate Key*, *Npv Accrual Adj*, *Npv Bef Acc Adj*, *Npv Bef Adj Lcy*, *Npv Fwd Rate*, *Zero Coupon Rate* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

After 2008 financial crisis, financial disclosure requirements have made swap valuation an important topic. Swap (Interest Rate or Currency Interest Rate Swaps) has an initial value as Zero. Changing market interest rate and time causes the swap to have a positive or negative value.

The value of a swap is the difference between the present value of the future cash flows of both fixed and floating rate leg. Swap value is calculated using Temenos Transact generic Swap Revaluation process.

The challenge to find the present value of future cash flow involves projection of future interest rates on the basis of prevailing interest rates for various tenors, as swap usually exchanges the floating rate cash flows (unknown) against fixed rate cash flows (known).

After the computation of cash flows for both the legs, the next step is to discount the cash flows.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Temenos Transact workflow of swap revaluation is explained below.


##### Definition of Generic Swap inTemenos Transact

According to business needs, system allows various types of schedules for swap contracts. However, not every type of swap can be revalued. Only generic swaps are revalued in the system. The following matrix has the list of generic and non-generic swaps:

| SWAP TYPE | IP SCHEDULE | PI SCHEDULE | METHOD | RE-VALUE? | REMARKS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IRS | YES | NO | ZERO.CPN.RATE | YES |  |
| YES | NO | WITH.RX | YES |  |  |
| YES | YES | ZERO.CPN.RATE | NO |  |  |
| YES | YES | WITH.RX | YES |  |  |
| NO | No Re-valuation-Case NOT Relevant for IRS Swaps |  |  |  |  |
| CIRS | YES | NO | ZERO.CPN.RATE | YES | RX excluded |
| YES | NO | WITH.RX | YES | RX included |  |
| YES | YES | ZERO.CPN.RATE | NO |  |  |
| YES | YES | WITH.RX | YES |  |  |
| NO | NO | ZERO.CPN.RATE | NO |  |  |
| NO | NO | WITH.RX | YES |  |  |
| NO | YES | ZERO.CPN.RATE | NO |  |  |
| NO | YES | WITH.RX | YES |  |  |

> **⚠️ Note:** Re-exchange of Principal (Rx)


##### Mechanics of Swap Pricing

Measuring the current market value of an interest rate swap involves the following steps:

Cash flows on fixed rate side are easily calculated for the entire period of the contract, given the interest rate and the period.

| Term | Rest Days | Annualised Zero Coupon Rates |
|---|---|---|
| 06M | 180 | 6.0000 |
| 01Y | 360 | 6.5080 |
| 1.5Y (Broken Date) | 540 | 6.8670 |
| 02Y | 720 | 7.2331 |

| Term | Rest Days | Par Rate (Coupon Curve Rate) |
|---|---|---|
| 06M | 180 | 6.00 |
| 01Y | 360 | 6.50 |
| 02Y | 720 | 7.20 |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Discount Factor for 6M period | DF 6m = 1/ (1+6/100) ^ (180/360) DF 6m = 0.9713 |  |
| Discount Factor for 1Y period | DF 1y = 1/ (1+6.508/100) ^ (360/360) DF 1y = 0.9389 |  |
| Discount Factor for 1.5Y period | DF 1.5y = 1/ (1+6.867/100) ^ (540/360) DF 1.5y = 0.90518 |  |
| Discount Factor for 2Y period | DF 2y = 1/ (1+7.2331/100) ^ (720/360) DF 2y = 0.86965 |  |

Cash flows and respective discount factors is multiplied to give the NPV of cash flows.

NPV of CF (i) = CF (i) * DF (i)


##### Example for Swap Revaluation

The bank has a 2-year interest rate swap of notional USD 1,000,000. Counterparty pays fixed 6.8% and bank pays USD 6-month LIBOR +0.5%, interest paid net semi-annually.

Assume that the forward 6-month LIBOR rates are 6%, 6.8117%, 7.1215%, 7.5534% for 6M, 1Y, 1.5Y and 2Y, respectively. Additionally, assuming the zero coupon rates are 6%, 6.508%, 6.867%, 7.2331% for 6M, 1Y, 1.5Y and 2Y, respectively.

Net present value of the fixed sides:

PV Fixed = 3.4*0.9713 + 3.4* 0.9389 + 3.4 * 0.90518 + 3.4 * 0.86965

PV Fixed = 12.5291

Net present value of the float side:

PVFloat = 3.5 * 0.9713 + 3.9058*0.9389 + 4.0608*0.90518 + 4.2767 * 0.86965

PVFloat = 14.462

Swap Value = (14.462 – 12.5291) * 10000

Swap Value = 19329.0


##### Enquiries

Swap Revaluations (SW.NPV.REVAL1) and SW.NPV.DIFF.CCY.REVAL enquiries help the user with a transparency on the revaluation performed for IRS and CIRS contracts, respectively. The option to drilldown on each contract opens up the Swap NPV Details (SW.NPV.DETAILS) enquiry from these enquiries. The cash flow details from Swap NPV Details (SW.NPV.DETAILS) enquiry can drilldown to Swap Schedule for FWD RR (SWAP.SCHED.FWD.RR) enquiry to observe the future rate calculation for floating rate side.

The workflow of enquiries is as given below:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| 01 MAY 2018 cash flow | = (5.00*1000000*30/36000) = 4167 |
| 27 MAY 2018 cash flow | = (5.00*1000000*26/36000) = 3611 |

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Short Per Days | = 12 |
| Short Per Rate | = 2.337000 |
| Long Per Days | = 39 |
| Long Per Rate | = 2.357000 |

The process of cross currency swap (CIRS) revaluation in Temenos Transact is similar to the interest rate swap revaluation. The only exception is that foreign currency cash flows are discounted with foreign currency zero rate yields arrived from same currency coupon curve setup in the system.

Similar to SW.NPV.REVALUATION (SW.NPV.REVAL) enquiry of IRS, this enquiry also has links to view the contracts and details of valuation calculation.

Treatment of Accrued Interest

By default, net present value of swap in Temenos Transact is calculated by subtracting the interest accrued for the current period from the sum of discounted values of future interest flows. The interest accrued is calculated for the days that run up to the previous day irrespective of accrual frequency set in SWAP.PARAMETER .

If the users want to subtract the actual accrual posted in the system to arrive at the net present value instead of the system calculated notional amount, then Npv Accrual Adj field in SWAP.REVAL.PARAMETER is set to Yes as shown below.

The accrued interest is stored in SWAP. BALANCES file as shown below.

The system then subtracts the accrual so far posted, from the gross discounted value of future cash flows and compute the net present value. Npv Bef Acc Adj and Npv Bef Adj Lcy fields in SWAP.BALANCES display the present value before accrual adjustment.

There are no Tasks available for Swap Revaluation feature.

### 8.18  Upfront Profit Allocation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Treasury incentivises the bank branches for mobilising business from non-treasury customers in the form of ‘Marketing Exchange Profit’.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Fixed Rate*, *Liability Treasury Rate*, *Rate*, *Treasury Fixed Rate*, *Treasury Rate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Treasury incentivises the bank branches for mobilising business from non-treasury customers in the form of ‘Marketing Exchange Profit’.

The difference between the treasury rate (exchange rate between treasury and bank branch) and customer rate (exchange rate between bank branch and customer rate) is termed as marketing exchange profit and is passed on to the branch profit and loss.


#### 🔧 Working With

The difference between the treasury rate and customer rate is the marketing exchange profit or loss. Treasury rate is input in Treasury Fixed Rate and customer rate in Fixed Rate (AS.FIXED.RATE). The prefix ‘AS’ indicates the asset side and ‘LB’ indicates the liability side on the field names. In the asset and liability types, treasury rate is inputted in Treasury Rate (AS.TRSRY.RATE) or Liability Treasury Rate (LB.TRSRY.RATE) field, and the customer rate is input in Rate (AS.RATE or LB.RATE) field.

The Upfront Profit Allocation functionality does not support cases, where the interest amount directly entered instead of a rate. The functionality also supports only fixed side.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Upfront Profit Allocation feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Upfront Profit Allocation feature.
