### 8.19  Treasury Configuring Payment Order


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`, `NDF`, `PO`, `PP.CHANNEL`, `PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES`, `PP.CONTRACT`, `PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE`, `PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND` ... +5 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Po Ref Product*
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a generic payment order product ID for treasury settlements and map it to the Po Ref Product field in TM.PO.INTEGRATION table.
2. Create a record in PP.MSGPAYMENTTYPE table for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments.
3. Create a record in PP.NODA.LIST for the payment order product ID created for treasury payments. The Order Initiation Type field in the PO application has a specific value for the payment order originated from the Treasury applications. To know more, refer to Configuring Payment Order.
4. Create a separate PP.SOURCE record for treasury settlements.


##### Imposing Required Credit Value Date

This enables the user to impose the required credit value date passed by Treasury application on the debit value date. Hence, the statement entries for settlement amount has the appropriate value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create a record in PP.CHANNEL table from where all treasury payments originate. The channel is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury payments.
2. Create a record in PP.SOURCEPRODUCTGROUP table to define source product group in Payments Hub. The source product is linked to the source that is created specifically for treasury settlements.
3. Create an EB.LOOKUP record that is similar to the PP.SOURCE record. This enables to map Order Initiation Type in PP.SOURCE to the value in TM.PO.INTEGRATION .
4. In the PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE table, set the debit value date output as required credit value date. The value date in statement entry posted by TPH is same as the required credit value date passed by Treasury applications. The above steps are applicable for FX, FRA and MM. However, the user needs to create a new EB.LOOKUP record for NDF .


##### Generating Forward Entries by TPH

This enables the user to choose the parameter option at TPH level to generate forward accounting or live entries with forward value date.

The user needs to perform the following actions:

1. Create four new products in PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table to provide all four possibilities of treasury settlement. The following record names are products created for domestic and international payments, which TPH uses to process treasury payments: Record Name Message Type Payment Type TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 MT103 Domestic Payment TRSY.C.103.O.I-20190417 MT103 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.I-20190417 MT202 International Payment TRSY.B.202.O.D-20190417 MT202 Domestic Payment
2. In the Forward Entry Flag field of PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND table, set as Y. A sample record of TRSY.C.103.O.D-20190417 is shown in the below screenshots. (To know more, refer to the table above). To process an NDF transaction, the user needs to create four more records by setting the Originating Source and Forward E ntry Flag to NDSTLMT and N, respectively.
3. Create a new record in PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT and link it to output parameters of the determined product. This helps to identify the output channel configured in PP.CONTRACT .
4. Create a new rule in PP.CONTRACT with the PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT defined. This enables TPH to determine the output channel for the payment initiated from Treasury.
5. In the PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES table, set the Update Cash Position field as Y. The cash flow positions for payments processed through TPH is updated.


> **Related Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`, `NDF`, `PO`, `PP.CHANNEL`, `PP.COMPANY.PROPERTIES`, `PP.CONTRACT`, `PP.DEBIT.VALUE.DATE`, `PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND`, `PP.MSGPAYMENTTYPE`, `PP.NODA.LIST`, `PP.ROUTING.PRODUCT`, `PP.SOURCE`, `PP.SOURCEPRODUCTGROUP`

## Appendix B: Consolidated Field Reference


This appendix consolidates all field description tables from across the documentation, grouped by sub-module. This provides a single reference for all field definitions.


### Treasury - FR (FR)


**Misc**

| Enquiry Name | Description |
|---|---|
| FRA.TRADE.POS | List of all trade type FRAs reflecting the position |
| FRA.HEDGE.POS | List of all hedge type FRAs reflecting the position |
| FRA.FIX.DEALS | List of all unfixed deals that crossed the fixing date |
| FRA.MAT.DEAL | List of deals to be fixed in next 10 days |
| FRA.UNCONF.BROKER | List of FRAs to be confirmed by the broker |
| FRA.UNCONF.CPARTY | List of FRAs to be confirmed by the counterparty |

**Misc**

| Reports | Description |
|---|---|
| FRA.REVAL | Positions revalued (Trade) |
| FRA.REVAL.DEAL | Position revalued on individual deal basis (Trade) |
| FRA.HEDGE.DEALS | List of outstanding hedges |
| FR.HEDGE.REVAL | Position revalued on individual deal basis (Hedge) |
| FRA.MTH.ACCRUALS | Accruals on hedge deals |
| FRA.RATE.SETTING.REPORT | Rate is due to be fixed (as specified on FRA.PARAMETER ) |
| FRA.OVERDUE.REPORT | Start date has passed but rate not fixed |
| OUTSTANDING.FRAS | List of all live transactions |
| UNFIXED.FRAS | Rate is not fixed |
| CUS.UNCONFIRMED.FRAS | Counterparty needs to confirm the FRAs |
| BROK.UNCONFIRMED.FRAS | Broker needs to confirm the FRAs |
| FRA.REALISED.PL.REPORT | P&L breakdown for each position |

**Misc**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Contract Rate (or FRA Rate ) | The interest rate that the two contracting parties negotiate on trade date. This rate is compared to the settlement rate during the calculation of settlement amount. It starts on the settlement (d3) date and ends on maturity date (d4). |
| Contract Period | The time between the settlement and maturity dates of the notional loan. This period can go upto 12 months. |
| Currency | The currency in which the FRA's notional amount is denominated. |
| Fixing D ate | This is the date on which the reference rate is determined, that is, the rate to which the FRA rate is compared. |
| FRA Buyer | The buyer of an FRA is the contracting party that borrows at the FRA rate (contract rate). |
| FRA Seller | The seller of an FRA is the contracting party that lends at the FRA rate (contract rate). |
| Master Agreement | Usually counterparties sign a master agreement between each other before entering into an Over the Counter (OTC) contract because huge amount of paperwork is generated and processed for every single deal without a master agreement in place. |
| Maturity Date | The date on which the notional loan is deemed to expire. |
| Notional Amount | The notional sum for which the interest rate is guaranteed and all interest calculations are based. |
| Reference Rate | The interest rate index to which the FRA rate is compared to determine the settlement amount. This is generally an IBOR-type rate index with the same duration as the FRA's contract period. For example, six months EURIBOR for an FRA in euros with a six-month contract period). |
| Settlement Amount | The amount calculated as the difference between the FRA and reference rate, as a percentage of the notional sum paid by one party to the other on the settlement date. The settlement amount is calculated after the fixing date for payment on the settlement date. |
| Settlement Date | The date on which the notional loan period (the contract period) begins and settlement amount is settled. |
| Spot Date | The market spot date applicable on the contract is usually two business days after the trade date. |
| Trade Date | The date on which the FRA is negotiated between the two counterparties. |
| Waiting Period | The period between the value date (d1) and settlement date (d3). |

**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FRA.PARAMETER | This table contains the parameter definition for FRAs to determine the valuation formula and frequency. Using this parameter users can define the following: Acceptable rate variations Spot and fixing date Timing and content of revaluation entries Default product category codes for Trade and Hedge transactions Parameter for confirmation matching Parameter for creating reports |
| 2 | MARKET.RATE.TEXT | This table allows users to define the floating rate option. The system populates user defined Floating Rate option code while populating the delivery related details. |

**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FRA Trade Buy | An FRA Trade Buy (Purchase) is a contract where the buyer is borrowing a notional sum at a fixed interest rate and for a specified period starting at an agreed date in the future. |
| 2 | FRA Trade Sell | An FRA Trade Sell (Sale) is a contract where the seller is lending a notional sum at a fixed interest rate and for a specified period starting at an agreed date in the future. |
| 3 | FRA Hedge Buy | An FRA Hedge Buy is a contract where the buyer gets into the agreement to borrow the notional amount with an aim of hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest, which is fixed at the start of the contract. |
| 4 | FRA Hedge Sell | An FRA Hedge Sell is a contract where the seller gets into the agreement to lend the notional amount with an aim hedging the risk of loss due to variation in rate of interest on it, which is fixed at the start of the contract. |

It allows the user to define different limit amounts for contracts on different maturity dates. When the LIMIT.TYPE field is set to: Utilisation - The Limit product holds the Utilisation Limit records. Validation - The Limit product holds the Validation Limit records, which constitutes the maximum cap allowed for the underlying Utilisation Limits within a Limit structure. Standalone - The Limit product holds the Standalone Limit records, which have the same functionality as Utilisation Limit records apart from the fact that they hold no parent or child Limits. SUPPRESS.ACCOUNTING field is set to ‘Yes’ to suppress any GL accounting performed against the Limit records under the Limit product. This field accepts the input when the Limit record has nothing set in the Reference Child field. When the THIRD.PARTY.EXPOSURE field set to ‘Yes’, it marks the given Limit records under the Limit product to hold the third party exposure for their Customer(s). Any exposure created against these Limit records are excluded from the bank’s risk reports. |

**Date Calculation**

| Deal | Description |
|---|---|
| Involves SPOT.BASE.CCY | When a deal involves Spot Base Ccy , the spot date for the non-spot base currency is determined first. If an FX Lcl Region is defined, then the same rules witnessed on the previous section is applicable. This spot date is then comparted to Spot Base Ccy holidays. If the date is a holiday in Spot Base Ccy , it is adjusted to the next common working day in both non-spot and spot base currencies. |
| Does Not Involve SPOT.BASE.CCY | A common spot date is obtained for the two currencies involved in the same way as the standard processing. If FX Lcl Region is defined, then the same rules shown above is applicable. The common date calculated is then compared to the Spot Base Cc y holidays. If the date is a holiday, it is adjusted to the next common working day for both currencies and Spot Base Ccy . |
| Both Sides are SPOT.BASE.CCY | A common working day is obtained for both currencies. The common date calculated is compared to all the Spot Base Ccy holidays. If the date is a holiday, it is adjusted to the next common date for both deal and all currencies defined in Spot Base Ccy . This method may result in a different date calculation in comparison to the standard calculation. |

| 1 | FX.PARAMETERS | The rules that determined the Foreign Exchange (FX) transactions are defined in the following files: Classifies spot and forward contracts, according to local central bank and internal reporting rules. Defines the spot default value date. Uses the OFS.SOURCE ID present in this field to perform FX.BULK.ORDER . Uses the version ID present in this field as VERSION to populate or create FX BULK DEAL master records. Defines default category code for spot, forward and swap transactions. Defines the precious metal currency codes, hence, any number of currency codes can be defined. Conditions under which deals are entered with split value dates. Indicators show if Profit & Loss (P&L) and EXCHADS entries are booked when revaluation of forward and spot contracts takes place. Creates rounding rule for transactions. The Cus Margin Default field determines if the FX Group Cond ID corresponding to a customer is defined in a FX contract or not (subjected to the existence of the condition priority setup in FX margin). The values accepted are Yes, No and None. If set as Yes, the FX Group Cond ID defaults from SEC.ACC.MASTER ( SAM ). If it is not available in SAM , it defaults from CUSTOMER.CHARGE . If set as No or None, the FX Group Cond ID does not default from SAM or CUSTOMER.CHARGE . However, the user can still define the margin percentage manually (together with treasury rate) and derive the customer rate in FX deal. |

| 3 | FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE | Classifies the deal types. A record in this application can control the default value for category codes, revaluation types, and allows delivery and types of options processing. The existing records can be amended and new records can be created. |
| 4 | FX.GEN.CONDITION | Identifies a specific group of customers, which can be cross-related to the group condition table, to define conditions applicable to that group. The groups are determined based on customer details such as sector and target. The criteria used and their priority are specified in the Condition Priority file in the record whose ID is FX.MARGIN. |
| 5 | FX.GROUP.CONDITION | Defines the spread or margin percentage for a specific customer, group of customers or default group. When a group customer is defined, the FX Gen Condition record needs to exist before any associated group condition is specified. For an individual customer, the ID is C , whereas, the default group ID is generally assigned as either 99 or 999. |
| 6 | FX.COMM.GROUP | Defines spread or margin based on currency, and the amount that falls in a range and is used in FX contracts. The FX Commission Group ID field in SAM is used in FX.BULK.ORDER application, and a reference to SAM is used in FX.GROUP.CONDITION . Hence, the margin is given in absolute terms or referred to FX Commission Group ID (based on which the margin is applied in an FX deal). |

**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX Spot | FX Spot is a contract of buying or selling a currency, commodity or security for immediate settlement (payment and delivery) on the spot date at a spot Rprice. |
| 2 | FX Forward | FX Forward is a contract of buying and selling an asset or a currency at a predetermined spot rate at a specified date in the future (which is greater than the spot date). The predetermined rate is called as the Forward Rate. |
| 3 | FX Swap | FX Swap is an agreement between counterparties to exchange currency. The agreement involves swapping of principal and interest payments between two different currencies. |
| 4 | Precious Metal Deal | Precious Metal Deals involve trading in various precious metals such as gold, silver, palladium, platinum and so on, in spot, forward or swap rates depending on the types of deals entered. |
| 5 | Single-rate Option | Single-Rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two specified dates at customer’s choice without incurring any penalty cost. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. |
| 6 | Multi-rate Option | Multi-rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two different option dates with different rates. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. In this, the applied rate depends on the period delivery. |
| 7 | Internal Deals | Internal Deals allow transfers between different positions or dealer desks. Hence, there is no need for accounting entries, payments, advices and so on. The system automatically updates the position, when an internal forex spot or a forward deal is entered. |
| 8 | Broker Deal | Broker Deals are entered when the counterparty is not known. The user needs to enter BR as sub-type and associated brokers deals. Once the counterparty name is known, BR is removed and the counterparty details are entered in the deal. |
| 9 | NDF Vanilla Deal | Non Deliverable Forward (NDF) Vanilla Deals is an hedging strategy, where parties in the contract agree to settle the profit or loss prior to the expiration date of the contract. A vanilla NDF transaction has an agreed rate fixing date, which is two working days before the settlement date. |
| 10 | NDF Exotic Deal | An Exotic NDF Deal allows in setting the fixing date as any date before the vanilla date in the tenure of the transaction. The fixing profit is discounted, if the NDF is fixed and settled early. The discount amount is amortised from the settlement date to the value date of the NDF. |

**Post Trade Events**

| Short Code | Name | Definition | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAMT | Early delivery | Trade will be settled early. | Full Early Delivery User creates a delivery tranche with complete contract balance and uses this code to indicate that the client has fully delivered the contract before maturity. The outstanding balance on the contract is updated as zero and the contract matures after authorization. |
| PEAM | Partial early delivery | Trade will be partially settled early. | Partial Early Delivery User creates a delivery tranche with partial amount available and uses this code to indicate that the client has delivered partial amount before the maturity date. The outstanding amount is reduced by the amount delivered. The contract does not mature until value date, as there is pending amount. |
| PRUR | Partial unwind rollover | Part of the trade will be settled on its original date and the remainder will rollover. | Partial Delivery and Partial Rollover on Due Date Partial amount is delivered on the maturity date and rest will be rolled over to an extended value date. The contract can be rolled over any time before the contract matures. |
| PRUW | Partial unwind | Part of the trade will not be settled. | Partial Cancellation Partial amount on the contract is cancelled and the outstanding or remaining amount is reduced by the cancelled amount. The contract will be in ‘live’ status until the value date for the settlement of outstanding amount. |
| ROLL | Rollover | Rollover of a previous trade. | Rolled Over Contract Marker The current trade is an extended trade and is linked to a cancelled trade. |
| UNWD | Unwind | Trade will not be settled. | Full Cancellation The complete contract amount is cancelled and there is no outstanding balance on the trade. |
| UNWR | Unwind rollover | Original trade will not settle on its original date and will be rolled over. | Full Rollover The complete contract amount is cancelled on the original trade and a new trade is booked with an extended value date for the same amount. |

**Post Trade Events**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Trade Event Type | Holds SWIFT codes for post trade events. The values are: UNWD - Complete amount on the contract is cancelled and there will be zero outstanding amount. PRUW - Partial amount, is cancelled and the outstanding deal amount is reduced to the extent of cancellation amount. |
| Canc Buy Date | Specifies the cancellation date of the bought currency. The date can be the same as Canc Sell Date or different in case of a split value date scenario. The cancellation buy date is always the current system date. |
| Canc Buy Amt | Specifies the amount of the bought currency to be cancelled. This amount is the full outstanding amount of the trade. |
| Canc Rate | Allows the usage of custom routines to derive the cancellation rate. The standard routine (model) calculates the indicative cancellation rate by deriving the forward rate or taking the spot rate based on the cancellation date (early or due date). The user can override the defaulted value, if required. |
| Canc Sell Date | Specifies the cancellation date of the sold currency. The date can be the same as Canc Buy Date or different in case of a split value date scenario. The cancellation sell date is always the current system date. |
| Canc Sell Amt | Specifies the amount of the sold currency to be cancelled. This amount is the full outstanding amount of the trade. |

**Post Trade Events**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Canc Pl Account | Specifies the charge account to be used while debiting or crediting the cancellation loss or profit. |
| Canc Pl Acc Ccy | Specifies the currency of the cancellation profit or loss settlement account. |
| Canc Pl Type | Specifies the charge type to be used to calculate cancellation charges. If input, the charge type must exist on FT.CHARGE.TYPE or FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record. |
| Canc Pl Amt | Specifies the charge amount entered or calculated, based on the charge type defined. |
| Canc Profit Pass | Specifies whether the cancellation profit will be passed on to the customer or retained by the bank. Y - Resulting profit upon cancellation of the contract is passed on to the client. N - Resulting profit upon cancellation is not passed on to the client. |

| Classification | holds the classification for the transaction type based on which a direction is assigned. Consider, AP is the first record created with Classification as Payments and ID suffix as 'P', then for all the subsequent records created, the system allows only suffix 'P' for payments classification. |

Direction as +1 for receipts classification. |

**Data Integration Management**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| GB Description | Holds the description of the record for mapping different message types to the events. |
| Message Type | Holds the message type records from IL.MESSAGE for which IL.EVENT mapping is done. |
| Message Tag | Holds the tag or element details to derive their values from the message. For mapping ISO15022 messages the value after the prefix ‘Tag’ must be specified. For mapping ISO200022 messages the opening elements alone must be specified. This field applies various symbols for different purposes like, ':' - Used as a conditional statement. For tag1PCRD:tag2, if tag1's value is PCRD, then tag2's values are retrieved. '[]' - Used when a field has multiple values from various tags. In decreasing order, priority drops. If Message Tag contains [tag1][tag2], there are two possible values in the corresponding field, from tag1 and tag2 each. Since the priority is in descending order; if tag 1 has no value, the system enters only tag 2's value in Event Field . '+' – Used when a field must store values from multiple tags. If Message Tag contains [tag1]+[tag2], the field stores the values of both tag1 and tag2, delimited by '/'. That is, the system enters tag1/tag2 values in Event Field . |
| Value Position | Determines the values to be picked from a tag or element and populates them in the associated Event Field . It is a multi-value field. For MT103 Tag32A is in the format of , that is, 32A:981209USD1000,00. The user can bifurcate the tag values and map to Event Field accordingly as below. Value Position 1.1 : 01-06 Event Field 1.1 : Value Date Value Position 1.2 : 10-REST Event Field 1.2 : Amount Value Position 1.3 : 07-09 Event Field 1.3 : Currency Similarly, the user can bifurcate specific positions alone and map to Event Field accordingly as shown below. Value Position 1.1 : 07-09 Event Field 1.1 : Currency |
| Event Field | Holds a valid field from IL.EVENT in which the above tag value must be populated. It is a multi-value field. For MT103 Tag32A is in the format of , that is, 32A:981209USD1000,00. The user can bifurcate the tag values and map to Event Field accordingly as below. Value Position 1.1 : 01-06 Event Field 1.1 : Value Date Value Position 1.2 : 10-REST Event Field 1.2 : Amount Value Position 1.3 : 07-09 Event Field 1.3 : Currency Similarly, the user can bifurcate specific positions alone and map to Event Field accordingly as below. Value Position 1.1 : 07-09 Event Field 1.1 : Currency |
| Conversion | Holds the routine used for any conversion of values derived from the messages. |

| Raw Message | Holds the raw messages of various SWIFT MT and ISO MX messages that are imported for event creation. |

| Currency | Holds the currency code for the event created. |
| Amount | Holds the amount derived from different messages. |
| Value Date | In case of manual events, this field captures the value date of the deal for which the event is created. In case of auto-updated events, this field holds the value date derived from tag 32 of the SWIFT MT message or the equivalent MX message strings. |
| Reporting Time | Holds the reporting time details based on, The availability of values in 13D tag in MT900, MT910, MT940, MT941, MT942, or MT950 messages. Credit time element of the camt.054, camt.053, or camt.052 messages. Manual input by the user. For STP event creation If the values in 13D tag or credit time element of the message are present, then the respective values are converted to one of the below formats and stored in this field. If not present, then the value of Event Date Time Creation is converted to one of the below formats and stored in this field. For Manual creation The user can enter the time in the specified format. If not present, then the value of Event Date Time Creation is converted to one of the below formats and stored in this field. Allowed formats are: . For example, 20240828T12:10. . For example, 20240828T12:10+ or 20240828T12:10-. . For example, 20240828T12:10+11:15 or 20240828T12:10-11:15. |

| Business Unit | Holds the business unit information with which the event record is associated. |
| Entity | Holds the entity information to which the event record belongs. |
| Country | Holds the country information with which the event record is associated. |
| Processed Status | Holds a flag value indicating the processing status of the event record. If the event record successfully creates or updates the subsequent transaction record in IL.TRANSACTION , the system updates the following values in this field. PROCESSED - Denotes successful creation or updation of transaction record. AMENDED - Denotes that an existing event is amended and is to be reconsidered for processing. NOT_PROCESSED - Denotes that transaction was not updated or created for an underlying event as the matching key was the same. |
| Account Id | Holds the account ID corresponding to clearing channels or Nostro. |
| External Acc No | Holds the actual account number that is assigned by the Account Servicing Institution to the account owner. It can be an IBAN or Non-IBAN account format. The system uses this number to identify or lookup the account during SWIFT or MX message processing. |

| Correspondent BIC | Holds the BIC of the correspondent, or the Account Servicing Institution required mainly for account lookup during SWIFT message processing. |

| Ordering Institution | Holds the ordering financial institution details other than the sender of the message. |

| Event Date and Time | Holds the date and time when the event received the message for creating the event record. This field updates the date and time for the first commit stage of the event only. |
| Related Reference | In case of auto-updated events, this field holds the value of related reference derived from tag 21 from SWIFT or its equivalent MX message. In case of manual events, the user must input the appropriate reference. |

| Dr Cr Indic | Holds the debit or credit indication of camt.054, camt.052, camt.053, MT942, MT940, and MT950 messages. |
| Transaction Status | Holds the status of a transaction which is used to update the status change of a transaction through its lifecycle based on the associated events. |
| Event Type | Holds the event type which decides the logic for updation of downstream tables in ILM. The allowed values are, None - The respective event updates IL.TRANSACTION . Transaction (Default) - The respective event updates IL.TRANSACTION . Balance - The respective event updates IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL . |
| Matching Status | Holds the matching status updated by the integrated reconciliation engine for the different lifecycles of a deal. The lookup values are, None - Matching status is not applicable for Transaction Type . Matched - Underlying Transaction Type is matched by reconciliation engine. Not matched - Underlying Transaction Type is not matched by reconciliation engine. |
| Cash Pos Type | Holds the different cash position types from IL.CASH.POS.TYPE . |

If the system finds an exact match for the matching key in transaction, then the event is marked as not processed. If the system does not find an exact match for the matching key in transaction, then the event is marked as processed and a Transaction is updated or created accordingly. The format for Matching Key is . |

MT103/202/pacs.008/pacs.009 (EP) to MT900/camt.054 with debit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with debit indicator(AP) or to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with debit indicator (SP). MT210/camt.057 (ER) to MT910/camt.054 with credit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with credit indicator (AR) or to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator (SR). MT900/camt.054 with debit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with debit indicator (AP) to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with debit indicator (SP). MT910/camt.054 with credit indicator/MT942/camt.052 with credit indicator (AR) to MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator (SR). Read the Working with Position Management User Guide for configurations of Transaction Type , Trans Status , Matching Status , and Cash Pos Type for each message. |
| Dealer | Holds dealer information of the associated event records. |
| Product | Holds the product information of the associated event records. |
| Business Unit | Holds the business unit information of the associated event records. |
| Entity | Holds the entity information of the associated event records. |
| Country | Holds the country information of the associated event records. |
| Manual Transaction | Holds a flag value specifying (defaulted by the system) if the transaction was created manually or automatically. Allowed values are, Yes – When the user creates the transaction manually. No – When the system creates the transaction even if events are created manually or automatically. |
| Dr Cr Indic | Holds the debit or credit indication of camt.054, camt.052, camt.053, MT942, MT940, and MT950 messages. |
| Related Reference | In case of auto-updated events, this field holds the value of related reference derived from tag 21 from SWIFT or its equivalent MX message. In case of manual events, the user must input the appropriate reference. |
| Matching Status | Holds the matching status updated by the integrated reconciliation engine for the different lifecycles of a deal. The lookup values are, None - Matching Status is not applicable for Transaction Type . Matched - Underlying Transaction Type is matched by reconciliation engine. Not matched - Underlying Transaction Type is not matched by reconciliation engine. |
| Cash Position Type | Holds the different cash position types from IL.CASH.POS.TYPE . |
| Tran Date and Time | Holds the date and time when the transaction record was created. This field updates the date and time for the first commit stage of the transaction only. |
| Auto Completion | Holds an indicator for transaction completion either by, the system (automatically) or the user (manually). This is based on the operations performed on message type and its related mandatory fields which update the Transaction Type , Trans Status , Matching Status , and Cash Pos Type respectively. This field holds the following values, Yes - The underlying transaction is completed automatically by the system. No - The underlying transaction is manually completed by the user amendment. |
| Matching Key | Holds the logic based on which transaction is updated using IL.TRAN.MAP.RULE . If the system finds an exact match for the matching key in transaction, then the system raises an error. If the system does not find an exact match for matching key in transaction, then a transaction is created or updated accordingly. The format for Matching Key is . |
| Tran Outs Liq Hrs | Holds a flag value indicating the transactions received after end-of-day statement messages (MT940/MT950/camt.053) or after Liq Mon Hrs . The allowed values are Yes and No. It is flagged as yes in following cases. If end-of-day statement is received for the current day, then it considers all transactions (MT900/MT910/camt.054/MT942/camt.052) received after it, until the next day’s opening time of Liq Mon Hrs . If end-of-day statement is not received or received after Liq Mon Hrs , it considers the time frame between Liq Mon Hrs of current and next day. |
| Input Date Time | Holds the date and time for each commit stage of transaction. |

**Liquidity Management**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Number | Holds the account ID for which the debit and credit movements are updated on a particular date. |
| Currency | Holds the currency of the account for which the credit and debit movements are updated on a particular date. |
| Opening Balance | Holds the opening balance of the account on a particular day. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Adj Act Bal value of the previous day record in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field as zero. This field is also updated when MT940/MT950/camt.053/MT941/camt.052 messages are received for the current day. |
| Ttl Credit Mvmt | Holds the sum of the total credit amount of an account during the day. |
| Ttl Credit Entries | Holds the total number of credit entries updated from IL.TRANSACTION with the following message types and the transaction status set as SN (Statement Not matched) received for the day: MT910 or camt.054 with credit indicator MT942 with credit indicator MT940/MT950/camt.053 with credit indicator |
| Ttl Debit Mvmt | Holds the sum of the total debit amount of an account during the day. |
| Ttl Debit Entries | Holds the total number of debit entries from IL.TRANSACTION with the following message types and the transaction status set as SN (Statement Not matched) received for the day: MT910 or camt.054 with Debit indicator MT942 with Debit indicator MT940/MT950/camt.053 with Debit indicator |
| Ttl Actual Balance | Holds the actual balance of the account at a particular time in the day. |
| Intraday Balance | Holds the latest intraday balance updated through statement messages on a particular day. |
| Intra Bal Time | Holds the time at which the latest intraday balance is updated through the statement messages on a particular day. |
| Susp Intra Bal | Holds the difference in balance, after the intraday balance information is received through statement messages (MT941 or camt.052). This field is updates in the below sequence: For first intraday hit the Susp Intra Bal is the difference between the Intraday Balance and Ttl Actual Balance fields. For remaining instances of nth intraday hit, all the Susp Act Bal fields (n-1,n-2… multivalue) are first calculated. Susp Intra Bal for the nth instance is then calculated as a difference between the Intraday Balance at the nth instance and the SusP Act Bal (n-1 multivalue). Susp Intra Bal (n-1,n-2,… multivalues )are maintained the same for multiple instances of the intraday hit. |
| Susp Act Bal | Holds the value after adjusting the total actual balance with the suspense intraday balance and the suspense EOD balance at a particular time in the day. |
| Susp Open Bal | Holds the difference between the opening balance updated through the statement message (MT950, MT940, or camt.053) and the calculated opening balance for the current day. |
| Net Bal Diff | Holds the net balance difference based on the number of intraday statement hits and EOD hit at a particular time of the day. |
| Adj Act Bal | Holds the latest values from the nth multivalue of the Susp Act Bal field at a particular time of the day. |
| Transaction ID | Holds the latest IL.TRANSACTION ID reference that has updated the balances for an account at a particular time of the day. |
| Time Indication | Holds the time indication information that was updated in IL.TRANSACTION for the following message types: MT900, MT910, or camt.054 with debit-credit indicator MT942, camt.052 with debit-credit indicator MT940, MT950, camt.053 with debit-credit indicator |
| Closing Booked Bal | Holds the closing balance of an account on a particular day updated through the statement messages (MT940, MT950, and camt.053). |
| Susp EOD Bal | Holds the difference in the balance after the EOD balance information is received through statement messages (MT940, MT950, or camt.053). This field is updated in the below sequence: All the Susp Act Bal (n-1,n-2… multivalue) fields are calculated. Once the Susp Act Bal is calculated the Susp EOD Bal is calculated using the below formula, The nth Susp Act Bal multivalue field is calculated based on the EOD statement hit. |
| EOD Bal Time | Holds the time at which the EOD balance was updated through the statement messages (MT940, MT950, or camt.053) on a particular day. |

| Days Post Value Date | Holds the number of days after the value date for an Event and Transaction to be removed from the live IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION tables and to be written to the respective history files. |

| Liq Mon Hrs | Based on the value configured here, the first and last records of IL.TIME.BASED.BAL are created which denotes the start and end time of the intraday position graph. . It should be configured in such a way that EOD statement is also processed within the time period. Consider a bank that has an SLA with its nostro correspondent to receive the EOD statement at YY:MM Hrs on a daily basis. This field should be configured as XX:MM - ZZ:MM, where XX:MM are the opening liquidity hours and ZZ:MM are the closing liquidity hours which should be greater than receiving time of the EOD statement (YY:MM) Hrs. |
| Time Freq Bal | Specifies the frequency in which IL.TIME.BASED.BAL records should be created within the Liq Mon Hrs configured. |
| Ext Reconciliation | Specifies if the intraday liquidity system is integrated with an external reconciliation engine. Allowed values are Yes and No . |
| Mode | Specifies the mode of Intraday Liquidity Management. Allowed values are: Standalone: The Intraday Liquidity solution is integrated with an external payment system, liquidity management system, or treasury management system which acts as the source system. Embedded: The Intraday Liquidity solution is integrated with the in-house Temenos payment system and other modules of Temenos which act as the source system. The system currently supports only the Embedded mode. |

When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘Y’ and the system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table with the Adj Act Bal value of the previous day record in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value, the system updates the Opening Balance field in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table with the Closing Balance value of previous day record in the IL.ACCOUNTS.DAILY.BAL table. When the Balance Rollover field in IL.ACCOUNT is set as ‘N’ and system has not received an MT940/MT950/camt.053 message for the previous day with a Closing Balance value , the system updates the Opening Balance field as zero in the IL.BALANCE.MVMT table. |

**MISC**

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| IL.PARAMETER | The IL.PARAMETER table defines the rules by which the ILM system operates allowing the users to pass through a stored procedure with a single parameter table. This is achieved without modifying the underlying code by having complex business logic within a single routine, making it easier to manage and execute. The configurations done here are used in the downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT , IL.TRANSACTION , IL.BALANCE.MVMT , and IL.TIME.BASED.BAL for processing the liquidity positions and balances based on the accounts. |
| IL.ENTITY | The IL.ENTITY table stores details of the entities which refers to a distinct unit that has its own legal and operational identity to perform the business functions for liquidity monitoring. It also allows the user to set up parent-child entity relationships, which are used to represent the hierarchical structures of the bank. This helps in monitoring the liquidity at an individual level or the overall liquidity at a lead entity level within the liquidity management solution. The entity configured here is used in downstream static tables like IL.ACCOUNT and IL.BUSINESS.UNIT , along with the dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity based on the entity. |
| IL.ACCOUNT | The IL.ACCOUNT table contains the nostro accounts for which intraday liquidity is to be monitored. Liquidity management in nostro accounts involves ensuring there are sufficient funds available to meet the bank's transaction needs. This requires careful monitoring of receipts, payments, and obligations to avoid overdrafts and optimize cash flow. Effective liquidity management helps banks maintain appropriate balances and improve their overall capital management framework. The accounts configured here are used in downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity positions and balances based on the accounts. |
| IL.SOURCESYS | A source system is an authoritative data source where core data elements are maintained and cash flow transactions originate. It relays all the liquidity-related SWIFT messages to Transact for processing it within the intraday liquidity solution. This solution is integrated with in-house modules such as TPH , DE , and EB.FILE.UPLOAD which acts as the source system and has the ability to integrate with any external source system to process the liquidity-related SWIFT messages. The source system configured here is used in downstream dynamic tables like IL.EVENT and IL.TRANSACTION for processing the liquidity based on the source system. |

**MISC**

| Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|
| Intraday Liquidity Position | The Intraday Positions screen provides the liquidity officer with the real -time intraday positions of a nostro account within the liquidity monitoring hours in a line graph format. |
| Cash Ladders | The Cash Ladder screen acts as an effective tool for managing liquidity, that displays the cash flows and obligations spread over time. The laddering helps manage operational costs by timing the incoming and outgoing funds. |
| Projections | The Projections screen provides the liquidity officer with the option to project the positions and transaction details from the current day within the liquidity monitoring hours. T to T+5 days projections is the default value for first-time selection. |
| Liquidity Events | A liquidity event is a message or data feed from an external system such as SWIFT, CBS, TMS, Payment Hub, and so on. Such liquidity events happen on a real-time basis. Hence, the ILM solution subscribes to such events and processes them in near real-time. An event can be created manually or automatically through STP. |
| Liquidity Transaction | A liquidity transaction contains the details generated through different events, such as receipts, payments, statements, and SWIFT messages from a source system for various entities in a liquidity management solution.​ A Transaction can be created manually or automatically through STP.​ It can also be automatically matched or manually matched by the user. Event to Transaction is a many-to-one relation. |
| Liquidity Balance Movements | Liquidity Balance Movements represent the Opening Balances, Intraday Balances, and Closing Balances on the account. Wherever possible, the balance movements are generated automatically from the bank's source systems such as the Core Banking System, Ledger Systems, Payment Hubs, and Treasury Management Systems. |

### Money Market (MM)


**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX.PARAMETERS | The rules that determined the Foreign Exchange (FX) transactions are defined in the following files: Classifies spot and forward contracts, according to local central bank and internal reporting rules. Defines the spot default value date. Uses the OFS.SOURCE ID present in this field to perform FX.BULK.ORDER . Uses the version ID present in this field as VERSION to populate or create FX BULK DEAL master records. Defines default category code for spot, forward and swap transactions. Defines the precious metal currency codes, hence, any number of currency codes can be defined. Conditions under which deals are entered with split value dates. Indicators show if Profit & Loss (P&L) and EXCHADS entries are booked when revaluation of forward and spot contracts takes place. Creates rounding rule for transactions. The Cus Margin Default field determines if the FX Group Cond ID corresponding to a customer is defined in a FX contract or not (subjected to the existence of the condition priority setup in FX margin). The values accepted are Yes, No and None. If set as Yes, the FX Group Cond ID defaults from SEC.ACC.MASTER ( SAM ). If it is not available in SAM , it defaults from CUSTOMER.CHARGE . If set as No or None, the FX Group Cond ID does not default from SAM or CUSTOMER.CHARGE . However, the user can still define the margin percentage manually (together with treasury rate) and derive the customer rate in FX deal. |
| 2 | FX.POS.TYPE | Assigns profit centre to the trading position, which can be amended as desired. |
| 3 | FX.TRANSACTION.TYPE | Classifies the deal types. A record in this application can control the default value for category codes, revaluation types, and allows delivery and types of options processing. The existing records can be amended and new records can be created. |
| 4 | FX.GEN.CONDITION | Identifies a specific group of customers, which can be cross-related to the group condition table, to define conditions applicable to that group. The groups are determined based on customer details such as sector and target. The criteria used and their priority are specified in the Condition Priority file in the record whose ID is FX.MARGIN. |
| 5 | FX.GROUP.CONDITION | Defines the spread or margin percentage for a specific customer, group of customers or default group. When a group customer is defined, the FX Gen Condition record needs to exist before any associated group condition is specified. For an individual customer, the ID is C , whereas, the default group ID is generally assigned as either 99 or 999. |
| 6 | FX.COMM.GROUP | Defines spread or margin based on currency, and the amount that falls in a range and is used in FX contracts. The FX Commission Group ID field in SAM is used in FX.BULK.ORDER application, and a reference to SAM is used in FX.GROUP.CONDITION . Hence, the margin is given in absolute terms or referred to FX Commission Group ID (based on which the margin is applied in an FX deal). |

**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FX Spot | FX Spot is a contract of buying or selling a currency, commodity or security for immediate settlement (payment and delivery) on the spot date at a spot Rprice. |
| 2 | FX Forward | FX Forward is a contract of buying and selling an asset or a currency at a predetermined spot rate at a specified date in the future (which is greater than the spot date). The predetermined rate is called as the Forward Rate. |
| 3 | FX Swap | FX Swap is an agreement between counterparties to exchange currency. The agreement involves swapping of principal and interest payments between two different currencies. |
| 4 | Precious Metal Deal | Precious Metal Deals involve trading in various precious metals such as gold, silver, palladium, platinum and so on, in spot, forward or swap rates depending on the types of deals entered. |
| 5 | Single-rate Option | Single-Rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two specified dates at customer’s choice without incurring any penalty cost. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. |
| 6 | Multi-rate Option | Multi-rate Option is the deal of exchanging one currency for another. The delivery takes place between two different option dates with different rates. The option occurs when the customer decides to take delivery of all or part of the transaction before the final value date. In this, the applied rate depends on the period delivery. |
| 7 | Internal Deals | Internal Deals allow transfers between different positions or dealer desks. Hence, there is no need for accounting entries, payments, advices and so on. The system automatically updates the position, when an internal forex spot or a forward deal is entered. |
| 8 | Broker Deal | Broker Deals are entered when the counterparty is not known. The user needs to enter BR as sub-type and associated brokers deals. Once the counterparty name is known, BR is removed and the counterparty details are entered in the deal. |
| 9 | NDF Vanilla Deal | Non Deliverable Forward (NDF) Vanilla Deals is an hedging strategy, where parties in the contract agree to settle the profit or loss prior to the expiration date of the contract. A vanilla NDF transaction has an agreed rate fixing date, which is two working days before the settlement date. |
| 10 | NDF Exotic Deal | An Exotic NDF Deal allows in setting the fixing date as any date before the vanilla date in the tenure of the transaction. The fixing profit is discounted, if the NDF is fixed and settled early. The discount amount is amortised from the settlement date to the value date of the NDF. |

**Call or Notice Placement Deal Processing**

| Accrual Method | Description |
|---|---|
| First day (default) | Performs accrual on the first day of the value date of the contract. |
| Last day | Considers the last day of the interest period for accrual while skipping the first day in the interest calculation period. |
| Both day | Denotes one-day additional accrual, as both first and last day are included in the accrual. |

**Misc**

| Enquiry | Description |
|---|---|
| Cash Flow | PM.CAS enquiry shows daily analysis of net inflows and outflows along with cumulative balance. |
| Liquidity Position | PM.GAP enquiry shows the future amounts placed and taken, and the average and break-even rate of a particular currency represented by different time band buckets (as defined on PM.CALENDAR). It also displays the future interest movements. |
| Nostro Position | NOSTRO.POSITION enquiry shows the current and forward positions of the Nostro accounts by currency. |
| Interest Rate Exposure | PM.IRE enquiry shows the asset and liability by maturity with average rate, calculation of the break-even rate for each period and cumulative balance. |
| Interest Rate Sensitivity | PM.INT enquiry shows the effect of profit and loss on increasing the interest rates in series of 25 basis points. |

**Misc**

| Product | Description |
|---|---|
| Taking (Deposit) | Taking (also known as a deposit) is a contract between two financial organisations, mainly banks or financial institutions, where one bank or financial institution borrows money from the other bank or financial institution. The terms and conditions of taking could vary, such as fixed term or call or notice basis with a fixed or floating interest rate linked to a base rate using a key. |
| Sundry Deposit (Payable) | Sundry Deposit is a simple one-time deposit without interest, on a fixed or call basis. The purpose is to allow the bank to record amounts due to clients, without having to pay any interest. |
| Placement (Loan) | Placement (also known as Loan) is a contract between two financial organisations, mainly banks or financial institutions, where one bank or financial institution lends money to the other bank or financial institution. The terms and conditions of placement could vary, such as fixed term or call, notice basis with a fixed or floating interest rate linked to a base rate using a key. |
| Sundry Loan (Receivable) | Accounts receivable is a simple one-time loan, without interest on a fixed or call basis. The purpose is to allow the bank to record amounts or miscellaneous items due from clients without having to pay any interest. |

**Misc**

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Call or Notice Placement | To lend a fixed amount of money in a specific currency, where the tenure of the contract ends based on call or number of days of notice. The frequency of interest payment needs to be specified, which can be fixed or floating. |
| 2 | Fixed Maturity Placement | To lend a fixed amount of money in a specific currency to the counterparty. The length of the tenure is fixed at the time of agreement. Interest rate on the contract value can be fixed or floating. |
| 3 | Call or Notice Taking | To borrow a fixed amount of money in a specific currency where the tenure of the contract ends based on Call or Number of days of Notice. The frequency of interest payment needs to be specified, which can be fixed or floating. |
| 4 | Fixed Maturity Taking | To borrow a fixed amount of money in a fixed currency. The length of the tenure is fixed at the time of agreement. Interest rate on the contract value can be fixed or floating. |

**RFR Linked Placement or Taking**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Rfr Convention | Market convention for rate compounding or averaging The MM application follows Lookback methodology. |
| Rfr Lookback Type | Type of Lookback method applied for rate compounding or averaging. It has the following types for rate calculations: Narrow Definition – Uses the original interest period day count with lookback rate. For example, if Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Friday’s weight (three days) to the Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift – Uses the original day count of the lookback rate. For example, if Wednesday rate is used for Friday, apply the Wednesday’s weight (one day) to the Wednesday’s rate. |
| Rfr Calc Method | Calculation methods for RFR averaging are: Compound Simple Amount NCCR |
| Rfr Spread Treatment | Spread treatment methods during the RFR averaging are: Spread-Inclusive - Uses the spread within the averaging calculation along with daily rates. Spread-Exclusive - Adds the spread separately after RFR averaging is done. |
| Rfr Period Day Count | Treatment of the last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It allows the following values: Full - Last RFR with day weightage, which is applicable for the full interest period. Today - Last RFR with its original day weightage, which is applicable till the current business day. |
| Rfr Decimals | Rounding value applied for RFR |

**RFR Linked Placement or Taking**

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Key | PERIODIC.INTEREST record key that has the RFR. |
| RF Rate | Stores the compounded Risk-Free Rate. This is a system updated field. |
| RFR Lookback Days | Number of lookback days considered for RFR calculations. |

Validation - The Limit product holds the Validation Limit records, which constitutes the maximum cap allowed for the underlying Utilisation Limits within a Limit structure.
