**Group Fixing or Floating Rate**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Instrument | Defines the application (for example, SWAP ). |
| Type | Subtype within SWAP group. This can be any type defined in the SWAP.TYPE application. |
| Currency | Currency to be fixed. Only one currency can be specified. |
| PI Int Key | Descriptor for the rate set supplying the fixing rates. In SWAP , this is the value in MARKET.RATE.TEXT . |
| Rate Selection | Uses mid or bid-offer rate from the rate table. Allowed values are: Middle – The fixing process calculates and uses the mid-rate between the Bid and Offer rates as defined in the rate table. Bid-offer – The fixing process uses either Bid or Offer as appropriate for the deal type (asset legs uses the offer, liability legs use the bid). |
| Effective Date | Date on which the new rate takes effect. For the SWAP application, This is the date in Rr Schedule Date or Rr Process Date . This date represents the Rr Schedule Date field when the Processed Date Fixing field in ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMETER is set to No. This date represents the Rr Process Date field when Processed Date Fixing field in ST.GROUP.FIX.PARAMATER is set to Yes. When the service is run, ST.GROUP.FIX records are processed in the sequential order in which they were created by matching the respective Rr Process Date field. Refer to Processed Rate Reset Date Fixing Logic for further information. For FRA application, this date represents the settlement date and not the fixing date. |
| Timing | Specifies when the operation is executed. Allowed values are: Wid (executed immediately after the ST.GROUP.FIX record is authorised) Service (rate fixing for the groups defined takes place only on running the service ST.EOD.GROUP.FIX ). |
| Allow Refixing | The fixing operation overwrites rates for trades that are already fixed (manually or automatically). Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Fixing List | Decides whether the list of trades fixed is required for the user to view a list of trades about to be fixed. Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Error Log | Decides whether the process should write to the log. Allowed values are Yes or No. |
| Trade Status | Decides whether a fixed trade goes directly to authorised or unauthorised status. Allowed values are: AUTH – Trade is authorised. WAIT– Trade is not authorised. |
| Last Run Date | The date, status (started or completed) and number of errors (if completed). The system controls and updates this field. |
| Pl Record Key | Allows the user to verify the PI record referred for Rate fixing and to alter Pl Record Key when necessary. When the user does not enter the PI record key, the system defaults to the existing PI record with the currency and rate code for the effective date specified. If no PI record exists for the effective date, the system loops and searches for an existing PI record by reducing one calendar day from Today. The system throws an override when a different dated PI record is selected by the user for the given effective date. It is an associated multi-value field of TYPE. |
| Fixing Rate | Allows the user to verify the rates defaulted from PI table based on the Pl Record Key field confirmed by the user. The system defaults the rates based on rate selection field (middle or bid offer) and would be referred to the Swap records for rate fixing by ST.GROUP.FIX service. It is an associated multi-value field of TYPE. |

**Misc**

| Product | Description |
|---|---|
| Vanilla Swap | The exchange of a fixed rate for a floating rate is undertaken. The notional principal is constant throughout the life of the contract |
| Currency Interest Rate Swap | The principal is either notional or exchanged but in different currencies |
| Amortizing Swap | The principal is amortized over the life of the contract |
| Accreting Swap | The principal is increased over the life of the contract |
| Roller-Coaster Swap | The principal is subjected to increase and decrease during the life cycle |
| Balloon Swap | A smaller portion of the principal amount is amortized while a larger amount is retained until the end of the contract |
| Basis Swap | Both legs of the swap involve a floating rate instead of fixed vs floating as seen on the vanilla swap |
| Risk-Free Rate Swaps | RFR swaps with Lookback and Lockout RFR market conventions in addition to Plain Arrears and Rest Cut-Off. It also enables the user to delay the actual interest payment and generate payment messages when the final RFR is available in the system. |

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Swap Parameters | This table allows the users to define the system lever parameter for processing of Swap contracts. The record ID of this table is 'SYSTEM'. User can also update parameter values for Days post maturity, Maturity Date, Defer online position update and Defer online schedule update. |
| 2 | Swap Reval Parameter | This table allows the user to parameterize the Swap Revaluation setup. The record ID of this table is 'SYSTEM' and consists of parameter values for PL Category, Revaluation Credit Code, Debit Code and setup related to Asset & Liability Short and Long rates selection, Zero coupon rate selection, NPV forward rate, NPV accrual adjustment. |
| 3 | Swap Type Record | This file contains the definition of all types of Swap contracts allowed on the system. It contains details such as Category Codes for Booking Revaluation Entries, Accounting (ON/OFF Balance sheet) and Revaluation Method. |
| 4 | Swap Agreement Type | This file stores the types of agreements that are used in Swap contracts. Each swap contract has to be linked to an agreement type, based on which the validations are performed. The user can modify an existing record and as well create new records. |
| 5 | Swap Activity Record | This file allows the user to define and control the delivery output for Swap module. The records in this file define all the activities that produce delivery outputs. These activities relate to specific events during the life of the contract. If required, the delivery pertaining to each of these events can be produced prior to the event itself. In this case, the number of days in advance of the event that the advices are produced is defined in this file. |
| 6 | Market Rate Text | This table defines descriptions of tradable interest rates that are recognised by SWIFT. The key of the periodic interest table corresponding to the rate described is linked in this file. Floating interest rates defined in Swap Contracts are must also be linked to this file. |

**Misc**

| S.No | Products | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest Rate Swap - Trade | Interest Rate Swap is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange the streams of Interest payments over a period of time. It does not involve the exchange of Principal, and the interests are calculated on the notional amount. The interest rates can be fixed or floating and the payment schedules are either generated from a frequency or can be manually defined. A Trade deal is a speculative transaction without an underlying asset. |
| 2 | Interest Rate Swap - Hedge | It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange streams of Interest payments over a period of time and or to lock in a profit or minimize the loss to offset a Loan or Deposit contract on bank book. |
| 3 | Currency Interest Rate Swap - Trade | It is an agreement between two counterparties to exchange the streams of Interest payments in different currencies over a period of time. Additionally, the principal amount can be exchanged between the counterparties at the beginning and end of the deal. Interest rates can be fixed or floating. The payment schedules can either be generated from a frequency or defined manually. |
| 4 | Currency Interest Rate Swap - Hedge | It is an agreement between the counterparties to exchange the streams of interest payment in different currencies over a period of time, mainly to lock in a profit (or minimize the loss) to offset a Loan or Deposit contract on banks book. |

**Past Due**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Liquidation Mode | Identifies how to handle overdue payments. The default for all contracts is Automatic but can be changed to Manual to invoke Past Due Processing. |
| Overdue Status | Identifies the status of the underlying PD.PAYMENT.DUE contract (GRA, PDO, NAB, WOF, CUR and so on) This is a no input field.. |

**Risk Free Rate**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Rounding | R ounding rules for RFR ( default ed on SWAP level ) |
| RFR Period Day Count | Treatment of last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It a llow s the following values: Full - L ast RFR with day weightage , which is applicable for the remaining period Today - L ast RFR with its original day weightage , which is applicable till the current business day |
| Rfr Paymt Dely Categ | Defines the suspense account category code for parking the interest amount during the delay payment period. |

**Risk Free Rate**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Coupon Rate | Coupon curve used to determin e the discount factors for revaluation of Overnight Index Swaps ( OIS ) contracts |
| RFR Zero Rate | C urve with zero rates for the revaluation of OIS contracts |

**Risk Free Rate**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| RFR Convention | Identifies the market convention used for rate averaging. The allowed values for swaps are: Plain Arrears – Indicates the daily averaging of RFRs Reset Cut-Off – Indicates the daily simple averaging of RFRs with last N days set as cut-off days. This uses the last RFR available in the averaging Lookback – Indicates the daily averaging of historical RFRs with a lag of N days set as lookback days to arrive at the average rate applicable for a given interest period Lockout – Indicates the daily compound averaging of RFRs with last N days set as lockout days. This uses the last RFR available in the averaging |
| RFR Lookback Type | Identifies the type of lookback method to be applied for rate compounding or averaging. There are two types of lookback methods: Narrow Definition – Original interest period day count is used with lookback rate for rate calculations. Example: If Wednesday’s rate is used for Friday, then apply Friday’s weight, that is, three days to Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift – Original day count of the lookback rate is used for rate calculations. Example: If Wednesday’s rate is used for Friday, then apply the Wednesday’s weight, that is, one day to Wednesday’s rate. |
| RFR Lookback Days | Identifies the number of lookback days to be considered for RFR calculations. |
| RFR Calc Method | C alculation method for RFR averaging: Compound Simple |
| RFR Spread Method | S pread treatment method during the RFR averaging: Spread-Inclusive - Spread is taken within the averaging calculation along with the daily rates Spread-Exclusive - S pread is added separately after RFR averaging is done |
| RFR Cut -O ff Days | C rystallisation period (Number of business days prior to period end date when rate referencing stops and last available RFR is used for the remaining days) for the reset cut-off market c onvention |
| RFR Payment Delay | Identifies whether the payment on the given interest period can be delayed by N days |
| RFR Rounding | Defaults from SWAP.PARAMETER and overrid es on SWAP.TYPE |
